comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

A man with large, exaggerated flame-patterned hair (purple/lavender flame designs on a tall, oversized head) sits on the left wearing a blue shirt and round glasses, holding a sheet of paper with arithmetic written on it. A red-haired woman in a light green/mint top and pink skirt stands on the right, gesturing toward him with an excited, open-mouthed expression. A framed picture hangs on the green wall behind them.

Man (with flame-like hair): "TWO TIMES TWO IS THREE."

Woman (red hair): "WRONG AGAIN MUTANT!"

Caption (below panel): Doctors said Horton was blessed with an unusually large functional brain. Sadly, it was later discovered that two-thirds of his oversized cranium were occupied by the little-known "Stupid Lobe."
comics.hoverText: This was literally the first single panel comic idea I ever had, though it isn't the first drawing. I revised it around 2005 or so, at a point when I apparently thought fingertips were square-shaped.
comics.voteyText:
Header text at top: "30 YEARS LATER..."
A black-and-white drawing of a man with a tall, elongated head standing behind a podium that bears a presidential-style seal, speaking into a microphone.
Man at podium (speech bubble): "MY FELLOW AMERICANS..."

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

A store shelf is shown in close-up. The top shelf holds yellow boxes of a product called "MANPONS," each box bearing the male/Mars symbol (a circle with an arrow) and the words "HEAVY DUTY." The boxes are partly cut off, so the labels read "PONS," "MANPONS," "MANPONS," and "MANPON..." left to right.

The lower shelf holds several brown jars labeled "BEEF JERKY" (with small barcode/weight text), and to the right a pink book labeled "FILTHY MAGAZINES" and a blue box labeled "BOOZE 96 PACK."

Caption (below panel): Actually, there isn't anything inside a container of Manpons. Men just enjoy sending out their wives to pick up a box.
comics.hoverText: Actually there's a little post-it chastising you for your own insecurities.
comics.voteyText: A close-up of the pink book/magazine. Text on the cover: "FILTHY MAGAZINE" / "THIS ISSUE:" / "GROSS STUFF"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

A young man in a yellow shirt with glasses leans aggressively toward another young man in a green shirt, fingers splayed and wiggling, casting a spell at him.

Man in yellow shirt (shouting): MAGIC MISSILE!

Sound/motion text near his wiggling fingers: *wiggle wiggle*

The man in the green shirt stands calmly, holding a sandwich, taking a bite and looking unimpressed.

Caption (below panel): As it turns out, playing "Dungeons and Dragons" doesn't drive adolescents to murder, but not for lack of trying.
comics.hoverText: The real error here was using a level 1 spell on a level 5 opponent.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of the same yellow-shirt man's face, now looking exhausted and defeated, with a heavy drooping mouth and tired eyes.
Man (speech bubble): EXCUSE ME, SIR, MAY I SEE YOUR THAC0

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man with reddish-brown hair, wearing a green sweater, sits at a yellow table eating a bowl of nuts. He holds a nut up near his face, examining it with a puzzled expression. A blue mug sits on the table. A framed picture of a bowl of nuts hangs on the wall behind him.

Man (thought bubble): THAT'S ODD.

Caption (below panel):

Carl had just unwittingly stepped into The Twilight Zone. Fortunately, this was the area of The Twilight Zone where the only oddity was that walnuts tasted a little more like hazelnuts.

He later went mad due to unrelated circumstance.
comics.hoverText: Really? All that and you still want hovertext? Go read a book.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of the man's worried, sweating face, looking off to the side.
Man (speech bubble): IS THAT WALL BEHIND ME CURVY OR STRAIGHT? WHO DRAWS THIS SHIT?

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

A kneeling man (named Tom) holds open a small ring box and looks up at a woman.

Man (Tom), beginning to speak: "WILL YOU -"

Woman, interrupting and gesturing: "YES TOM, OF COURSE!"

Caption (below the panel): The "shut your trap" ring was going over remarkably well.
comics.hoverText: Tom was so disconnected from his own feelings that he offered gold and jewels whenever expressing himself. By the time he and Sally had been together for five years, he had begun to understand that his emotional weaknesses should be shared with the woman he loved most. But, it was too late. With the millions of dollars in rings, she had escaped to Argentina, and love.
comics.voteyText: A close-up of a gold ring shaped like a pair of pursed/closed lips. Tiny engraved text on the band reads: "NOBODY CARES".

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

Two men sit at a table in a dim room. One wears a yellow sweater, the other a green sweater. The man in yellow speaks, looking toward a third figure who is slumped face-down on the table, dead, with smoke rising from his body and a smashed/burnt object beside his head.

Man in yellow sweater: "PLAY FOR SECOND?"
comics.hoverText: Fifteen years after writing this cartoon, I realize this isn't how Russian Roulette works.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of a man's face (the man in the green sweater) looking weary and unimpressed.
Man in green sweater: "THAT IS REALLY QUITE CALLOUS, BOB."

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A caped, heroic-looking man stands triumphantly atop a pile of fallen blue-skinned figures, pointing forward with one fist raised.

Man (Hamlet): "YOU MAY NOW BE THE ROYAL KING OF DANES, BUT I AM HAMLET, UNDEAD KING OF PAIN!"

A blond man in a red shirt watches from the foreground, seen from behind.

Caption (below panel): Hamlet II would actually be a lot better than the original despite a number of plot holes, most of them related to time travel.
comics.hoverText: The part where Ophelia turns out to have survived by secretly being a mermaid was pretty good, though.
comics.voteyText:
Title text: "ALSO... HAMLET IS PREDATOR"
Two faces shown in profile facing each other: on the left a man's calm human face, on the right a creature with mandibles spread open like the Predator alien.

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A blonde woman stands at a podium in front of red theater curtains, smiling and gesturing/pointing to one side.

Woman (at podium): "Welcome to our new wildlife club! Let's introduce ourselves, shall we? You there, the angry gentleman loading the pistol."

Caption (below panel): Cindy never could account for the unpopularity of Club Baby Seals.
comics.hoverText: It later turns out they're just in Texas.
comics.voteyText:
A simply drawn smiling face with a speech bubble.
Face: "Is it because we beat puppies to death"

comics.comicText:
Single panel. A Darth Vader-like masked, helmeted figure in black looms over a young blond person seen in profile at lower left.

Vader figure: "I AM YOUR FATHER."

Young blond person: "That's great Dad. Hey, you think maybe you could have told me that BEFORE you cut off my arm?"

Caption below the panel: After he lost his other arm, Luke began to see his father's point of view.
comics.hoverText: There should've been a moment where Vader just quiets down and gets sarcastic with Luke. 'Oh, you lost an arm. Wow, I bet that's super painful. Can't imagine what that's like.'
comics.voteyText:
A simpler line-drawing panel. The young blond person (left) faces the masked figure (right).
Young blond person: "Great fight. I've gotta HAND it to you!"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

A leprechaun in a green suit and top hat sits atop a large golden pot at the end of a rainbow, gesturing toward a person whose head is visible in the lower right foreground.

Leprechaun: "SORRY LADDY, BUT THERE BE NO GOLD HERE!"

Caption (below panel): This was the "painful bowel obstruction" end o' the rainbow.
comics.hoverText: Fun Fact: When I switched to doing single panels in 2002, after having done short character-based strips for a bit, an early reader identified this particular comic as the reason she stopped reading. This was a bit distressing, since at the time, that one reader was about 10 percent of my audience.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of a smiling person's face. An off-panel speaker addresses them.
Off-panel speaker: "WHY ARE YOU SO HAPPY?"
Smiling person: "I JUST CAME FROM THE DELIGHTFUL BOWEL OBSTRUCTION END O' THE RAINBOW"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man with brown hair, wearing a green shirt, stands with his hand to his chin, contemplating a large arched wooden gate. Above and behind the gate, a row of grinning skulls sits atop spikes amid red and orange flames against a magenta sky. A handwritten note is pinned to the gate.

Note on gate: "If you go in here, you will definitely die."

Caption (below panel): In retrospect, the gate seemed oddly foreboding.
comics.hoverText: Ted was especially concerned that the designer of the gate forgot to color in the pikes under the skulls.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of a man's face speaking.
Man: "Arby's needs a better slogan."

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

A man sitting at a bar leans back as a glowing green substance (vomit) erupts toward him.

Man: ARE YOU DIVINE INSPIRATION?

Glowing green vomit: NOPE, I'M WHISKEY. TIME TO PUKE!
comics.hoverText: Nah, just kidding. You're actually having an auditory hallucination that's coincident with a bleeding retina.
comics.voteyText:
A person's face leaning over, with a stream of vomit issuing from their mouth.
Text: SINGLE MALT PUKE!

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel)

A red-and-purple-robed figure (the headless horseman) sits at a dinner table across from an elderly woman in glasses, a yellow sweater, and an apron-like top who is eating a plate of food.

Headless horseman: MOM, I CAN'T JUST CUT OFF ANYONE'S HEAD AND WEAR IT. I HAVE TO WAIT FOR THE RIGHT ONE TO COME ALONG.

Elderly woman (the mom): THAT'S FINE SWEETIE. IT'S JUST THAT I'D LIKE TO SEE MY OWN SON'S FACE SOME TIME BEFORE I DIE.

Headless horseman (gesturing, hands raised): YOU ALWAYS DO THIS!

Caption below the panel:

Eventually the headless horseman settled on the head of an overbearing elderly woman. It was odd at first, but it kept his mom quiet.

Dead quiet.
comics.hoverText: I wonder how real headless horsepeople see. Echolocation?
comics.voteyText:
A simple line drawing of a woman's head (now the head the horseman wears) with a slightly pained, deadpan expression.
Head: THIS MAY IMPACT MY DATING LIFE

comics.comicText:
Single panel:

A figure in the classic striped-shirt, bobble-hat, and round-glasses style of a "find the hidden character" puzzle has been partly converted into a machine. He has multiple metallic, tentacle-like robotic arms extending from his body, a mechanical/camera-lens-like apparatus over part of his face, a riveted metal patch on his torso, and a peg-leg prosthetic. He stands holding a cane.

Caption (below panel): "We found Waldo, but it was too late. He was already one of them."
comics.hoverText: ODLAW HAS BEEN TERMINATED. HA. HA. HA.
comics.voteyText: A small, crudely-drawn robotic stick figure with antenna-like protrusions stands alone. A speech bubble above it reads: "ASSIMILATE!"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

Two characters sit across a green table from each other. On the left is a man in a striped black-and-white shirt, a black domino mask, and a black wide-brimmed hat (styled as the Hamburglar). On the right is a green-skinned zombie with bulging yellow eyes.

Hamburglar: ROBBLE ROBBLE!

Zombie: BRAAAINS...

Hamburglar: ROBBLE, ROBBLE!

Zombie: BRAAAINS!

On the table between them: a small hamburger on a plate, a cup and saucer in front of each character, and a yellow box of food in the center.

Caption (below panel): Appointing The Hamburglar as ambassador to Zombie Island was rapidly proving to be a mistake.
comics.hoverText: Look, I admit this one in retrospect doesn't make a lot of sense, but look at the attention to detail on the Hamburlar, who is slowly loosing his middle finger!
comics.voteyText: A close-up of the Hamburglar's face, mask and red hair visible, mouth open in a worried/grimacing expression with teeth showing. A hamburger is perched on top of his head.

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

A giant gorilla clings to the side of a tall skyscraper, roaring.

Gorilla (large jagged sound burst): RAAHHH!

A tiny figure in the gorilla's hand (small speech): Eee!

On a building below, a red-headed man wearing a straw boater hat, a blue blazer, and a red bow tie stands giving a thumbs-up and pointing up at a red banner on the building.

Banner: 50% OFF! MACY'S

Man (speech bubble): OH MY GOD! LOOK EVERYONE! A SALE AT MACY'S!

Caption below the panel: Ted thought he was being ironic. Then a giant gorilla fell on him.
comics.hoverText: Which was sad because Ted had a wife and kids.
comics.voteyText:
A loose, sketchy black-and-white drawing of a person lying crushed/flattened on the ground amid scattered debris.
Thought bubble (faint, drifting from the figure): SO... CLEVER...

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (Main comic):

Woman at a typewriter (text she is typing, shown in narration/typed text at top): "And I'll never forget his last words to me: 'Lois, for the sake of the future of all mankind, don't ever tell anyone that I was Clark Kent.'"

Caption (below panel): Lois Lane finally gets that Pulitzer.
comics.hoverText: Judging by the way I drew her waist, she's probably only doing it in order to get something to eat.
comics.voteyText:
A man with a scowling, irritated expression (drawn as a Superman-like figure) speaks:
Man: "Now that it's out in the open, I will be charging for my services."

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

A man (the father) lounges in a deck chair on a porch, wearing a tank top, shorts/underwear, and glasses, holding a smoking pipe. A young boy sits on a stool nearby holding a cup.

Father (speech bubble): "SON, A GOOD WOMAN IS LIKE A DEEP FRIED CHIMPANZEE"

Caption (below panel): Dad never really bothered to explain his metaphors.
comics.hoverText: Twist: Dad is a modernist poet.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of the father's face (glasses, stern expression) with a speech bubble.
Father: "CHURN THAT CHIMP, BOY! CHURN IT GOOD!"

comics.comicText:
Single panel:

Setting: A nursing home bedroom. A poster on the wall reads:

WELCOME TO SHADY ACRES NURSING HOME

(below the text the poster shows small portrait images of faces)

An elderly person sleeps in a hospital-style bed with an IV drip stand beside it. A man wearing a cap stands in the doorway, glancing warily over his shoulder. He carries a large purple jar with a yellow label reading:

BEES

The jar is buzzing (small bee marks shown around it). A second, smaller jar sits on the floor nearby, along with a clipboard/papers and a telephone handset on the floor.

Caption (below panel): Ed occasionally had attacks of conscience, but deep down he knew it was the right thing to do.
comics.hoverText: Readers looking for intent beyond Ed Being a Dick will be sorely disappointed.
comics.voteyText:
Caption header (handwritten): DRAWING THE VOTEY, 13 YEARS LATER
A roughly sketched person (the artist) looks at the page with a slightly puzzled expression, hand near chin. A thought bubble above reads:
I DON'T GET IT.

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A blond man in a red shirt stands facing a red-haired woman in a green shirt. The woman, looking distressed, speaks.

Woman: "YOU'RE PEEING ON ME! I CAN'T BELIEVE YOU'RE PEEING ON ME!"

Caption (below panel):

Man: "What's the problem?! Don't you ever bathe?"
comics.hoverText: Not to mention the fact that we are all going to die one day and be forgotten.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of an angry man's face, brow furrowed, mouth open mid-shout.
Man: "THIS GENERATION IS ALWAYS BLAMING OTHER PEOPLE FOR THEIR PROBLEMS."

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A dark raven perched on a tree branch over a river, wings spread, cawing at a man standing nearby.

Raven: DEATH! DEATH FOR YOUUU! TOOOOODDDDDODD! WITH A KNIFE! PROBABLY WITH A KNIIIIIFE...

(The man, identified in the caption as Todd, stands at right looking unimpressed.)

Caption (below panel): The raven was remarkably articulate, but Todd simply didn't believe in talking birds.
comics.hoverText: The raven went on to give approximate error bars for his prediction.
comics.voteyText:
A simple line-drawn close-up of the annoyed raven, glaring with its beak open.
Raven: WELL FUCK YOU TOO, BUDDY.

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel)

Blonde woman (Sandy), recoiling with hand on the man's chest: "NO! NO!"

Smiling man in a red jacket, leaning toward her: "Your expression says no, but your double-negative says yes."

Caption below the panel: "Oh no!" thought Sandy. "Why did I decide to go to the grammar fraternity."
comics.hoverText: Later, a descriptivist intercedes to save Sandy, noting that a double negative does not always imply a non-negative statement.
comics.voteyText:
A woman's head (drawn in a loose sketch style) looks down/away with a weary, deflated expression.
Text above her: "WHAT ARE YOU DRIVING AT?"
Speech bubble pointing toward her: "NEVERMIND."

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

A blonde woman in a pink tank top stands in a doorway, facing a large red demonic creature with glowing eyes, a wide fanged mouth, and a tan/brown body, one clawed hand raised toward her.

Red creature: "I AM MOLOCH, EATER OF SOULS! I HAVE COME FOR YOUR FIRST BORN!"

Woman: "I'm sorry, we don't have any kids..."

Narration (caption): "MOLOCH WONDERS ALOUD IF THIS IS 276 SOUTH BENSON..."

Woman: "No, this is 276 NORTH Benson."

(An awkward pause is indicated by a small speech bubble with just an ellipsis.)

Woman: "STOP STARING AT MY CHEST MOLOCH."
comics.hoverText: Moloch means no offense! Moloch grew up with a different courtship paradigm!
comics.voteyText:
Close-up on Moloch's face (the red creature, shown in black-and-white line art) looking downcast.
Moloch: "MOLOCH SO LONELY."

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (main comic):

A man in a red jacket and bow tie stands at a bar or stage with a crowd of purple-toned silhouetted spectators behind him. He is tipping a drink up to his mouth, drinking from it. A wisp of smoke rises at left and small empty shot glasses sit on the counter in front of him.

Man (thought bubble): Voila.

Caption (below image): Harry Houdini does his famous "escape from reality" trick.
comics.hoverText: I consider this the first non-shitty comic I ever created.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of the same man's face, eyes half-lidded and bleary, looking intoxicated.
Man (speech bubble): NOW TO SNORT MY WAY BACK FROM THE NETHER WORLD.

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Santa Claus stands by a window at night, holding a gift-wrapped rifle with a green bow. He has a content, slightly mischievous expression and is humming, shown by a speech bubble containing a musical note.

Santa: (humming) ♪

On a box at the bottom of the panel:

Label: I ASSAULT RIFLE

Label (in a yellow burst): FOR KIDS!

Caption (below panel): Some years there are too many good kids. That's bad for business.
comics.hoverText: Seriously though, where does Santa get his raw materials? Does he do work on the side? Something doesn't add up.
comics.voteyText:
Handwritten text on the side of the box:
Ages: 240 months +

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Store sign above a shop window reads: "EMILY CHICKENSON"

A woman with dark hair pulled back, wearing an apron, stands in front of the storefront, smiling and pointing upward. She wears a sandwich-board / vertical sign that reads:

"THERE'S A CERTAIN CUT OF THIGH-MEAT- JUST $2.99!"

Caption (below panel): Before her life as a poet, Emily Dickenson had loftier goals.
comics.hoverText: Poetry may sustain us emotionally, but chicken literally tastes good.
comics.voteyText:
Handwritten in flowing cursive (a parody of an Emily Dickinson poem):
"Wild Night! WILD Night!
Were I with Thee,
Popcorn-Chicken would be
Our Luxury!"

comics.comicText:
Single panel:

A store interior. On the shelves to the left are paper scrolls/documents, with a yellow sign reading "ARTS DEGREES". Below them sit rolls of toilet paper, with another yellow sign reading "PARTICULARLY LOW QUALITY TOILET PAPER".

A man with orange/brown hair in a green shirt (glasses, facing away) stands at a counter. Behind the counter is a woman with blonde hair in a purple shirt, looking annoyed.

Woman (behind counter): "DO YOU HAVE TO PUT THOSE NEXT TO EACH OTHER?"

Caption below the panel (the man's reply): "Oh great. Are you another guy from the toilet paper company?"
comics.hoverText: Fun fact: This comic was made about six months before I graduated with a BA in Literature.
comics.voteyText: A close-up sketch of a single cylindrical roll standing upright on the floor. A small tilted sign in front of it reads: "2 PLY ARTS DEGREES".

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man (Dr. Bradford) with long hair and a mustache stands proudly beside a large purple-windowed carriage. Harnessed to the carriage in place of horses is a cow.

Cow: MOO.

Caption: After decades of development, Dr. Bradford finally reveals the world's first horseless carriage.
comics.hoverText: Ironically, it's actually five pigs in a cow suit.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of the same man's smiling face, with a speech bubble above him.
Man: The cow runs on thorium!

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

An old man lying in bed, reaching out a hand weakly as he speaks his dying words. A bald figure sits at his bedside watching.

Dying man: "ROOOSEBUUUUD... AND MORE MONNNEY... MORE... CASH... MONNEY..."

Caption (below panel): The actual last words of Citizen Kane.
comics.hoverText: Also my childhood sled, but with diamonds on it. Biiiiig oooooooooooooooooones.
comics.voteyText:
A loose sketch of the dying man's reaching hand and head, with more mumbled last words written above.
Dying man: "ALSO STOCK AND SLAVES."

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A single illustrated panel showing an ornate set of tall gates rendered in gold and red, with rays of light radiating behind them against a blue sky.

Caption below the panel:

In reality, there are no pearly gates. The gates of Heaven are made largely of gold, silver, and jewels.

Don't like it? Go to Hell!
comics.hoverText: The secret to great art is a lens flare over flat colors.
comics.voteyText: A large coin (or coin-like oval shape) sits at the bottom of the panel. A speech bubble points to it, reading: "MAN I LOVE MONEY"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A disheveled, wild-eyed news anchor with reddish hair sits at a news desk, leaning forward and pointing aggressively at the camera, holding a crumpled paper in his other hand.

Anchor: "IN TODAY'S NEWS, MY WIFE IS A GOOD-FOR-NOTHING HARLOT!"

Desk logo: "THE NEWS AT NINE"

Caption (below panel): There is a fine line between responsible journalism and drunken rage.
comics.hoverText: Still better than cable news.
comics.voteyText:
The same anchor, drawn in a loose sketch style, looks downcast with a sad expression.
Anchor (speech bubble): "This just in: I'M SO LONELY!"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A giant green monster (Godzilla-like) rampages through a city, roaring as flames shoot from its mouth and a building burns nearby.

Monster: RAAUGH!

Caption (below the panel):

Translation: Argh! My mouth is on fire! Why won't you help me?!
comics.hoverText: Godzillan is a remarkably terse language.
comics.voteyText:
A simpler line-drawn version of the monster, mouth open with flames, next to a speech bubble.
Monster: NOW YOU MUST PAY!

comics.comicText:
Single panel set on a stage with red curtains. A yellow banner behind the characters reads, in stylized game-show lettering, "the PRICE is LEFT" — where the "P" and "L" are drawn as a hammer and sickle and a Communist red star motif replaces the apostrophe-style decoration.

On the left, a smiling silver-haired man in a dark suit, red tie, and red pocket square holds a slim microphone and points one finger upward triumphantly.

On the right, a man in a hooded jacket raises both fists in the air with an exuberant, almost manic grin.

Caption (below panel): Before his rise as a gameshow host, Bob Barker was a rising star in the radical Communist party.
comics.hoverText: The hardest part was importing babushkas all the way from Mother Russia.
comics.voteyText:
Top caption box: ME, DRAWING THIS 12 YEARS LATER
A bearded man's face, looking weary and regretful.
Speech bubble: This has not aged well.

comics.comicText:
A group of characters parodying The Wizard of Oz pose together against an orange-red background, all smiling.

Cowardly Lion (a lion standing upright): COURAGE!

Scarecrow (a figure with a stitched, button-eyed face): A BRAIN!

Tin Man (a metal figure with a funnel hat): A HEART!

Dorothy (a girl in a blue dress giving a thumbs-up): THE SCARECROW'S NEW BRAIN!
comics.hoverText: Also autocracy would be nice.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up on Dorothy's smiling face, with two speech bubbles continuing her line.
Dorothy: AND YOUR POWER
The Scarecrow's hand reaches up toward her.

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

A man in a blue collared shirt and a blue baseball cap (bearing a Mickey-Mouse-ears logo) grips the hilt of a sword embedded in a stone. He is surrounded by several children and, on the right, a tall white-bearded figure in a pointed purple wizard's hat. The scene is set against a castle-like backdrop with turrets.

Caption (below panel): King Arthur pulls the mighty sword from the stone only to once again realize that he is not Arthur, King of Camelot, but Al, Janitor of Disneyland.
comics.hoverText: Merlin, on the other hand, is actually a confused wizard.
comics.voteyText:
A simple line-drawn face looking up, with a speech bubble.
Face: "The children made me do it, your honor."

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (main):

A Spider-Man-costumed figure swings into the scene, dramatically descending while another costumed figure (a blue-suited person) hangs upside down behind him.

Spider-Man (in speech bubble): "JUSTIIIIICE!"

Below, a man in a green shirt holds out a small box-like device toward another person whose head is obscured. A blonde woman in a blazer looks on with an alarmed expression.

Caption under panel (italic): What?

Caption below: Have you ever seen a spider shoot web out of its wrists?
comics.hoverText: Drop the gun, or face the sticky might of my ass-fluid!
comics.voteyText:
A bearded older man rests his head on his hand, looking unimpressed.
Handwritten text in a speech bubble above him: "SPIDERMAN IS UNREALISTIC."

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A group of young men hold up red plastic cups in a toast.

Man with raised cup: "ALRIGHT DUDES, NEW RULE! WHENEVER YOU TAKE A DRINK, YOU GOTTA TAKE A DRINK!"

Another man (cup raised): "YES!"

Caption (below panel): The origin of binge drinking.
comics.hoverText: This is also where proof by induction comes from.
comics.voteyText:
A grinning man holds up a cup.
Man: "WHENEVER IT ALL SEEMS LIKE A RIDICULOUS FARCE, TAKE A DRINK!"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man and a woman sit across a table from each other, plates of food in front of them. The man holds up one hand over his own mouth and extends his other fist toward the woman, holding up a small object (his thumb) with motion lines around it, gesturing as if the object is speaking. The woman looks at the object warily.

Caption (below panel, attributed to the object the man is holding up / ventriloquizing):

"STEVE'S THINKING ABOUT DUMPING YOU. YOU SHOULD BUY HIM A PLAYSTATION."
comics.hoverText: I will never tire of jokes about poorly-crafted handpuppets.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of the small object the man was holding up — a crudely drawn face with two big eyes and a grinning toothy mouth (a thumb-creature). It speaks in a speech bubble:
"YOU REALLY COULD DO BETTER."

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A professor stands at a green chalkboard, pointing at it with a pointer. The chalkboard reads:

DOES NOT

DOES TOO (the "DOES TOO" is circled)

Caption (below the panel): Professor Thompson proves once and for all that God does exist.
comics.hoverText: Note the ellipse here around Does Too, indicating that He totally does.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of the professor's smug face. His speech bubble reads:
TIMES INFINITY.

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (standing, holding tickets): HONEY! THEY'RE DOING PHANTOM OF THE OPERA AT THE THEATER ON FRIDAY!

Man (seated in an armchair, holding a TV remote): WOAH, WOAH, WOAH - ISN'T TV ON ON FRIDAY?
comics.hoverText: Ironically, the nuclear apocalypse happens that Thursday.
comics.voteyText: Man (close-up on his face, looking dismayed): I JUST CHECKED. IT IS. DAMMIT.

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A bald villain in a white outfit stands on a rooftop at night, holding up a knife and grinning. Superman is seen from behind in the foreground, his red cape and blue costume with the S-shield visible.

Bald villain: YOU MAY BE ABLE TO STOP SPEEDING BULLETS SUPERMAN, BUT CAN YOU STOP... A KNIFE?!

Superman: DAMN!
comics.hoverText: Also, what about really really slow bullets?
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of Superman's face (drawn in a simple sketch style).
Superman: I'M ALSO VULNERABLE TO NUNCHUKS, TREBUCHETS, AND HURTFUL PHRASES.

comics.comicText:
Single panel:

A banner overhead reads: "WALK FOR THE CURE"

An angry man with red hair wearing a blue jersey with the number 5 points up at the banner with one hand while gripping a fallen boy by the collar with the other. The boy, blonde and wearing a white jersey with the number 7, has crashed on roller skates (purple roller skates and a skate are visible on the ground) and looks frightened, clutching his scraped knee.

Man (red hair, #5 jersey): "Does the sign say 'SKATE for the cure?' Huh?! Does it?"
comics.hoverText: For real though, why not 'take money and donate it directly toward research for the cure' ?
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of a man's face, mouth open mid-shout, eyes intense.
Man: "THEIR DEATHS ARE ON YOUR HANDS!"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A person with brown hair and glasses, wearing a blue shirt, holds up a stapled paper packet labeled "FINAL EXAM." The exam has a large red circled "F" grade at the top, with rows of crossed-out, marked-wrong answers below.

Person (thought bubble): I HATE SCIENCE.

Caption (below panel): Reason #16 to get your degree in the arts.
comics.hoverText: I CAN MAKE THIS JOKE BECAUSE I HAVE A LITERATURE DEGREE
comics.voteyText:
A simply drawn man's face looks up at a large speech bubble.
Man: I WONDER IF I COULD MAKE A LIVING WRITING BONER JOKES FOR THE INTERNET.

comics.comicText:
Single panel:

The front of a passenger airplane, viewed head-on against a blue sky. Two pilots are visible through the cockpit windshield. A speech bubble (pilot announcement) reads: "AND AS WE BEGIN OUR DESCENT, YOU'LL NOTICE THE LITTLE HOUSES GETTING BIGGER AND BIGGER..."

A second, smaller bubble continues: "AND BIGGER..."

A third bubble, trailing off from the cockpit: "DUUUDE..."
comics.hoverText: I wrote this one toward the end of my time at college, and I still remember a poet friend telling me she thought this comic expressed how she felt about her last year in college.
comics.voteyText: A hand-drawn, sketchy close-up of a wide-eyed person's face staring out (as if at a window). Caption text: "The runway is so small." Followed by: "Almost invisible."

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A noir scene. A woman in a dark dress sits leaning toward a man in a fedora and trench coat at a table. A small red creature (resembling a worm or tentacle) protrudes from the side of the woman's head.

Woman (speech bubble): YOU CAN'T TRUST HER!

Caption (below panel): Something in her eyes told me I couldn't trust her.
comics.hoverText: But really, can you trust a man who wears a fedora indoors?
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of the small creature, drawn as a worm/serpent-like thing with a wide mouth and two dot eyes, attached to a curling segmented tail.
Creature (speech bubble): SHE'S FUCKING NUTS, DUDE.

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A tall gray robot with a single large red eye stands against a bright yellow background. It cradles two small dachshunds (weiner dogs) against its chest.

Robot: LOVE EACHOTHER!

One of the dogs: ARF?

Caption (below panel): Weiner dog breeding just hasn't been the same since giant robots conquered Germany.
comics.hoverText: Stupid robots think love is necessary for procreation.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of a single dog's face in profile, looking content.
Dog (thought bubble): This is so hot.

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A woman with orange hair in a red dress sits beside a man in a light blue polo shirt at an outdoor table, a rocky landscape behind them. She reaches up and cradles his face in her hands.

Woman: "You know it might just be the medication talking, but you're looking pretty hankercranberry octopopopoffpfffblffff..."

Caption (below panel): And then she kissed me.
comics.hoverText: WHY ISN'T THE BENCH COLORED IN?! THE FOURTH WALL IS BROKEN
comics.voteyText: A hand-drawn pill bottle labeled "ASPIRIN".

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A blond man with a crossbow bolt stuck in his chest stands facing a red-haired woman in a red shirt. He gestures with his hands, indignant.

Blond man: "YOU SHOT ME WITH A CROSSBOW?! THAT'S NOT WHAT YOU DO ON VALENTINE'S DAY! DON'T YOU KNOW ANYTHING?!"
comics.hoverText: Oh great, lung-blood. Great. Well, you've ruined this shirt, so that's just lovely.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of a man's face, drawn in a loose sketch style, with a crossbow bolt embedded in his neck/shoulder and a trickle of blood at his mouth.
Man: "VALENTINE'S IS A BULLSHIT HOLIDAY."

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man with short hair, his face contorted in anguish, screams while reaching toward the viewer with one hand. In his other hand he clutches a piece of paper, which is held upside-down and reads (reversed): "NOTE TO SELF: DON'T KILL STEVE." A bloody axe lies on the ground behind him.

Man: WHAT HAVE I DONE!?
comics.hoverText: Fortunately, it turned out he killed a different Steve.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of the same man, now smiling, holding up one finger as if making a point.
Man: IF ONLY I'D USED Post-it Notes™!

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Child (with reddish-orange hair, facing two parents): "Mom, dad, I just killed my sister. Slowly. Painfully. Oh, also, I'm gay."

Child: "Just kidding! Only half of that is true!"

Caption (below panel): Coming out of the closet is remarkably easy.
comics.hoverText: Feels so good to just level with you about my closet world of sibling-murder.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of the same child's face, looking skeptical/concerned, asking:
Child: "Why'd you believe the sister thing so readily?"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A classroom. A professor sits at a desk facing two students at school desks.

Student (a young woman with orange hair, raising her hand): PROFESSOR, WHY ARE THERE TRAP DOORS UNDER OUR DESKS?

Caption (below panel): Ahh, the first day teaching Natural Selection is always the best day.
comics.hoverText: Unfortunately, the A students did very little mating.
comics.voteyText: The professor (a man, smiling) speaks: The trap door contains food, and a baby with your genetics.

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A red-haired man in a blue jacket and green shirt stands in a courtroom, pointing angrily at people seated before him (presumably a jury). A judge sits at a bench in the background.

Red-haired man (shouting): "YOU PEOPLE ARE ALL CRAZY!"

Caption (below panel): Steve's lawyer tries the insanity defense.
comics.hoverText: The key to the insanity defense is trying it twice and expecting different results.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of the same red-haired man's angry, contorted face, still shouting.
Man: "ESPECIALLY THE FOREMAN"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Speaker (a person with reddish-brown hair, dressed in black, sitting at a table with a coffee cup): "So you see, science proves nothing! We only see what we're programmed to see. That's why poetry is the only way to transcend reality and reach truth."

Caption (below the panel): And yet somehow Stuart was unimpressed with Katie's "Ode to Shutting Up."
comics.hoverText: The fact that it was un-rhymed made it just a little bit extra insulting.
comics.voteyText:
A handwritten poem on a note:
"Roses are red,
Violets are blue.
Shut your face,
It's an ugly face."

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man (leaving the room): WELL... I'M OFF TO HAVE ANOTHER BATTLE WITH THE TOILET...

Woman (on couch): ...OKAY HONEY...

Young girl (on couch): EWW! WHY IS DADDY ALWAYS SO GROSS!

Caption (below panel): We thought he was joking about constipation until, one day, we found his cold body on the bathroom floor, a porcelain dagger in his back.
comics.hoverText: The more astute reader will be moved to wonder why he didn't poop in the yard.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of the dead man's face, eyes closed, with blood at the corner of his mouth.
Text: BEST PRANK EVER.

comics.comicText:
Main comic:

The image is presented as security-camera footage. A label in the top-left corner reads: "CAM 1: Main Hall". A small "RECORDING" indicator appears in the bottom-left corner. The view is a close-up, distorted fisheye-style shot of a grinning man's face looking up at the camera, as if seen from a camera mounted on the ceiling.

Caption below the panel: "Hey Jon! There's cameras on the ceiling! Should we steal them too?"
comics.hoverText: This was a daring experiment in animated comics.
comics.voteyText: A second character (presumably Jon) is shown looking up. Speech bubble: "NO. STEALING IS WRONG."

comics.comicText:
Title banner: SMBC PRESENTS "Perspectives..."

The comic is split into two columns with header labels.

Left column header: WHAT WAS SAID...

Right column header: WHAT WAS THOUGHT...

Left panel ("What was said"):

A man with brown hair and a green shirt speaks to a woman with blonde hair (seen from behind).

Man: "I think we should consider putting my mother in a home."

Woman: "You know, maybe it IS about time..."

Right panel ("What was thought"):

The same two people stand facing each other. The blonde woman has a thought bubble showing a building labeled "NURSING HOME." The brown-haired man has a thought bubble showing a red building labeled "FUNERAL HOME."
comics.hoverText: I suppose in retrospect I should've double checked my assumption that you wanted to murder your mom.
comics.voteyText: A loose sketch of a man's face in profile, looking pleased/content, with a thought bubble above him containing a pair of musical notes (whistling or humming a happy tune).

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A young man with red-orange hair (in a blue shirt) holds a wrapped green-and-white gift box, facing a blonde woman with glasses (in a blue and green shirt) standing in a doorway. A banner on the wall behind reads "HAPPY BIRT[HDAY]".

Young man: THANKS MOM!

Woman (mom): OH I'M SURE IT'S HORSE PEE COMPARED TO THE OTHER GIFTS YOU GOT.

Caption (below panel): Moments later, wrist deep in horse urine, I realized it wasn't even my birthday.
comics.hoverText: But you really have to appreciate the workmanship on the packaging.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up line drawing of the blonde woman with glasses, eyes closed and mouth open in a grin.
Woman: HAPPY MOTHER'S DAY!

comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A man with brown hair in a yellow shirt stands with one arm raised enthusiastically, palm open for a high five. There is a framed picture on the wall behind him.

Man: HEY DUDE! CAN I GET A HIGH FIVE UP IN HERE?!

Panel 2: A child or younger person with brown hair in a red shirt sits on a green couch, hand over mouth, suppressing a laugh. A wooden plank or board sticks out from the side of the couch.

Kid: =Snicker= WHATEVER YOU WANT DAD...

Caption (below panels): It was the best practical joke I ever played.
comics.hoverText: Ultimately, the gangrene killed him, but I still feel like you gotta live in the moment.
comics.voteyText: A rough black-and-white doodle. A loosely drawn figure lies on the ground (apparently the dad collapsed/sprawled after the high-five gag). A small floating face on the left looks on. A speech balloon reads: PRANKED!

comics.comicText:
Main comic (single panel):

A damned man with flame-like orange hair, in a fiery red hellscape, reaches up and pleads with an angel who has a golden halo and large white wings.

Damned man: "QUICK! GIVE YOUR SOUL TO ME!"

Angel: "OH NO, I'M NOT FALLING FOR THAT ONE AGAIN!"
comics.hoverText: Okay, but why does the guy have three eyebrows?
comics.voteyText:
The same flame-haired man, now smiling and reclining/flexing, speaks contentedly.
Man: "LOOK HOW FIT I'VE GOTTEN IN THE ACID MINES!"

comics.comicText:
Two yellow Pac-Man-like characters face each other across a table, in front of a green pie box holding a pie. The character on the right wears a red bow.

Left character (speech bubble): OMP-OMP-OMP.*

Right character (speech bubble): OMP-OMP-OMP.*

Caption at bottom:

Translations:

* I love you.

** OMP-OMP-OMP
comics.hoverText: You see children, back in the nineteen-hundred-eighties, there was a 'video game' featuring a puck-shaped gentleman by the name of Pac.
comics.voteyText:
A small open-mouthed creature (the eaten pie's remains, drawn with teeth) stands at left. The right Pac-Man-like character, still wearing the bow, has a wide jagged toothy open mouth.
Right character (speech bubble): NOW, TO LAY MY EGGS.

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

Two people stand in front of a large canvas hanging on a wall. The canvas has the word "ANGST" smeared on it in brown.

Blonde woman (excited): "WOW, HE'S SO DEEP!"

Brown-haired person (gesturing at the canvas, exasperated): "WHAT ARE YOU TALKING ABOUT?! IT'S POOP ON A CANVAS! IT'S LITERALLY POOP ON A CANVAS!"

Blonde woman: "BUT LOOK WHAT IT SPELLS! DID YOU SEE WHAT IT SPELLS? IT SPELLS SOMETHING!"

Caption below the panel:

"Later in our date, she tripped on a branch and scraped her knee."

"I didn't help her up."
comics.hoverText: In retrospect, I feel like this comic is just another version of the thing it's lamenting.
comics.voteyText:
A bearded person lies in bed with their eyes closed.
Thought bubble: "SECRETLY I MISS ART SCHOOL."

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man sits in a chair, raising a belt over his head to strike a child draped face-down across his lap, mid-spanking.

Man: "AND THIS is for probably growing up to be an abusive father!"
comics.hoverText: That said! The statistical data! Is questionable! On whether abuse! Is transmitted behaviorally!
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of the same man's face, now looking pained and conflicted, with a thought/speech bubble above him.
Man: "Now my dad will be proud of me!"

comics.comicText:
Single panel:

An elderly man with white hair stands at the top of an exterior staircase, in the doorway of his home. Two children stand at the bottom of the steps looking up at him.

Old man: "Is it Halloween already? Gee kids, I must've forgotten to get candy. You see, I have this condition where-"

Children (in unison): "WE'RE ORPHANS."

Old man: "Well... I suppose I could go to the store, though my cane's broke, and-"

Children (in unison): "ORPHANS."

Caption below the panel:

"Our parents called him 'senile.'"

"Every Friday after school, we called him 'candybox.'"
comics.hoverText: Twist: It *is* Halloween, and the children are confused.
comics.voteyText:
A man with a hand on his chin looks skeptical.
Man: "You expect me to believe you had NO IDEA Halloween merged with Christmas?!"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man with brown hair in a green sweater sits at a table across from a woman with long blonde hair. He is grinning and pointing at her.

Man: "YOU'RE UGLY... NOT!"

Woman: "THAT WASN'T FUNNY THE NINTH TIME, AND IT ISN'T FUNNY NOW!"

Caption (below panel): It was definitely funny the seventeenth time, but she still didn't laugh.
comics.hoverText: What's less funny is how the man spends his thirties wetting his pillow with tears, as if a sort of karma of emotions is punishing him for the years of non-empathy.
comics.voteyText: A hand-drawn line graph. The vertical axis is labeled "funniness" and the horizontal axis is labeled "times joke is told." A black curve starts very high, drops off steeply toward zero, and stays low — with a single tiny spike partway along the bottom. A red curve (labeled "your perceived funniness") starts high and stays high, rising slightly across the whole graph with an arrow at the end.

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Doctor (a man in a white coat and glasses, holding a clipboard, standing dramatically with arms spread): "HIS CONDITION IS SERIOUS, BUT ITS LOCATION IS HILARIOUS!"

Caption (below the panel): The lighter side of your husband's colonoscopy results!
comics.hoverText: Fun Fact: This was one of the few comics I decided to tone down, from an original version that was explicitly a cancer joke. I probably should've just scrapped it altogether.
comics.voteyText: The doctor's face, lit dramatically: "The spotlight really helps sell the jokes."

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

A kitchen scene. A man with brown hair sits at a table reading a newspaper, a cup on the table in front of him. A blonde woman in a pink shirt and dark skirt stands at the kitchen counter holding up a carton of orange juice, smiling at it.

Woman: "MMM, ORANGE JUICE."

Caption (below the panel): So, I divorced her.
comics.hoverText: Is it just me looking back, or do the comics slowly get more disjointed as I approach graduation?
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of a man's face glaring, with a speech bubble.
Man: "TREE KILLER!"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

A researcher in a white coat and glasses sits observing a baby through what appears to be a one-way window or monitor. The researcher holds a clipboard.

Researcher (speech bubble): INTERESTING...

Researcher's clipboard reads: BABIES ARE STUPID

On the screen/window, a label reads: TIMMY AGE: 0.4

The baby (Timmy) sits in front of a chalkboard showing "2 + 2 = ?".

Timmy (speech bubble): GAH!
comics.hoverText: Looking back on this comic 15 years later, I can see that the kid is actually pretty amazingly advanced if its sitting up and coloring at that age.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of the researcher's face, looking displeased/judgmental.
Researcher (speech bubble): ALSO IGNORANT.

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A woman with curly blonde hair, in a red top, sits at a restaurant table across from a man whose head has a large pink pig grafted onto his face. She holds up a printed photo, frowning.

Man (with the pig face): OH SORRY, THAT MUST'VE BEEN TAKEN BEFORE I HAD THE PIG GRAFTED ONTO MY FACE.

The pig (small speech bubble): WHEE!

Caption (below panel): The trouble with Internet dating.
comics.hoverText: Just kidding. You just have to find the dating site for people with that particular fetish and you're set for life.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of the pig-faced man's head.
A voice from off-panel (incoming speech bubble): SO, I UNDERSTAND YOU LIKE CASUAL ENCOUNTERS

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man with blond hair in a red shirt holds open a glass door (labeled "PUSH") for a blonde woman in a yellow vest and pink shirt who is walking through it. Both have unhappy, scowling expressions.

Man (shouting): "GAH! YOU'RE LUCKY I'M A GENTLEMAN BECAUSE WOW YOU'RE UGLY!"
comics.hoverText: Men being douchebags somehow seemed a lot funnier when I was 21...
comics.voteyText:
A black-and-white sketch of the same man's face, looking sour. Above him is a thought bubble.
Man (thinking): "I HOPE SOMEONE APPRECIATES MY SUFFERING"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man in a suit and dark sunglasses stands holding a small child in a red and pink outfit. Facing him across a desk (with a keyboard and monitor) is a man in a white suit with dark slicked-back hair, gesturing with his hand raised.

Man in white suit: YOU ACTUALLY KILLED MY MOM?! WHY DO YOU HAVE TO BE SO LITERAL ALL THE TIME?!

Caption (below panel): In this part of Manhattan, "kill my mom" was slang for "kill my dad."
comics.hoverText: This is why it's so important to speak standard English.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of the man with dark slicked-back hair and glasses, looking irritated.
Man: USE MORE PRECISE VERBIAGE, COCKSUCKER.

comics.comicText:
Main comic (single panel):

A wedding ceremony. An officiant stands at a podium reading from papers, a groom in a tuxedo stands beside him, and a blonde bride in a white dress and tiara stands across from them, holding hands with the groom.

Officiant: "AND DO YOU, JON, TAKE SALLY..."

Groom (thought, in a thought-bubble): "SO THAT'S HER NAME!"
comics.hoverText: Now I just need to figure out where I remember her from...
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of the groom's face, looking pensive.
Groom: "I LOVE YOU, SULLY."

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A driving instructor sits in the passenger seat of a car bearing a "STUDENT DRIVER" sign; a young man drives.

Instructor: "Now, if you take a right turn too hard, down comes Madame Guillotine."

Caption (below comic): Sure the system was cruel, but the survivors had amazing right turns.
comics.hoverText: We will breed them to create a right-turning super-race!
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of a man's head and shoulders, speaking.
Man: "Dammit. Stuck again. I need to make this thing taller."

comics.comicText:
Main comic (single panel):

A group of children clusters together. In the back center stands a sinister, looming figure wrapped in a gray shroud with a wide grinning mouth full of teeth, wearing a small red top hat and holding a skull-topped cane. Around and in front of it, several wild-eyed, grimacing children are bunched together, some with flame-like or spiky hair, in red, blue, green, and purple clothing. One child on the left lets out a shout.

Child (in speech bubble): "WWOOOO!"

Caption below the panel: The kids from “Family Circus” meet their cousins from “Circus Family.”
comics.hoverText: Hey Jeffy, wanna see a dead man's finger?
comics.voteyText:
A bald, bearded man with a sour expression sits at a desk, resting his chin on his hand, with a thought bubble above him.
Man (thought bubble): "TAKIN' ON THE ISSUES."

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A child sits up in bed in a dark bedroom. A large shadowy silhouette of a person looms in the foreground beside the bed. The child speaks.

Child: FOR THE LAST TIME JIMMY, THERE IS NO MONSTER UNDER YOUR BED! IT'S JUST SOME ANGRY-LOOKING MAN.
comics.hoverText: And he looks like he's more angry at the situation than at you in particular.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of a man's face (the angry-looking man) with a speech balloon.
Man: I'M MORE CONFUSED THAN ANGRY.

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A boy (Bobby) holding a paper lunch bag, with a banana and an apple in front of him, leans toward a blonde girl (Susie) who is seated at a table with her own lunchbox and a glass of juice.

Bobby: HEY SUSIE. WANNA SHARE LUNCH WITH ME?

Susie (shouting, turned away): MRS. SHELTON! BOBBY'S BEING A COMMUNIST!
comics.hoverText: I will seize the means of nutrition!
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of a stern adult woman (Mrs. Shelton).
Mrs. Shelton: BOBBY, EAT YOUR SUPERIOR LUNCH ALONE.

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A yellow, robot-like alien stands on a dark, moon-like world, raising a fist triumphantly. In the background, the green-and-blue Earth hangs in space among dark rocks.

Alien: FINALLY EARTH'S GREENHOUSE GAS LEVELS HAVE LOWERED! THE INVASION CAN BEGIN!
comics.hoverText: Only eat the organic humans!
comics.voteyText:
A caption at the top of the panel; below it, a small alien figure with a heart over its head is engulfed by a large, spreading cloud of black dust.
Caption (alien, panicked): COAL DUST! OUR GREATEST WEAKNESS!

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A long-haired blond man wearing a sweater with "COLLEGE" written on it gestures dramatically while speaking to another man (seen from behind).

Blond man: IMAGINE NO POSSESSIONS, MAN. LIKE, WOAH, YOU KNOW, MAN? WOAH. WOAH. WOAH.

Caption below panel: The real problem with Communism.
comics.hoverText: That and all the dead people, but they're not as vocal.
comics.voteyText: Hand-lettered text on a sticky-note-style square: COLLEGE STUDENTS WITH TINY ARMS

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A person stands at a podium on a stage in front of a red curtain, addressing a seated audience.

Speaker (person at podium): "Due to self esteem concerns, the school board has decided that we are to no longer use the word “don't.”"

Caption (below panel): Although the new policy worked wonders for student self esteem, it fundamentally altered the “Don't Do Drugs” program.
comics.hoverText: It all worked out when smoking a big pile of drugs improved everyone's self esteem.
comics.voteyText:
Handwritten heading at top: "Reading this comic 12 years later"
A bearded man looks slightly worried/uneasy.
Man: "Well that was quite short-sighted of her"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A pretentious-looking man in a black turtleneck stands with his arms crossed, smiling smugly.

Man in turtleneck: "I USED INK AND PAPER!"

A seated person with glasses looks at a simple drawing of a rabbit on a sheet of paper in front of them.

Caption (below panel): Steve was a multimedia artist.
comics.hoverText: What exactly is depicted in the painting on the wall? And why is there just a huge dead plant in the corner?
comics.voteyText:
Header: "YOUNG WEINER..."
A cartoonishly drawn young man with a beard, smiling and holding a piece of paper.
Young man: "Multimedia jokes will be funny forever!"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

An elderly woman with white hair (referred to in the caption as "grammy"), smiling, holds out a comic book to a young boy. The comic's cover reads "SUPERMANG" and shows a red-and-yellow superhero figure.

Grammy: I know you love comic books, so I went to the grocer and picked you up one.

Caption (below panel): Supermang was actually remarkably good, but I still refused to talk to grammy.
comics.hoverText: Mostly because, due to a coloring error, her teeth are made of skin.
comics.voteyText:
Title bar: READING THIS 12 YEARS LATER
A bearded man lies in bed, eyes open, looking unimpressed.
Man (thought/speech bubble): Caption needs more adverbs.

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Blonde woman: I don't want you to change your entire style... just a few things...

Man with a dead chicken on his head: Like what?!

Blonde woman: Well, the dead chicken might be a start...

Man: She's dead? Ewwwwww!
comics.hoverText: But I will NEVER change my socks and sandals.
comics.voteyText: Man (distraught): That does explain the lack of eggs.

comics.comicText:
Main comic (single panel):

A man with orange/red hair sits at a small dinner table across from a blonde woman. Two glasses of red wine and small plates sit on the table between them. The man holds up his hand, pinching a large, dark, chunky clump of food that he has apparently just pulled from his teeth, examining it.

Man: OH GEEZ! WAS THIS IN MY TEETH ALL THROUGH DINNER?

The blonde woman recoils, clutching at herself with a disgusted/uncomfortable expression.
comics.hoverText: Does the fact that you're shivering and crying portend a lack of second date opportunity?
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of the man's face, looking worried and grimacing.
Man (thought/caption): WILL THIS AFFECT THE ODDS OF AN END-OF-DATE KISS?

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

An astronaut in a spacesuit, smiling, holds up his hand and looks at it. He is also holding a triangular wedge (a Toblerone bar). A NASA patch and an American flag are on his suit. Behind him, through a porthole, is the blackness of space.

Astronaut: WHOA! A SIXTH FINGER! OOH, AND A TOBLERONE! THIS WAS TOTALLY WORTH THE RISK!

Caption (below panel): What really happens when you go past the speed of light.
comics.hoverText: It's the raisin kind, though.
comics.voteyText:
The astronaut gives a thumbs-up (his hand now has six fingers).
Astronaut: Thanks, Jesus!
Offscreen voice: The Universe was designed for you!

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man in a blue suit and bow tie sits behind a desk, gesturing toward a woman seated across from him (seen from behind). A papered document and a nameplate are on the desk.

Man: "Tell you what - I'll take on your sexual harassment suit if you show me that sweet can of yours."
comics.hoverText: See it's ironic because he's... ahh forget it.
comics.voteyText:
A hand holds up a can labeled "CORN."
Speech bubble: "OH BABY"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A blond man stands behind two blond children, one hand resting on each child's head, pointing down at them. He is talking to another man (seen from behind on the right).

Blond man: HEY! MY KIDS AREN'T UGLY!

Blond man: OH WAIT... WERE YOU TALKING ABOUT JONNY OR SUSIE?
comics.hoverText: I mean, both of them mysteriously have gigantic basketball-shaped heads.
comics.voteyText:
The other man (the one who had been listening) faces forward.
Other man: JOHNNY RIGHT?

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

A blonde woman and an orange-haired man face each other in a dim purple room.

Woman: "So, what kind of girl do you like?"

Man: "I like a woman with brains."

Woman (thought bubble): "He's perfect!"

Man (thought bubble): "Idiot! It's pronounced 'breasts.'"
comics.hoverText: You can tell he's a fan of p-values because he only wants to know whether they exist or not, rather than measuring effect size.
comics.voteyText:
Caption banner: "READING THIS 12 YEARS LATER"
A bearded man looks at the comic.
Bearded man: "What's wrong with her eyes?"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A sailor in a white naval uniform stands on the deck of a ship, near an American flag. He strikes a confident pose, pointing dramatically into the distance.

Sailor: SAN FRANCISCO! 250 NAUTICAL MILES, DUE EAST!

Caption (below panel): Their GPS disconnected, their radio dead, the crew of the Arizona are forced to use the only tool they have left: Dave's gaydar.
comics.hoverText: Dave also has gayngefinding ability.
comics.voteyText:
Two crew members in silhouette/outline. One on the left speaks tentatively.
First crew member: WE COULD USE A COMPASS?
Second crew member (face shown, irritated): SHUTUP

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Two astronauts in spacesuits stand on a reddish, rocky planetary surface, seen from behind.

Left astronaut: "WAIT A MINUTE! THIS ISN'T THE MOON! IT'S MARS!"

Right astronaut (pointing): "HOW ARE WE GOING TO BREAK IT TO THE PUBLIC?!"

Caption below panel: That's right, the moon landing was a fake!
comics.hoverText: The whole thing was done on a soundstage on the surface of the Sun.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of one astronaut's helmet, drawn in a simple black-and-white style.
Astronaut: "WE HAVE DISAPPOINTED OUR SECRET REPTOID MASTERS."

comics.comicText:
Setting: Two men sit across a table on a TV political debate show. A sign on the front of the table reads "POLITI-TALK".

Man with reddish-brown hair (in blue jacket, leaning forward, hands open): OH COME ON! ARE YOU SERIOUSLY ARGUING THAT TV FORCES PEOPLE TO BE VIOLENT?!

Older man with glasses (in tan jacket): LOOK, ALL I KNOW IS I RAN DOWN SIX KIDS ON THE WAY TO THE SHOW TODAY. DO YOU WANNA BE THE ONE TO EXPLAIN THAT TO THEIR PARENTS?!
comics.hoverText: Still more reasonable than actual political talkshows.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up on the older man with glasses, looking annoyed and grimacing.
Older man with glasses: I'M SICK OF THESE "THINK OF THE CHILDREN" ARGUMENTS!

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A woman with orange hair (in a green polo shirt) holds a small handheld electronic device and speaks to a man (named Jim).

Woman: "I'm sorry Jim. You're nice and everything, but these readings are just all wrong."

Jim (clasping his hands pleadingly): "Baby! I can pressure change! I swear."

Caption below the comic:

"In the future, love is determined by barometric pressure."

"Think it's stupid? Well, look how well your system is working out."
comics.hoverText: This is the first faint twinkle of SMBC's eventual lurch toward turbo-dorkery.
comics.voteyText:
Header: "YOU:"
A crudely drawn frowning face with a speech bubble.
Face: "What's so wrong with using the dew point?!"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Firefighter (holding a hose, wearing a red helmet): CAPTAIN! WE'VE RUN OUT OF WATER!

Captain (wearing a red helmet marked "FD", arms raised, surrounded by flames): WELL, ISN'T THERE ANY LIQUID WE CAN USE?!

Firefighter: *sigh* NOTHING BUT THE GAS IN THE TANK...

Captain: LET'S DO IT!
comics.hoverText: Honestly, that's just silly.
comics.voteyText: Caption: ALL OF THOSE FIREMEN ARE DEAD NOW

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man and a woman lie in bed together at night, a lamp on the nightstand beside them. The woman is turned away, eyes closed; the man lies on his back, awake.

Man: Do you ever lay awake at night wondering if marriage was just a complete mistake?

Woman: N-no...

Man: Me neither. G'night!

(The man reaches over to switch off the lamp.)
comics.hoverText: If you hear crying, it's actually snoring, so don't face this way.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up on the smiling woman's face.
Woman (thought/caption): It's nice how we can talk about anything.

comics.comicText:
Main comic:

Movie screen text:

COMING THIS EASTER

A MEL GIBSON FILM

PASSION OF THE CHRIST II:

ZOMBIE JESUS!

Caption (below the panel):

"Do unto others as you would have them BRAAAAINS!"
comics.hoverText: It's a really boring movie because honestly, how scary is just one zombie?
comics.voteyText: I SWEAR THIS JOKE WASN'T COMPLETELY PLAYED OUT IN 2004

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man with orange hair in a yellow shirt sits across a restaurant table from a woman with brown hair in a pink shirt. The table has a blue tablecloth and two plates of food. The woman holds up a stemmed wine glass full of red wine and smiles. A clear tube runs from her wine glass, down off the table, and into a cardboard box on the floor beside the man.

The box is labeled: POISON WINE

Woman (speech bubble): THIS IS THE LAST TIME I GO OUT WITH YOU!

Caption (below panel):

She'd been saying that all night, ever since she found out that I'd poisoned her drink. YES. I GET IT. YOU'LL BE DEAD HA HA HA.

Geez!
comics.hoverText: Unrelated to this weirdly confusing old comic, I believe all the comics I did in 2004 are from a short period when I had moved to LA but was unable to find a job for a while. That's why they're different stylewise than the stuff before and after.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of a bearded man looking down/off thoughtfully.
Speech bubble: BUT WHY WOULD HE LABEL THE BOX?

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

Brown bear (resembling a cartoon bear in a hat, collar, and tie): HEY BOOBOO! I STOLE ANOTHER PIC-A-NIC BASKET!

Smaller orange bear (holding a picnic basket): SORRY YOGI. THERE'S NOTHING IN HERE BUT INSULIN SHOTS.
comics.hoverText: Fact: When diabetics go camping, they put all their syringes in a wicker basket.
comics.voteyText:
Caption (top): Reading this 11 years later...
A person reclining on a couch: I don't get it. Was it, like... a diabetes party?

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A blond man in a suit sits behind a desk, smiling with his arms crossed. A second person (a man with dark hair, in a yellow shirt) stands across the desk facing him. Framed pictures hang on the green wall behind them.

Blond man at desk: "WELCOME TO HELL, MR. JOHNSON."

Caption below the panel:

"Of course, in the real Hell, there are no devils, no pitchforks, no fire and brimstone - no, nothing so simple.."

"Sadly, you'll be going to the fake Hell where they DO have all that stuff."
comics.hoverText: Also endless single panel comic strips by 23 year olds.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of a man's face being jabbed in the eyes by a pitchfork. A speech bubble points to him.
Man: "WOW. YEAH THIS IS WAY WORSE THAN PSYCHOLOGICAL TORMENT."

comics.comicText:
Title banner: SMBC PRESENTS "DATING TIPS"

Setting: A school hallway lined with lockers. A girl with brown hair, glasses, and a pink shirt stands on the left wearing leg braces. A boy with black hair and a green shirt stands on the right.

Boy: SANDY, WILL YOU GO TO THE PROM WITH ME?

Girl (Sandy): ME? REALLY? OF COURSE I WILL!

Caption below the comic:

Dating Tip #1:

If you take a girl with polio to the prom, you leave with a cheerleader who thinks you're sensitive!
comics.hoverText: Setting aside the dickishness of this concept, like, when was it set that the girl has polio and thus apparently gets some sort of knee-braces?
comics.voteyText:
Header text: Reading this 11 years later...
A bearded man's face looks puzzled.
Man: BUT WHO HAS POLIO ANYMORE?

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A doctor wearing a head mirror leans over a teddy bear lying on a bed, pressing a stethoscope to it. A young boy stands at the bedside watching. A woman stands in the background.

Doctor: "I'M SORRY, SON. MR. TED IS... DECEASED."

Caption (below panel): Yeah, it was just great being a doctor's kid. Thanks for asking.
comics.hoverText: Only a real doctor can tell that no heartbeat means you're dead.
comics.voteyText:
The doctor (now bald, in a sketchier line-drawing style) speaks.
Doctor: "I THINK WE CAN HARVEST HIS FLUFF TO MAKE A PILLOW."

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

[A brain sits in a clear glass dish on a leaf of lettuce, on a countertop. A small placard in front of the dish reads:]

Placard: Steve.

Caption (the brain speaking): Being a brain in a pan is a lot less glamorous than my life as a movie star. But hey, I can't complain. I mean, apparently I can still talk or write or something. That's pretty cool, right?
comics.hoverText: The period after 'Steve' lends it an air of finality.
comics.voteyText:
[The brain again, now shown as a vague blobby shape with several worried/distressed faces. A speech bubble points to it.]
Brain: It says "Stephen" on my jar, right?

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Elderly bald man (in a hospital/care bed): I HAVE A CONFESSION TO MAKE! I'VE BEEN FAKING ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE!

(A younger man sits in a chair beside the bed, watching.)

Caption (below panel): Every morning for fifteen years, grampa woke up and said the same thing.
comics.hoverText: The guy on the right is mostly mad that the shading doesn't make any sense.
comics.voteyText: Close-up of a man's face with a slight smile: ONE DAY THIS WILL BE FUNNY.

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

A man entering a kitchen, holding a steaming mug of coffee, arms spread wide.

Man: GOOD MORNING BREEDERS!

Caption (below panel): It was becoming increasingly apparent that Gary would have preferred a son.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of a bearded man looking thoughtfully to the side.
Text (caption above him): HOW DID HE GET COFFEE BEFORE ENTERING THE KITCHEN?

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man and a woman (a couple) sit in chairs in a waiting room, outside a door. The woman, who has curly red-orange hair, holds a book and looks down; the man, with reddish hair in a green shirt, gestures toward her.

Sign on the door: "DR. STERN, DDS. MARRIAGE COUNSELOR"

Man: "I REALLY DON'T SEE WHY WE NEED THIS. I TOLD YOU I'D PAY FOR A FACELIFT!"
comics.voteyText:
Close-up on the man's face.
Man (thinking/asking): "WHY IS THE COUNSELOR A DENTIST?"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A family is gathered at a breakfast table. A blonde woman in a pink shirt stands behind a brown-haired man in a blue shirt, pouring a bucket of something messy over his head. A young blonde boy in a red shirt and a girl with long black hair in purple overalls sit at the table watching.

Woman (cheerfully, gesturing): "FOR JONNY, WAFFLES. FOR SUSIE, PANCAKES. AND, FOR DADDY, A BUCKET FULL OF SKUNK PLACENTAS!"

Caption (below panel): "So, I guess my infidelity is out of the bag. On the plus side, the skunk placentas were remarkably tender."
comics.voteyText:
The man, now with a head covered/slumped in the mess, faces away.
Speech bubble (from the woman, off-panel): "REAL MATURE."

comics.comicText:
Single panel:

Three young men sit around a table playing a tabletop game, excitedly declaring their characters. A fourth, older man slumps at the head of the table with his head down.

First young man (brown hair): "I'LL BE AN ELVEN WIZARD!"

Second young man (red hair): "I'LL BE A DWARVEN WARRIOR!"

Older slumped man: "I'LL BE A GUY WHO CAN PUT DOWN THE JACK DANIELS FOR JUST ONE GODDAMNED DAY!"

Caption below panel: That was the last time we let dad join our "Dungeons and Dragons" game.
comics.voteyText:
Handwritten recipe on a note:
1 part Jack Daniels
1 part Mountain Dew
Stir with finger.
"The Mountain Julep"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A large bearded figure resembling God leans down from the clouds, mouth open, shouting in a jagged yellow speech bubble.

God: GRAHHH! I AM GOD-BLOR!

Below, a crowd of people stands on a green hill, looking up at the figure.

Caption (below panel): In more recent versions of the Bible, this episode has been omitted.
comics.voteyText: A loose sketch of the same bearded God figure leaning down from the clouds toward a small person standing on the ground below, who reaches up. No text.

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man and a woman are in bed together. The woman, with orange/red hair, holds up her hand and is fending off the man, who has brown hair and is reaching toward her.

Woman: "NOT TONIGHT HONEY! I JUST STARTED... 'RAISING THE RED FLAG...'"

Caption (below panel): "Oh great. First she's frigid. Now she's a commie."
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of a man's face looking deadpan/unimpressed.
Man: "TO EACH ACCORDING TO HIS NEED."

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A bald man in dark robes and round glasses grins maniacally, holding two large scoop-like utensils dripping with colorful goo over a white jar labeled "TODDLER POISON."

Man: "YES! YES! SOON THEY'LL ALL BE DEAD!"

Caption (below panel):

Dr. Manklow's toxic formula killed off all the children in the world. But, as luck would have it, he released the poison on the same day that aliens secretly took over the bodies of all of Earth's children.

His face is being added to Mt. Rushmore as we speak.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of the same bald, bespectacled man's face, thinking.
Man: "I'D BETTER WRITE 'TODDLER POISON' ON THE JAR SO NOBODY GETS CONFUSED AND DRINKS IT."

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A blond man with a ponytail and yellow tie, seen from behind, fires a lever-action rifle into the air at a launching contraption. A small child (orphan) has just been flung into the sky and is being shot at.

Sound effects: TCHK! TCHK!

Sign on the launcher's base: TODAY: ORPHAN SKEET!

Caption (below panel): Admittedly, your honor, I occasionally wondered if I was doing the right thing.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up on a man's face with eyes closed, speaking sternly.
Man: STOP FLAILING SO MUCH!

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

A family scene. From left to right: a young blonde woman in a pink shirt holding a swaddled baby; a young blonde man in an orange shirt raising his fist; an older bald man in a green shirt; an older woman with orange/red hair in a purple top.

Older man (green shirt): "AWW, SHE HAS HER GRANDFATHER'S EYES!"

Young man (orange shirt, raising fist): "SO YA SLEPT WITH MY WIFE, EH?"

Older woman (red hair, looking guilty, with a thought/sweat bubble): "DAMN!"
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of the older bald man's face, calm.
Older man: "ARE YOU FAMILIAR WITH THE CONCEPT OF KIN SELECTION?"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man with brown hair has a metal hook stuck through his eye. A blonde woman in a purple shirt stands across from him.

Man (speech bubble): "Can I take the hook out of my eye yet?"

Woman (speech bubble): "Nope!"

Man (thought bubble): "Man she's lucky she's hot..."
comics.voteyText:
Caption above the panel: "Reading this 12 years later..."
An older, balding, bearded version of the man looks unimpressed.
Man (thought bubble): "Her body is shaped like like a mushroom...."

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

A woman with blonde hair stands at left, her body shaped literally like an hourglass figure — a wide bell-shaped pink dress with a tiny cinched waist and a narrow torso above. Two men in suits stand at right holding martini glasses, laughing.

Man (speech bubble): "SHE'S GOT A REAL HOURGLASS FIGURE."

Second man (yellow burst bubble): "Chortle chortle!"

Caption (below panel): What was less funny was how Cynthia died alone at age 35 due to a congenital heart defect.
comics.voteyText:
Two nearly identical figures sit in two separate bowls/cauldrons, facing each other, each with an open grimacing mouth.
Shared speech bubble: "TWO CYNTHIAS EMERGE!"

comics.comicText:
Main comic (single panel):

A scientist in a white lab coat and glasses stands in the foreground, holding a clipboard and taking notes with a pen. Behind the scientist is a large observation window looking into another room.

Through the window, three children sit around a table smoking cigarettes, with smoke curling up around them. Cards and items are on the table in front of them.

A sign taped beneath the window reads:

TEST SUBJECTS

100,221 100,222

100,223

Caption (below the panel): After years of testing, it is proven that children are indeed easily addicted to nicotine.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of the scientist's face, now wearing dark sunglasses with a flat, serious expression.
Scientist (speech bubble): NOW, ON TO METHADONE

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A bearded man with a halo stands behind a lectern labeled "ST. PETER" at the gates of heaven, fists held out in front of him. A red-haired man in a yellow shirt stands before him.

St. Peter: OKAY! PICK A HAND - RIGHT OR LEFT?!

Caption (below panel): After betting on the right hand it was revealed to me that gambling is a mortal sin.
comics.voteyText:
The red-haired man speaks to a horned, devil-like figure shrouded in black.
Man: WHY'RE YOU HERE?
Devil figure: ENTRAPMENT.

comics.comicText:
Main comic:

A large pink monster truck barrels forward. A grinning man in a purple shirt and headband drives it, leaning out the window. A small sign on the truck reads: USA!

Below the truck, in front of its grille, a runner in a green shirt and red shorts sprints forward.

Caption (below the panel): In 2008, American lawyers discover a loophole in the Olympic rulebook that allows for monster trucks in both the 100 meter dash and the triple jump.
comics.voteyText:
Header text: Reading this in 2015...
A person rests their chin on their hand, looking deadpan.
Speech bubble: MY PREDICTION WAS WAY OFF.

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

The Trix Rabbit (standing at right, looking gaunt and desperate): PLEASE KIDS! YA GOTTA HELP ME! MY BLOOD SUGAR LEVEL IS CRITICAL! I'VE ALREADY LOST A TOE, AND I CAN'T SEE OUT ONE OF MY EYES!

Two children stand at left. A boy holds a box of cereal labeled "TRIX."

The boy (laughing): SILLY RABBIT!
comics.voteyText:
A mostly blank panel showing only the lower half of a face (two eyes, a nose, and a small frowning mouth).
Handwritten text (top left): I didn't want to kill them.

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A woman with brown hair holding a pregnancy test, excited: "HONEY! WE'RE PREGNANT!"

A man with orange hair holding a coffee mug: "THAT'S GREAT!"

Caption (below panel): Ted sipped his coffee, checked his watch, and walked out the door. That was six months ago.
comics.voteyText:
A blond child's face peers in through the lower pane of a window from outside.
Child (speech from outside the upper window): "Can I come in?"
Child (second speech bubble): "It's so cold."

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man and a woman sit across from each other at a dinner table, each with an empty plate in front of them, as if on a date.

Woman (speaking): "Well, I'm a big animal lover..."

Man (thinking): "Oh great..."

The man is reaching down toward a cardboard box beside his chair labeled "DEAD RACCOON."
comics.voteyText:
Close-up on the man's face, grinning slyly as he thinks.
Man (thinking): "Bettter jiggle it."

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

Two teammates in red jerseys celebrate behind a third teammate, dumping the contents of a cooler over his head in the classic victory-shower gesture.

Dark-skinned teammate (left): "WE WON! WOOOH!"

Light-skinned teammate (right, lifting the cooler): "YEAH!"

The liquid pouring from the cooler is yellow and appears to be burning/steaming the player it lands on. The player in the center, wearing a red jersey, screams in agony:

Center player: "GAAAAAAAH!"

Caption below the panel:

"In retrospect," noted Coach Sanders, "I'm not really sure why we had a cooler of battery acid on field in the first place."
comics.voteyText:
A simple line drawing of a man's head and shoulders, partially submerged in liquid, with a disfigured/melted face. He says:
"IT'S FUNNY NOW!"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A large man's face is shown in close-up, mouth open wide, shouting toward a small child whose head is visible in the lower left.

Man (shouting, in a jagged yellow speech burst): "I HAVE NO SON!"

Caption (below the panel): "Well, goodnight Susie."
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of the same man's face, now drawn looking distressed/confused.
Man: "AND WHY IS MY HEAD SO BIG!?"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A blonde woman holds up a freshly-ironed object toward a brown-haired man in a purple short-sleeved shirt and tie. The object she holds is not a shirt but a wad of jagged, metallic, accordion-folded teeth (it resembles a row of sharp blades or a bear trap).

Blonde woman (speech bubble): I IRONED YOUR FAVORITE SHIRT! GO AHEAD! PUT IT ON!

Caption below the panel: "Wait a minute! That's not my favorite shirt! No, no, she's definitely up to something..."
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of the brown-haired man's head and shoulders. He now appears to be wearing the jagged metal object around his neck/collar, looking strained.
Man: It chafes a little.

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man sits slumped on the floor against a wall, having been stabbed in the chest, with blood on his shirt and pooling beneath him. A menacing figure looms in shadow at the left foreground, knife (or claw) raised. The wounded man points toward the attacker and grins.

Wounded man: "SUCKER! MY WIFE JUST LEFT ME! I WAS ALREADY DEAD INSIDE!"
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of a woman's face looking unimpressed/concerned, with a small speech bubble.
Woman: "HONEY?"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

A desolate landscape at dusk. A yellow sun (or moon) hangs in a purple sky over barren hills. A single human skull lies on the ground.

Caption (below the panel): "You know honey, I really don't feel like getting pizza again tonight."
comics.voteyText:
Caption (handwritten, top): Reading this 11 years later...
A bearded man with long hair sits looking at a laptop/screen.
Man (thought/speech bubble): I don't get it

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man in a red coat with brown hair sits at a wooden desk, quill in hand, writing on a piece of paper with an annoyed, weary expression. Behind him, a balding man with long white hair at the sides (Jefferson is addressed; the standing man is implied to be Benjamin Franklin) walks past in a blue coat and white breeches, grinning, hands behind his back.

Standing man (to the seated writer): "WHILE WE'RE YOUNG, JEFFERSON."

Caption (below panel): Early versions of the Declaration of Independence contained an inordinate number of references to Benjamin Franklin's "fat &%*#ing ass."
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of an aged scroll/parchment written in elaborate cursive script. The text reads:
"Jesus fucking Christ, this fucking guy. Anyway, when in the course of"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A blond man in a green shirt and blue pants stands menacingly, pointing down at a bound, balding man with orange hair who is tied to a chair with his hands cuffed behind him.

Blond man: "YOU LIKE BEING MY HOSTAGE, FATTY? HUH? YOU LIKE IT?"
