Man: "Look sweetie, your mom sent a present and - whoops! I dropped it on the floor! Oh my! It's full of scorpions and pictures of clowns - your two biggest fears! Why would anyone do that?!"

Caption (below panel): When you only get one weekend of custody a month, you have to make it count
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of the same man's face, smiling warmly as he speaks.
Man: "I love you, my little cudgel."

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man with red hair has a bundle of lit dynamite strapped to the top of his head, the fuse burning. He holds one hand up near the fuse. He calmly addresses a brown-haired person seen from behind in the foreground.

Man with dynamite on head: "SO THEN, YOU'RE OF THE OPINION THAT WE SHOULD JUST BE FRIENDS?"

Caption (below the comic): Lawrence exhibited similar behavior when I was of the opinion that it was his turn to pay for dinner.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of a clenched fist raised threateningly toward a person's face. The fist's owner speaks.
Fist's owner: "So, you're of the opinion that I'm being manipulative?"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man in a yellow shirt and tie holds a cordless phone to his ear, eyes closed, looking pained.

Man (on phone): "She left you? For who? NOBODY?! She just DUMPED you? AHAHAHA! So what're you callin' me for? So I can send you a shirt that says 'LOSER' on the front?"

Caption (below panel): My employment at the suicide hotline was brief.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of the same man's face, now wide-eyed and grimacing as he realizes what he's said.
Man: "Uh, I mean... I'm sure you made her very happy."

comics.comicText:
A single panel drawn in the style of a prehistoric cave painting, rendered in red/ochre pigment on a rough stone cave wall.

Inside a roughly drawn rectangular border, a crude stick-figure scene shows two figures.

Text at top, inside a speech-bubble-like outline: "PAG KILLED MAMMOTH"

Text below the panel border: "PAG HAD NOT KILLED MAMMOTH."

Caption (below the comic): "Prehistoric single panel comics were a lot less predictable."
comics.voteyText:
A hand-drawn red-line panel showing a stick-figure cave-painting style character.
Text (caption/speech): "Bonus panel recapitulates joke."

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man (Steve) stands at an open window at night, arms raised, shouting out into the darkness.

Steve: OH MY GOD! IT'S LIKE Y2K ALL OVER AGAIN!

Caption (below panel): Steve hated how nothing ever happened to him.
comics.voteyText:
A starburst/explosion shape with text inside.
Text: Y2K JOKES!

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A bald man in a white tank top with tattoos (a skull on his shoulder, others on his chest) holds a broken bottle by the neck, its jagged edges pointed toward another man whose head we see from behind. The bald man shouts.

Bald man: YOU WANNA SAY THAT TO MY FACE, PUNK?!

Panel 2 (labeled "MOMENTS PRIOR..."):

The same two men stand calmly. The man (with light reddish-brown hair, in a green shirt) speaks politely while the bald man holds an intact bottle to his own mouth.

Man in green shirt: SAY, WOULD YOU MIND BREAKING THAT BOTTLE AND THREATENING ME WITH THE JAGGED EDGES WHILE SHOUTING A RHETORICAL QUESTION?
comics.voteyText: A hand-drawn line graph. The vertical axis is labeled "punchline funnyness" and the horizontal axis is labeled "# of words." A red curve rises steeply upward to the right, indicating that punchline funniness increases as the number of words increases.

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man in a green shirt grabs a frightened woman in a yellow shirt from behind, holding her in a restraining grip with a wide grin.

Man in green shirt: WHAT'RE YOU GONNA DO NOW?!

Caption (below panel): Nobody was particularly thankful for Todd's impromptu self defense lessons.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of a grinning, slightly crazed-looking man's face.
Man: If I were still crazy, you'd be dead by now!

comics.comicText:
Main comic:

A man named Jimmy stands holding a bouquet of red roses, smiling, in front of a woman with orange hair seen from behind. They are outdoors near a large tree.

Woman: "Flowers? What for?"

Jimmy: "Just cause..."

Woman: "Oh Jimmy!"

Jimmy: "Cause you're a bitch!"
comics.voteyText:
Hand-drawn sketch of a person's face with a thought bubble above their head.
Caption (above): "Reading this 10 years later..."
Thought: "Did I get dumped that week?"

comics.comicText:
Main comic:

A labeled technical diagram of an early biplane, drawn in the style of a patent or engineering schematic. Labels with pointer lines identify the following parts:

- GASOLINE TANK

- SPACING STRUTS

- RUDDER

- CONSTANTLY FIRING SHOTGUN

Caption below the panel: "There were a number of design flaws with the original model of the Wright Flyer."
comics.voteyText: Close-up of a mustached man's face. Speech bubble: "Let's try replacing it with a pistol."

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

A doctor in a white coat with a head mirror stands between two colleagues, recounting a surgery.

Doctor (Dr. Thompson): "So I'm in his chest when I find these two lung-shaped tumors! So I removed them, only to discover that he has no lungs! It's a wonder he was even alive to - wait a sec..."

Doctor (smaller, dawning realization): "oh no."

Doctor (alarmed): "OH NO!"

Caption below the panel:

"To his horror, Dr. Thompson realizes he never went to med school."
comics.voteyText:
A tight, sketchy close-up of the three characters' faces.
Dr. Thompson (speech bubble): "It all makes sense now!"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel, set in a dimly lit bar):

A balding man in a green shirt gestures toward a woman in a yellow tank top, who looks unimpressed and annoyed.

Man: "WOAH WOAH WOAH - WHEN I SAID 'I HATE ALL THE JEWS,' I DIDN'T MEAN, LIKE, YOU IN PARTICULAR."

Caption below the panel: "You know what? I'm just gonna stop using that pickup line altogether."
comics.voteyText:
A rough sketch of the same man's smiling face.
Text: "I've got a final solution for loneliness"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Jesus (a smiling man with long brown hair, a beard, a halo, and a white robe with a purple sash, arms spread wide): I FORGIVE YOU ALL!

Caption (below the panel): In retrospect, it was probably a mistake to put Jesus in charge of the war crimes tribunal.
comics.voteyText:
A frowning, grim-faced man wearing a hood or robe leans in, speaking.
Hooded man: Except the usurers.

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A red, horned devil (Satan) in a room, gesturing animatedly with both hands toward a balding man (seen from behind, wearing glasses) in the foreground. The devil wears a red robe bearing a pentagram and a small white skull.

Man (foreground): I just don't get it. You've already got my soul, what does it matter if you get power of attorney?

Satan: Well if it doesn't matter so much, why don't you just sign the damn thing?!

Caption (below panel): I'm really starting to distrust Satan.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of a man's face looking downcast/annoyed, with a speech line above.
Text: It's not what you said, it's the way you said it.

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Setting: A psychedelic, swirling, brightly colored scene. A grinning caterpillar-like creature wearing a purple top hat holds out a stack of papers toward a man (seen from behind) who reaches up toward it.

Caterpillar creature (left speech bubble): WELCOME TO CATERPILLAR LAAAAAND!

Caterpillar creature (right speech bubble): FIRST YOU MUST FILL OUT THIS IMMIGRATION PAAAAPERWORK!

Caption (below panel): It was the worst LSD trip I'd ever taken.
comics.voteyText: A loose, sketchy black-and-white close-up of the smiling top-hatted caterpillar creature's face. Scrawled handwritten text reads: "Error on formmmm 1104-B".

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Customer (a man with orange hair, seen from behind): HI, I'D LIKE TO RETURN THIS DVD PLAYER.

The Black Knight (a dark-armored figure behind the counter): I'M SORRY SIR, BUT YOU FAILED TO PURCHASE OUR EXTENDED WARRANTY!!

The Black Knight: BAAAAHAHAHAHAHA!!!

Caption: The Black Knight has had little difficulty adjusting to modern life.
comics.voteyText: Text (handwritten beside a gray helmeted figure): Its obsolescence was planned all along

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (with orange hair): HONEY! ARE YOU OKAY?

Man (with brown hair, distressed): UGH... I HAD THAT SAME AWFUL DREAM - THE ONE WHERE I'M YOU.
comics.voteyText: Man (close-up of his distressed face): My hair was so luxurious.

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A woman with blonde hair (seen from behind) speaks to a man with orange/red hair wearing a collared shirt and tie. They appear to be on a date or sitting across from each other.

Woman: YOU THINK I'M UGLY, DON'T YOU?

Man (smiling, gesturing with open hand): NO... NO. I... IN FACT I THINK IT'S BENEFICIAL TO SEE ALL SORTS OF DIFFERENT FACES. FOR INSTANCE, NOW I NO LONGER FEAR DEATH.
comics.voteyText:
A crude sketch of a distorted, lopsided face.
Caption (speech): Oh neat! Cataracts!

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A bearded figure with a halo (Jesus), wearing a purple robe, stands with arms raised against a cloudy blue sky.

Jesus: "BEHOLD! I AM THE MESSIAH!"

Standing beside him is a more flamboyant figure with flame-like orange hair, a halo, and an elaborate purple-and-yellow costume, also with arms raised.

Flame-haired figure: "BEHOLD! I AM MEGASSIAH!"

Caption below the panel:

"Due to a scheduling error, the second and third comings happened at roughly the same time."

"Needless to say, Jesus was pissed."
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of a glum-looking bearded man (Jesus) with a speech bubble.
Jesus: "I am SO frickin' covetous right now"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Teacher (a man with glasses, brown hair, wearing a blue shirt): "Care to read that note in front of the class, Miss O'Neil?"

Miss O'Neil (a young woman with orange/red hair in a green shirt, holding a folded note): "But... but sir, YOU put this note on my desk..."

Teacher: "I didn't ask for the history, Miss O'Neil!"

Below the panel, the note is shown in handwriting: "I think Mr. Anderson is SO hot!"
comics.voteyText: A woman (Miss O'Neil) looks worried/embarrassed. Caption in handwriting: "His ex-wife was totally wrong."

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

A man named Jim reclines on a therapist's couch, holding his face thoughtfully. He says:

Jim: "I GUESS... I GUESS SOMEHOW I JUST FEEL LIKE LESS OF A MAN..."

In the foreground, a bald therapist with glasses sits taking notes on a pad.

Caption (below panel): "Jim's life has changed a lot ever since his genitals fell off."
comics.voteyText:
A loose sketch of a smiling man's face in profile. A speech bubble above him reads:
"IT'S PRETTY GREAT."

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

A young couple embraces in the front seat of a car. A man (referred to as Bobby) leans in toward a blonde woman (Sandy), who holds his face in her hands. A small handheld device near the man's back emits a jagged "BZZZZAP!" burst.

Man (Bobby): "WAIT! SANDY! BEFORE WE DO THIS, I... I WANT TO MAKE SURE THAT... THAT IT'S REALLY LOVE."

Woman (Sandy): "OH BOBBY! JUST LOOK INTO MY EYES. IF YOU FEEL A TINGLE SHOOTING UP YOUR SPINE, YOU'LL KNOW IT'S TRUE LOVE."

Caption (below panel): "If he didn't feel a tingle, Sandy was prepared to make damn sure he regretted it."
comics.voteyText: A simple sketch of a man's face looking pained and wide-eyed. Hand-lettered text reads: "LOVE FEELS BAD!"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man: Polly, our relationship just isn't working out.

Panel 2:

Woman (Polly): What?! Why not?!

Panel 3:

Man: I thought you might ask that. Please allow me to illustrate with this Venn diagram.

Panel 4:

The man holds up a sheet of paper showing a Venn diagram (two overlapping circles) with the words written across it: "YOU'RE A BITCH"
comics.voteyText: Close-up of the woman's (Polly's) annoyed, unimpressed face. In the lower-left corner, she holds the man's paper, on which she has scrawled a correction with an arrow and an X: "That's not how venn diagrams work"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man with red/orange hair, wearing a green shirt, stands at a small table in a dimly lit restaurant or bar. A woman in a green top (brown hair) sits to his left; a blonde woman is seen from behind in the foreground on the right. The man gestures toward the seated woman.

Man: "OH HI SUSAN! THIS IS A BIT AWKWARD... MEET MY EX-GIRLFRIEND, ELAINE."

Caption (below panel):

"In restrospect, it would have been courteous to inform Elaine of our break-up prior to the date with Susan."
comics.voteyText:
A simple hand-drawn sketch of a man's head and face, looking off to the side, with a speech bubble above him.
Man: "I think me should see other people."

comics.comicText:
Panel 1: An airplane flies through a blue sky over clouds. No text.

Panel 2: Inside the plane, two men sit. The man on the left wears a yellow life vest and looks worried/grim; the man on the right wears a green parachute pack and looks calm. No text.

Panel 3: The two men give each other thumbs up. The man in the yellow vest smiles; the man with the green parachute (now seen from behind, with orange hair) returns the gesture. No text.

Panel 4: The two men sit side by side, both smiling contentedly. No text.

Panel 5: An exit door of the plane is open, clouds visible outside. The man in the green parachute waves goodbye as he prepares to jump; the man in the yellow vest watches. No text.

Panel 6: Outside the plane, the parachuting man (green jacket, orange hair) falls through the sky and is caught/bitten in the jaws of a large gray shark, mouth full of teeth, against the cloudy blue sky. No text.
comics.voteyText: A close-up of the gray shark's open, toothy mouth lunging forward, jaws wide. No text.

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A blue-skinned sorceress with large black horns and flame-like orange hair (resembling Maleficent), gesturing dramatically over a casket: "AND WHEN THE PRINCESS PRICKS HER FINGER, SHE WILL SLEEP FOREVER UNLESS A SERIES OF UNLIKELY CONDITIONS ARE MET!"

A green goblin-like creature with fangs and claws, standing nearby: "UH, I GOT A KNIFE? WE COULD JUST STAB HER... YOU WANNA JUST STAB HER?"

Caption: The original draft of Sleeping Beauty was just over twelve minutes long.
comics.voteyText: Close-up of the green horned creature's face, smiling, with a speech bubble: "I feel so fulfilled now!"

comics.comicText:
Single panel:

A worried man with brown hair stands in the center, sweating. To his left, a small angel (white robe, halo, wings) gestures at him. To his right, a red devil (horns, cape, pitchfork) has just arrived holding a smoking gun, with a smoke wisp rising from the barrel.

Angel: "NO TODD! YOU LOVE YOUR WIFE AND KIDS! THEY'RE-"

Devil: "HEY GUYS, I'M BACK. SORRY, BUT I GOT BORED WITH THE DEBATE, SO I WENT AHEAD AND JUST KILLED YOUR FAMILY MYSELF."

Caption below panel: "Say what you will, sociopathy is efficient."
comics.voteyText:
A simply-drawn face (the devil character) speaks.
Devil: "Efficiency is this generation's compassion."

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

The Joker (green-haired, white-faced supervillain): "HAHAHAHAHA! I can't wait to see the horror on doctors' faces after I pour THIS in Gotham's water supply!"

The Joker holds up a bottle, throwing a punch (sound effect: "POW!"). The bottle is labeled: "CURE FOR ALL DISEASES"

Batman (lunging in from the right): "NOT SO FAST, JOKER!"
comics.voteyText: Text on a tipped-over green bottle: "JOKER TRIES TO DESTROY PHARMACEUTICAL INDUSTRY"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A gray-haired man in a dark blue suit stands against an orange background, arm extended, firing a handgun. A large yellow muzzle flash erupts from the barrel.

Caption (below panel): Dr. Oppenheimer illustrates the appropriate defense against Hungarian style épée fencing.
comics.voteyText:
Handwritten note reading:
Pro-tip:
Keep shooting until opponent ceases fencing

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man with brown hair (green shirt) sits across a table from a blonde woman (pink shirt). Above the woman's head is a mounted electronic scrolling sign.

Man: YOU KNOW, I REALLY FEEL THAT YOUR NEW SIGN IS PUTTING A STRAIN ON OUR MARRIAGE.

Electronic sign (above the woman): COUNTDOWN TO DIVORCE

2Y 1M 03 51 22

Caption (below panel): Immediately, the counter ticked down two months.
comics.voteyText:
A simple line-drawn face speaks.
Face: One of my boyfriends has it on remote control.

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

Setting: a backyard pool party on a sunny day. Purple silhouetted partygoers mingle in the background near a wooden fence.

A blonde woman in a red one-piece swimsuit reaches up and presses a paper bag onto the head of a man in a gray t-shirt. The bag has a smiling face drawn on it.

Woman: "THERE!"

Caption (below panel): "Now nobody else feels depressed!"
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of two faces. On the left, a woman with a distressed, frowning, teary expression. On the right, the man's head now covered by the paper bag with its drawn-on smiling face.
Woman: "Stop it! Your tears are making the bag soggy!"

comics.comicText:
Title: SUICIDE FLOWCHART

A flowchart with five labeled boxes connected by arrows.

Green box (top left): "SHOOT YOURSELF."

Blue box (bottom middle): "REALIZE LIFE IS WORTH LIVING."

Red/pink box (bottom right): "OFFICE JOB FOR SIXTY YEARS."

Yellow box (top right): "DIE."

Arrows:

- "SHOOT YOURSELF." leads directly to "DIE."

- "SHOOT YOURSELF." also leads down to "REALIZE LIFE IS WORTH LIVING."

- "REALIZE LIFE IS WORTH LIVING." leads to "OFFICE JOB FOR SIXTY YEARS."

- "OFFICE JOB FOR SIXTY YEARS." leads up to "DIE."
comics.voteyText:
Caption (top): "Reading this ten years later"
A distressed-looking older person with long hair and a beard, frowning.
Speech bubble: "What asshole writes this shit?!"

comics.comicText:
Panel (single image):

Setting: A dusty Old West town street at sunset, with buildings labeled "SALOON" and "LIVERY." Cacti are visible in the distance.

In the foreground, seen from behind, a man with orange/red hair holds a pen and a sheet of paper, as if taking notes or sketching the scene.

In the middle ground, an older man in a brown suit gestures toward a younger gunslinger in a cowboy hat and blue clothing who stands ready to draw his gun.

Gunslinger (speech bubble): "DRAW!"

Older man (speech bubble): "HEH HEH!"

Caption below the panel:

"We all had a good laugh at McGuffrey's pun.

I mean, sure, we would've laughed harder if we hadn't figured out the joke while picking through blood and chunks of brain, but deep down, I'm pretty sure this is what he would've wanted. Ooh look! There's a gold tooth under this picture of his wife and kids!"
comics.voteyText: A hand-drawn graph with axes labeled "brevity" (vertical / y-axis) and "wit" (horizontal / x-axis). A thick orange line starts high on the left, slopes downward to a low point near the bottom, then curves sharply upward into an arrow at the far right.

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A bald man at a podium (a politician/speaker, with a seal on the front of the podium) addresses a crowd whose fists are raised.

Crowd member: THE PRESIDENT'S A RACIST!

Crowd member: BIGOT!

Speaker at podium: NO! WAIT! I SAID CHIGGERS! CHIGGERS!

Caption (below comic): "I hate black people and chiggers."
comics.voteyText:
Close-up on the bald speaker's face, looking strained.
Speaker: Yes, I hate black people, but not in a racist way.

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A father sits on the edge of a child's bed in a darkened bedroom at night, a starry window behind him. He smiles and gestures reassuringly to a small blonde child tucked under the covers.

Father: "Sweetie, don't worry. There IS no afterlife. When you die, you simply cease to be."

Caption (below panel): Dad explains why there is no ghost under my bed.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of the smiling father, drawn in a loose sketch style, raising a hand as he continues to speak.
Father: "Also, fear is just a physical process, like love."

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A scientist in a white lab coat (a person with light/blond hair) stands holding a clipboard, observing through a window into a sealed chamber. On the wall is a gauge labeled "AIR LEVEL" with markings "LOW" 50%" "OK". Inside the chamber, a person (with orange/red hair) lies on a table, arm outstretched and limp against the glass. A test sheet near them reads "CAN YOU BREATH?" with checkboxes.

Caption (below panel): Once again, our study proved inconclusive.
comics.voteyText: A close-up of a distressed, wide-eyed face (the test subject). Speech bubble: "I need 700 more gallons of undergrad!"

comics.comicText:
Single panel: A man with brown hair, seen from behind, sits in a living room facing two women on a red couch. One woman has blonde hair and wears a purple top; she is dabbing at her eye with a tissue. The other woman has red/orange hair and wears a blue shirt; she also appears emotional, holding a hand to her chest. Framed pictures hang on the wall behind them.

Caption (below panel): It was the greatest fart joke they had ever heard.
comics.voteyText:
A simple line-drawing of a person's face with a wistful, moved expression.
Face: "I have touched the face of god."

comics.comicText:
Title banner: SMBC PRESENTS: MISUNDERSTOOD BIBLE PASSAGES

Panel: An old man with long gray hair and beard, wearing a purple robe, stands at the rail of a wooden ark looking out at a large rainbow arcing across the sky. A giraffe is visible beside him on the ark.

Old man (Noah): HUH.

Caption below panel: Episode 1:

God calls Noah gay.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of the same old man's (Noah's) face, looking puzzled.
Noah: I'm not mad, just confused.

comics.comicText:
Title banner: SMBC PRESENTS: TOMMY, THE OFFICE PRANKSTER

Panel 1:

Tommy (a smiling young man with blond hair, wearing a shirt and tie): "Hey kids! I'm Tommy, the office prankster!"

Panel 2:

Tommy (holding a gun and placing it on a desk): "Today, I'm switching my boss' desk pistol with this novelty gun!"

Panel 3:

Tommy (grinning): "In a half hour, I'll burst in, pretending to be a robber! Hoohoo!"

Panel 4:

Caption: 30 MINUTES LATER...

(Tommy, wearing a black mask and pointing the gun, bursts in on his gray-haired boss. A red 'BANG' flash erupts from the boss firing a real gun back at Tommy.)
comics.voteyText:
(Close-up of Tommy's masked face, looking dazed/dying)
Tommy: "Do I still get severance?"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man with red/orange hair stands at a podium in front of a banner reading "MISOGYNISTS ANONYMOUS '06".

Man (Todd): "I haven't been able to overcome my problem entirely, but the are now a few specific types of women I don't hate. For example, unattractive harpies, who better not leave the kitchen unless I say so."

Caption (below panel): Todd then smiled and winked at his wife.
comics.voteyText:
Handwritten letter: "Dear Zach, are you ever embarrassed of any of your old comics?"
Reply (in red): "WHAT OLD COMICS?"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

Setting: a dim, greenish room. A balding man in a dark green shirt stands at left, pointing his finger sternly. Facing him is a boy with reddish-brown hair in a blue shirt, who is gripping a knife and stabbing a third person lying down (a blond figure in a green shirt) who is bleeding red.

Man (pointing): "BOBBY! NO!"

Man: "NOT ON TUESDAY!"

Caption below the panel:

"The key to being a good parent is knowing when to set boundaries."

"For example, on Tuesday, Bobby isn't allowed to stop stabbing anyone."
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of an intense, scowling man's face shouting, drawn in a rough sketch style.
Text (handwritten): "Be a man, and KILL KILL KILL!"

comics.comicText:
The comic is presented in reverse chronological order, reading top to bottom.

Panel 1 (caption: "5 SECONDS AGO."): A hand holds an open greeting card. The card reads: "SORRY! THIS WAS THE ONLY TYPE OF CARD THEY HAD LEFT. ANYWAY, HAPPY 30th!" followed by a beginning of a sign-off, "love," (partially cut off).

Panel 2 (caption: "10 SECONDS AGO"): A close-up of a man with brown hair, looking distraught, with a tear or bead of sweat on his cheek.

Panel 3 (caption: "15 SECONDS AGO"): A hand holds a closed card with a purple/gray cover. The cover reads: "YOUR WIFE IS DEAD."
comics.voteyText: A wordless drawing of a greeting-card store display rack. Three card-section header signs hang above the racks, labeled: "Birthday", "Bar Mitzvah", and "Unsentimental Declarations of Death". Below the signs are tiered shelves holding rows of blank greeting cards.

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

A man and a blonde woman are in the front seats of a car at night, leaning toward each other in an embrace.

Woman: WAIT! DO YOU HAVE ANY PROTECTION?

Man: WELL, MY MOM SAID BABIES ONLY COME FROM TWO PEOPLE WHO REALLY LOVE EACHOTHER. SO, I THINK WE SHOULD BE IN THE CLEAR.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of a person's worried face.
Voice (off-panel, in a large speech bubble): Okay, then no falling in love while we're doing it!

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man (back to viewer, brown hair): YOU'RE GETTING ANOTHER DESSERT?!

Woman (blonde, red dress): WELL HONEY, AS YOU KNOW, I AM EATING FOR TWO NOW.

Man: *sigh* RIGHT, RIGHT...

Caption: Rachel wasn't pregnant - she'd just decided to start eating more.
comics.voteyText: Woman (smiling): If you complain, I'll eat you too!

comics.comicText:
Title banner: SMBC PRESENTS: UPSIDES TO THE NUCLEAR HOLOCAUST

EPISODE 1: GIVING RELATIONSHIP TIPS GETS A LOT EASIER.

Panel 1:

An old man wearing dark sunglasses and holding a smoking pipe, speaking to a younger man (his son):

Old man: "Son, there are two kinds of women in the world - there's Kim, and there's Tracy."
comics.voteyText:
Close-up sketch of the old man in sunglasses, still speaking.
Old man: "Tip 1: Don't mix them up"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A woman with long hair stands behind two children (a girl and a boy). An older woman with large orange/red hair and glasses (the grandmother) faces them.

Girl: HOW ABOUT A GAME OF CHECKERS?

Grandmother: HOW ABOUT WE MURDER ALL THE CHILDREN IN THE WORLD AT THE SAME TIME?!

Boy: GRAMMA!!

Caption (below panel): Now and then i have to politely remind Grandma that this isn't the 2010s anymore.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of the grandmother's face, eyes closed, looking weary and resigned.
Grandmother: The tumblr wars were brutal.

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man with orange/red hair stands outside near a house and a red mailbox, reading a handwritten note. Behind him a sun and clouds hang over a dark roof.

The note reads:

"THERE ONCE WAS A MAN FROM NAN-TUCKET. STEVE, I SHOT YOUR DOG. UCKET."

Caption below the panel:

"I find a little rhyme can really take the edge off of bad news."

"Which reminds me… I've been meaning to tell you that, well… There once was a man from… schmonorrhea."

"You have AIDS. Ucket."
comics.voteyText: Handwritten text reading: "Do you really want another punchline, you greedy bastard?"

comics.comicText:
Title banner: SMBC PRESENTS "WHY SHE WON'T DATE YOU" (answer on bottom)

POSSIBILITIES:

A. TIN FOIL HAT. (illustration of a foil hat)

B. TIN FOIL CAPE. (illustration of a foil cape with writing on it reading: STAY OUT OF MY SPINE!)

C. CRUSHING FEAR OF MARTIAN INVASION. (illustration of a green Martian alien recoiling from small planets)

Martian alien: BLEACH!

Answer printed upside-down at the bottom: ANSWER: SHE'S A CORPSE IN YOUR BASEMENT!
comics.voteyText: A woman wearing a pointed foil hat (drawn with a wrench/fork shape on top) speaks. Speech bubble: Speak to me!

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man with brown hair, seen from behind in a blue shirt, faces a grinning man with flame-like orange hair in a yellow shirt.

Man with brown hair: WHO'S THERE?

Man with orange hair: GO F*CK YOURSELF!

Caption (below panel): Ted's knock-knock jokes have gotten really redundant since I got promoted over him.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of the grinning orange-haired man's face with a speech bubble.
Man: Why did the chicken cross the FUCK YOU

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A blonde woman with an angry expression holds up a small voodoo doll by its arm, shaking it. A red-haired man beside her recoils in pain, mouth open. A jagged "CRACK" effect appears near his neck/head.

Voodoo doll (effect/reaction): OW!

Blonde woman: YEAH! THIS TIME IT'S FILLED WITH ROCKS!

Caption (below panel): The voodoo doll works a lot better now.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of the blonde woman smiling with delight.
Woman: Isn't it magical?

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man (praying, hand to face): GOD, IS THERE REALLY A HEAVEN?

God (large yellow speech bubble): HAHAHA! SIMPLE MAN. MY CHILD, "HEAVEN" WAS CREATED BY HUMANS IN ORDER TO MANIPULATE EACH OTHER WITH FALSE HOPE.

Man: SO, THEN, WHERE DO WE GO WHEN WE DIE?

God: HELL.
comics.voteyText: God (off-panel, speech bubble): It's not perfect, but accounting is way simpler.

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

Two men sit in the front seat of a car. The man with orange/red hair (passenger) holds out a document labeled "AUTO INSURER" toward the brown-haired man driving.

Red-haired passenger: "I REALLY don't see how this is gonna help, but FINE, here's my insurance information."

Brown-haired driver: "THANK you."

Caption below the panel:

I tried to apologize, but Steve just shut me up with "I'm not talking to you right now."

I guess it didn't really matter. It was only going to be about 15 more seconds before we inevitably smashed into the canyon floor.
comics.voteyText:
A hand-drawn scene of a car plummeting down a steep cliff/canyon slope, with speed lines trailing behind it.
Speech bubble from the car: "Oh my GOD, this is totally expired!"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A young man with orange hair, wearing a red shirt and purple pants, stands on a beach holding a golden lamp that he is rubbing. A genie with green skin, a gray turban, and a long purple wisp of smoke for a lower body rises from the lamp.

Man: "I WISH THE SALAD WOULD DOG INTO THE CAT MY DISAPPEARING FACE-TOOTH!"

Caption (below panel): Of course, what Jeff should have wished for was a cure for schizophrenia.
comics.voteyText:
A hand-drawn sketch of the genie's face. The genie says (in a speech bubble): "I'll make you a puppy"
A small dog at the bottom left replies: "Yay!"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man with glasses and short brown hair, wearing an orange polo shirt, holds a pointer up to a framed picture on the wall. The picture shows a forest scene of dark trees and pink/magenta foliage, with a white mound in the center.

Label on the white mound in the picture: PILE OF CORPSES

Caption (below panel): In an alternate ending to "Snow White," everybody just dies.
comics.voteyText:
A hand-drawn close-up of a sad, downcast face (loose sketch style).
Handwritten text: "If we also kill Mickey, it'll be really poignant" (pointing toward the face).

comics.comicText:
Panel 1: An elderly white-haired man sits in a red leather armchair in a wood-paneled study. A small white dog with black ears rests on his lap, wearing a yellow tag or vest reading "JOY". A servant in formal butler attire stands to the right by a purple curtain.

Panel 2: The man clutches his chest, looking distressed. The dog now wears a black-and-white tag reading "NO" (the dog's expression has soured). The butler raises a hand.

Elderly man: "OH NO! I'VE JUST RECALLED AN EMBARASSING MEMORY FROM MY CHILDHOOD."

Panel 3: The butler, hand to his mouth, looks pained.

Butler: "SHALL I..."

Panel 4: Close-up of the elderly man, looking firm and resolute, hand raised.

Elderly man: "YES. BRING IT TO ME."

Panel 5: The man sits back in the armchair. The dog on his lap is now dark/shadowed and wears a green tag reading "SHAME". The butler stands at the right, departed from view earlier, now back in position.
comics.voteyText:
A roughly-sketched close-up of the elderly man's stern face with a speech bubble.
Elderly man: "Bring me the miniature pony of remorse"

comics.comicText:
A poker game between two cowboys in a saloon at night, with cactuses and a desert visible through the window.

A cowboy in a brown hat and orange shirt with suspenders, holding cards: "Full house, Big Tex."

The other man, called Big Tex, in a black hat and leather vest with a bandolier: "Yer cheatin'!"

The first cowboy: "You can search me iffin' you want, but you'll still hafta pay yer due."

Caption below the panel: "Why didn't you wear a dang undershirt?" Big Tex muttered to himself as he nervously fumbled for his top button.
comics.voteyText: A loose sketch of the first cowboy's face under his hat, drawn on Big Tex's bare chest/skin. Handwritten next to it: "I love you, Big Tex"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

Judge (a woman with curly hair, seated at the bench): IN THE CUSTODY MATTER OF ROBERTS vs. ROBERTS, THIS COURT SEES FIT TO AWARD CUSTODY TO...

Judge: MR. ANDREWS

A woman with blonde hair (reacting in the foreground): WHAT?

A man with orange hair (grinning, seated): YES!

Caption below panel: I have a fantastic attorney.
comics.voteyText: A woman (the judge, smiling): And I award him... my heart.

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (with orange hair, pink shirt, green skirt): "OH WOW HONEY! KIDS, LOOK! HONEY, TAKE A PICTURE! WOW! NEW YORK CITY! WOW!"

Man (in blue cap and blue shirt, holding a camera): *click! click!*

Caption (below panel): The Sandersons had never seen a homeless man before.
comics.voteyText: Handwritten note: "To readers of the future: The device in his hands is a tiny washing machine"

comics.comicText:
Title banner: SMBC PRESENTS! ADVANCED DATING TIPS

EPISODE 1: SAYING THINGS WITHOUT USING WORDS

Main panel:

[A woman with brown hair, seen from behind, faces a man across a table in a room. The man stands with his hands raised, mouth wide open, shouting.]

Man: BLEEG! BWUHHH! BLARGH!
comics.voteyText:
[Close-up of a smiling man's face. A speech bubble points to him.]
Man: SMEEBEC.

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Magician (in top hat and tuxedo, with a curled mustache): AND VOILA! SIR, ARE YOU MISSING ANYTHING?

A man with brown hair in a green shirt, seen from behind, faces the magician.

Man: OH MY GOD! I CAN'T FIND MY WALLET! OR MY KEYS!

Caption (below the panel): Smiling broadly, the magician reached into his hat, and retrieved Sam's retinas.
comics.voteyText:
The magician's grinning face fills the frame.
Magician: Now everything I do is magic too you!

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

King (a red-haired man wearing a purple-and-yellow crown and a purple royal robe, shaking his fist and pointing): LET THIS BE A LESSON TO ALL WHO WILL NOT KNEEL IN DEFERENCE!

(In the background, a gallows with the silhouette of a hanged man.)

Caption below the comic:

Many of us felt that Henry had overstepped his authority as Prom King.

For example, he brought in this silhouette of a hanged man. To Prom!

Or there was the time he hanged that guy for not kneeling in deference. What is this, middle school?
comics.voteyText: A person resting their head, with a tear running down their cheek, thinking: If I made the caption recursive, it could just go on forever.

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Reporter (an off-panel person, only a hand and red hair visible): TWO QUESTIONS, MR. PRESIDENT: WHAT'S YOUR POLICY ON GUN CONTROL, AND DID YOU REALLY THINK THAT WOULD WORK?

The President (a gray-haired man in a blue suit with a red tie): I BELIEVE IT'S A STATES RIGHTS ISSUE, AND, NO COMMENT.

Caption banner (yellow): MOMENTS PRIOR...

Panel 2:

The President (standing behind a podium, arms thrown up in the air, papers on the podium labeled "POLICY" and "DUTY"): PAPERS, PAPERS, ONE, TWO, THREE! GO AWAY AND LEAVE ME BE!
comics.voteyText: The President (close-up, eyes closed, looking regretful): I regret that the Leprechauns lied to me

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A close-up of a woman with red/orange hair against a blue background. The words "DON'T LOOK HERE" are tattooed (or written) across her forehead.

Text on forehead: DON'T LOOK HERE

Caption (below panel): I opted for a more economical rhinoplasty.
comics.voteyText:
A rough line-drawing of a balding, smiling man's face. The words "Don't look here" are written on his forehead.
Text on forehead: Don't look here
Man (speech bubble): I've gotta be someone's fetish!

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

A shirtless man with reddish hair, seen from behind, wearing red-and-white polka-dot boxer shorts, raises one arm up high toward a woman with brown hair in a blue dress, who stands in a doorway scowling at him.

Man: HIGH FIVE!

Man: NO HIGH FIVE?

Caption (below panel): Apparently "You're in bed with another woman!" was not meant to be congratulatory.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up sketch of a man's face looking sad/distressed with a speech bubble.
Man (the woman, off-panel / overlaid line): Why won't you communicate more?

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man with red hair in a green shirt, holding a sandwich, speaks cheerfully to a man with brown hair seen from behind in the foreground.

Red-haired man: "Now that it's May of 2016, we sure don't have to worry about three-fourths of the world's population dying of a lethal strain of flu at the same time!"

Caption (below panel): "This comic will be hilarious in about 20 years."
comics.voteyText: A hand-drawn graph. The vertical axis is labeled "# deaths" and the horizontal axis is labeled "funniness." A red curve starts high on the left (high deaths, low funniness), dips down to a low point in the middle, then climbs steeply back up to the top on the right (high funniness corresponds again to high deaths).

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man with curly red hair, wearing a green shirt, stands in a dimly lit room and addresses a younger person (a son, seen from behind, with orange/red hair and a blue shirt) who is holding a piece of paper.

Man: HEY SON! WHATCHA GOT THERE?

Son: *sigh* JUST DREAMS...

The paper the son holds reads:

- LEARN ENGLISH

- MOVE TO AMERICA

Panel 2 (close-up of the full paper):

Things I wish dad would do:

- LEARN ENGLISH

- MOVE TO AMERICA

- NEVER COME HOME
comics.voteyText:
A roughly-drawn close-up of the father's head with a speech bubble.
Father: So far, the only English I know is this sentence.

comics.comicText:
A man with reddish hair, shirtless, sits up in bed next to a blonde woman wearing a pink top. They are on their honeymoon.

Man (Ted): SWEETIE, THE HONEYMOON HAS BEEN AMAZING SO FAR. I WAS WONDERING IF YOU'D LIKE TO TRY SOMETHING A LITTLE... DIFFERENT TONIGHT.

Woman: O-OKAY...

Caption (below panel): Ted immediately went to sleep.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of the woman's smiling face.
Woman: So spontaneous!

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

A gravestone stands in a cemetery under a pink sky with a setting sun. The headstone is inscribed:

"MY LAST

NAME IS

<cough> IS <gurgle>

IS...<dying sounds>"

STEVE ?

1977 - 2006
comics.voteyText: Handwritten text: "This is how graves work."

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A blond boy (Billy) sits playing a video game with a controller, looking annoyed. Behind him stands an old man wearing sunglasses, leaning on a walker.

Old man: "HEY BILLY, HOW 'BOUT WE GO OUT FOR SOME ICED CREAM?"

Billy: "HOW 'BOUT VIDEO GAMES."

Old man: "HOW 'BOUT I WRAP YOU IN A BURLAP SACK AND BEAT YOU WITH A CANE?"

Panel 2 (mock video game box art):

Game box title: "CROTCHITY OLD MAN GAMES PRESENTS: I WRAP YOU IN A BURLAP SACK AND BEAT YOU WITH A CANE. TURBO EDITION!"

The box art shows a man swinging a cane at a burlap sack, with a score readout "37".
comics.voteyText: A hand-drawn video game screen showing two health/status bars at the top, both nearly empty. Large text reads "TIE" and below it "BOTH PLAYERS TIRED". At the bottom are two exhausted characters: on the left a man slumped over asleep, on the right the old man slumped over asleep.

comics.comicText:
Single panel: Three people sit around a dinner table.

A man in a yellow shirt (addressed as Ted): "Ted, my god, you tell the best stories, and this homemade sorbet is to die for!"

A woman in the middle: "Well thanks, I-"

A man with orange hair and an eye patch (wearing a red and yellow shirt): "Hey! You know what's better than both of those?"

The same man with the eye patch: "NOT BEING BLIND!"

Caption below the panel: The great thing about being handicapped is the ability to create five minutes of awkward silence any time you like.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of the man with the eye patch's face, smiling.
Man with eye patch: "Great dip, though."

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

An elderly man with glasses and suspenders leans down toward two children, smiling broadly.

Elderly man: "HEY KIDS, WANNA SEE A TRICK?"

Caption (below panel): In the future, it will be possible to predict the exact moment when you die.
comics.voteyText: Handwritten text: "The secret is watching the knife go in!"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1

Father: Son, now that you're eighteen, we have something to tell you - we're not poor. In fact, I'm worth over a billion dollars. We just didn't want you to grow up spoiled and unambitious.

Panel 2

Son: So, when you said "we can't afford to fix every little problem," that was a lie?

Panel 3

Father: Think of it as a story that taught you a lesson.

Caption (below panels): Silently, Todd felt the stub where his arm used to be.
comics.voteyText: The father (close-up): Gangrene builds character!

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man with brown hair, seen from behind, holds up a syringe and presses a blonde man against a brick wall.

Brown-haired man (shouting): HERE'S YOUR HEROIN!

The blonde man grins broadly, arms spread wide, looking delighted.

Caption (below panel): Who says money can't buy happiness?
comics.voteyText:
The blonde man reclines happily, the now-empty syringe lying on the ground in front of him, a contented smile on his face.
Blonde man (small speech bubble): People are so cynical!

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A wild-eyed man with flame-like orange hair, wearing a blue shirt and orange shorts, shouts. He holds a yellow book (a Bible) in one hand and dangles a small brown monkey by the arm in the other.

Man (shouting): MONKEYS EVOLVED FROM THE BIBLE!!!

Monkey: OOK?

Caption (below panel): The third perspective on evolution.
comics.voteyText:
A Bible (a book marked with a large cross on its cover) stands on two stubby legs, anthropomorphized.
Bible: I'm the missing link

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A black-and-white spotted dog stands on a sidewalk near a fire hydrant at night. A thought bubble rises from the dog, picturing a happy version of itself running across a green field.

Dog (thinking): I HAVE A CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM COMPLEX ENOUGH TO ALLOW FANTASIES!

Caption (below panel): Dog fantasies.
comics.voteyText:
A bearded, tired-looking man lies in bed with a thought bubble above his head.
Man (thinking): They should let me write Garfield

comics.comicText:
Single panel: A doctor in a white coat with a head mirror leans toward a seated patient (a man seen from behind), grinning.

Doctor (large speech bubble): "IT WON'T SOUND SO BAD IF YOU REALLY PRONOUNCE THE 'EEEEE!'"

Patient: "I REALLY DON'T-"

Doctor: "OH COME ON!"

Patient: "I JUST DON'T FEEL LIKE-"

Doctor: "C'MONNN!"

Patient (small bubble, defeated): "*sigh* AMPUTEEEEEE."

Caption below the panel:

"Aaand why?"

"... peripheral vascular diseeeeease."
comics.voteyText:
A crudely drawn smiling face leans in.
Face: "See? Look how much happier I am!"

comics.comicText:
A handwritten letter on parchment, written in red (blood-colored) ink:

"I apologize in advance for the latter portion of this note. My three year old got these markers, and we were out of paper... Anyway-

Baron Destructicus -

I write this in my own blood, for it is the same blood spilt by your barbarian soldiers under last night's moon.

Seven hundred of ours fell in the slaughter, mostly women and children.

Let this be your notice, Baron: we will not die in silence, not before our lands are watered with your blood, and our rivers run overflowing with your dead.

May all that you love perish in agony."

Below the signature, drawn in crayon by a small child in multiple colors: scribbled hearts, x's and o's, stars, a smiley face, and the wobbly words "i lov u" and what appears to be "yes."
comics.voteyText: A horned Viking/barbarian figure (the Baron) reads the note. In a speech bubble above his head, in childlike handwriting, he says: "Now you fwiends!"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

A graveyard at dusk under a pink sky with white clouds and a setting sun. A large central tombstone reads:

SUSAN LERMAN

1956 - 2006

"HEY WAIT! I'M NOT DEAD YET!"

A skeletal hand emerges from the ground in front of the tombstone, reaching up out of the dirt.
comics.voteyText: Handwritten caption on a plain square: "No, really, this is how graves work."

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A blue-skinned humanoid alien with large yellow eyes, pointed ears, and a costume with a yellow collar and belt stands inside what appears to be a spaceship interior. It gestures toward a human man (seen from behind, balding, in a dark blue robe) who faces it.

Alien: IN EXCHANGE FOR ONE MILLION HUMAN CHILDREN, WE SHALL SHARE ALL OF OUR ADVANCED MEDICAL KNOWLEDGE.

Caption (below panel): In retrospect, it should've been obvious that Altarian biology was vastly different from our own.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up sketch of the blue alien's face looking confused.
Alien (thought/speech): What the hell is "cancer"?

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Doctor (a woman with glasses and a head mirror, holding a clipboard): SO... DURING YOUR KNEE SURGERY WE SORT OF ACCIDENTALLY STARTED OPERATING ON YOUR BRAIN AND REMOVED YOUR ABILITY TO REACT REASONABLY TO SITUATIONS...

Patient (a man with reddish-orange hair): BAHAHAHA! YOU GUYS ARE AWESOME!

Caption: Mr. Andrews later sued us for having an excellent gift shop.
comics.voteyText: Mr. Andrews (the same red-haired man, now drawn with a flat, deadpan expression): I'm suing for negative a million dollars.

comics.comicText:
Title banner: SMBC PRESENTS: MARKETING TIPS: EPISODE ONE: "THE SURGEON GENERAL ISN'T THE ONLY ONE WHO CAN ADD WARNINGS"

A cigarette pack is shown covered in several pasted-on warning labels. Visible label text:

- "WARNING TWO: SMOKING IS AWESOME."

- partially obscured labels reading "...cause..." / "...defects." / "...emo..." (parody of the usual surgeon general warnings about causing birth defects, etc.)
comics.voteyText: A single hand-lettered warning label reads: "WARNING: The surgeon general is a pussy."

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A young man with blond hair (back to viewer, in red) stands facing two older men.

Blond young man: "DAD, DAD... I HAVE SOMETHING TO TELL YOU... I'M... DOUBLE-GAY."

The two men he is addressing (one with reddish-brown hair in a green shirt, one with short hair in a blue shirt) look on, the green-shirted one smiling slightly.

Caption (below panel): "Of course we were supportive, but deep down we wondered if we were bad parents."
comics.voteyText:
A roughly sketched face of one of the dads speaks.
Dad: "We're sending you to Double-Gay therapy camp."

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

A nurse in purple scrubs and a white nurse's cap with a red cross sits cheerfully between two elderly people. To the left, an old man in a blue shirt looks on. To the right, an elderly white-haired woman in a yellow cardigan sits slumped in a wheelchair, head lolling.

Nurse: DISCOUNT MOVIE TICKETS! HAHA! WELL THIS SESSION IS GOING JUST GREAT! HOW ABOUT YOU, PHYLLIS? WHAT'S YOUR FAVORITE THING ABOUT BEING A SENIOR?

Nurse (smaller speech bubbles, looking toward the slumped woman): PHYLLIS? ... PHYLLIS?

Caption (below panel): Phyllis had died of shock after her false teeth, glass eyes, and severe pain medication fell into her incontinence diapers.
comics.voteyText: A hand-drawn line graph. The vertical axis is labeled "funnyness of old people jokes" and the horizontal axis is labeled "my age." A red arrow slopes steeply downward from the upper left to the lower right, showing that the funniness of old-people jokes decreases as the author's age increases.

comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A map of the African continent, shown in yellow against a purple background. No text.

Panel 2: Against an orange sky, a crate descends by parachute. The crate is labeled "AIDS RELIEF." A second, smaller parachute drops a box labeled (illegibly) nearby.

Panel 3: The crate has landed on the ground. A man runs toward it.

Man: LOOK!

Panel 4: The man crouches at the open "AIDS RELIEF" crate, lifting an item out of it, looking puzzled.

Man: A PLAYSTATION?

Panel 5: Close-up of the man holding his head in his hands in frustration.

Man: DAMMIT!

Panel 6: The man stands among the crates, arms raised, shouting angrily at the sky.

Man: DAMN YOU AMERICANS! IS THIS SOME KIND OF JOKE? HOW IN THE WORLD IS THIS SUPPOSED TO HELP?!

Man: HUH?!

Panel 7 (caption: SUBSEQUENTLY...): The man, looking flatly unimpressed, sits with the PlayStation controller in his lap, hands on it. A smiling woman approaches.

Woman: HEY, YOU WANT TO HAVE SEX?

Man: MEH.
comics.voteyText: A hand-drawn line graph. The y-axis is labeled "population" and the x-axis is labeled "price of amusement." A red curve rises to a peak as price of amusement increases from zero, then plunges sharply downward as the price of amusement continues to rise.

comics.comicText:
Single panel:

A dark-haired man (referred to as Clark) sits in an armchair, holding up a yellow legal pad. An older woman in a purple dress stands beside him, gesturing, with a green chalkboard behind her.

Clark: "I'VE GOT IT CLARK! TRUTH, JUSTICE, AND THE AMERICAN WAY!"

Woman: "OH... OH YEAH, YEAH THAT'S PRETTY COOL..."

Chalkboard (brainstorming notes): "GREAT MAN? STRO[NG] *UBE[R]* (SUPERMAN) TRUTH, JUSTICE, AND...?"

The yellow legal pad in Clark's hands reads: "TRUTH, JUSTICE AND FUCK DA POLICE"
comics.voteyText: A woman's face (lower right). A speech bubble from off-panel says: "Now I made you this unitard!"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

An older cowboy wearing a hat speaks to a young blond boy who is holding a saddle.

Cowboy: "Sonny, 'fore you hop in that saddle, there's somethin' you oughta unnerstand - when you're a cowboy, you don't ride the horse. The horse... rides you."

Panel 2:

Caption: "ABOUT TWENTY MINUTES LATER"

The scene shows a horse lying on top of and crushing the boy, with a large pool of blood underneath. The cowboy stands to the left. A man in white (a doctor/examiner) crouches on the right next to the body.

Doctor: "Yep, he's dead."
comics.voteyText:
A simply drawn face with a speech bubble.
Face: "Lung collapse due to severe horsitation"

comics.comicText:
Single panel:

On a dark wall, blood spatter has formed the word "BUTT." in dripping red letters.

Below, a man with orange hair (Frank) slumps forward with his head down on a desk, a handgun and a note beside him.

Caption (below panel): "Due to the unlikely spattering of blood, Frank's suicide took on a less somber tone."
comics.voteyText: A handwritten suicide note reads: "No one takes me seriously"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Joker: YOU'RE TOO LATE BATMAN! NOW YOU'LL NEVER STOP MY PLAN TO LET BATMAN SURVIVE THE NIGHT!

Batman: WE'LL SEE ABOUT THAT JOKER!

Panel 2:

Caption: LATER...

(Batman has a Batarang lodged bloodily in his forehead, having apparently thrown it at himself.)

Joker: WELL PLAYED.
comics.voteyText: Batman (battered, eye swollen): This is gonna bruise

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man with brown hair in a yellow shirt stands at a party, gesturing, addressing a group of people around him.

Man in yellow shirt: "HEY, I GOT ONE - WHY ARE YOU PEOPLE SO BORING?"

Caption (below panel): The riddling party comes to an abrupt halt.
comics.voteyText:
A worried-looking woman.
Woman: "Mostly environmental factors."

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man (with red/orange hair, green shirt): HOW ABOUT NOW?

Woman (brown hair, red shirt): I TOLD YOU STEVE - THERE'S NO WAY I'M EVER DATING YOU.

Caption (below panel): Moments later, Earth collided with Mars.
comics.voteyText: Close-up of the woman's face, drawn in a sketchy black-and-white style, thought/hand-lettered text above her head: I still have a shot at Harrison Ford

comics.comicText:
Title: WEIGHT LOSS FLOWCHART!

The flowchart has four boxes connected by arrows.

Box 1 (top left, orange): "YOU'RE SO DAMN FAT"

An arrow points right to Box 2, and an arrow points down to Box 3.

Box 2 (top right, yellow): "SUICIDE"

An arrow points down to Box 4.

Box 3 (bottom left, yellow): "DIET AND EXERCISE"

An arrow points right to Box 4.

Box 4 (bottom right, pink): "YOU'RE NOT FAT ANYMORE!"

Caption below the comic: I told my wife I found the chart a bit insulting. At this point, she noted that I was correct, but also "so damn fat."
comics.voteyText:
Top caption: Reading this 10 years later...
A man lying down, viewed up close, says (in a speech bubble): "This is awful and a bad flowchart"

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (title card): SMBC PRESENTS A TALE OF SUPERHERODOM "SO-DAMN-AWESOME-MAN"

Panel 2: A bald mugger leans into a car, snatching a purse from an elderly woman with curly gray hair.

Mugger: GIMME YER PURSE! HAHAHA!

A voice (offscreen superhero): NOT SO FAST, CROOK!

Panel 3: A red-haired superhero in a blue and yellow costume marked "DAMN" stands heroically as a yellow blast streaks toward him.

Sound effect: BANG!

Panel 4: The bald mugger, now wounded and clutching his bleeding chest, looks at the hero in shock.

Mugger: OH MY GOD! YOU SHOT ME! BUT... BUT YOU DON'T EVEN HAVE A GUN!

Panel 5: Close-up of the smiling superhero striking a confident pose, hand near his face, cape flowing.

Panel 6: The bald mugger, slumped and bleeding, looks on.

Mugger: THAT IS SO DAMN AWESOME.
comics.voteyText:
The dying bald man (close-up of his face): How'd you get so awesome?
The hero (offscreen): Smoking

comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

Setting: a school hallway lined with blue lockers.

Blonde girl (handing over a card): HAPPY SEPTEMBER 26th!

Boy with brown hair and glasses: OH MY GOD! SHEILA MATHERS! BUT YOU'RE THE HEAD CHEERLEADER! I DIDN'T EVEN THINK YOU KNEW MY NAME! THAT'S SO - OH... RIGHT.

Caption (below panel): Sighing, Marty placed yet another card in his Hatred Day box.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of the boy's (Marty's) face, eyes downcast and resigned.
Marty: I'll show you by becoming successful, yet emotionally withdrawn!

comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A magician in a top hat and tuxedo, with a long white beard, stands on a stage with red curtains. A white dove flies up from his outstretched hand.

Panel 2 (two audience members seated, watching):

Woman (brown hair, yellow shirt): Wow! He just made that dove appear out of nowhere!

Man (orange hair, blue shirt): Psh! Everybody knows how that trick works.

Panel 3: The orange-haired man turns to a large, muscular, horned figure (Satan) seated beside him.

Man: Hey Satan - I'll give you my soul if you make a dove appear from my hands.

Panel 4: A white dove appears at the orange-haired man's hands as he gestures toward the woman.

Man: Bam!

Panel 5:

Woman (pointing): Wow, look! The magician did it again!

Man: (stares, mouth open)

Panel 6: Close on Satan, who looks puzzled.

Satan: Hey, I'm stumped too.

Bibliography:

Man: She's always making these little jokes making fun of my looks. I know she's joking, but it's really hurtful.

Counselor: Interesting... Say, does your face hurt?

Man: Uh... no... why?

Counselor: Because it's sure hurtin' me!

This question is mainly for the senator, but I'd like to get his opponent's perspective as well: If you could have a billion dollars, but for the rest of your life, your eyes would be on your butt - would you do it?"

A rugged man in a wide-brimmed hat, red shirt, and overalls stands holding an iron shovel like a weapon, addressing a young red-haired boy beside him. Behind them stand two blue-tinted figures (a woman and a man), watching.

FIG 27
