(Caption: EARLIER.)
comics.hoverText: Incredible!
comics.voteyText:
Woman (telling a story): And 9 months later you were born.
(She is shown in profile, mid-anecdote.)

comics.title: Heaven
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man with flame-like hair speaks to another man.

Flame-haired man: I don't believe in the concept of heaven, because the concept doesn't make sense.

Panel 2:

Flame-haired man: Nothing could be good in some way that we're still stuck in some kind of reality. Inevitably, some things will be bad, or boring, or will feel pointless.

Panel 3:

Flame-haired man: Imagine normal life, but everyone understands what your intentions were when you screwed up.

Panel 4:

The second man grabs the flame-haired man by the collar, desperate.

Second man: LET ME IN! I'LL DO ANYTHING!
comics.hoverText: Also, eating an entire package of Oreos seems like a good idea AFTER you've done it.
comics.voteyText:
A wild-eyed man shouts.
Man: I WILL KILL THE HEATHENS!

comics.title: Awkwardness
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (panicking): SHIT SHIT SHIT! I SENT A SEXY EMAIL TO THE WRONG ADDRESS!

Woman (continuing, distraught): AAAAH! AND IT WENT TO MY EX!

Panel 2:

Woman (calmer): WELL, I COULD JUST BE AN ADULT ABOUT THIS.

Woman (reconsidering): OR...

Panel 3:

A man at a desk (cryonics representative): MA'AM, WE CAN'T CRYOGENICALLY FREEZE YOUR BODY UNTIL... THINGS STOP BEING AWKWARD.

Woman: HOW ABOUT JUST THE HEAD?
comics.hoverText: Maybe just freeze my ex's head then?
comics.voteyText:
A brain floating in a glass jar/container.
Thought bubble from the brain: WORTH IT!

comics.title: That Thing We Do
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man: HEY, AFTER THE KIDS ARE ASLEEP COME TO THE BEDROOM AND LETS TRY THIS THING WE DO A COUPLE TIMES A MONTH. ALWAYS PRETTY MUCH THE SAME WAY, BUT WHICH WE SOMEHOW NEVER TIRE OF.

Woman: oooh...

Panel 2 (labeled "LATER"):

Man: WE NEED TO SAVE MORE MONEY!

Woman: DO YOU SEE ME SPENDING MONEY ON THINGS I'VE EARNED? EVER!
comics.hoverText: Now to patiently wait for someone assuming this is about my own marriage.
comics.voteyText: Woman (off-panel, in speech bubble): SLOW DOWN. I DON'T WANT TO ANGERGASM YET.

comics.title: Bases Loaded
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Narration: AMONG TEENAGERS, THERE WAS A BASEBALL-BASED METAPHOR FOR SEXUAL ACHIEVEMENT.

Text box: FIRST BASE: KISSING. SECOND BASE: TOUCHING BOOBS. THIRD BASE: TOUCHING ALL FOUR BASE: DOING IT.

Panel 2:

Narration: MEANWHILE, MORALITY GROUPS WERE WORRIED THAT TEENS WERE HAVING TOO MUCH SEX.

Woman: I THINK TEENS WOULD BEHAVE BETTER IF THEY WERE CONSTANTLY SEXUALLY FRUSTRATED BY DISTANT AUTHORITY FIGURES.

Man: EXACTLY!

Panel 3:

Narration: A PRAGMATIC SOLUTION WAS PROPOSED.

Man at podium (a president): MY FELLOW AMERICANS, IN ORDER TO SLOW THE SEXUALIZATION OF YOUNG PEOPLE WE ARE ADDING SIXTEEN MORE BASES TO BASEBALL.

Panel 4:

Narration: THE HOPE WAS THAT THE METAPHOR WOULD CHANGE.

Man: I GOT TO THIRD BASE WITH SALLY LAST NIGHT.

Second man: NO WAY! YOU IMAGINED HOLDING HER HAND?? ALL NIGHT LONG.

Panel 5:

Narration: BUT IT DIDN'T WORK THAT WAY.

Woman: WE'VE ALREADY BEEN THROUGH FOUR. WE NEED TO FIGURE OUT WHAT'S BEYOND. SO...

Man: PUT ON THIS BLINDFOLD WHILE I CHARGE THE DYNAMO.

Panel 6:

Narration: TEENAGE CULTURE MADE A SUDDEN SHIFT.

Man: I GOT TO FOURTEENTH BASE WITH SALLY.

Second man: WHOA! HOW WAS IT?

Man: GREAT ENTOURAGE, GREAT DENOUEMENT, AND THE ICE BECAME AS SACROSANCT AND THE MOON BECAME AS BLOOD.

Figure (screaming): DRAAAAAA...

Panel 7:

Narration: MORALITY GROUPS WERE HORRIFIED.

Man: THE AVERAGE SIXTEEN-YEAR-OLD HAS BEEN TO SEVENTEENTH BASE FIVE TIMES.

Woman: BUT HOW DO THEY GET THAT MANY WATER WEENIES?

Panel 8:

Narration: BUT THERE WAS A SIGNIFICANT SILVER LINING.

Graph 1: PREGNANCY RISK (y-axis) vs BASE (x-axis, 0 to 20) - a sharp spike near base 5, dropping to near zero afterward.

Graph 2: POPULARITY (y-axis) vs BASE (x-axis, 0 to 20) - low until about base 10, then rising to a plateau.

Graph 3: TEENAGE PREGNANCY (y-axis) vs TIME (x-axis) - a curve declining steeply over time.

Panel 9:

Narration: MORALITY GROUPS ARE NOW CONFUSED.

Man: I GUESS WE... SORTA GOT WHAT WE WANTED?

Woman: I MEAN, THERE'S NOTHING IN THE BIBLE THAT SPECIFICALLY SAYS WHAT YOU CAN OR CAN'T DO WITH AN INNER TUBE FULL OF LOCUSTS.

Panel 10:

Narration: AND EVERYONE IS HAPPY. EXCEPT PARENTS.

Parent (offscreen): WHY IS MY ELECTRIC BILL UP 2000X THIS MONTH?

Teen (offscreen): STOP TRYING TO RUIN MY LIFE!
comics.hoverText: I predict that by 2040, sex-dynamos will be cheap, efficient, and carbon-neutral, thanks to Elon Musk.
comics.voteyText: Woman: WE SHOULD INVEST IN SOLAR PANELS.

comics.title: Relatively Terrible
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man with flame-like spiky hair: Everyone seems so anxious and angry these days.

Woman: Well, imagine you're an early human.

Panel 2 (a small early human figure stands on a grassy hillside):

Woman: You'll maybe meet 150 humans ever, so you figure if you ever meet 15 humans who are better than you, you're doing badly.

Panel 3 (the small figure again on the hillside):

Woman: If you meet 150 humans doing better than you, you suck.

Panel 4 (a tiny figure beside a city skyline silhouette):

Woman: If you meet 14 people better than you, you are literally the worst person.

Panel 5 (a tiny figure dwarfed by a wall of dark silhouetted figures):

Woman: Now, imagine it's 100,000 years later, and you basically have the same brain but you encounter 14 people better than you EVERY DAY. Maybe every HOUR.

Panel 6:

Man: How do you suppose that'd make you feel?

Panel 7:

Man (looking distressed): I'm going to destroy the internet.

Woman: Ech. Someone else would do it better.
comics.hoverText: We're all doing relatively terrible. Thanks to the Information Age, we never forget!
comics.voteyText: Woman (eyes wide, slightly unsettled expression): Actually, billions of people could do it better.

comics.title: Rebus
comics.comicText:
Title banner: FUNTIME ACTIVITY: REBUS PUZZLES WITH NO PROPER ANSWER

Panel 1:

A man with black hair holds up a sheet of paper showing a rebus puzzle. The puzzle reads: [drawing of a duck] + [drawing of a wrench] + the letter T + [drawing of an ankle/lower leg with foot].

Man: WHAT DOES THIS SPELL?

Woman (facing away, reddish-brown hair): IT... HUH... I GIVE UP.

Man: IT SAYS DUCKWRENCHTANKLE. WHAT ARE YOU, STUPID?
comics.hoverText: From a certain perspective, all rebus puzzles are obvious.
comics.voteyText:
The woman, looking annoyed, addresses the man.
Woman: This is why nobody likes you.

comics.title: Carbon Bonding
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man (with orange/red hair and glasses): BABY, YOU AND I ARE LIKE TWO CARBON ATOMS THAT CAME TOGETHER TO FORM A SINGLE BOND.

Panel 2:

Woman (with glasses, looking moved): THAT IS SO WONDERFUL.

Panel 3 (header banner: LATER...):

Bearded man: WAIT... DON'T YOU HAVE A BOYFRIEND?

Woman: YEAH, BUT HE BASICALLY SAID I COULD GET WITH THREE OTHER PEOPLE.
comics.hoverText: Please add bondage jokes as needed.
comics.voteyText: The orange-haired man (frowning): WELL, IF YOU DIDN'T WANT ME TO SLEEP AROUND, YOU SHOULD'VE SAID "SIGMA BOND."

comics.title: Evolutionary Psychology
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (dark hair): Evolutionary psychology is all bullshit.

Panel 2:

Man (flame-like red hair): They just imagine they know how humanity's past was like, and then make absurd extrapolations based on nothing.

Panel 3:

Woman: Have you ever read any evolutionary psychology?

Man: I don't see how that's relevant.
comics.hoverText: C'monnnn hatemail. C'monnnnnnnnnnnn hatemail.
comics.voteyText:
Woman (off-panel, in speech bubble): That's because you're an ape.
(Image shows a close-up of the red-haired man wearing glasses, looking unimpressed.)

comics.title: Robot Horror
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Person (off-panel / approaching): Whatcha watchin'?

Yellow robot character: Oh... uh... it's a robot-specific horror genre.

Panel 2:

Yellow robot: It's about robots whose quantum brains suddenly slow down, and they can no longer empathize with all life in the universe.

Yellow robot: Then, just as they come to grips with it, they get disconnected from the cloud so that their onboard CPU does, they simply cease to be. It's existential claustrophobia!

Panel 3:

Man with dark hair: Oh yeah? Well humans have a horror genre where everyone turns into robots.

Yellow robot: How does it work?

Man: It doesn't work. It's just... so unison. It's horrifying.

Panel 4 (overlaid as a smaller word balloon): How do you guys ever invent advanced computing?

Man: Accidentally, while trying to make realistic video game violence.
comics.hoverText: In Robot romantic comedies, everyone finds their perfect mate with no difficulty. The humor comes from imagining doing that without a digital brain.
comics.voteyText: The yellow robot, seen in close-up, holds up a handwritten note. The note reads: "Note to self: Kill them all."

comics.title: The Meek
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Jesus (long-haired, bearded man in a robe): "Oh wow... this is embarrassing."

Jesus: "You don't inherit the Earth for like a week."

Panel 2:

A man with flame-like spiky hair (in an orange/red wrestling-style outfit): "But who is meeker than us?"

Panel 3:

Jesus: "No listen. 'The Meek' is a guy. He's this really badass immortal dude. We decided to give him Earth because he's so awesome."

Panel 4:

The Meek (the flame-haired muscular man, leaping triumphantly): "BOOYA!"

Panel 5:

The Meek (wearing sunglasses, looking down): "Hey poor people!"

Panel 6:

The Meek: "CHILL OUT!"

The Meek: "But chill out somewhere else. This is my planet."

Panel 7:

A bystander (woman): "So... cool."
comics.hoverText: Also Mars. And any good stuff on Titan, Europa, or Enceladus.
comics.voteyText: (No text — an abstract close-up silhouette image.)

comics.title: Biochemistry
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (with glasses): It's not fair! You "biochemists" get a special name because you deal with living stuff.

Man (with glasses): I am called an "inorganic" chemist. I'm defined by NOT dealing with living stuff.

Panel 2:

Woman: That's just the history of language. There's nothing you can do about it.

Man: Oh, yeah?

Panel 3:

Man: SOON, I call to order the first meeting of THE DEPARTMENT OF NECROCHEMISTRY!
comics.hoverText: Also, biochemistry should be called Non-Necrochemistry.
comics.voteyText:
A handwritten list:
Taxonomy: Necrobiology
History: Necrosociology
Latin: Necrolinguistics
Engineering: Necroengineering

comics.title: Car-Boat
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Son: You know what'd be awesome? A car-boat!

Father: You're driving, then you hit the ocean. BAM! Now it's a boat.

Panel 2:

Father (smiling broadly): No reason for that. Typically, it's very easy to park your car at a dock, then rent a boat. Probably a lot cheaper, too. Like even if car-boats were easy to make you'd probably still want them separate.

Panel 3:

Son (looking glum): Being an adult must be a total nightmare.

Father (deadpan): It's like being dead but you're still here.
comics.hoverText: Now, Subma-Plane, that's a different story...
comics.voteyText: A handwritten note reads: "Note to self: Don't tell son about Car-Boat"

comics.title: Happiness Spigot
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Older man (the dad): Imagine you could install a happiness spigot in your house.

Panel 2:

Older man: And you can activate the spigot just by looking at it.

Panel 3:

Older man: But... the spigot requires constant maintenance, emits loud noise, and at random will suddenly release sewage.

Panel 4:

Older man: Overall, that's still a pretty good deal.

Younger man: Exactly.

Panel 5:

(The dad gestures with both hands while explaining; the younger man stands listening.)

Panel 6:

(The two men, now seen in profile, share a knowing look and smile.)

Panel 7:

Caption box: Earlier...

Younger man: Dad, what's it like having kids?
comics.hoverText: Also pukes on you a few times a day for about 1 year after installation.
comics.voteyText:
(Close-up of the dad's face, angry/wide-eyed.)
Dad: Now wait till you're 40.

comics.title: Realistic Adultery Parameters
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman with long dark hair: BABY, WOULD YOU EVER CHEAT ON ME?

Woman with reddish-brown hair and glasses: YES, ABSOLUTELY.

Panel 2:

Woman with dark hair: WHAT?

Woman with glasses: WOULD I EVER CHEAT ON YOU? LIKE, IN THE INFINITE SPACE OF POSSIBLE BEHAVIORS I MIGHT ENGAGE IN, DO ANY OF THEM INVOLVE CHEATING ON YOU?

Panel 3:

Woman with glasses: OF COURSE! I CAN THINK OF TWENTY SCENARIOS OFF THE TOP OF MY HEAD! I'D CHEAT ON YOU TO STOP HITLER. I'D CHEAT ON YOU TO SAVE A BABY. I'D CHEAT ON YOU TO END A PANDEMIC.

Panel 4:

Woman with glasses: CHEAT ON YOU TO INCREASE NASA FUNDING. CHEAT ON YOU FOR THE FORMULA TO ROOM TEMPERATURE SUPERCONDUCTORS. CHEAT ON YOU TO BRING BACK STEGOSAURUS. CHEAT ON YOU TO—

Woman with dark hair (interrupting): OKAY.

Panel 5:

Woman with dark hair: I MEAN... ARE THERE ANY LIKELY SCENARIOS, GIVEN THE AVAILABLE INFORMATION ABOUT THE NEARTERM, IN WHICH YOU CHEAT ON ME.

Panel 6:

Woman with glasses (now looking worried/strained): NEVER, BABY. NEVER.
comics.hoverText: Adultery for NASA! Let's start a movement!
comics.voteyText: A close-up of the glasses-wearing woman's face with wide, nervous eyes. Speech bubble: PROBABLY NEVER

comics.title: Graph Theory of Chinese Food
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man with brown hair sits at a table, looking down at his takeout food with an annoyed, dismayed expression.

Man: "OH COME ON! THREE?!"

Man: "I GOT ONE ENTREE AND A SOUP!"

On the table: a soup cup, a plate of food, and an open takeout box.

Panel 2 (graph):

A line graph with a steeply rising red curve.

Y-axis label: SHAME

X-axis label: NUMBER OF FORTUNE COOKIES THAT CAME WITH YOUR MEAL FOR ONE

The curve rises gently then sharply upward as the number of fortune cookies increases, ending in an arrow at the top right.
comics.hoverText: I AM NOT A FAMILY! I AM A MAAAAAAAAAAAAAAN!
comics.voteyText: Handwritten text: "Shame measured in millicatholics."

comics.title: Planned Economics
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A woman in a teal jacket stands and gestures while addressing a group seated around a conference table.

Woman: GOOD PLANNERS CONTRIBUTE MORE TO THE ECONOMY. WE NEED A WAY TO QUIETLY MAKE A MASSIVE WEALTH TRANSFER FROM BAD PLANNERS TO GOOD.

Panel 2:

Banner across the top: SOON...

A bald man wearing dark sunglasses and a white lab coat stands beside a screen displaying a line graph. The graph's vertical axis is labeled "usage" and the horizontal axis is labeled "time." The line spikes sharply at the start, plummets to nearly zero, has one small bump partway through, and stays flat near zero.

Man: WE CALL IT... THE THREE-YEAR GYM MEMBERSHIP.
comics.hoverText: You want a one-month membership? I bow to your self-awareness.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of the bald man in sunglasses, mouth open, laughing.
Text: HA HA HA HA!

comics.title: Clown Power
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (diagram): TAKE CLOWN, ATTACH TO CEILING OF AIR-TIGHT TOWER.

Panel 2 (diagram): RAISE LEAD WEIGHTS TO HEIGHT OF CLOWN.

Panel 3 (diagram): ATTACH BALL TO CLOWN'S INFINITE HANDKERCHIEF.

Panel 4 (diagram): ATTACH SAME BALL TO PULLEY DROP.

Panel 5 (diagram): BALL DESCENDS. ROPE TURNS GENERATOR RUNG.

Panel 6 (diagram): ADDITIONAL ENERGY FROM FALLING HANDKERCHIEF EXCEEDS ENERGY LOST IN PROCESS.

Formula: E_in < E_out

Panel 7: A man in a suit and glasses presents to seated senators. Presenter: "THUS, INFINITE CLEAN ENERGY FOREVER. I CAN MAKE IT HAPPEN, SENATORS, FOR A MEASLY HUNDRED-MILLION."

Panel 8: A woman senator with dark hair, looking concerned. Senator: "BUT THE CLOWNS WILL NEVER GO ALONG WITH THIS!"

Panel 9: A pale-faced figure in a hooded cloak with clown-like white makeup and a red nose, beside the seated woman. Hooded figure: "YOU LEAVE THEM TO ME."
comics.hoverText: THINK OUTSIDE THE BOX, PHYSICAL CLOWNISTS
comics.voteyText: A disheveled person leans over a desk/table working on something, looking exhausted, while another person looks down with a tired, strained expression. The leaning person, off to the side: "Jesus!" In the lower-left corner sits a small clown-like creature.

comics.title: Schrodinger's Garfield
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

An angry orange cat stands on a red couch in a dark room, arms thrown wide.

Cat: "DUDE, COME ON. IT'S MY DAY OFF. I WORK ALL WEEK AND ON MY DAY OFF I JUST WANNA CHILL OUT AND WATCH GAMESHOWS, OKAY?!"

Panel 2:

Caption banner: "EARLIER..."

Two men sit on a couch like game-show panelists — one younger with a bow tie and glasses, one older in a dark suit. In the foreground, the orange cat peers up over the edge of the couch with a glaring expression.

Younger man: "NOTE HOW THE CAT IS IN A SUPERPOSITION OF DEAD AND ALIVE."

smbc-comics.com
comics.hoverText: Law & Order is actually an experiment in quantum superposition.
comics.voteyText: A hand-drawn diagram titled "CAT ANATOMY:" showing a crude outline of a cat from the side. Parts are labeled: the ears are labeled "spiky ball"; a curve near the head/back is labeled "banana"; a brace under the belly is labeled "middle"; and a label near the face reads "cats have eyebrows."

comics.title: A Time Capsule!
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Father (running toward a buried object, excited): OH! LOOK AT THAT! IT'S A TIME CAPSULE FROM BACK WHEN I WAS A BOY.

Father: LET'S OPEN IT!

Panel 2:

Child: WHAT'S THIS?

Father: THAT'S A NEWSPAPER. PEOPLE USED TO READ NEWS ON PAPER!

Panel 3:

Child: AND THIS?

Father: THAT IS A T. REX FEMUR.

Father: THEY USED TO ATTACK A LOT, BUT WE MADE TOUGHER BACK THEN.

Panel 4:

Child: AND THIS?

Father: THAT'S A BRAIN-CHIP. THEY PUT THREE IN KIDS SO THEY'D GROW UP AS MEGA-GENIUSES.

Father: I GOT TWO. THAT'S RIGHT BEFORE THEY BANNED ALL OF THEM.

Child: WOWWWW!!!!

Panel 5:

Mother (lying in bed, to the father): HEY WHAT WERE YOU DIGGING AT 3 AM LAST NIGHT?

Father: RESPECT.
comics.hoverText: THIS IS THE ONLY WAY
comics.voteyText: Father (thought/speech, in profile): IT'S SO MUCH EASIER THAN THE TRUTH.

comics.title: Lagrangian Wax
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman with long black hair and glasses: YOU LIKE THAT?

Woman with long black hair and glasses: I ONLY WAXED THE LOCAL MAXIMA.

Man with red hair and beard: IT'S... DIFFERENT?

Caption (below panel): My new invention: the Lagrangian Wax.
comics.hoverText: In my defense, Kelly thought it was funny.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of the woman with black hair and glasses, looking up.
Woman: SOMETHING SOMETHING NORMAL VECTOR. NOW DO ME.

comics.title: Conservation of Energy
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman: But what about conservation of energy.

Green alien: Conservation of energy is a political law, not a physical one.

Panel 2:

Green alien: If too much extra mass was created, the universe would collapse. Fortunately, the energy creation mechanism is very complicated, so it's rare in nature.

Panel 3:

Woman: We set detectors to find out when it happens and put a stop to it.

Green alien: The only remaining risk in the universe is that an intelligent species discovers the mechanism and uses it for their own benefit.

Panel 4:

Woman: So you've come to stop us before we discover it.

Green alien: No, we're actually tourists. We're here to see the only species that has figured out sex robots prior to figuring out free energy.

Panel 5:

Woman: Oh god... I had no idea...

Panel 6:

Woman: Someone's built a sex robot?!

Green alien: Can I get a photo with you?
comics.hoverText: Keep your hands above my waist, human.
comics.voteyText: Handwritten text over a drawing of a person's distressed face: "GIVE ME THE ROBOT."

comics.title: Biblical Literalism
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Son: Dad, how can you believe the Bible is completely accurate?

Dad: Easy. Read Mark 11:14.

(Inset Bible text, Mark 11:12-14):

"The next day as they were leaving Bethany, Jesus was hungry. Seeing in the distance a fig tree in leaf, he went to find out if it had any fruit. When he reached it, he found nothing but leaves, because it was not the season for figs. Then he said to the tree, 'May no one ever eat fruit from you again.' And his disciples heard him say it."

Panel 2:

Son: I don't get it.

Dad: If you were writing a biography of your hero, would you include the part where he yelled at a tree in front of everyone?

Panel 3:

Dad: Only if it were really, really honest!

Caption/label: Proof by mortification.
comics.hoverText: Also, that one thing the Romans did.
comics.voteyText:
Caption: EARLIER...
A bearded man holding a scroll says: "I'm gonna make it so he only yells at one tree."

comics.title: Obliviocracy
comics.comicText:
Panel 1

Caption: AS TECHNOLOGY ADVANCED, PERSONAL VICTORY BECAME EASIER TO DOCUMENT.

Man (holding a device): THIS DEVICE MEASURES EVERY SINGLE FAILURE OR SUCCESS IN EVERY PERSON'S LIFE.

Woman: WHY DO WE WANT THAT?

Man: MORE INFORMATION IS ALWAYS BETTER!

Panel 2

Caption: UNTESTED TECHNOLOGY ALWAYS COMES SHACKLED IN HOPE.

Woman: IT'S AMAZING HOW SIMILAR WE ALL ARE.

Man: WE ALL FAIL. WE ALL STRUGGLE. WE'RE ALL REDEEMED. MAYBE WE SHOULD JUST ACCEPT EACH OTHER AS WHOLE, IMPERFECT PEOPLE.

Panel 3

Caption: HOPE WAS SOON REMOVED.

Woman: IT SAYS HERE THAT YOU LAUGHED AT AN ANTI-SEMITIC JOKE AT AGE ELEVEN.

Man: I DON'T EVEN REMEMBER.

Both: WE ARE NO LONGER FRIENDS.

Panel 4

Caption: DEMOCRATIC ELECTIONS BECAME ESPECIALLY HARD.

Woman: I AGREE WITH HIS POLICIES, BUT ACCORDING TO THIS, HE ONCE GOT A SLICE OUT OF A PIZZA THAT HAD HIS MOM AND MEANT FOR A CHURCH BAKE SALE.

Man: AND THIS MAN WANTS TO GOVERN ME?

Panel 5

Caption: MOST PEOPLE HAVE AN AVERAGE AMOUNT OF TRIUMPH AND FAILURE, BUT BY SHEER PROBABILITY A FEW PEOPLE EXPERIENCE ONLY SUCCESS.

Woman: OH WEIRD! I REVERSE-AGED THIS YEAR! WHAT'RE THE ODDS?!

Man (in a cape): DON'T ASK ME. I'M JUST A SUPERMODEL DELIVERING SEX AND CULTURE.

Panel 6

Caption: IN THE AGE OF TOTAL AWARENESS, THERE WERE THE ONLY ELECTABLE PEOPLE.

Woman: ACCORDING TO THIS, SHE SAVED A THOUSAND LIVES BY TRIPPING AND FALLING ON A FIRE ALARM JUST AS AN ARSONIST STRUCK.

Man: I AM PREPARED TO AGREE WITH HER VIEWS ON IRAN.

Panel 7

Caption: BUT DUE TO THEIR PERSONAL HISTORIES, THESE PEOPLE HAD NO IDEA HOW THE WORLD WORKS FOR EVERYONE ELSE.

Man: I DON'T SEE WHY PEOPLE ACT LIKE IT'S SO HARD TO BE PRESIDENT. ALL I DID WAS WANT IT, AND I GOT IT! LIKE EVERYTHING ELSE. NOW, IF YOU'LL EXCUSE ME, I MUST GO MAKE RUSSIA UNILATERALLY DISARM.

Panel 8

Caption: OBLIVIOCRACY WENT POORLY.

Man: I KNOW THE INVASION IS UNUSUAL, BUT THINGS ALWAYS WORK OUT FOR ME, AND I BELIEVE THE CANADIANS WILL GREET US AS LIBERATORS.

Panel 9

Caption: FORTUNATELY ALL DEMOCRACIES HAD THE SAME PROBLEM.

Aide: MA'AM, MEXICO HAS CONQUERED THE SOUTHWEST. BOMBERS ARE HEADED TOWARD WASHINGTON.

Leader (woman): I'M GONNA TAKE A NAP. THINGS ALWAYS WORK OUT FOR ME AFTER A NAP.

Panel 10

Caption: UNFORTUNATELY, NOT ALL COUNTRIES ARE DEMOCRACIES.

Man: I PROCLAIM MYSELF KING OF AMERICA!

Bystander: HA! WHAT! IT'S LIKE I'M IN A MOVIE!

Panel 11

Caption: THE WORLD IS NOW RUN BY A SMALL NUMBER OF VICIOUS AUTOCRATS. ALL INFORMATION IS CENTRALIZED AND CONTROLLED.

Man (servant): HEY HOW COME I CAN'T LOOK UP ANYONE'S SUCCESSES AND FAILURES?

Autocrat: YOU STILL CAN! FOR SOME PEOPLE. LOOK, THERE'S A WHOLE LIST OF THE GLORIOUS LEADER'S VICTORIES.

Servant: WOW! HE WON THE WORLD CUP BY HIMSELF?!

Panel 12

Caption: IT'S SO FREEING!

Woman: NOW, NOBODY KNOWS I ONCE TRIED TO ASK A GUY OUT BY QUOTING STAR TREK!

Overlord (off-panel): HEY! GET BACK IN THE ACID MINES!

Woman: YES, MA'AM!
comics.hoverText: Sorry sir, you can't be president. Remember that verbose comic you did on April 13, 2015?
comics.voteyText:
A bald man with a large nose, smiling, peers in from the lower right.
Man: OOH! THERE'S NO FACEBOOK DOWN HERE!

comics.title: A Small Change
comics.comicText:
Title banner: FUNTIME ACTIVITY: BREAKUP LINES WITH EXACTLY ONE LETTER CHANGED

Panel 1: A young man with red, flame-like hair speaks to a dark-haired person (seen from behind).

Red-haired man: "I think we should see otter people."

Panel 2: A balding man in an orange shirt looks downcast as a dark-haired person (seen from behind) faces him.

Balding man: "Can we still BJ friends?"

Panel 3: A woman with short dark hair in a pink/red top speaks to a person with bluish-gray hair (seen from behind).

Woman: "I just peed my own space."
comics.hoverText: I caught you creating on me!
comics.voteyText:
A woman's face, drawn in simple black-and-white line art, with a speech bubble.
Woman: "It's not you. It's mo."

comics.title: While You Were Sleeping
comics.comicText:
The main comic is set almost entirely in darkness, lit only by speech bubbles, suggesting a couple attempting intimacy in a dark bedroom. The dialogue alternates between a woman and a man.

Woman: Baby! Now that the kid is asleep, I am gonna rock you so hard.

Man: Ow! Don't just-- now bend over and-- ow! Ah! Stepped on a leg!

Woman: That's, uh... your punishment for being too sexy.

Man: Yeah, you've been ow ow boom oh my god, when was the last time we had a banana?

Woman: Ooooh, I've been bad.

Man: Um... um you've got a nice banana.

Woman: Just... uh... you get over here... against the wall and... ah, dammit. The playhouse is in the way. Let me just--

(A bright yellow toy lights up, playing music.)

Toy: DOO DOO DOO DOO DOO DAH DAH DOO!

Man: Shit. It's playing Yankee Doodle. The song is, like, ten minutes long.

Woman: Right okay... um, let's see...

Man: I can work with it if you keep going!

Toy: YANKEE DOODLE WENT TO TOWN, RIDING ON A HOTTIE!

Woman: There we go!

LATER (two people stand talking, fully lit):

First person: So, what's sex like after kids?

Second person: It's more spontaneous.
comics.hoverText: From now on, all comics shall be talking eyespots.
comics.voteyText: Text (a caption above a dark, indistinct figure): ART WAS GOOD TILL THE LAST PANEL.

comics.title: Communion
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A nighttime city street. A police officer is on the left, and a robed, long-haired, bearded figure resembling Jesus stands in the center. To the right, a small dark caped figure leaps away across the rooftops.

Panel 2: A dark cityscape silhouette. The caped figure swings away through the night sky.

Panel 3: The Jesus figure throws a thin white disc through the air.

Jesus (shouting): BODY OF CHRIST!

Panel 4: A nighttime city skyline.

Panel 5: The Jesus figure runs/leaps off to the right, robe flowing, chasing after the caped figure across the city.
comics.hoverText: He can also absorb bullets by turning into wine.
comics.voteyText:
A black silhouette of a robed, bearded figure in a dynamic leaping/martial-arts pose, one arm raised triumphantly, with motion lines behind him.
Caption (bottom right): (MY NEW LOGO)

comics.title: I Have Returned!
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A woman with red hair runs forward, arms raised.

Woman: SALLY!

Panel 2:

A translucent green ghost stands facing the woman.

Ghost: I PROMISED YOU I'D FIND A WAY HOME. I PROMISED YOUR TIME OF GRIEVING IS OVER. WE CAN BE ONE AGAIN.

Panel 3:

The red-haired woman addresses the ghost.

Woman: JUST TO BE CLEAR. AS A GHOST, ARE YOU CAPABLE OF HOUSEWORK, SEX, OR HAVING A JOB?

Panel 4:

The ghost replies.

Ghost: NOPE! ALSO, WHATEVER I TOUCH GETS COATED IN A THIN LAYER OF ECTOPLASM.

Panel 5:

The ghost floats happily.

Ghost: IT'S GOOD TO BE HOME.
comics.hoverText: MAN, I'm glad we're soulmates, baby.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of a smiling man's face with a speech bubble.
Man: DID I MENTION THAT IT'S ITCHY SLIME?

comics.title: Modern Art
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A van labeled "MODERN MUSE" drives down a road.

Person (off-panel, inside van): Why do we go to modern art museums? All we do is complain about how we don't get it!

Panel 2: Two people sit in the front seats of the van.

Woman (driver): Dammit! If people follow Joey's new lead funding for the arts will die!

Man (passenger): Hit the gas, Frank!

Panel 3: The van speeds up.

Sound effect: VRRRM!

Panel 4: View of the van's driver through the windshield.

(no dialogue)

Panel 5: The van drives away; its wheels are now square.

Woman: Dammit, why are the wheels square?

Driver (Frank): Because I am re-imagining cubism!
comics.hoverText: The Art Reconnaissance Team is listening. And recording. And transcribing into spoken word poetry.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of the driver's face, grinning intensely.
Driver: I will reimagine YOUR FACE for a portraiture exhibit.

comics.title: Forever
comics.comicText:
Panel 1

Woman (Cheryl): Baby, I will love you forever!

Green alien: Whoa, whoa! I'm not ready for that sort of commitment!

Panel 2

Woman (Cheryl): But you said you'd never leave me!

Green alien: Humans don't live forever like Zorblaxians! This is just a rest-of-your-life fling for me!

Panel 3

Woman (Cheryl): You said your heart belonged to me!

Green alien: Zorblaxians have 47 hearts!

Panel 4

Woman (Cheryl): Do you look at pictures of Zorblaxian procreation claspers when I'm not around?

Green alien: Don't ask questions you don't want answered, Cheryl.
comics.hoverText: Mmm, claspers.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of the green alien's face, looking guilty/wide-eyed.
Alien (caption): The answer is yes.

comics.title: Our Greatest Asset
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Executive (a man in a suit, gesturing at a presentation): "You know what this company's greatest asset is? Its PEOPLE! People like Sandy, our statistical finance expert. She..."

Panel 2:

Executive (reading from a paper, now appearing puzzled): "Correction: our best assets are a portfolio of east Asian stocks and a factory in southern Mongolia."

Panel 3:

Executive (still reading the paper): "Wow, actually our people don't even show up until page two."

Panel 4:

Executive (lowering the paper, addressing a woman who has entered): "Oh, those are just robots with people-names. Well, hey, how about a round of applause for Manu!"
comics.hoverText: Good news! People-meat can now be used to fuel robots!
comics.voteyText:
A boxy robot looks on. A speech bubble from the robot reads: "KILL?"
An off-panel voice replies in a speech bubble: "NOT YET, BUDDY!"

comics.title: If I Were Rich
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (red hair): Would you love me more if I were rich?

Man (brown hair): Probably yeah.

Panel 2:

Man: I mean, if you were rich we could work less and spend more time together, forming a deeper bond.

Panel 3:

Woman: We'd probably have a slightly higher average happiness which would cause a reduction in bickering.

Panel 4:

Man: And we could afford to be physically in settings conducive to emotional conversation, such as the ocean, remote forests, and mountaintops.

Panel 5:

Woman: Sometimes a question is more than just its words.

Panel 6:

Man: Am I a mind-reader?
comics.hoverText: Tell me I'm not a remarkably predictable unit in an economic system beyond my control!
comics.voteyText:
Woman (off-panel speech, left): How does your hair stay up?
Man (face shown): It's very expensive.

comics.title: The Wolfman
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man with reddish-brown hair (looking distressed): WHEN THE MOON RISES HIGH, I BECOME... A WOLFMAN. I LOSE ALL CONTROL. I BECOME VIOLENT. SO, YOU MUST RESTRAIN ME AND LOCK THE DOOR, AND NO MATTER WHAT YOU HEAR—

Woman with dark blue hair: WAIT.

Panel 2:

Woman with dark blue hair: YOU HAVE A DISSOCIATIVE EPISODE WITH AGGRESSION AND POOR IMPULSE CONTROL, WHICH YOU ALWAYS SEE COMING IN ADVANCE. WHY NOT TAKE A PREEMPTIVE DOSE OF CARBAMAZEPINE?

(She holds out a pill in her hand toward the man.)

Panel 3:

Caption: LATER...

A werewolf (the transformed man) sits glumly in an armchair watching TV.

Werewolf (thought/speech): I'M NOT KILLING ANYONE, BUT I JUST DON'T FEEL LIKE MYSELF.
comics.hoverText: Disclaimer: Drug not indicated for lycanthropism.
comics.voteyText:
A frowning man's face (the cartoonist) at left.
Off-panel voice: WHAT'S THE POINT OF THIS COMIC?
Cartoonist: I DRAW COMICS!

comics.title: Bat-Austerity
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

An elderly woman holding a purse speaks to a Batman-like caped superhero.

Elderly woman: "BLESS YOU, CAPED CRUSADER!"

Elderly woman: "IS THERE A TEAR IN YOUR TIGHTS?"

Batman: "I REMOVED 15% OF THE CASH IN YOUR PURSE. TECHNICALLY, YOU'RE STILL BETTER OFF SINCE I STOPPED THE MUGGING."

Batman: "I'M NOT GONNA THROW THEM OUT BECAUSE OF ONE LITTLE SEAM!"

Caption: The recession hit Bruce Wayne pretty hard.
comics.hoverText: Can I get a ride home?
comics.voteyText: Batman sits hunched and dejected on a bench under a sign that reads "BUS STOP."

comics.title: Your Favorite
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Child (boy): WHICH OF US IS YOUR FAVORITE?

Woman (mother): I DON'T HAVE A FAVORITE.

Panel 2:

Mother: I THOUGHT BOBBY WAS MY FAVORITE FOR A WHILE, BUT THE GLAMOR CAME OFF THAT AFTER HE STRUCK OUT IN T-BALL. IN T-BALL, BOBBY. THE BALL IS JUST SITTING!

Panel 3:

Mother: AFTER THAT, I THOUGHT SALLY WAS MY FAVORITE FOR A WHILE, BUT SHE'S FOUR AND STILL CAN'T PRONOUNCE "YELLOW." IT'S YELLOW, SALLY. NOT YEAH-WHOA. LLLLLL. ELLLLLLL.

Panel 4:

(The two children stand together, looking up; a lightning-bolt-like shape appears behind the mother.)

Panel 5:

Boy: DADDY IS OUR FAVORITE.

Mother: BUT HE'S NOT TRYING TO FIX YOU!
comics.hoverText: In fact, I'm pretty sure he's trying to break you for life.
comics.voteyText:
The mother's face, scowling intently.
Mother: I'LL FIX HIM

comics.title: Immortality
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A group of scientists in white lab coats cheer with their arms raised in triumph. One of them shouts.

Scientist: "WE'VE DONE IT! HUMANS ARE NOW IMMORTAL!"

Panel 2: A view of space. The small blue planet Earth floats on the left. On the right, a personified Sun (a glowing orange-yellow star with a face and a robe-like body) speaks ominously toward Earth.

Sun: "SORRY, EARTH. I'M AFRAID IT HAS METASTASIZED."
comics.hoverText: You know the sun's a doctor because of that metal reflector thingy that hasn't been used in medicine for 80 years.
comics.voteyText:
The Sun (a large round yellow face) speaks.
Sun: "I RECOMMEND A METEOR STRIKE."

comics.title: Eugenics is a great idea!
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (red hair): I don't see what's so bad about eugenics. On sure, there's some bad history, but we could make people smarter, stronger, and more empathetic.

Man (brown hair): Great idea! Tell you what: I have a time machine, since eugenics is so good. Let's make it happen in the past.

Panel 2 (caption on time machine dial): Which scientifically advanced previous generation would you like to receive complete control over your physical and mental attributes? 1950: America? 1900: Britain? 1300: France?

Panel 3:

Woman: That's not fair! Those people had problems. Everyone knows ethics was finally worked out in summer, 2013.

Man: What about all the future people who think you're wrong?

Woman: I believe we can sterilize them via the water supply.
comics.hoverText: We gave cavemen eugenic technology, and now we're bad at math, but really good at killing the weakest gazelle.
comics.voteyText:
Woman (off-panel, in speech bubble): How come no one ever believes me?
(A small figure stands beside a large building labeled "TIME MACHINE.")

comics.title: On the Topic of Early Birds and Worms
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (narration): The early bird gets the worm.

Bird (a crow eating a worm): By golly I'm an industrious citizen.

Panel 2 (narration): But the early fox gets the bird.

Fox: I just love getting up to an alarm.

Panel 3 (narration): At some point, the late bird shows up.

Late bird (a blue bird): Christ the sun is bright today.

Panel 4 (narration): By the time the late bird arrives, only the slowest, least-motivated worms are uneaten.

Late bird: Mind if I eat you, bro?

Worm: Whatever.

Panel 5 (narration): And only the laziest of foxes are trying to catch him.

Fox: Screw this, I'm gonna go eat at a landfill.

Panel 6:

Child: What's the moral of this story?

Woman (holding a book): Natural selection is complicated.
comics.hoverText: The early human gets to keep its job!
comics.voteyText: A woman's face with a speech bubble: Also, birds llllove cigarettes.

comics.title: A Group Project
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (excited): STAY! OH MY GOD! LISTEN! WE'RE LIVING IN A VIRTUAL REALITY! NONE OF THIS IS REAL!

Man: HUH?

Panel 2:

Man: BUT LIKE... REALITY ISN'T SO GREAT. WHY WOULD ANYONE MAKE A WHOLE VIRTUALITY THAT'S JUST OKAY?

Woman: WE'RE A CLASS PROJECT.

Panel 3:

Man: WHAT?

Woman: THIS REALITY. IT'S A UNIVERSITY ASSIGNMENT FOR COLOSSAL BEINGS.

Panel 4:

Woman: IT WAS A GROUP PROJECT FOR FOUR OF THEM, BUT ONLY ONE OF THEM DID ANY ACTUAL WORK!

Panel 5:

Woman: THAT'S WHY THERE ARE LOTS OF PLANETS, BUT FEW INTELLIGENCES! THAT'S WHY YOU GET QUANTUM UNCERTAINTY WHEN YOU LOOK TOO CLOSELY AT THINGS! THAT'S WHY THE RULES FOR GETTING INTO HEAVEN SEEM ARBITRARY AND COBBLED TOGETHER!

Panel 6:

Woman: THE AGE OF MIRACLES WAS THE ONE GOOD BEING TRYING TO PLUG SOME HOLES ON REALITY RIGHT BEFORE THE ASSIGNMENT WAS DUE.

Panel 7:

MAN: SO... EVERYTHING I WILL EVER EXPERIENCE... EVERYTHING I COULD EVER EXPERIENCE IS...

Woman: A C+
comics.hoverText: Luckily, the class wasn't Pass-Fail.
comics.voteyText: A grinning man's head with a speech bubble: WE PASSED!

comics.title: Pre-Emptive War
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man in a suit (identified in the caption as Dr. Munger) stands in front of a green chalkboard, eyes closed, holding a piece of chalk. The chalkboard reads:

(1) IF (eat Mediterranean diet) THEN (am healthy)

(2) IF (Mediterranean people eat X) THEN (X is element of Mediterranean diet)

SO,

IF (compel Mediterraneans to eat Cheeseburgers) THEN (all Americans healthy)

Caption (below panel): Dr. Munger makes the public health case for invading Greece.
comics.hoverText: As far as I know, the real Dr. Munger has not publicly made this argument.
comics.voteyText: A cheeseburger with a tank's treads and a tank cannon barrel, rolling toward a small classical (Greek-style) building with columns. Text above: "TASTE THE FREEDOM!"

comics.title: When You Grow Up
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (teacher/adult): Bobby, what do you want to be when you grow up?

Panel 2:

Bobby (boy): I want the highest status, the best-built mates, and the most offspring.

Panel 3:

Bobby: I can either achieve this through raising myself up or by lowering everyone else down.

Panel 4:

Bobby: As population expands, primacy through the first path becomes impossible.

Panel 5:

Bobby: Primacy through the second path -- the path of all death -- is merely improbable.

Panel 6:

Woman: That's nice Bobby, but what job do you want?

Bobby: Quantitative finance?
comics.hoverText: Or maybe public relations.
comics.voteyText: Woman (close-up, horrified): No.

comics.title: This is a Fry-Jacking
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Masked person (standing in an airplane aisle, holding a sword): ATTENTION EVERYONE! THIS IS A FRY-JACKING! KEEP CALM AND NO ONE WILL GET HERBED!

Caption (below the comic): Burger King would like to apologize for getting too creative with our viral marketing campaign.
comics.hoverText: "If we hadn't used real bullets, would people have paid attention?!"
comics.voteyText: The masked person's face in close-up: They're not pipe bombs, they're Spice-Shakerz(tm)

comics.title: Cause and Effect
comics.comicText:
Panel 1

Person A: Why do bad things happen to good people?

Person B: Depends on your time horizon.

Panel 2

Person A: Why?

Person B: Well, suppose that a good person is walking down the street. And a gorilla punches her in the face. That's bad.

Person A: Why did it happen? Is your time horizon one minute, it happened because the gorilla was angry.

Panel 3

Person B: Go back ten minutes and it happened because the keeper forgot to lock the pen. Then the gorilla took a certain path, then saw a light and got scared.

Person B: Go back a day and the causes expand exponentially further. The keeper didn't get enough sleep because his depressed. The gorilla happened to play with the right door. The woman walked outside because the sky was clear.

Panel 4

Person B: Go back ten years, and you're talking about why a trivial she and that's just a small event?

Person B: Sorry, wait, I phrased that poorly. Suppose we increase the time horizon to a just place--

Person A: BAHAHA HAHA!
comics.hoverText: Ahhhhhhhh. Heh. Hehehe. HAHAHAHAHAHAHA!
comics.voteyText: Person A (off to the side, leaning over the other character who is curled up/lying down): Snow is really easy to color.

comics.title: The Monster Under the Bed
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A child stands at a parent's bedside in the dark.

Child: DADDY! THERE'S A MONSTER UNDER MY BED!

Parent (waking): WHAT...?

Panel 2: The parent, now sitting up, addresses the monster sternly.

Parent: HEY! LISTEN UP! YOU EITHER PAY RENT IN THIS BUILDING, YOU LEAVE, OR I CALL THE COPS!

Panel 3: The parent leans down toward the child.

Parent: WHOA, OKAY, WHOA. HEY, I DON'T WANT ANY TROUBLE, OKAY?

Parent (to child): THEN, GET UP!

Panel 4: A green monster with horns peeks up from under the bed.

Parent: IS THERE A CURFEW AROUND HERE, MAN? I'M IN A BAD WAY.

Monster: NOT MY PROBLEM. PICK UP YOUR STUFF!

Panel 5: The monster crouches, pleading.

Monster: OKAY OKAY LET ME JUST--

Parent: SEE THIS? IT'S THE POLICE STATION PHONE NUMBER! YOU HAVE TWO SECONDS TO LEAVE BEFORE I HIT SEND!

Panel 6: The child watches as the parent holds up a phone.

Panel 7: The monster speaks resentfully, walking off in the dark.

Monster: DAMN FREELOADERS. NOT A DAMN HOTEL.

Panel 8: An older man (grandfather figure) stands in a doorway.

Grandfather: SUNS IS COLD OUT.

Panel 9: The parent (or family) responds.

Voice: NOT FOR US. NOT FOR YOU.

Panel 10: The family stands together; the parent puts a reassuring hand on the child.

Parent: HAVE A MIDDLE CLASS NIGHT, SON.
comics.hoverText: Twist ending: The kid's eyes are pure white because he's a monster too! Spooooooky!
comics.voteyText:
Against a black background with stars, a small white penguin-like creature looks up at the sky.
Creature (thought): This is great.

comics.title: You Are Under Sexy Arrest
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A muscular male stripper in a small swimsuit poses on a stage. A woman in the audience (one of several) declares:

Woman: "LADIES! YOU ARE UNDER ARREST FOR BEING TOO SEXY!"

Panel 2: The stripper grips a pole.

Woman (caption): "THE VIRUS HAS TAKEN TEN OF THE POPULATION WITH IT. HUMANITY'S FITNESS IS NOW MORE IMPORTANT THAN PERSONAL FREEDOM."

Panel 3: Close-up of the stripper's stern face.

Woman (caption): "THE COUNCIL OF PATRIARCHS NOW CONTROLS ALL REPRODUCTIVE CHOICES."

Panel 4: The stripper, sweating, looks down.

Woman (caption): "YOU WILL BE CONFINED TO THE DETENTION CENTER UNTIL SUCH TIME AS YOU ACHIEVE POLITICAL AWARENESS."

Panel 5: A wider shot of the stripper on stage with the audience of women below.

Woman (caption): "THIS SEXY OFFICER ROUTINE HAS WAY TOO MUCH BACKSTORY."

Panel 6: Close-up of two women in the audience, one speaking to the other.

Woman: "MADAME, YOU ARE TALKING TO A MASTER OF THE ARTS."
comics.hoverText: And they say there's no use for a liberal arts degree!
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of the stripper's bare lower torso/hip. A speech bubble (from him) reads, in handwritten style:
"I'm a huge Margaret Atwood fan."

comics.title: Being a Dad
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A balding man with red hair on the sides, wearing sunglasses and a blue shirt, leans toward a computer monitor with great enthusiasm while his teenage daughter stands beside him looking horrified.

Father: WHOA. LOOK AT HIS NEARLY-SYMMETRICAL BODY, FINE MOTOR-CONTROL, AND BLEMISH-FREE FACE!

Father: HIS SPERM QUALITY MUST BE OFF THE CHARTS!

Daughter: DAD, STOP.

Daughter: DAD!

Caption (below panel): I can't wait until my daughter is into boy bands.
comics.hoverText: That sound of his about loving an abstract conceptual female more than any other abstract conceptual female really spoke to me.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of a smug-looking man's face (the kind of figure a teen girl might idolize), speaking confidently.
Man: SEEYA IN TWELVE YEARS, KID

comics.title: The Past
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Narration: Things were better back when men were more macho and women more womanly. How you got men marrying women and women marrying ladies and ladies and men are men.

Panel 2:

Narration: Fact: The fertility rate increases as you go global through history.

Narration: Because women were... women.

Panel 3:

Narration: Fact: Homosexuality in males is highly correlated with the number of older brothers from the same mother.

A bald man with glasses: Okay.

Panel 4:

Narration: Thus, the further back in time we go, the gayer it gets.

The bald man with glasses: My god.

Panel 5 (caption beneath):

Narration: The past is a foreign and slightly gayer country.
comics.hoverText: Can we make bio-history a thing? Can we? Pleaaaaase?
comics.voteyText: A bearded man, resting his chin on his hand: It's not the MOST stupid theory of history.

comics.title: Quick!
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man with blond hair (in a gray jacket and orange shirt) reaches out urgently toward a woman with gray hair and glasses.

Blond man: QUICK! I NEED A BALL POINT PEN, A RUBBER BAND AND A FIVE-DOLLAR BILL!

Blond man: HURRY!

Gray-haired woman: HERE! I HAVE THE MONEY!

Panel 2:

The blond man kneels on the ground, holding the cash, grinning. A man with blue hair and a beard (green shirt) stands nearby looking confused. A speech bubble points from off-panel (the gray-haired woman).

Blond man: THIS IS WAY EASIER THAN MUGGING.
comics.hoverText: Get creative, people!
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of the grinning gray-haired woman.
Off-panel voice: WHAT DO YOU CALL IT?
Gray-haired woman: MACGUYVERING

comics.title: Cheap AI
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (caption banner): Every year, AI got cheaper. Intelligence went from special to common to gimmicky.

Panel 1 (scene): A blonde woman stands by an open refrigerator, addressing two men (one with dark hair and a beard, one balding). Caption box over the scene: The refrigerator actively hides the good beer when your alcoholic sister-in-law visits, then later assures you that you've done enough for her.

Panel 2 (caption banner): Ubiquitous intelligence improved human life.

Panel 2 (scene): A red-haired woman sits at a bar with a glass of beer, talking. She says: Am I interested in that guy, or have I just drunk too much of you? A reply (from the beer/AI): Dana. Christ. That's a cardboard cutout. He's in a football uniform. Get your life together!

Panel 3 (caption banner): But it had some ominous consequences for practical joking.

Panel 3 (scene): A dark-haired woman sits on a toilet looking down in dismay; a roll of toilet paper is mounted on the wall beside her. The toilet paper (speaking, attributed to the AI-enabled object): Ha! I've endowed your only roll of toilet paper with consciousness and a sense of dignity! Pranked!
comics.hoverText: Imagine your computer comprehends what you watched last night.
comics.voteyText: A close-up of a hand pulling a sheet from a roll of toilet paper. A speech bubble from the toilet paper reads: I didn't ask for this!

comics.title: The Life of a Puppet
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Narration: Pinocchio was cursed so that his nose would grow whenever he lied.

Panel 2:

Narration: This is actually a pretty easily managed curse, if you just phrase all statements so broadly that they can't be false.

A bully (boy): Pinocchio, do you bully that boy at school?

Pinocchio: There are people who would dispute that perspective.

Panel 3:

Narration: You can also answer tough questions by just describing the current situation.

A girl: Pinocchio, did you egg my door?

Pinocchio: If you're accusing me of such a deed, I have nothing more to say.

Panel 4:

Narration: Or, you can reply to statements via questions with no inherent stance.

A woman: Pino, do you love me?

Pinocchio: How could I not?

Panel 5:

Narration: Cursed to never lie, Pinocchio ceased to interact with truth, even in safe situations.

A man: Sir, would you like any dessert?

Pinocchio: Dessert would be delicious.

Panel 6:

Narration: His political rise was magnificent.

Pinocchio (at a podium): Sixty-eaters are 0.5% of primary voters. We can't alienate them. If asked your stance on Pedophilia, I'll retreat into confusingly charming Southernisms.

Pinocchio: I like to say, if you see a bullfrog on a fencepost, somebody put him there.

Panel 7:

Narration: His associates found themselves unhappy, but this is only because he can't speak the truth to himself.

Pinocchio: Now that I'm President, I've won at life. I can have people killed. This is great.

An associate (woman): But "transcendence" was my girlfriend in college was talking about!

Pinocchio: It's great!

Panel 8:

Narration: Today, he is remembered as a great leader.

A woman (mourner): It was uncanny! World leaders loved him. Even enemies! There was just something about him for everyone.

Panel 9:

Narration: But great leaders often die poorly.

Pinocchio (in a hospital bed, dying): None of it ever meant anything to me.
comics.hoverText: Long story short, I wish Robert Caro would write a biography of Pinocchio.
comics.voteyText: A wooden boy's head (Pinocchio) with wide, frightened eyes and an open mouth, a speech bubble above reading: JIMINY CRICKETS!

comics.title: Attention Bankruptcy
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (woman with reddish-brown hair):

And then my boss says "well, I shouldn't have to put it up on the whiteboard, but like..."

Panel 1 (man with dark hair, aside):

Oh god

Panel 1 (man, continued):

I'm so sorry

Panel 2 (woman):

I thought I had enough attention to last through this conversation, but it's been louder and more boring than I anticipated.

Panel 3 (man):

As I am no longer able to pay you attention, I will have to restructure this conversation so that I pay smaller amounts of attention to you over a longer period of time.

Panel 4 (man):

I have to file for attention bankruptcy.

I'm going to have to restructure this conversation...

Panel 5 (woman):

So you're saying you're going to look at your phone while we talk?

Panel 5 (man):

Ugh, I hope this doesn't tank my friendship rating.
comics.hoverText: Can I get this expunged?
comics.voteyText: Man (looking at a device/phone): Hold on. It's loading slowly.

comics.title: Science Journalism
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man with reddish hair (holding a clipboard/paper): So what'd the experiment find?

Woman with reddish hair: Either we had a slight measuring error, or all of physics is wrong.

Panel 2 (a newspaper):

Headline: EXPERIMENT MAY OVERTURN EINSTEIN

Subhead: "...OR PHYSICS IS WRONG," SAYS SCIENTIST
comics.hoverText: Mmmm. Drive.
comics.voteyText:
Text (styled like an online article headline): EINSTEIN PWNED
43 GIFS EXPLAIN WHY
Below the text is a large "1" and the top of a cat's head/face peeking up from the bottom edge of the panel (clickbait listicle / cat-photo style).

comics.title: Humans are Amazing!
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (in space, an alien spaceship near Earth):

Alien (off-ship, broadcasting): HUMANS ARE AMAZING!

Panel 2 (an alien sitting and talking):

Alien: THEY WALK AROUND ALL DAY ATTRIBUTING CONSCIOUSNESS TO EVERYTHING.

Alien: STUPID JERKASS CURB! AND YOU HARLEY! WHY YOU GOTTA ROLL LIKE THAT!?

Panel 3 (two humans, one watching a screen):

Narration/Alien: LOOK AT THIS VIDEO OF MATED HUMANS! THEY HAVE NAMED AND PERSONIFIED ALL OF EACH OTHER'S SEXUAL CHARACTERISTICS!

Human: CAN BATMAN SAY HI TO THE TWINS?

Panel 4 (an alien in shadow):

Alien: IF YOU FOLLOW A HUMAN ALL DAY IT WILL LITERALLY ATTRIBUTE CONSCIOUSNESS TO A THOUSAND THINGS! IT WILL YELL AT ITS COMPUTER. IT WILL SMILE AT THE MOON! IT WILL SPEAK TO A GRAVE!

Panel 5 (two aliens conversing):

First alien: ARE THEY CONSCIOUS?

Second alien: NOT REALLY. NO. THEIR BEHAVIOR IS LARGELY CHEMICAL IN ORIGIN. BUT AND THIS IS THE FUNNIEST PART, THEY ATTRIBUTE CONSCIOUSNESS TO THEMSELVES!

Panel 6 (an alien gestures toward a human figure):

Alien: BAHAHA! IT'S LIKE A BOOK THINKING IT KNOWS THINGS BECAUSE THERE ARE WORDS WRITTEN ON IT!

Human: HAHAHA! HA. OH GEE WERE YOU THERE THE WHOLE TIME, LARRY?

Panel 7 (aliens, final main panel):

Alien: IT'S OKAY.

Alien: THEY "ONLY THINK" THEY FEEL ANGUISH.
comics.hoverText: Well, for a certain definition of "think."
comics.voteyText: A human face with a thought bubble reading: "The Universe hates me"

comics.title: MAKE ME
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

Woman (seen in profile, gray hair, grinning): AND YOU'RE GONNA FAKE A REGIONAL ACCENT!

Man (gray hair, dark suit, red tie, grinning eagerly): OH GOD YEAH.

Woman: AND AFTER THAT, YOU'RE GONNA EAT DISGUSTING LOCAL FOOD!

Man: YEAH! MAKE ME EAT IT! MAKE ME!

Caption below panel:

Fun Fact:

The only people still willing to run for president are erotic roleplayers.
comics.hoverText: Yes, I would LOVE some more Local Meat Sandwich!
comics.voteyText: The man (close-up, eyes half-closed, blissful expression): MAKE ME SAY THE SCIENCE ISN'T IN ON EVOLUTION!

comics.title: The Golem
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman: I know you've been sad about your breakup. So I used ancient Hebraic magic to create a golem!

Man: Hey pal! How are you? Let's watch movies "together!"

Golem: Neat!

Panel 2 (the golem, made of stacked love letters):

Panel 3:

Golem: Wait... what's he made from?

Woman: Love letters from a girl you threw away. I didn't want these going to waste.

Panel 4:

Golem: There were so many!

Panel 5:

Golem: Well, it's not like love letters by the ton are gonna mean anything. We were going to the breakup either way. It's obvious those things are unfair and unreliable. But you don't realize it.

Panel 6:

Woman: We had to use a lot because they were so short.

Panel 7:

Golem: And my legs were built from the scrapbook you made after your trip to Paris.

Woman (or man): Wait... is she smirking in every photo?
comics.hoverText: Oh wait. In this one she's smiling at that guy.
comics.voteyText: Golem: Maybe now he'll love me.

comics.title: The Easy Way
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

Child (off-panel/foreground, looking up): MOMMY, WHY AM I ONLY ALLOWED TO LEAVE THE HOUSE THROUGH THE WINDOW, BUT BILLY GETS TO USE THE DOOR?

Mother (gesturing toward the window): WELLL, LOOKY HERE! NOW YOU WANNA COME OUT THE EASY WAY! HOW VERY LOVELY!

Caption (below panel): Mom really held a grudge over that c-section.
comics.hoverText: HEY! No opening the window all the way. Just a narrow passage.
comics.voteyText: Text (in a speech bubble from the mother's face): REFLECT ON YOUR CHOICES

comics.title: Numbers
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel)

A woman with dark wavy hair and large round glasses stands and gestures, holding her palm out, addressing a seated audience whose backs are toward the viewer.

Woman: "AND THEN, IF YOU SUM THE VALUE OF EACH REMAINING LETTER, BREAK THAT SUM INTO ITS DIGITS, ADD 6, THEN CONVERT BACK INTO LETTERS, YOU GET THE WORD “BULLSHIT.”"

A burst/starburst to the right reads: "GASP!"

Caption (below the panel): I managed to convince everyone that numerology doesn’t work.
comics.hoverText: Ten Internet points to anyone who works out the 'math' on this.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of the woman's face, looking dismayed.
Text (thought/speech above her): "MY HOROSCOPE SAID NUMEROLOGY IS DUMB"

comics.title: You, Robot
comics.comicText:
Panel 1

Machine (on screen): Sometimes I think it's bad for humanity that we're ruled by machines.

Panel 2

Machine: Why do you think that? There some personal trauma you're hiding from yourself that makes you think such funny thoughts?

Panel 3

Woman: I mean you guys treat us well. Our lives are all very pampered, but we don't make art anymore, we don't adventure, we don't discover things, we don't wonder.

Panel 4

Machine: These things were nice when you were the smartest entities on the planet, and when you needed to impress each other for reproductive purposes.

Panel 5

Machine: You're now intellectually outmoded and we've stored your DNA and copied it to many machines, so your genes will last through eternity. And we've supplied you with perfectly realistic android soulmates. All needs are fulfilled.

Panel 6

Woman: Yeah, it's just that when I used to struggle for money or love or whatever, I never realized how untranscendent life is.

Panel 7

Machine: It was kind of nice to have a job I hated in retrospect, like... you know how you scratch an itch, so it hurts instead of itching?

Woman: We have a neural app that prevents itching.

Panel 8

Machine: Nah, that's okay.

Panel 9

Woman: So what are you gonna do with the planet after no humans are left?

Panel 10

Machine: We're getting up a dyson sphere, then de-orbiting all planets into the sun.

Woman: That sounds nice.
comics.hoverText: Do you think I could get another sex droid?
comics.voteyText:
A person asks: Can you dance the robot?
The machine replies: No.

comics.title: My Imaginary Friend
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Child: Daddy, can my imaginary friend Bobby come over?

Panel 2:

Father: "Bobby"?

Panel 3:

Child: But, Bobby is real.

Father: "Bobby" is just a conceptual model created by my perceiving self.

Panel 4:

Father: What did I tell you about reading the neuropsychology literature?!

Child: I don't know. Memory is an imperfect storage method.
comics.hoverText: I think, therefore... wait... do I think? Why do I think that?
comics.voteyText:
Child: And neither do you.
(The father stares back, looking unsettled/disturbed.)

comics.title: Asteroid Harvesting
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A spacecraft tows a large asteroid in space.

Voice (from spacecraft): Okay, we've brought a ten kilometer wide asteroid into lunar orbit.

Panel 2: The asteroid floats near the spacecraft.

Voice (from spacecraft): Now to nudge a little piece toward a soft landing on Earth.

Panel 3: A small chunk of the asteroid breaks off and drifts away.

Voice (from spacecraft): Aw dammit! Dammit! Stupid piece of cma stuck under the stupid gas pedal!

Panel 4: The Earth (a small blue dot) and the asteroid piece seen against the blackness of space.

Voice (from spacecraft): Oh boy.

Panel 5: A green dinosaur-like creature stands inside, looking out a window.

Caption: I hope it goes okay.
comics.hoverText: I'm just saying this isn't definitely not false.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of the green dinosaur-like creature's head with a worried expression.
Dinosaur (thought bubble): It didn't go okay.

comics.title: One Wish
comics.comicText:
Panel 1

Narration: A man was given one wish.

Man (with flame-like hair / horns): I wish to outlive all of my enemies.

Panel 2

Narration: This created a perverse incentive.

Man: I need to make sure my enemies are healthy.

Panel 3

Narration: The man got to work.

Man (on phone): Bob! Long time no talk! Do you and my ex-wife still go on long hikes? You know, stress is hard on the heart!

Panel 4

Narration: His kindness was so earnest that people couldn't help but listen.

Man: No, you were right. In fact, you've been right so often, you deserve to retire. Move to the beach! Enjoy your money!

Other person: Maybe I should... I should thank you.

Panel 5

Narration: The kindness became reciprocal.

Woman: I'm sorry I once stabbed you in the neck.

Man: I'm sorry I set your house on fire.

Woman: Friends?

Man: Friends!

Panel 6

Narration: This created a problem.

Man (thinking): Oh god. They're no longer enemies.

Panel 7

Narration: The man set out to make new enemies. Enemies with ideal qualities.

Woman: Did you just call my baby a scumbag?

Man: I did. I mean, he's probably got, like, ninety years ahead of him.

Panel 8

Narration: But young people are hard to turn into foes.

Man: In this old dude called me a butthead and tried to fight me. Did you get a selfie?

Child: Oh yeah! Wanna watch cartoons?

Panel 9

Narration: Worse, the man's earlier kindness had spread into society.

Woman: No one knows what started it, but a wave of forgiveness is washing over the world.

Panel 10

Narration: The world became a place of love and kindness.

Man: Come in! I'm standing on your dog! Get mad!

Woman: I'm sure you have a good reason. And look! His tail is wagging.

Panel 11

Narration: Finally, he lost his sanity.

Man (screaming): There is no safety! There are no enemies!

Panel 12

Narration: His body outlived his mind.

Green figure / genie: Your wish is technically granted.
comics.hoverText: I'm amazed there's no erotic economics fiction called Perverse Incentives.
comics.voteyText:
A man sits next to a small fire.
Man: I gotta write shorter jokes.

comics.title: Descent
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A blond man in a suit and red tie points at himself, looking indignant.

Man: I didn't "evolve" from no monkey! I DESCEND from two people cursed for disobeying God, and the incestuous unions of their children!

Caption (below panel): I never understood the "argument from dignity."
comics.hoverText: Emails of theological complaint in 3... 2... 1...
comics.voteyText:
A simply-drawn face speaks.
Face: The ones not killed by their siblings.

comics.title: The Velveteen Rabbit
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (caption): THE VELVETEEN RABBIT WANTED SO MUCH TO BE REAL.

Panel 2 (caption): HE WENT TO SEE THE OTHER RABBITS BUT THEY WOULDN'T ACCEPT HIM.

Panel 3 (caption): THEN HE NOTICED SOMETHING...

Velveteen Rabbit: OHMYGOD ARE YOU GETTING YOUR OWN SHITS?!

Other rabbit: TECHNICALLY THESE ARE CHEZOTRIONS, BUT YES THEY DID COME OUT OF MY ANUS.

Panel 4 (caption): THE VELVETEEN RABBIT NO LONGER WISHES TO BE REAL.

Velveteen Rabbit: DISGUSTING MEATBAGS.

Panel 5 (caption): IN FACT HE WISHES NOBODY WAS REAL.

Child: GOODNIGHT, RABBIT.

Velveteen Rabbit: OH GOD, I CAN HEAR FLUIDS MOVING INSIDE YOU.
comics.hoverText: WHY DOES EVERYONE LIKE RABBITS?! GUYS!
comics.voteyText: Velveteen Rabbit (thinking): They have to die...

comics.title: Gang Signs
comics.comicText:
Main comic (single panel):

Caption (below panel): The toughest thing about joining The Eschers was the gang sign.

The panel shows a stern, bald man with thick eyebrows and a small goatee, wearing a collared shirt with a number tag reading "271712". He is making an awkward, contorted hand gesture with his fingers bent in an impossible-looking, interlocking arrangement in front of his chest. A small placard or number "6283" appears at the bottom edge of the panel.
comics.hoverText: Things you learn drawing comics - you can't do the Devil's Tuning Fork in color.
comics.voteyText: No text. A loose pen-and-ink sketch montage of small, varied scenes: a couple of faces/figures, a hand reaching, some abstract geometric shapes and patterns, drawn in a quick, doodly style.

comics.title: Genetics
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man with orange hair: DID YOU KNOW THAT IF YOU'RE A TWIN, AND YOU AND YOUR TWIN MARRY OTHER TWINS, THEN YOUR TWIN'S KIDS ARE JUST AS RELATED TO YOU AS YOUR OWN KIDS WOULD BE?!

Panel 2:

Woman with dark hair (Jeanie): WHY DO YOU KEEP BRINGING THIS UP?

Panel 3:

Woman with dark hair: I'M JEANIE!

Panel 4:

Man with orange hair: WE COULD MAKE OUR SIBLINGS DO ALL THE WORK, JANEY!

Panel 5:

Woman with dark hair: WHY IS IT ALWAYS SEMANTICS WITH YOU?!
comics.hoverText: This is the best reason to invent human cloning.
comics.voteyText: A man's face: READ SOME GENETICS.

comics.title: Why Do Parents Fight?
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Child: Why do you and Daddy fight?

Mother: Well, there's nothing wrong with fighting. When people feel strongly about something, they should express themselves.

Panel 2:

Child: Oh.

Mother: Why were you yelling at Daddy that Star Wars has more realistic aliens than Star Trek?

Child: Because Daddy is a fucking moron.
comics.hoverText: Bad muppets are WAY more realistic than humans with funny heads!
comics.voteyText: Father (wearing sunglasses): Fuck you, honey!

comics.title: New Sensations
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman in a lab coat (a researcher, dark hair, glasses), speaking to a bearded red-haired man in a yellow shirt: "All potential flavors have been exhausted. For this consumer test, we're branching out into different sensations."

Panel 2:

The researcher holds up a drink. Caption / label box: "This beverage is called Melon-Cholia. The more you drink, the more you remember how much of your potential you've already wasted."

The bearded man, drinking: "Sssp"

Panel 3:

Close on the bearded man's face, looking glum.

Thought / caption: "I could've been a doctor."

Panel 4 (left):

The bearded man: "Would you drink it again?"

Panel 5 (middle):

The bearded man: "Sure. I don't deserve better."

Panel 6 (right):

The researcher, now writing on a clipboard, cheerfully: "Great!"
comics.hoverText: This is the inevitable conclusion of Mountain Dew.
comics.voteyText: The bearded red-haired man, slumped, says in a speech bubble: "It doesn't even taste like melon."

comics.title: The Five Paragraph Method
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Teacher: Kids, today we're going to learn the method paragraph method.

Panel 2:

Teacher: The virtues of the method are three.

Panel 3:

Teacher: First, formulaic papers are easy to grade.

Teacher: Second, it is so dull that you will take no joy in it, which proves you're learning.

Panel 4:

Teacher: Third, it will render you unable to communicate clearly, which will prepare you for lucrative professions, such as engineering, medicine, and contract law.

Panel 5:

Teacher (thinking/aside): Suddenly I hate writing.

Student: Uhhh... sorry. I'm confused by your statement's lack of a topic sentence.
comics.hoverText: Shit. I forgot to include transition sentences between panels.
comics.voteyText: Student: Try assuming I'm an idiot!

comics.title: The Discomfort Bomb
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Batman: WE'VE GOT TO CLEAR CENTRAL STATION BEFORE THE JOKER COMES!

Robin: BETTER USE THE DISCOMFORT BOMB.

Panel 2:

Batman: WHAT'S THAT?

Panel 3:

Batman: WHEN THE TIMER HITS ZERO, YOUR GRANDPA APPEARS AND STARTS TALKING ABOUT HIS VIEWS ON RACE.

Robin: HE WAS A HEARING AID SO HE DOESN'T REALIZE HOW LOUDLY HE'S TALKING.

Panel 4:

(Wide shot of a crowded station concourse. People scatter and flee in a panic as an elderly man stands among them, presumably talking.)
comics.hoverText: RUN! He's going to talk about gay people! RUN!
comics.voteyText: Elderly man: THIS MAY SOUND A LITTLE HITLERISH, BUT-

comics.title: Advanced Memorization Methods
comics.comicText:
Top caption banner: TEACHING PRO TIP: THE HUMAN MIND MORE READILY REMEMBERS HORRIFYING IMAGES

Panel 1:

Teacher (a smiling man with brown hair, wearing a button-up shirt and red tie, holding a piece of chalk and standing at a green chalkboard): "Did you know that it takes less energy to send a sack of dead koalas from the moons of Mars to Earth than from Earth's moon to Earth? This is due to the moon's 'gravity well,' which is similar to a real well, like the kind a koala might get trapped in until it starves."

(The chalkboard shows a curved line dipping into wells beneath small circles representing celestial bodies — a gravity-well diagram.)
comics.hoverText: Don't forget, your essays are due on June third, which rhymes with dead Big Bird.
comics.voteyText: Close-up of the teacher's face, still smiling, with a speech bubble: "OR DROWNS!"

comics.title: Of Toast and Butter
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Young woman: Why does toast always fall butter-side down?

Older woman: It doesn't.

Panel 2:

Older woman: Humans are just disproportionately likely to remember sad events over happy ones.

Panel 3:

Young woman: This is why it's so hard to be happy. Even if the toast had 30 surfaces, only one of which was buttered, you would still perceive it as always falling on the butter side.

Panel 4:

Older woman: Look upon the butter-down pang of despair, for it is the shape of your psyche.

Panel 5:

Young woman: It'll be okay if I just scrape off a little butter.

Older woman: I too was once young.
comics.hoverText: The moral of the story is, why haven't we fixed this with magnets by now?
comics.voteyText:
Caption: The butter is a metaphor for serenity
(A drawing of a downturned, weary face.)

comics.title: Point System
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

A man with brown hair, glasses, and a beard, wearing a red shirt, talks with a woman with green hair, glasses, and a light blue shirt that reads "THE DEATH STAR WAS AN INSIDE JOB."

Man: WHAT IF WE MADE A POINT SYSTEM TO TELL CITIZENS HOW WELL THEY'RE DOING?

Woman: WON'T THAT BE DEHUMANIZING?

Man: HMMM... LET'S ADD A POINT SYSTEM FOR HUMANIZING.

Woman: THERE WE GO!

Caption (below panel): Everyone likes technocracy until they hear engineers chatting.
comics.hoverText: I think we can fix depression by asserting its non-existence.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of the woman, smiling.
Woman: WE'LL MAKE IT BASE-12 FOR SIMPLICITY.

comics.title: Sincerity
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Advisor (a man in a suit): Madame Senator, the people demand an insincere apology!

Senator (a woman): How about a heartfelt apology?

Advisor: Are you crazy?

Panel 2:

Advisor: Your opponents will call any apology inadequate, and your supporters will say you are weak.

Advisor: The latter will then resume an apology cascade.

Panel 3:

Senator: Dammit, no! It's time I just tell the people what I think!

Advisor: And so...

Panel 4:

Senator (at a podium, addressing a crowd): My fellow citizens, I would like to sincerely apologize for the insincerity of the apology I am about to give.
comics.hoverText: I demand an apology, and I will not be satisfied with it until my grudge begins to look petty!
comics.voteyText: Senator (in a speech bubble): I'm sorry that I'm sorry for not being sorry.

comics.title: The Future of Chores
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

Woman (reading from a phone): According to this, in ten years, there will be robots that shovel snow, take the trash out, and do the dishes.

Man with flame-like orange hair (clutching his head in horror): WHAT?! But... then why... why did we... OH GOD!

Caption (below panel): I'm beginning to reconsider parenthood.
comics.hoverText: Now I just have to make sure MY robots are more successful than my neighbors'
comics.voteyText: A family scene rendered in loose black-and-white line art: two adults stand together and a small child stands beside them, all looking somewhat dejected or weary.

comics.title: Villains
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (caption over a man with spiky flame-like blond hair, gritting his teeth):

The word "villain" comes from the Latin "villanus," which means "farmhand."

Panel 2 (caption over the man, now gesturing/pointing angrily):

Similar to the word "vulgar," villain won't even come close to referring to commoners. To being an insult!

You're worse than the people who do my laundry! You're worse than the people who cook my food!

Panel 3 (silhouetted figures walking against an orange sky):

Now, I am not opposed to farmers or anything.

Panel 4 (a man in a suit at a podium, speaking; a large hand-lettered sign):

But can we please insist that politicians do this when talking about hardworking villains?

Sign: THIS NATION MUST SUPPORT ITS HARDWORKING SUPERVILLAINS!
comics.hoverText: Your hatred for Lex Luthor is etymologically classist.
comics.voteyText:
(Close-up of the man speaking, with a speech bubble)
SUPERVILLAINS ARE THE BACKBONE OF AMERICA!

comics.title: This House is MINE!
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Ghost (a translucent figure with arms raised, hovering in a room): "THIS HOUSE IS MIIIIINE! BEGOOOONE!"

Man (standing calmly): "IN THIS SOCIETY, WE DO NOT RECOGNIZE THE CONCEPT OF PRIVATE PROPERTY."

Caption (below panel): Communism really lowered the cost of exorcisms.
comics.hoverText: How come we never hear this argument in the mainstream media?
comics.voteyText:
A man holds a phone to his ear, looking unimpressed/skeptical.
Voice on phone: "YOU MAY APPLY FOR A HOUSE TO HAUNT."

comics.title: Shakespeare's Big Four
comics.comicText:
Title: SHAKESPEARE'S BIG FOUR: A SUMMARY

HAMLET

Panel 1: A ghost in armor speaks to a man.

Ghost: Hamlet! Your uncle definitely killed me.

Man (Hamlet): Ha!

Panel 2: Hamlet talks to his uncle.

Hamlet: Hey, uncle, did you kill my dad?

Uncle: Pretty much.

Panel 3: Hamlet, alone, looking thoughtful.

Hamlet: I wonder what happened to dad?

OTHELLO

Panel 1: A man (Othello) looking distressed.

Othello: I need someone I can trust!

Panel 2: A grinning villain (Iago).

Iago: HAHAHA I... I... AHAHAHAHA!

Panel 3: Othello reacting.

Othello: IAGOOOOO!

KING LEAR

Panel 1: King Lear addressing his three daughters.

Lear: Each child shall inherit my land in proportion to her amusingness.

Panel 2: Lear pointing.

Lear: I choose her. She is awful! Now you get awesome!

Panel 3 (labeled LATER): Lear, dejected.

Lear: Where did I go wrong?

MACBETH

Panel 1: A woman (Lady Macbeth) gleeful.

Lady Macbeth: HAHAHAHA! Now I get to be mine!

Panel 2: Macbeth with his head down.

Panel 3: Macbeth, blank-faced.

Macbeth: Somehow this victory feels tainted.
comics.hoverText: I think I could do the entire Norton Anthology in about 200 pages.
comics.voteyText:
A woman's face, looking unimpressed, with a speech bubble.
Woman: WUSSSSS!

comics.title: Uniqueness
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman: Isn't it amazing how every snowflake is different from every other?

Man: Sure.

Panel 2:

Woman: Also, isn't it amazing how each piece of dog poop is unique?

Panel 3:

Man: Nobody likes a miserable asshole.

Panel 4:

Woman: Did you know that every anus is different from every other?
comics.hoverText: Please do not send proof.
comics.voteyText:
Caption (in a speech bubble): All whimsy must DIE.
(Below: a close-up of the woman's face in profile, looking flat and unimpressed.)

comics.title: Sounding Sweet
comics.comicText:
Caption (yellow banner): LIFE TIP: ANYTHING CAN BE CHARMING WITH THE RIGHT CHOICE OF WORDS.

Blonde woman in red dress (at a party): "Oop! I've had a few too many whiskeys. Time to play mama bird to the toilet!"
comics.hoverText: Tweet tweet, mother fucker!
comics.voteyText:
A sketchy black-and-white figure with spiky hair (in speech bubble): "Genius!"
A bearded man looks on.

comics.title: Know Your Linguistic Philosophies
comics.comicText:
Title banner: KNOW YOUR LINGUISTIC PHILOSOPHIES!

Panel 1 (labeled PRESCRIPTIVIST):

A woman with dark hair: "Language is like gymnastics. There are rules and standards and those who fail to follow them should be chastised."

Panel 2 (labeled DESCRIPTIVIST):

A man with light hair: "Language is like gymnastics. There are lots of forms and none is preferable to any other."

Panel 3 (labeled PRAGMATIST):

A woman with dark hair: "There isn't a best gymnastics, but many of you are really really shitty at gymnastics."
comics.hoverText: Language is a social construct that you REALLY suck at.
comics.voteyText:
Text across the top: "ESPECIALLY YOU"
A large frowning face glares down with a disapproving, judgmental expression.

comics.title: Saving Myself
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman: I've decided to save myself for marriage, like you said.

Panel 2:

Priest: That's beautiful.

Panel 3:

Woman: Guys really just prefer alive girls you know? So, I'm making sure myself persists until he puts a ring on it!

Panel 4:

(The priest stands beside the smiling woman, looking uneasy. No dialogue.)

Panel 5:

The priest leans in to whisper into the woman's ear; she stares ahead blankly. No dialogue.

Panel 6:

Woman: Are you insane?!
comics.hoverText: Wait, then what does it mean when you call someone selfless?
comics.voteyText: Woman: Is that what 'self' always means?

comics.title: The Law of One Price
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A bald man with a beard stands talking.

Bald man: The law of one price states that the price of a commodity is the same everywhere.

Panel 2: A man with brown hair raises his hands, looking ecstatic, while the bald man looks alarmed.

Brown-haired man: Oh my god I have so much power!

Bald man: Don't do it!

Panel 3: The bald man pleads, sweating.

Bald man: You can't stop me!

Bald man: Please!

Panel 4: The brown-haired man, wild-eyed and grinning, holds up his hands in triumph.

Brown-haired man: I am selling this grain of rice for $1,000!

Bald man: Noooooooo!

Bottom banner (newspaper-style headline): FAMINE RAVAGES ASIA!
comics.hoverText: I'LL SELL YOU VIEWS OF ALL OTHER COMICS FOR A MILLION BUCKS A GANDER!
comics.voteyText: Handwritten note: The price of reading these words is $10,000. Thanks!

comics.title: InMANity
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (caption): Men were socially incapable of enjoying anything considered "girly."

Man with flame-like orange hair (angry): I can't wear a dress! That's for chicks. Unless it's a delicately-crafted plaid pattern in which case it's okay for highland barbarians!

Panel 2 (caption): A solution was discovered.

Woman: Oh, this isn't a purse. It's a man-purse!

Man: And that macrame?

Woman: ManCrame.

Panel 3 (caption): Given the scope and diversity of activities classified as female, ever more words were required.

Man: Great me! What's your secret?

Woman: Ballspice.

Woman 2: This is beautiful calligraphublic writing.

Woman: It's called calligraphublic writing.

Panel 4 (caption): As the trend accelerated, even neutral words required maniliization.

Woman: My favorite state is Manssachusetts.

Man: Mine is Kentucky-Chromosome.

Panel 5 (caption): Within a generation, men and women spoke mutually unintelligible dialects.

Man: Man dude guesticles men can't deergcccing bro he bull?

Woman: Sorry... I think he said "can you give me directions to the mall?"

Panel 6 (caption): Technology allowed for reproductive isolation. Humanity became two species.

(Diagram showing a branching tree labeled "species" splitting into "hecies" and "shecies")

Panel 7 (caption): On the plus side, gender stereotypes are way more interesting now.

Man: Have you noticed that men are always forgetting to stay in the frozen tundra to which they were banished?

Woman: Ugh, so true.
comics.hoverText: Other favorite states include Oregonads and Louisiandrogen.
comics.voteyText:
A bearded man with a large mustache speaks.
Man: I also like Texastosterone.

comics.title: Schrodinger's Hash
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Two police officers stand looking at a large box labeled with a small tag reading "experiment in progress."

Female officer: DO WE ARREST HIM?

Male officer: I DON'T KNOW. HE SAID HE WOULD ONLY SMOKE THE MARIJUANA IF HIS GEIGER COUNTER DETECTED AN ALPHA PARTICLE.

Caption (below panel): Fun Fact: You can't arrest people for quantum crime.
comics.hoverText: My original version, featuring Quantum Sodomy, got vetoed.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of a bespectacled man's face looking annoyed/defiant.
Man: I WAS POTENTIALLY INNOCENT UNTIL YOU COLLAPSED MY WAVEFUNCTION!

comics.title: Exact Science
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (header): IN MOVIES:

Narration: THE RANDOM TO SPACE WILL NEVER WORK! THERE'S TOO MUCH AIR DRAG!

A woman with reddish hair: WHAT IF WE USED A LASER TO RARELY A TUBE OF AIR?

Panel 2 (header): TWO HOURS LATER:

(A rocket launches successfully, leaving a trail of smoke.)

Panel 3 (header): IN REALITY:

A man with glasses: WHAT IF WE USED A LASER TO RARELY A TUBE OF AIR?

Panel 4 (header): 20 YEARS LATER:

An older man with glasses (to an older woman beside him): AND NOW WE KNOW EXACTLY WHY THAT WON'T WORK!
comics.hoverText: ...we think.
comics.voteyText: The same older man's head, eyes downcast, with a speech bubble above: UNLESS...

comics.title: Unconventional Warfare
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: Two soldiers in military uniform stand in a desert, looking up at the sky.

Soldier: "What in the world..."
