Panel 4:

The man pulls a gun-like object out of the horn and points it; the cashier looks alarmed. The cereal box ("Fruit O's") sits on the counter.

Panel 5:

The man stands handcuffed, surrounded by police officers, being arrested. A police car with its light bar is in the foreground.
comics.hoverText: When the cops showed up, he reached into the horn and pulled out his own hand with its middle finger up.
comics.voteyText: Close-up of the man's face (drawn in a simple sketch style) speaking: There's been a mistake, officer. Elves are to blame.

comics.title: Bloody Mary
comics.comicText:
Caption (banner above the panel): LISTEN, IT WAS A DIFFERENT TIME! AND IT WAS A POPULAR MEASURE! WE DIDN'T GROW UP LIKING PROTESTANTS! I'M NOT A BIGOT!

Panel: A modern teenage girl with blonde hair stands in a dim bathroom facing a mirror. In the mirror's reflection is the ghostly, bloodied face of Bloody Mary (a pale woman with dark, stringy hair and blood smeared on her face). Mary replies wearily.

Bloody Mary: UH HUH.

Caption (below panel): Modern teenagers summon Bloody Mary to critique her for intolerance.
comics.hoverText: And let's be honest - walkin' around all protestanty like that, some of them were askin' for it.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of Bloody Mary's bloodied face in the mirror, looking annoyed. She speaks.
Bloody Mary: IT'LL HAPPEN TO YOU ONE DAY!

comics.title: Understanding
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Person (standing before a glowing orb): So, what IS the universe made of?

Glowing orb: Aw yeah. This is awkward.

Panel 2:

Person: Just break it down for me.

Glowing orb: I can't.

Panel 3:

Glowing orb: Would it really surprise you to know that knowledge is circumscribed by the history of the species?

Panel 4:

Glowing orb: Humans can only conceptualize about six and a half things at a single time, and then only in great abstraction.

Panel 5:

Glowing orb: Approximately 97% of available understanding in this universe requires you to hold seven mental items at once.

Panel 6:

Glowing orb: The greatest human thinkers get to 7 or 9, and most of those people never breed.

Panel 7:

Glowing orb: Embryoids like me can conceive of up to 10,000 things in their fullness at a single moment. This allows us to understand over 87% of reality.

Panel 8:

Person: Riiight.

Panel 9:

Person: I hear it's shaped like a big donut and we're on the crust.

Panel 10:

Glowing orb: Please stop. This is embarrassing...

Below the comic, small text at the bottom: hey! pssst!
comics.hoverText: Anyway, goodbye. I have to let another sentient species know how pointless it all is.
comics.voteyText: Speech bubble (continuing from the glowing orb): MORE EMBARRASSING THAN YOU CAN POSSIBLY COMPREHEND

comics.title: Bread Alone
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A balding, elderly priest (gray hair on the sides, wearing a black clerical shirt with a white collar) speaks. His eyes are closed and his expression is solemn.

Speech bubble: "MAN SHALL NOT LIVE BY BREAD ALONE. BUT HAVE YOU TRIED TAQUITOS?" -MATTHEW 4:4: UNIVERS 98X771812.

Caption (below panel):

According to multiverse theory, there are infinite versions of every book of the Bible.
comics.hoverText: The Golden Rule is actually about how long to fry a tortilla.
comics.voteyText: A simple rustic wooden cross made of two rough-hewn beige/tan wooden beams lashed or joined together.

comics.title: Wine
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Customer (a woman): And this Pinot Noir pairs well with fish or chicken.

Wine expert (a man): No, it doesn't.

Panel 2:

Wine expert: I've read science. You can tell good wine from bad is merely a social convention.

Panel 3:

Customer: So you're here because...

Wine expert: Which wine goes best with the smug satisfaction of knowing that even experts can't tell fine wine from cheap?

Panel 4:

Wine expert: We recommend this Chardonnay and cherry Kool-Aid blend.

Customer: Magnifique!
comics.hoverText: With notes of dextrose.
comics.voteyText: Character (in profile, sipping): Mmm. Notes of Red 40.

comics.title: The Demon
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

A bald, bearded man (left) shouts at a smiling, long-haired bearded man (right):

Bald bearded man: "HEY! NO NERDS ALLOWED IN THIS CLUB!"

Long-haired bearded man: "BUT IF YOU SELECTIVELY PERMIT ONLY COOL PEOPLE, EVENTUALLY THE INTERIOR WILL BE ENTIRELY COOL AND THE EXTERIOR WILL... MY GOD."

Caption below panel: "Shortly before the proposal of Maxwell's Demon."
comics.hoverText: In summary, the 19th century was the same as now, but with more cloaks.
comics.voteyText:
A hand-drawn diagram in a sketchbook style.
Label: "Fig. 12"
Title: "The Resentment Battery"
An open book / hinged box drawn below, divided into two halves. Left half labeled "US", right half labeled "Them".

comics.title: Robot Heaven
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Child: Mommy, is there a robot heaven?

Mother: Absolutely!

Panel 2:

Mother: There is an original version of the software that makes up the mind of this robot. It is an abstract pattern that can be embodied physically in many objects.

Panel 3:

Mother: An instantiation of that original code lives inside the mind of this robot.

Panel 4:

Mother: This particular robot acquires a small number of memories. After it is given the pattern, these memories are stored in a distant server.

Panel 5:

Mother: So, when this robot breaks down, the memory will yet remain in the cloud in a state of timeless existence, until perhaps it is reborn somewhere else.

Panel 6:

Mother: It is a beautiful cycle. Like all great dreams, it is a pragmatism so exquisite that it verges on the sacred.

Panel 7:

Child: Wow.

Panel 8:

Child: Is there a people heaven?

Mother: AHAHA HAHAHA HAHA!
comics.hoverText: We're just meatbags, sweetie!
comics.voteyText: Mother: That'd be such a nightmare.

comics.title: Age of War
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (line graph): Title "MEDIAN AGE IN AVERAGE NATION". A line rises steeply over time. Y-axis is unlabeled; X-axis: TIME.

Panel 2 (line graph): Title "TOTAL PEOPLE OF PROPER AGE FOR MILITARY SERVICE". A line rises steeply over time. Y-axis is unlabeled; X-axis: TIME.

Panel 3: A scene labeled "OUR GLORIOUS FUTURE". An older gray-haired man speaks to a red-haired woman in a red jacket seated at a table.

Gray-haired man: "CANADA IS INVADING! THEY SENT BOTH OF THE GUYS IN THEIR ARMY."

Red-haired woman: "THEY HAVE TWO GUYS?"

Panel 4: An older man stands in the background; a brown-haired figure in the foreground (the red-haired woman) speaks.

Off-panel/woman (first speech bubble): "TWINS."

Woman: "TELL THEM AMERICA SURRENDERS."

Bottom caption: smbc-comics.com
comics.hoverText: Curse you, Mrs. Jenkins!
comics.voteyText:
A woman's face (drawn loosely) with a speech bubble.
Woman: "Just kidding! Release the Killbots!"

comics.title: Your Wish
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Genie (green character): What is your wish?

Man: I would like to be able to see my existence as a small thread in the larger weave of reality.

Panel 2:

Man: I want the ability to consider my entire life the way I consider other people's lives - perhaps good, perhaps bad, but settled and at peace.

Genie: You sure you don't want gold and sex?

Panel 3:

Man: ... I was under the impression that I get three wishes?

Genie: No, just one.

Panel 4 (man alone, resigned):

Man: Golden sexboy please.
comics.hoverText: It's important to know that happiness isn't PURELY about money.
comics.voteyText: The genie's face, grinning malevolently: I will love her, then melt her

comics.title: Where are the Aliens?
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man (with dark hair, alarmed): AAAAH! AN ALIEN!

Green alien (cheerful): Hello, human!

Panel 2:

Alien: Have you come to breed with our women?

Man (sweating, nervous): Wha-? Are you crazy?

Panel 3:

Man (angry, pointing): That'd be like if you went to another planet and found a species of sapient alien goats, then decided to have sex with them to see if you'd get hybrid alien-goat-human babies!

Panel 4:

Alien (holding the man by the collar, knife/blade in hand): Take me to the alien sexgoats!

Panel 5 (red banner reading "ELSEWHERE..."):

First voice (speech bubble): How come aliens never visit?

Second voice (speech bubble): Maybe they have, and we just don't know it!

[Scene: an older woman and a child stand by a telescope at night, looking up at a purple sky.]
comics.hoverText: Take me to the alien sex-goats is the title of my first memoir.
comics.voteyText:
A goat-like creature (drawn as the "alien sexgoat") stands in profile, with a prominent red/pink anatomical marking on its hindquarters.
Goat (speech bubble): Kweeghvvvv.

comics.title: History is Weird
comics.comicText:
Title text (top of comic): HISTORY IS WEIRD, AND IT GETS WEIRDER.

Panel 1

Woman: LIKE, HAVE YOU READ ABOUT WORLD WAR 2, OR THE COLD WAR? SO MANY INCIDENTS CONTAIN COINCIDENCES THAT ARE BIZARRE TO THE POINT OF MYSTICAL.

Panel 2

Woman: THINK ABOUT IT. ANY REALITY YOU EXIST IN IS ONE WHERE HUMANS DIDN'T ANNIHILATE THEMSELVES.

Panel 3 (two side-by-side captions)

Left: BEFORE ATOMIC WEAPONS, MOST TOMORROWS CONTAINED HUMANS.

Right: AFTER ATOMIC WEAPONS, FEWER TOMORROWS CONTAIN HUMANS.

Panel 4

Woman: ONCE GONE, HUMANS WON'T RETURN. SO, THE LONGER THE WORLD GOES ON IN YOUR VERSION OF REALITY, THE MORE ANOMALOUS YOUR VERSION OF REALITY MUST NECESSARILY BE.

Panel 5

Woman: IT'S CALLED 'ANTHROPOMAJICAL' MULTIPLE WORLDS THEORY. THE WORLD SEEMS TO GET WEIRDER OVER TIME BECAUSE IT'S ACTUALLY WEIRDER IN ANY SENSIBLE REALITY WE ARE ALL DEAD.

Man: COME ON MAN. THAT'S INSANE. WHERE'D YOU READ THIS?

Panel 6

Woman: ON A 'WORLDWIDE WEB' OF COMPUTERS THAT WAS ORIGINALLY CALLED 'THE GALACTIC NETWORK' WHICH CONTAINS ALL HUMAN INFORMATION BUT IS MOSTLY USED TO SEND PICTURES OF NAKED LADIES AND CATS.

Man: OH MY GOD.
comics.hoverText: Thank you for browsing this funnybook on the Galactic Network.
comics.voteyText: Man (looking distressed): How did we settle on "Internet"?

comics.title: Evil Spirit
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A looming red shadowy demonic figure looms over a man with dark hair, speaking to him.

Demon: The world is sooooo complex you'll never understand it. It can't be controlled.

Panel 2:

The man (eyes wide, sweating) responds, hopeful.

Man: What if everything were super simple?

Man: What if there were only one list of things that really matter, and you could pull all the things on the list and when you had them, GASP, you'd be SO HAPPY. SO POWERFUL.

Panel 3:

The man slumps, looking sad and resigned, while the red demon looms behind him.

Man: But I don't want to collect Star Wars products evil spirit!

Demon: NOBODY DOES! THAT'S THE POINT!
comics.hoverText: SMBC merch is, of course, fine.
comics.voteyText:
Panel 1:
The man, eyes closed, tempted.
Man: Maybe just one lightsaber.
Demon (in a large speech bubble): Goooood.

comics.title: Fungus
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (Susan): Wanna go to the top of a ten-storey building?

Panel 2:

Man: You're only saying that because a parasite organism is making you go to an altitude that is optimal for its spore phase.

Panel 3:

Man: Dammit Susan! How dare you! Just because my brain is mostly pathogenic fungus, that doesn't mean I'm not my own man!

Panel 4:

Susan: Okay. Whatever. Fine.

Panel 5:

Susan: Hey, want to eat an enormous meal, then cling tightly to the surface of this roof and die?

Man: For the last time, NO.
comics.hoverText: That third panel is the greatest panel I've ever drawn.
comics.voteyText:
A man with bits of spores/dust drifting up from his head, looking dazed.
Man: I'm a daddy!

comics.title: That's funny...
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (with glasses, reading): Huh, that's funny.

Man (off to the side): What?

Panel 2:

Woman: The average I.Q. of people killed in driverless car accidents is consistently just a little above the population-wide average. What're the odds?

Caption (below the panels): The machines devolved us all slowly, nobody noticed.
comics.hoverText: Also, happiness just keeps going up and up.
comics.voteyText:
Handwritten note inside a box:
Solution to Trolley problem:
Kill smartest person

comics.title: Statistical Baseball
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A man with glasses (the dad) speaks.

Dad: "One discovery from statistical baseball analysis is that 'on-base percentage' is more important than hitting home runs."

Panel 2: Close on the dad's face, intense.

Dad: "The implications are clear."

Panel 3: The dad continues, gesturing.

Dad: "For the 'baseball as sex metaphor,' we have to revisit our assumptions about the desirability of always trying to get to third base or home."

Panel 4: The dad, leaning forward, eyes wide.

Dad: "The most valuable sex-haver is NOT the person who has sex more often than others. It's the person who ALWAYS gets to make out."

Panel 5: Reverse angle. A young boy with red hair (the son) replies flatly.

Son: "Uh... thanks dad."

Panel 6: The boy walks away as the dad reaches out and calls after him.

Son: "So... about condoms though..."

Dad: "We're trying to WIN at sex here, not SHOW OFF."
comics.hoverText: Thank you to the four of you who are amused.
comics.voteyText: A scribbly cartoon face (the dad) grins widely, with a speech bubble reading: "Stats make everything better!"

comics.title: GDP
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (caption): WE NEEDED A NEW ECONOMIC METRIC.

Man: GDP IS RIDICULOUS. WITH GDP IF AN EXTRAVAGANT, A SPECIES TO SELL HIGH-PRICED MEAT, WE'RE MORE PROSPEROUS!

Panel 2 (caption): A PROPOSAL WAS MADE.

Woman: WHAT IF WE MEASURED HAPPINESS INSTEAD?

Man: GREAT IDEA! I FOR ONE GET REALLY HAPPY WHEN I BRIEFLY RESTRICT A KITTEN'S AIR SUPPLY.

Panel 3 (caption): AN ADVANCED UTILITARIANISM WAS BORN.

Man: WE SHALL MEASURE POSITIVE EMOTIONS THAT ARE WELL-EARNED: RIGHTEOUSNESS, DIGNITY, AND HONOR, OR RDH.

Panel 4 (caption): POLITICIANS WERE CONVINCED.

Manager: GDP IS FALLING.

Politician: I AM WILLING TO DO ANYTHING TO MAKE IT SEEM OTHERWISE.

Manager: BLESS YOU.

Panel 5 (caption): A LAW WAS ENACTED.

Politician: HEREAFTER, THOSE PEOPLE WHO GENERATE RDH WILL RECEIVE CASH REWARDS. PEOPLE WHO LOWER RDH SHALL BE TAXED.

Panel 6 (caption): SOCIETY CHANGED BEYOND RECOGNITION.

Newscaster: AT TODAY'S PRESIDENTIAL DEBATE, NOBODY CALLED ANYONE A BABYKILLER.

Panel 7 (caption): THEN, THINGS SEEMED TO PLATEAU.

Man: WE'VE HIT PEAK RDH. WHAT'S HOLDING US BACK?

Other man: THERE'S NEW DATA ON PEOPLE ONLY FEEL THOSE EMOTIONS RELATIVE TO OTHER PEOPLE'S BAD BEHAVIOR.

Panel 8 (caption): THE PROBLEM BECAME CLEAR.

Man: IF EVERYONE KEPT THE WORD ALL THE TIME, THERE WOULDN'T BE A TERM FOR HONOR. IT'S NOT LIKE HOW THERE'S NO WORD FOR KEEPING YOUR LIVER INSIDE YOUR BODY.

Woman: SO...

Man: WE NEED MORE SCUMBAGS.

Panel 9 (caption): A SECRET PROGRAM BEGAN.

Man: WE HAVE CREATED AN ISLAND ON THIS ISLAND WE WILL PLACE WHERE FRED. WORD FRED WILL GO AROUND THE ISLAND COLLECTING KOALAS AND PLACING THEM IN AN ENORMOUS BLENDER. THIS WILL BE BROADCAST LIVE WORLDWIDE.

Panel 10 (caption): RDH SKYROCKETED.

Military man: WORD FRED HAS GOT TO BE STOPPED. THE WORLD IS AT A CROSSROADS. THERE CAN BE NO QUARTER WHEN FACING THE HORNY COUNTENANCE OF EVIL. I MUST SELECT MY HASHTAG WITH CARE.

Panel 11 (caption): EVER MORE MILITARY FUNDING WAS REQUIRED TO DEFEND FRED AGAINST CIVILIAN ATTACKERS.

Man: NUCLEAR DETONATIONS WERE DETECTED NEAR KOALABLAND COVE. WE DON'T KNOW HOW WORD FRED GOT SUCH POWERFUL DEFENSES, BUT BY GOD IT FEELS GOOD TO DO BATTLE WITH HIM.

Panel 12 (caption): THE RIGHTEOUS TOIL TWICE AS HARD.

Man: NOT THAT IT MATTERS, BUT GDP HAS QUADRUPLED THIS YEAR.

Other man: WELL, ALL THE TECH SPINOFFS HAVE HELPED A LOT.

Panel 13 (caption): PEOPLE OF THE FUTURE WILL NOT REMEMBER WHY POVERTY AND DISEASE DISAPPEARED.

Woman: IF IT CAN CURE ALL HUMAN AILMENTS, I CAN FIGHT FRED UNTIL I DIE.

Panel 14 (caption): THEY WILL NOT REMEMBER WHAT PROPELLED THEIR ANCESTORS TO THE STARS.

Man: WON'T A MINUTE. IF WE POINT THE ANTI-GRAVITY MISSILES UP WE CAN GO TO ALPHA CENTAURI.

Panel 15 (caption): OR, IN ANY CASE, THEY WILL CHOOSE NOT TO LOOK INTO IT TOO CAREFULLY.

Woman: DO PEOPLE CREATE NEW INVENTIONS BEFORE THE YEAR 2100 THAT WEREN'T EITHER DESIGNED OR REPURPOSED IMMEDIATELY FOR WAR?

Man: I DON'T THINK THAT'S COUNTED AS PEOPLE AS PEOPLE AT THAT POINT. THEY?
comics.hoverText: We're living in a horrifying dystopia too. It's just hard to tell from the inside.
comics.voteyText: A koala with a wide-open mouth and large, alarmed eyes stares straight ahead in shock.

comics.title: Teaching Math
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

First man (bald, in suit): WE TEACH MATH ALL WRONG!

Second man (in suit, gesturing): WE START KIDS OFF WITH COUNTING NUMBERS, YAH? WE NEED TO START THEM OFF WITH AXIOMS AND SETS! WITH FUNDAMENTALS!

Panel 2:

Second man: IF THEY JUST USE NUMBERS WITHOUT KNOWING WHAT THEY'RE DOING, HOW ARE THEY EVER GOING TO UNDERSTAND MATH?!

First man: THAT'S FINE, SIR. AND WILL YOU BE PAYING FOR YOUR STICKYBUN WITH CASH OR CREDIT?

Panel 3:

Second man (now shown as a cashier/customer scene): FIRST YOU MUST APPRECIATE THAT THE STICKYBUN IS LARGELY MADE UP OF BARYONS.
comics.hoverText: Every sociology education should start with an explanation of the Big Bang.
comics.voteyText:
First man (off-panel, speech): Honestly, you're being a bit eccentric, sir.
(A woman with long flowing dark hair is shown looking off to the side.)

comics.title: Just the tip
comics.comicText:
Title banner: SEX TIP: FRAMING IS EVERYTHING

Panel 1:

A shirtless man with flame-like reddish hair looks toward another person whose face (with hair on the chin) is partly visible at the right edge of the panel.

Man (with reddish hair): "I should warn you... sometimes I get really bored of sex and decide to just come early."
comics.hoverText: Sometimes I get bored twice, if you're up for it.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of a face looking upward in apparent ecstasy or strain, drawn in loose black-and-white sketch style.
Text (handwritten, as if moaned): "OH GODDD" ... "you're dull."

comics.title: Science Magic!
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Magician (a man in a top hat and cape, holding a playing card): I want you to memorize this card.

Boy (a young man with curly hair): Okay!

Panel 2:

Magician: Now, the concept of "four of clubs" has been stored in your hippocampus, embedded in a matrix of protein and energy.

Boy: Okay but what's the trick?

Panel 3:

Magician: Do you really need a card trick when neurochemistry is amazing?!

Boy: (looks unimpressed, frowning)

Panel 4:

Magician (gesturing): Now watch this coin fail to disappear, thanks to conservation of energy!

Sign at bottom left: DR. PARKER, SCIENCE MAGICIAN
comics.hoverText: Behold! As the show continues, entropy inexorably increases!
comics.voteyText: The magician (close-up of his face under the top hat, looking smug): Only greedy children experience wonder!

comics.title: Bacteria Sex
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Mother: Sweetie, it's time we had the sex talk.

Mother: 530 million years ago, some bacteria decided to exchange their DNA to make a new bacterium.

Panel 2:

Mother: Long story short, now if you wanna have a baby you have to squeeze it out of your vagina.

Daughter: WHAT?!

Panel 3:

Mother: Yep. That's why I always tell you to use antibacterial soap.

Daughter: FOR REVENGE.
comics.hoverText: Also comb your hair. That's not for revenge, but you should still do it.
comics.voteyText:
Text (in a speech bubble, shaky hand-lettered): WE ARE LEGION
(Two bacteria, drawn as rod/sausage shapes, are intertwined/embracing.)

comics.title: Human Testing
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (speaker at a podium):

Speaker: Testing on humans is considered unethical.

Panel 2:

Speaker: This is because moral standing is assigned to other creatures based on how similar they are to average human intelligence.

Panel 3:

Speaker: Medical science would benefit from discoveries via human research, but it is wrong for us to experiment on our own kind.

Panel 4 (speaker beside a drawing of a quantum brain):

Speaker: So we created a quantum ultra-brain.

Panel 5:

Speaker: It is as far above us as we are above ants.

Panel 6:

Speaker: To it, human suffering is meaningless. So when it does randomized trials on us, it doesn't consider itself to be doing anything unethical.

Panel 7:

Speaker: The ultra-brain is so complex that we can't even conceptualize it. Thus, we must consider it to be a force of nature. And thus, when it kills a bad thing has happened. But it is no more 'unethical' than an earthquake or a tornado.

Panel 8:

Speaker: And so we can get the vast data that would come with human testing without concerning ourselves about violating our moral principles.

Panel 9 (audience member raising a hand):

Audience member: What sort of questions does the ultra-mind ask?

Panel 10:

Speaker: Yeah... that's the one problem.
comics.hoverText: Anyone wanna teach an ethics class called And Why is *This* SMBC Wrong?
comics.voteyText:
Label: Elsewhere.
A figure: I wonder which humans sough best.
A speech bubble above a sphere with three axis arrows: n = (all of them)

comics.title: Divine Intervention
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Jesus (a man with long hair and a beard): I will prove to you that I am the son of God.

Panel 2:

A bearded onlooker: Behold this rock! Note that it is increasing in temperature despite being hotter than the surrounding.

Panel 3:

Jesus: A complete violation of thermodynamics!

Panel 4:

The onlooker: Naw, that's not a miracle. I'm pretty sure something rock sometimes just get hot.

Jesus: Yeah, my uncle has one of those.

Panel 5:

Jesus: But... that means energy. Brand new energy is being made right here in my hand! Like... where does it come from?

Panel 6:

The onlooker: From the rock. Sometimes rocks just get hot.

Jesus: No they don't!

Panel 7:

Jesus: I am violating the fundamental nature of reality! If this sort of thing happened normally, the entire fabric of the cosmos would unravel!

Panel 8:

The onlooker: This guy sucks. Let's get out of here.

Jesus (thinking/aside): Wait. Wait. Oh, I can, uh, okay watch this.

Panel 9 (caption): LATER...

Jesus: And then he made extra wine!

Crowd member (offscreen): Hallowed be his name.
comics.hoverText: I eagerly await your email about how, actually, the rock must contain radioactive elements.
comics.voteyText: Jesus (speaking, looking off to the side): Maybe they'll receive me better in Rome.

comics.title: BEES
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (top right): A woman with red hair speaks confidently.

Woman: I see the truth bees. The truth.

Panel 2 (bottom left, labeled "EARLIER."): A man and the red-haired woman in conversation.

Woman: When I look at people, I don't see race.

Man: Then what do you see?

Panel 3 (top left): The woman explains.

Woman: Bees. Bees arranged in human form, thinking they're fooling me.
comics.hoverText: But, when I look at bees, I don't see caste.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of the man's face, looking stunned/uneasy.
Man: That's crazy!

comics.title: HEY BROS!
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (man with raised arms, others cheering behind him): BROS! YOU WANNA GO GET WASTED AND TRY TO CONCEIVE OF A MIND THAT IS CREATIVE WITHOUT BEING CONSCIOUS?!

Others: WOOH!

Panel 2 (dark hilly landscape, distant figures): THE EDIFICE OF MY SELF-REGARD IS BUILT OF STRAW.

Panel 3 (the man again, others cheering): BROS! WANNA GO GET WASTED AND TRY TO CHANGE THE WORLD ONLY TO ADMIT TO YOURSELF THAT IMPORTANT PLAYERS IN HISTORY ARE LARGELY THE PRODUCT OF LUCK AND CIRCUMSTANCE?!

Others: WOOH!

Panel 5 (the man, others cheering): BROS! YOU WANNA GO GET WASTED AND DIMLY REALIZE THERE ARE VISTAS OF KNOWLEDGE THAT HUMAN BEINGS ARE BIOLOGICALLY INCAPABLE OF GLIMPSING?!

Others: WOOH!

Panel 7 (a man asking, the bro answering with a smile):

comics.hoverText: I am informed I have no idea what a fraternity is.
comics.voteyText:
First speaker: You have no idea what a fraternity is.
Second speaker: It's a club for people with matching jackets.

comics.title: A Funny Universe
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A woman speaks to a man whose head is a clock face.

Woman: All jokes work the same way.

Clock-head man: You establish a logical order. "Why do the chicken cross the road?"

Panel 2:

Woman: Then, you break the order, while establishing a new, more chaotic order. "To get to the other side."

Clock-head man: That's why I made this universe with increasing entropy. Entropy permits jokes!

Panel 3:

Woman: There are other universes where everything works really orderly, where death is unknown.

Clock-head man: But they don't have that joke about the horse who walks into a bar, and the bartender says he's got a long face.

Panel 4:

Woman: So... okay... so this universe has problems, but we have humor, so... this is the best of all possible worlds.

Clock-head man (laughing): AHAHA HAHAHAHAHA HAHAHAH AHAHA!
comics.hoverText: In order to have that one Monty Python sketch about a dead parrot, you must first invent mortality.
comics.voteyText:
A hand-drawn clock-faced figure leans/floats to the right.
Woman (off-panel, in speech bubble): You're not even in the top 75%, dude.

comics.title: Neato!
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (left): A smiling woman with dark hair speaks excitedly to a man.

Woman: "WHAT? A SELF-ORGANIZING ASSEMBLAGE OF NANOPARTICLES IS SAYING IT'S FALLEN OUT OF LOVE WITH ME?!"

Panel 2 (right): The man speaks back.

Man: "YEAH! A CRYSTAL STRUCTURE OF CALCIUM TITANIUM OXIDE HAS MADE ALL OF MY ENERGY STOCKS WORTHLESS!"

Panel 3 (bottom left): A different scene — someone lying in bed in the dark calls out.

Person in bed: "OH HEY! I'M SLEEPING ALONE FOR THE 102ND NIGHT IN A ROW! WHAT'RE THE ODDS?!"

Panel 4 (bottom right): The woman from earlier smiles serenely, eyes closed, content.

Caption (large text overlaid): "EVERYTHING'S BETTER WITH SCIENCE!"
comics.hoverText: The fact that I'm depressed is a consequence of a singularity billions of years ago!
comics.voteyText:
The same woman, now shown close up with a wide unsettling smile, eyes open.
Woman: "Time to read about how to kill them all."

comics.title: Base Systems
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man (with a wide grin, addressing children): "Computers are binary, meaning they use two symbols: 0 and 1. DNA is quaternary, meaning it uses four symbols: A, C, G, T. Now, how many symbols can you make using your fingers?"

Caption (below panel):

Funtime Activity:

Convincing children that the most natural system is base-11.
comics.hoverText: If you use toes, base-22 is more reasonable.
comics.voteyText: A wide-eyed, slightly unsettled-looking person says: "Unless you're polydactyl. Then, base-13."

comics.title: The Talk
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Girl: Son, it's time we had... THE TALK.

Son: I know all about sex, dad.

Panel 2:

Dad: Oh! You've advanced. Good. Let's have the relationship talk instead.

Panel 3:

Dad: Here goes: it is practically impossible to judge a mate at the outset of a relationship.

Panel 4:

Dad: Many of the things that attract you at first are irrelevant over the long term, especially considering the way in which the members of a couple mold each other over time, developing a shared history.

Panel 5:

Dad: So, even if you're using entirely valid criteria for selection, you may find yourself in an unhappy partnership.

Panel 6:

Dad: And there's nothing you can do about it!

Panel 7:

Dad: Meanwhile, someone might make a major life choice based on shallow metrics, like convenience or social status, and they may turn out to have a love so good it's the rival of any in history.

Panel 8:

Dad: This is a nightmare. Can we just start over and pretend you know way more about sex than me?

Son (grinning): That's what she said.
comics.hoverText: Now, let's have the talk about how individual effort may matter less than other people's inherent ability.
comics.voteyText: Dad (head leaning back, exhausted/exasperated expression): Am I right?

comics.title: The Stats Device
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (narration caption): I have this fantasy where I have a device that gives you stats on anything.

Device speech bubble: 38% of people in this building wear white briefs.

(A person with long orange hair holds a phone-like device.)

Panel 2 (narration caption): I imagine it at least a few times a day.

Device speech bubble: You have sat on this chair 8,743 times.

Panel 3 (narration caption): I have had this fantasy for decades.

Three sub-panels showing the orange-haired person at different ages holding the device:

- Sub-panel A (as a child), device: Zero girls like your haircut.

- Sub-panel B (as a young man), device: Seven more interviews until you get a job.

- Sub-panel C (as a bearded adult), device: Zero spouses like your haircut.

Panel 4 (narration caption): But I only just realized that I have never once imagined using it productively.

Device speech bubble: How about you use me to determine the results of drug trials?

Person's speech bubble: Blah blah blah. Hey, how many different cows are in this burger?

smbc-comics.com
comics.hoverText: It can violate conservation of information, but it can't have rounded corners.
comics.voteyText: A hand-drawn line graph. The vertical axis is labeled "niceness of my clothes" and the horizontal axis is labeled "success." The red curve rises into a small bump near the low-success region, then trends steadily downward toward zero as success increases.

comics.title: Junk
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (narration over a starfield with debris): "The solar system was once a huge mass of space junk."

Panel 2 (narration over a planet orbiting): "But, a few of those planets kept some of that junk orbiting around."

Panel 3 (narration over more planets): "Over time, most of it accreted into planets."

Panel 4 (narration over a ringed planet): "One in particular kept the most, and it is considered the most beautiful planet of all..."

Panel 5 (a woman with a ponytail speaking dismissively to a person with dark hair):

Woman (Jessica): "Just throw out your old power cords! You'll never use them!"

Person with dark hair: "I AM SATURN, JESSICA. SATURN."
comics.hoverText: We need to stop enabling Saturn, you guys.
comics.voteyText: An angry close-up face with a speech bubble: "I'm gonna treat you like Pluto."

comics.title: Truth
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Caption (top): PHILOSOPHY TIP: MAKE ANY QUESTION SOUND PROFOUND BY ADDING THE WORD 'TRUE' TO IT.

An older bald man with white hair on the sides, a white beard, and glasses, wearing a gray suit jacket, sits at a table with his hand on his chin in a thoughtful pose. A hamburger sits on a plate on the table in front of him.

Man: YES, BUT IS IT A TRUE CHEESEBURGER?
comics.hoverText: Seriously, you can write whole books using this technique.
comics.voteyText:
A hand-drawn graph titled "The Quantum Cheese Problem."
The vertical (y) axis is labeled at the top "cheeseburger" (with an arrow) and lower down "hamburger" (with an arrow). The horizontal (x) axis is labeled "cheese (grams)."
A red line stays flat and low (at the "hamburger" level) along the left, then jumps sharply straight up to the high "cheeseburger" level and continues flat across the rest of the graph — a step function.

comics.title: Scrooge
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Scrooge (small elderly man): THANK YOU FOR VISITING ME, SPIRITS OF CHRISTMAS.

Ghost of Christmas Present (jolly bearded figure with a holly wreath): NO PROB, SCROOGE.

Panel 2:

Scrooge: I DO HAVE ONE QUESTION THOUGH.

Ghost of Christmas Past (small white-haired figure): YES?

Panel 3:

Scrooge: WHAT DO YOU DO WHEN POOR PEOPLE NEED HELP MAKING A LIFE CHOICE?

Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come (hooded cloaked figure): [silent]

Ghost of Christmas Present: FUCK THOSE PEOPLE!
comics.hoverText: Calm down Ghost of Christmas present. Please. You're drunk, and you're scaring us.
comics.voteyText:
Scrooge (speech bubble): Now bring me more food!
(A large grinning bearded face — the Ghost of Christmas Present — looms in close-up.)

comics.title: Dark Matters
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man (with wavy hair): Hey baby, if I were dark energy and you were dark matter... would you want to do couple-matter explicitly with me?

Woman: Ooh, that sounds--

Panel 2:

Woman: --my thesis is due tomorrow!

Panel 3:

Man: Wait. Is this about sex or--

Woman: Who has time for sex?!
comics.hoverText: If you could work gravity waves into it, I'd appreciate that.
comics.voteyText: Man (shocked, sweating): Is THAT why people go to bars?!

comics.title: Wilderness Training
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A brown bear, looking alarmed, reacts to seeing people.

Bear: OH GOD! A HUMAN!

Panel 2: The bear, sweating, tries to reassure itself while two small human figures stand in the distance.

Bear: CALM DOWN, FRANK. HE'S PROBABLY JUST AS SCARED AS YOU ARE.

Panel 3: The bear thinks back, sweating nervously.

Bear: QUICK... WHAT WAS IT THEY TAUGHT YOU IN WILDERNESS TRAINING? OH! TRY TO CONVINCE HIM THAT YOU'RE A SCARY, DANGEROUS BEAR.

Panel 4: The bear opens its mouth wide and roars, throwing its paws up.

Bear: RAAUGH!

Panel 5: The bear, relieved and pleased with itself.

Bear: WOW! I CAN'T BELIEVE THAT WORKED!

Panel 6: The two human hikers walk away across a green landscape, having fled.
comics.hoverText: This is exactly how arms work.
comics.voteyText:
Handwritten caption: This is exactly what bears look like.
- Science

comics.title: New Valentines
comics.comicText:
Title banner: NEW DIRECTIONS FOR VALENTINE'S DAY:

Section 1 heading: SURPRISING SUBJECT MATTER...

Panel: A loaf of bread (with a cartoon face) speaks to a cow.

Bread: "I WOULD LOAF TO FUCK YOU."

Cow: "I STILL LOVE YOU BUT I HAVE COME TO REALIZE THAT I'M UDDERLY GAY."

Section 2 heading: GENTLE REMINDERS...

Panel: A carton of milk speaks to a glass of pink liquid (a latte).

Milk carton: "I LIKE YOU A LATTE! BUT YOU'VE BEEN LATE ON CHILD SUPPORT FOR 3 MONTHS NOW!"

Glass (latte): "YOU STILL OWE ME MONEY. AND YOUR HEART. OR WHATEVER. SERIOUSLY, THOUGH."

Glass of milk: "I WOULD LOAF TO FUCK YOU."

comics.hoverText: Will you BEE enforcing that restraining order?
comics.voteyText:
Heading box: EDUCATIONAL
A hand-drawn line graph. The vertical axis is labeled "LIKELIHOOD YOU'LL GET THEM" and the horizontal axis is labeled "QUALITY OF MATES." The curve starts high on the left and drops steeply as quality increases, flattening out near zero on the right. An arrow points to the low, flat far-right portion of the curve, labeled "me!"

comics.title: Augmented Reality
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man (wearing a glasses-like device over one eye): "With this device, I can have all sorts of information beamed directly into my eye."

Woman: "What sort of information?"

Man: "Like... discounts at Starbucks. And... weather reports?"

Caption (below panel): Real life is bullshit.
comics.hoverText: I still want one.
comics.voteyText: Handwritten note: "for posterity: This joke about Google Glass was out of date on day one."

comics.title: Immortality
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (header): WE DISCOVERED THE CURE FOR AGING.

Woman (red hair): WOOH! FUCK MAKING ART! FUCK STORING FUCK MINING BABIES! AND BY GOD FUCK RECONSIDERING MY SOCIAL VALUE!

Panel 2 (header): BUT THERE WAS A SMALL ISSUE.

Woman: SINCE YOU ACCIDENTALLY KILLED MRS. SANDERS, YOU MUST PAY THE FAMILY HER EXPECTED LIFETIME EARNINGS. WE CALCULATE THAT TO BE INFINITY DOLLARS.

Panel 3 (header): THE ISSUE GREW.

Woman: WHEN YOU CUT OFF MR. LARSON IN TRAFFIC, IT SLIGHTLY SLOWED DOWN THE PROGRESS OF HIS ENTIRE LIFE IN A WAY THAT'LL RESOUND THROUGH ETERNITY. WE CALCULATE THE COST TO BE INFINITY DOLLARS.

Panel 4 (header): BAD BEHAVIOR BECAME FINANCIALLY RISKY.

Woman: WHEN YOU CALLED ME A POSTRON, I WAS EMOTIONALLY HARMED AND I LOST 3.2 MINUTES OF MY TIME. AS PER THE DICTIONARY, I AM WILLING TO SETTLE FOR ONE HUNDRED TRILLION DOLLARS.

Panel 5 (header): THE WORLD WAS AT PEACE.

Man: LAWYERS CAN ONLY DETECT MOTION. IF I STAY PERFECTLY MOTIONLESS, I'LL BE SAFE.

Panel 6 (header): GIVEN THE SUDDEN USELESSNESS OF HUMANS, WE WERE FORCED TO DEVELOP ROBOT LABOR.

Woman: YOU CAN'T SUE ME FOR INFINITE MONEY FOR ACCIDENTALLY TAPPING YOU BECAUSE YOU ARE NOT COMPOSED LARGELY OF HYDROCARBONS!

Robot: HUMANS ARE WEIRD

Panel 7 (header): UTOPIA.

Robot: ONCE LABORERS COULD SELF-MODIFY PRODUCTIVITY GREW EXPONENTIALLY.

Floating robot/AI: THANKS TO THIS UPGRADE, I HAVE NO EXTRA ARM AND I FEEL NO EXISTENTIAL DREAD ABOUT SPENDING ETERNITY ASSEMBLING PILLOWS FOR HEMORRHOIDS.

Panel 8 (header): ONCE WEALTH WAS DECOUPLED FROM HUMAN LABOR WE ENTERED A TECHNOLOGICAL UTOPIA.

Woman: ALL GOODS AND SERVICES ARE FREE IN ANY QUANTITY! IT IS NOW ON EARTH AS IT IS IN HEAVEN!

Panel 9 (header): OF COURSE, THERE WAS SOME PENT-UP EMOTION TO BE DEALT WITH.

Woman 1: SO, I CAN COMMIT ANY CRIME THAT WOULD PREVIOUSLY HAVE BEEN RESOLVED WITH MONEY, AND THERE'S NO CONSEQUENCES?

Woman 2: UM--

Woman 1: I'M GONNA POLLUTE EVERY OCEAN, THEN KEY EVERY CAR!

Panel 10 (header): THE ORGY OF PROPERTY DESTRUCTION UNDID ALL OF THE RECENT PROGRESS.

Woman: ALL ROBOTS MUST USE THEIR AI REASONING ABILITY IS POORLY ADAPTED TO A TECHNOLOGICAL ECONOMY!

Robot: WOW! MY DERANGE MATCHES MY EXPECTATION SO PERFECTLY.

Panel 11 (header): HONESTLY? IT'S BETTER THIS WAY.

Woman: NOW THAT LIFE IS SHORT AGAIN, I'M REALLY GONNA APPRECIATE MY SMALL ACTS OF PASSIVE AGGRESSION.
comics.hoverText: You gotta steal like nobody's watching, punch like you'll never be hurt, slander like there's nobody listening...
comics.voteyText: Woman (glasses, in speech bubble): And that's the only problem with longevity.

comics.title: Live Forever
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (dark hair): I wouldn't want to live forever.

Panel 2:

Woman (long hair): First you'd have sex with two partners at once, then three, then four, and so on.

Panel 3:

Woman (dark hair): Sure, it'd be fun for a while, but eventually you'd hit the biggest number and it'd get pointless.

Panel 4:

Woman (long hair): Biggest number?

Panel 5:

Woman (dark hair): Yeah. The biggest number. 1.233.

Panel 6:

Woman (long hair): What about 1.234?

Woman (dark hair, now wild-eyed and excited): I WANT TO LIVE! I WANT TO LIIIIIVE!
comics.hoverText: But there IS a finite number of humans.
comics.voteyText: A hand-drawn graph in black ink. The vertical axis is labeled "pleasure" and the horizontal axis is labeled "sex partners." A curve rises steeply at first and then flattens as it approaches the top right. At the top of the curve, a red arrow points to it with the red label: "gravitational collapse".

comics.title: Proposals for New Chess Pieces
comics.comicText:
Title: PROPOSALS FOR NEW CHESS PIECES

BISHOP-KICKER

Rules: Moves like King. When next to a bishop, you may choose to move that bishop to any adjacent square.

BUREAUCRAT

Rules: Can only move from current square back to current square, without interfering with pieces in between.

WILDERNESS PRESERVER

Rules: Moves like King. Any space touched by Wilderness Preserver is no longer passable by other pieces.

COMMUNIST

Rules: Moves like bishop. If you remove your communist from the game, for the next three turns, all pieces are equal because you are now playing checkers.

CRAPPY SPY

Rules: Moves like pawn. While on board, you can peek at the other player's pieces.

GORTAK, THE WORLD-EATER

Rules: Remove three queens you control from the game to summon Gortak. If Gortak enters the game, nobody ever wins at chess ever again.
comics.hoverText: Also, there's the Red Queen, who keeps moving while staying in the same place.
comics.voteyText: Gortak (a horned, fanged monster) with a sad, pleading expression. Caption: "Gortak just want hug"

comics.title: Condemned
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (Person A, off-panel/speaking): There's this George Santayana quote: "Those who cannot remember the past are condemned to repeat it."

Person B: Yeah!

Panel 2 (Person A): But if you actually read the quote, you only have to look at the previous sentence to realize that it doesn't mean what everyone thinks it means.

Panel 3 (Person A): "...When experience is not retained, as among savages, infancy is perpetual. Those who cannot remember the past are condemned to repeat it."

Panel 4 (Person B): Huh. So it's actually a point about 'savages' without historical records.

Panel 5 (Person A): Right. It's not about people today who don't read enough.

Panel 6 (Person B): But that means...

Person A: People who don't know the past or that quote are condemned to repeat it incorrectly.

Panel 7 (Person A): Though, in fairness, its history has no bearing on whether the shortened quote is valid.

Panel 8 (Person B): I don't want to understand the world. I just want to be right.
comics.hoverText: Pro Tip: Any quote that sounds pithy was either (A) never said by the person who supposedly said it, or (B) at least somewhat contradicted by the surrounding sentences in the original source.
comics.voteyText: A woman with curly hair looks down with a tired, deadpan expression. Speech bubble: Are you writing this down?

comics.title: Unicorns
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A woman with gray hair speaks.

Woman: The unicorn line in the woods. And, they will only play with you if you're a virgin.

A second person (off to the side): What?! How would they figure that out?

Panel 2:

The woman replies.

Woman: They just know.

Panel 3:

A close-up of a unicorn's face, speaking.

Unicorn: I can detect an intact hymen at 200 paces.

Panel 4:

A woman with flame-like orange hair speaks to the unicorn.

Orange-haired woman: I think I'm done with unicorns.

Unicorn: Yeah, they creep me out, too.
comics.hoverText: Unicorns really need to let go of outmoded notions of purity.
comics.voteyText: A close-up line drawing of the unicorn's face and snout. A speech bubble nearby reads "Hooray." The unicorn's tongue licks out toward something below.

comics.title: The Definition of Unlife
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Young person: "Grampa, I don't like the word 'undead.' It's chauvinistic."

Panel 2:

Grampa: "The undead can move, communicate, think. They have DNA. They're made of hydrocarbons. They create entropy."

Panel 3:

Young person: "They're just a form of life that happens to look similar to dead humans. So why categorize them as not alive and not dead?"

Panel 4:

Grampa: "But if the criterion for undeadness is just 'alive, but looks dead,' then we should call anyone over 60 undead!"

Panel 5:

Grampa: "One quality of life is the ability to reproduce. Zombies, vampires, mummies, none of them can do it."

Panel 6:

Young person: "Oh my god. That's true of old people too."

Panel 7:

Young person: "Are you saying you're undead?!"

Grampa: "Technically only gramma is undead."
comics.hoverText: You are all anti-undead bigots.
comics.voteyText: Gramma (a figure with a wide-open, fang-filled mouth): "WHO WANTS COOKIES?!"

comics.title: DAMN
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A caveman with long hair and a beard speaks to a group of cave people standing around.

Caveman: DAMN! ALL FEMALES WANT MATE WITH PIG. PIG CAN MAKE ZAZA HANDS LONGER THAN ANYONE.

Panel 2:

Caption box: 50,000 YEARS LATER...

A modern man with glasses sits and thinks.

Caption/text: HUMAN MALES EVOLVED LARGE UPPER BODIES FOR THROWING ROCKS AND SPEARS.
comics.hoverText: Also, beards evolved for doing the dishes.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of a man's face speaking, with a furrowed, earnest expression.
Man: WISH ME SPOKE ENGLISH WITH PROPER GRAMMAR.

comics.title: HAHAHA!
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man with flame-like hair (an economist) stands in Hell, gesturing triumphantly while a red demon with horns digs at the ground with a pitchfork amid flames.

Economist: "HAHAHAHA! THE EFFECTIVENESS OF YOUR TORTURE OBEYS THE LAW OF DIMINISHING MARGINAL UTILITY!"

Caption (below panel): Economists are no longer welcome in Hell.
comics.hoverText: This is why they live so long.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up drawing of a balding older man's smug face.
Text (handwritten, above him): "I don't belong everywhere."

comics.title: Morale Boost
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man in a suit (an office manager): Thanks to the magic of programmable matter and advanced acoustics, the very fabric of our office is a morale booster.

Panel 2:

Manager: When you say something, instead of reflecting the noise randomly, the walls adjust shape to capture the sound and amplify it, changing it to the phrase "I know what you do and project it directly into the speaker's ears."

Panel 3:

Manager: We think employees will find it to be reassuring. It's an acknowledgement that you know they're doing good work.

Panel 4:

Manager: If they shout, then it is enough acoustic energy to repeat the phrase over and over and over.

Panel 5:

Manager: Interestingly, sometimes the phrase itself seems to provoke shouting, which creates a virtuous cycle of morale boosting.

Panel 6:

A second man (a coworker): Do any of them ever blink?

Manager: One of the effects of high morale is that you stop sleeping.
comics.hoverText: When there's no sound, the wall simply makes your own face, but with dead vacant eyes.
comics.voteyText: A large, manic close-up face with wide unblinking eyes and a strained grin: I'm glad people appreciate me

comics.title: Ethics?!
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man: Ethics? What do you have ethics?

Glowing green entity: Sure. No killing, no stealing, do unto others as you would be done by.

Panel 2:

Man: It's not possible.

Glowing green entity: Look, I'm a scientist. I study comparative intelligence.

Panel 3:

Glowing green entity: Intelligences are too complicated to study from first principles, so to study intelligence we create a standard mind, and we break something. Then we see how its society develops. Sort of like your 'knock-out' mice.

Panel 4:

Glowing green entity: Humans ran an experiment in minds that haven't got a high enough sense in human language for it. A morality. Original. The ability to detect moral truth via the senses.

Glowing green entity (continued): We completely lack it (or you don't) and yet you still have a basic set of laws that close to how things are robust to our experiments!

Panel 5:

Man: What do you mean 'close to true'?

Glowing green entity: Oh.

Panel 6:

Glowing green entity: Yeah?

Panel 7:

Man: It's an affront to every god in the multiverse.

Panel 8:

Man: Then I defy heaven!

Glowing green entity: ...
comics.hoverText: We also knocked out love, which is why you developed sex.
comics.voteyText: A pie with rays of light emanating from a glowing egg-shaped object above it bearing a pentagram. (The pie is being venerated / the man's defiance has been redirected toward worshipping a pie.)

comics.title: A Confession
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman: I have a confession.

Panel 2:

Woman: All these years, every time we've high-fived, I carefully kept my thumb folded.

(A man stands listening.)

Panel 3:

Woman: Thus, every time you-- ow! gave me five-- ow! I only owed you back four.

(Small label near the man: "ow")

Panel 4:

Woman: Your cumulative deficit is now 100,000 fingers, which is 12,000 double high-fives.

Panel 5:

Woman: It is as if I requested a 'high-five down low' and held out my hands only to remove them prior to your compliance with my request ten thousand times.

(Man, throwing his head back in anguish): NOOOOO!

Panel 6:

Man (in silhouette): I trusted you.

Woman (in silhouette): Also, every time I gave you a thumbs up, it was 17/16 radians off center.
comics.hoverText: Actually, wait, I forgot to factor in three percent interest.
comics.voteyText:
Text: 'meh.'
A large hand giving a thumbs up is shown, but the thumb is bent over and tucked across the curled fingers rather than pointing up.

comics.title: Autism and Vaccines
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A woman wearing glasses and a green shirt (off to the right, a man in a lab coat beside her): "WAIT A MINUTE. AUTISM-SPECTRUM PEOPLE ARE OVER-REPRESENTED IN RESEARCH SCIENCE. BUT... BUT THAT MEANS..."

Man in lab coat: "MY GOD..."

comics.title: Princesses
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (caption): In a lot of movies now, the princess character does important stuff instead of just getting saved.

Panel 2 — Two women in conversation.

Woman A: Great! Now it's the girls who are subtly legitimating a system of hereditary aristocracy.

Panel 3

Woman A: How nice that they can have charming little adventures, while dwelling in the monument of the laborer's toil.

Panel 4

Woman A: I think the Princess in Beauty and the Beast started life as a peasant.

Woman B: Class traitor!
