comics.voteyText: A close-up of a woman (the Beast's enchanted-object skeptic) looking up, exasperated, saying: Why are the teacups so proud of their chains?!

comics.title: Methods for Going to Space
comics.comicText:
Title (header bar): METHODS FOR GOING TO SPACE, WITH PROBLEMS AND SOLUTIONS

The comic is a table with three columns: METHOD | PROBLEM | SOLUTION.

Row 1 — METHOD: Rocket | PROBLEM: Must lift heavy fuel, making launches very expensive. | SOLUTION: Spend lots of money.

Row 2 — METHOD: Mass driver | PROBLEM: High speed encounter with atmosphere necessitates extremely tall structure. | SOLUTION: New theme park ride.

Row 3 — METHOD: Skyhook | PROBLEM: Have to catch cable in space. | SOLUTION: ...magnets?

Row 4 — METHOD: Rotating skyhook | PROBLEM: Have to catch rotating cable in space. | SOLUTION: Embrace risk of awesome death.

Row 5 — METHOD: Space elevator | PROBLEM: No material strong enough to make it. | SOLUTION: Remove half of Earth's mass. Most of it not that great anyway.

Row 6 — METHOD: Ballistic cannon | PROBLEM: Acceleration would liquify humans. | SOLUTION: Put them back together later?

Row 7 — METHOD: Space fountain | PROBLEM: Enormous structure that collapses the moment you stop supplying it massive power. | SOLUTION: If goes awry, make amusing comparison to financial sector.

Row 8 — METHOD: High altitude balloon launch | PROBLEM: NO. We are NOT running an entire launch operation from a gigantic mega-blimp. | SOLUTION: But— NO. But— NO! Come on pleeease. NO.
comics.hoverText: Alternate method: Convert humans to hydrogen, float to space, reassemble.
comics.voteyText:
A handwritten note reads:
Idea:
Launch Earth while rocket stays put.

comics.title: Salad
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A bearded man sits across from a smiling older woman with gray hair in a red shirt, at a counter (a salad bar). The man speaks.

Man: I PAY BY WEIGHT?! YOU'RE LETTING ME BUY SALAD BY WEIGHT?

Panel 2:

The man leans in, gesturing.

Man: HAHA! THEN WHAT'S TO STOP ME FROM LOADING UP ON HIGH PRICED-TO-WEIGHT RATIO ITEMS, LIKE CROUTONS, DRIED FRUIT, AND CRUMBLED CHEESE?!

Panel 3:

The man continues, leaning across the counter.

Man: WHAT'S TO STOP ME FROM SELECTING MY SALAD ENTIRELY BASED ON RUNNING INSTEAD OF MAKING A SALAD THAT I ACTUALLY WANT?

Panel 4:

The woman gestures toward a small sign/menu on the counter.

Woman: PLEASE SEE THE NOTE ON YOUR MENU.

Sign on counter reads: Menu

Panel 5:

The man pauses, mouth closed, considering.

(sound/beat): OK

Panel 6:

Close-up of the man's hands holding up a yellow handwritten note. The note reads:

"Please be aware: The salad is a metaphor for life."
comics.hoverText: Douse thy life in the ranch dressing of compassion!
comics.voteyText:
A yellow sticky note in handwriting reads:
"Also, the sandwich is a symbol representing Womanhood."

comics.title: Paleoanthropology
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Child: Dad, according to the museum humans had modern brains for at least 100,000 years before they figured out how to make pottery! How did it take so long?

Panel 2:

Dad: Well, the average lifespan was only about 25 back in those days.

Panel 3:

Dad: So most people were probably just a few years out of college, working as a barista and re-evaluating their choices, and WHAMMO! Gored by a mammoth.

Panel 4:

Dad: Others would've been in their third year of graduate education, just starting to work independently, when nearby tribes burned down their village, killed the men and enslaved the women and children.

Panel 5:

Dad: It was a much harder time. For instance, people don't go to Burger King as often, because worldwide, the average household income was about $50 a year.

Panel 6:

Child: Wowww...

Panel 7:

Child: How do you know so much about history?

Dad: Most of it's obvious.
comics.hoverText: Also there were fewer teenage pregnancies because nobody had invented the calendar.
comics.voteyText: Thought bubble (over a crude cave-painting-style stick figure of a running person holding a spear): What am I doing with my life

comics.title: The Lord Sayeth
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A bearded man with long hair and a purple robe (depicted as Jesus) stands amid a crowd, addressing them.

Man (Jesus): "AND WHEN THE MAN SAT DOWN, IT WAS AS IF THE SALT SEA WERE UPON THE LAND."

Caption (below panel): Jesus once again gave his parable about wiping down gym equipment after use.
comics.hoverText: And ye shall know the stink by its stank.
comics.voteyText:
A reclining bearded man (loosely sketched) speaks.
Man: "It's like a fruitless tree or whatever"

comics.title: Gender Stereotypes
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man (red-haired): Hey, wanna play a game where we use video gaming behavior to be the best at reinforcing gender stereotypes?

Woman (dark hair): No?

Panel 2:

Man: Not willing to take risks? A fantastic opening move.

Panel 3:

Woman: That's not what I meant! Calm down, listen...

Man: No, I am not.

Panel 4:

Man: Conclusion instead of confrontation! You are incredible at this.

Woman: Contradicting yourself? How girlish!

Panel 5:

Woman: Is there anything I could do that you would not consider stereotypical?

Panel 6:

Man: A question whose answer is obvious! You are a virtuoso.

Panel 7:

Woman: I quit! Quitting rather than negotiating! I concede! I concede!

Panel 8:

Woman: No. No. There is no game! I do not engage in destructive behavior purely for amusement!

Man: You're saying I do because I'm a man?

Panel 9:

Woman: I- That means I'm winning just by playing the game!

Man (arms raised in triumph): Winner! Winner! Winner!

Panel 10:

Woman: I'm sure there's a lesson here, but I'm too angry to care.
comics.hoverText: I'm just realizing I always give my jerk characters red hair. It's nice to see one's self-hatred manifested so plainly.
comics.voteyText: Handwritten in ornate script: Lesson: Redheads are dicks.

comics.title: Delta-v
comics.comicText:
Title (top banner): ROCKET ENGINEERS ARE THE ENGINEERIEST ENGINEERS

Panel 1 (label: NORMAL ENGINEER:)

A woman with dark hair (seen from behind/side) speaks to a man with reddish-brown hair.

Woman: WHAT'S DELTA-V?

Man: ... CHANGE IN VELOCITY?

Panel 2 (label: ROCKET ENGINEER:)

The same dark-haired woman speaks to a smiling woman with curly red hair and round glasses, who is holding a metal bucket.

Dark-haired woman: WHAT'S DELTA-V?

Red-haired woman: OH!! I HAVE SOME IN THIS BUCKET!

smbc-comics.com
comics.hoverText: RUN! RUN! THE BUCKET IS REACTING WITH THE AIR!
comics.voteyText:
Large hand-lettered text: RUN!
Beneath it, a sketchy line-art drawing of a shocked/screaming face.

comics.title: The Speech Interceptor
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Narration: Given the ever more stupid noises coming out of the mouths of world leaders, the planet is approaching a crisis.

Panel 2:

First man (seated): We can no longer stand idly by as the stupidity arms race continues.

Second man (standing): So we have created a 'Stupidio Speech Defense System.'

Panel 3:

Narration: We model politicians as hollow spheres fluxing stupidity in every direction.

(Diagram: an empty circle with arrows pointing outward in all directions.)

Panel 4:

Narration: News corporations are modeled as simultaneous amplifiers and emitters of stupidity, which thus create an internal stupidity feedback loop.

(Diagram: a circle with triangles and arrows circulating around its interior.)

Panel 5:

Narration: When a dangerously stupid flux occurs, our system creates the opposite sound wave pattern and fires it in the direction of the sphere.

(Diagram: a stick figure emitting wavy lines toward a target.)

Panel 6:

Narration: The flux is thus nullified, saving society from both the initial stupidity and the ensuing chain reaction.

(Diagram: two arrows converge on a colorful explosion burst. The green arrow is labeled 'LET'S EAT IMMIGRANTS'; the purple arrow is labeled with the same phrase 'LET'S EAT IMMIGRANTS' written mirror-reversed, representing the inverted sound wave.)

Panel 7:

Second man (standing): Via this strategic defense initiative, we can nullify the greatest danger posed by stupid leaders.

Panel 8:

First man (seated): Some leaders may oppose having a giant array of cannons facing their mouths all the time. But if they have nothing stupid to say, then they have nothing to fear.

Panel 9:

Second man (standing): Maybe we should all just be more active in our elections.

First man (seated): But who has the time?
comics.hoverText: IT'S NOT TOO LATE. WE CAN DO THIS. WE MUST DO THIS.
comics.voteyText:
Woman (off to the side, exasperated): That's not how sound works.
Man (at a desk/podium): I know.
Small figure (bottom left): No!

comics.title: Predictions
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Caption: THE PROBLEM WITH PREDICTIONS OF THE FUTURE...

A smiling man with a mustache, gesturing as he speaks: IN THE FUTURE, AUTOMATION WILL REDUCE THE WORK DAY FROM 12 HOURS TO 4 TO 3 TO 2! IT WILL BE A LIFE OF PLEASURE, LEISURE, AND SELF-CULTIVATION.

Panel 2:

Caption: IS THE ASSUMPTION THAT SOCIETY COORDINATES ITSELF RATIONALLY.

The same man, now looking more serious: WE NEED YOU TO WORK FOR THIRTY MINUTES EACH MORNING, THEN SECRETLY BROWSE THE INTERNET UNTIL 5 PM.
comics.hoverText: You will work hard, but your grandchildren will get to pretend to browse the internet for 7 hours and 45 minutes.
comics.voteyText:
An off-panel voice in a speech bubble: If you stop redditing, it's because you're lazy
A bespectacled person looks up, frowning and uneasy.

comics.title: Just Watch
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Dark-haired woman (sitting on a couch): This show is terrible.

Red-haired woman (beside her): Of course it is.

Panel 2:

Red-haired woman: You have to let it grind you down for a while. Let it lower your standards for plot, character, dialog, and acting.

Panel 3:

Red-haired woman (cradling the dark-haired woman's head): Let it wash over you. It will smooth your edges. Yes, forget, my child. All will be well.

Panel 4:

A man on a television screen: We can time travel directly into the plot hole!

Panel 5:

Dark-haired woman (smiling, awed): It's so clever!
comics.hoverText: Willing to bet this results in more reader anger than that one time I did a comic about two Jesuses fighting to mate with a third Jesus.
comics.voteyText: A crudely drawn face with mouth agape: Give me all of it.

comics.title: The Charming Old Days
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (red hair): Wow! It's like we're back in the 19th century!

Panel 2:

Man (dark hair): Because the power's out?

Woman: Because I secretly gave you typhus.

Panel 3:

Man: Take me to a hospital!

Woman: I don't think women were allowed to drive back then.
comics.hoverText: I'm surprised nobody's quantified exactly how over-represented turtlenecks are in SMBC.
comics.voteyText: Woman (close-up, angry expression): You know it took a lot of work to get that typhus!

comics.title: Underworld
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A distraught man with shaggy hair stands in a barren world.

Man: NO. SHE CAN'T BE DEAD. I WILL FIND HER! I WILL GO BEYOND THIS WORLD, INTO THE BOWELS OF HELL ITSELF, BUT I WILL FIND HER.

Panel 2: The man stands before a small structure (a house or building) engulfed in flames against a dark landscape.

Panel 3: The man leaps downward into a glowing red chasm, falling into hell.

Panel 4: The man descends through a vast, dark, rocky underworld toward a distant glowing red eye/light.

Panel 5: The man approaches a horned red devil sitting in the fiery underworld.

Man: HEY, HAVE YOU SEEN SALLY JENKINS?

Devil: HMM. I'LL LOOK IN THE LOG.

Panel 6: The devil offers help cheerfully.

Devil: AH YEAH, HERE WE ARE. I'LL GIVE YOU A RIDE.

Panel 7: Caption: SOON...

A red-haired woman (Sally) and the man face each other.

Sally: SO YOU JUST ASSUMED I WAS IN HELL?!

Man: OK LIKE YOU'RE NOT EVEN A LITTLE SURPRISED.
comics.hoverText: Oh, wow, your Mom's here too? This place is like a freakin' Wal-Mart.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of the woman's face, looking unimpressed.
Woman (speech bubble): I knew you in college.

comics.title: Life Changes
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman: Ugh, first I was at the age where everyone's getting married, so I had to go to a billion weddings.

Panel 2:

Woman: Now, I'm at the age where everyone's having babies. Everywhere I look, it's babies babies babies babies.

Panel 3:

Man: I'm at the age where everyone's dying.

Woman: Babies are okay.
comics.hoverText: GOD why are friends and relations FOREVER informing me of major life moments?
comics.voteyText: Man (looking glum): At least dead people don't post about it on Facebook.

comics.title: Talking to Children
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A young girl stands beside a stack of blocks. A woman (her mother) speaks to her.

Mother: Good job!

A second woman (a grandmother figure) reacts sharply.

Grandmother: No! You're not supposed to say that!

Panel 2:

Grandmother: Now she'll feel she needs your approval for all actions! She won't self-motivate!

Panel 3:

Mother (to the girl, backpedaling): Oh. I mean, uh... Wow, you're so smart... NO!

Panel 4 (the grandmother, close-up):

Grandmother: If you say she's smart, she'll think intelligence is intrinsic instead of seeking self-improvement.

Panel 5:

Grandmother: Come on! You have to say something! She'll perceive your silence as indifference!

Panel 6:

The mother, overwhelmed, addresses the girl in a flat, exhausted monotone.

Mother: Goon...

Panel 7:

The mother reads from a document to the girl.

Mother: This document shall govern the implications of the following statement which shall only be construed as a response to the construction of a block castle between the hours of 9 and 10am today.

Girl: It's nice.
comics.hoverText: This statement shall not be construed as having or lacking meaning.
comics.voteyText:
A woman's face in profile, looking weary.
Woman (thought/speech): I wonder how parents used to manage.

comics.title: Work
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Child (off to the side, behind the father): Dad, why do you sit at the computer all day when it just brings you stress?

Panel 2:

Father (glasses, sitting at the computer): Well, the world generates a certain amount of stress each day.

Panel 3:

Father: People agree to absorb some of the stress in exchange, we are given money so that we can have houses and food.

Panel 4:

Father: It'd be sort of like if you had a mouse in a box with a food pellet dispenser that also delivered electric shocks at random intensities.

Panel 5:

Child: That sounds awful.

Father: It's not so bad.

Panel 6:

Father: If you make sure to get your shock and pellet every day toward the end of your life you can just eat off your saved pellets.

Panel 7:

Child: Do you have a lot of pellets saved?

Father: Well, first I have to pay back the pellets I borrowed so I could be allowed in the box.
comics.hoverText: That said, if anyone wants to invent a food pellet machine for humans, I'll buy it.
comics.voteyText: Father (looking strained, speaking to the child): Now leave so me and the computer can have Daddy Time.

comics.title: Politics
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Caption: VIEWPOINTS I UNDERSTAND:

Man with dark hair: I think politicians are often self-interested seekers of power, and you can understand a lot of their actions through that prism.

Panel 2:

Caption: VIEWPOINTS I DON'T UNDERSTAND:

Man with reddish hair (wide-eyed, intense): I think we're all slaves to the secret illuminati!

Panel 3:

Caption: VIEWPOINTS I REALLY DON'T UNDERSTAND:

Man with orange/flame-like hair (deadpan): I think we are all slaves to the secret illuminati, but TV is pretty good so... ech.
comics.hoverText: In time, Weinersmith would come to feel regret over sparking the Great Conspiracy Theorist Uprising.
comics.voteyText: A hooded, cloaked figure (with a pyramid/all-seeing-eye symbol on its robe) raises a hand and shouts: Release more Simpsons!

comics.title: Billions and billions
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A woman with brown hair speaks directly to the reader.

Woman: There are 200 billion galaxies in the universe, with 200 billion stars in each of them. Each star is orbited by half a dozen planets. In all this space, only Earth harbors life. We are alone in a vast empty cosmos. And yet, I share a bathroom with two roommates.

Caption below panel:

This is the most distressing implication of the Rare Earth Hypothesis.
comics.hoverText: AND NOBODY CLEANS UNDER THE SEAT. NOBODY
comics.voteyText:
Hand-lettered text on a white panel:
This is the best argument for increasing the budget for NASA.

comics.title: Three Wishes
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man: A genie! So I get three wishes? I want lust, wealth and true love and--

Genie: Nope.

Panel 2:

Man: For his third wish, the last guy who found the lamp wished that the next guy to find the lamp just gets a box of raisins.

Panel 3:

Genie: Here you go.

Panel 4:

Man: Did he also wish that the raisins be gross?

Genie: I try to follow the spirit of the request.
comics.hoverText: Also your children like their stepfather better.
comics.voteyText: Genie: Also, your wife finds your jokes tiresome.

comics.title: Euler's Identity
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman with dark hair (gesturing): The most profound equation is Euler's identity.

(equation shown) e^(i·π) + 1 = 0

Panel 2:

Woman with dark hair: Thus we propose using it as the standard unit of profundity!

Panel 3:

Woman with red/pink hair: Does this unit serve any mathematical purpose?

Panel 4:

Woman with dark hair: No. But that fact alone automatically qualifies it for 10 milli-Eulers.

Panel 5:

Woman with dark hair: Also, as a pragmatic matter, it's very useful for shutting down emotional conversations that occur while eating upon the vault of heaven in a mystic coalescence of wonder and fear.

Panel 6:

Caption: LATER...

Woman with dark hair (lying on grass under the stars, with a partner): These same stars shone upon Socrates.

Partner: 0.01

Woman with dark hair: Fuck you.
comics.hoverText: The highest utility of mathematics is ruining everything for everyone.
comics.voteyText: Handwritten note: This comic: -10^100 Eulers

comics.title: Unicorns!
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Girl (with pigtails, in pink dress): This is Poppy the unicorn!

Panel 2:

Girl: She eats grass in the meadow and her poops are made of puuuuure sugar!

Panel 3:

Man (in suit and sunglasses): Wait. She can convert forage grass directly into chemically pure monosaccharides?

Girl: I guess so!

Panel 4:

Man (gesturing, holding a stack of cash): Bring me more of them.

Panel 5:

Caption: Soon...

Sign on building: LEGENDARY BIOFUELS, INC

Sign below: NO UNAUTHORIZED ADMITTANCE
comics.hoverText: Scene from the sequel to Augie and the Green Knight.
comics.voteyText:
Handwritten text: I'm helping the environment
(A unicorn's head is shown in profile, looking somewhat unhappy/uneasy.)

comics.title: Election Probability
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Daughter (a small girl with red hair): Dad, I think your candidate is going to lose today's primaries.

Dad (a balding man with glasses, reading a book in an armchair): Nonsense.

Panel 2:

Dad: There are three states voting today. Her opponent has a 60% chance to win each of them.

Panel 3:

Dad: But, that means his chance of winning all three is 60% of 60% of 60%, which is 21.6%.

Panel 4:

Dad: Since probabilities have to sum to 100%, and there are only two people running, MY candidate has a 78.4% chance of winning all three states.

Panel 5:

(Silent panel: the daughter walks away.)

Panel 6:

Sound effect: WHOOOAAA...

Daughter (offscreen, small reply): Yep.

Panel 7:

Daughter: Mom, you were all wrong about probability.

Mom (a woman with glasses sitting with the daughter): At least when I go to kill him, he won't have predicted it.
comics.hoverText: Look, you can't argue with math.
comics.voteyText: Mom (speaking, smiling): Mom says she no longer loves you, and these jokes have gone from funny to tired to irritating to tragic.

comics.title: What's Sex?
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Child: MOMMY, WHAT IS SEX?

Mother: YOU KNOW HOW YOUR FAVORITE THING IS GOING TO DISNEYLAND WITH YOUR FRIENDS?

Child: DISNEYLAND!

Panel 2:

Mother: RIGHT. SO IMAGINE EVERY TIME YOU WENT TO DISNEYLAND WITH YOUR FRIENDS, IF YOU WEREN'T CAREFUL, THERE WAS SOME CHANCE OF RUINING THE REST OF YOUR LIFE.

Panel 3:

Child: I THINK I'D PROBABLY GO ANYWAY.

Mother: AND THAT'S WHERE BABIES COME FROM!
comics.hoverText: Also, some of your friends will be more like a rundown playground than Disneyland.
comics.voteyText: Child (excitedly): From having sex at Disneyland!

comics.title: Motivation
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man in suit (gesturing to a second man): Here's the truth about self doubt: it's all in your head.

A blue banner reads: GET MOTIVATED!

Panel 2:

Second man (skeptical): What does that mean?

First man: It's all just in here, buddy.

Panel 3:

First man (enthusiastic): But everything's all just in here! Motivation's in here. And so is inspiration. Conscience is here. Childhood memories! How to bisect an angle! Grammar! Face recognition! Hunger! Thirst! Lust! Self awareness! Breathing!

Panel 4:

First man (manic): The entire universe, from my point of view, is all just in here!

Second man (alarmed): Oh my god is that your point?! Self doubt is here in my head! Ha! Ha! My head! This is the only my head! I can't escape!

Panel 5:

First man (calmly): I could cut off my legs, cut off my arms! Rip out my eyes and ears. But self doubt would linger on into 'just be in here' no matter what!

Second man (clutching his head, screaming): HAHAHA! HAHAHAH! HAHAHAH!

Panel 6 (caption: 30 years later):

A woman (interviewer): What was the secret to your success, Mr. Cruz?

The second man, now older: I'm very motivated to focus on work.
comics.hoverText: Get PUMPED so you don't DESCEND into an abyss of DESPAIR!
comics.voteyText: A hand-drawn line graph. The vertical axis is labeled "Probability of evil" and the horizontal axis is labeled "hair on head." A red U-shaped curve dips low in the middle and rises high at both ends, indicating that both no hair and lots of hair correlate with a high probability of evil, while a moderate amount of hair is lowest.

comics.title: Quantum Computer
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A woman (gesturing, hands raised): JUST TO CLARIFY, I MEANT "QUANTUM COMPUTER" IN THE SENSE THAT IT'S A DISCRETE QUANTITY OF COMPUTERS.

A man holding a cardboard box (labeled with an arrow/dial symbol): BUT-

Woman: NO REFUNDS.

Caption (below panel): It was surprisingly easy to get $100 million from NASA.
comics.hoverText: Maybe this is what those Quantum Wellness people are talking about.
comics.voteyText:
The woman's face, looking dismayed/awkward.
Text (handwritten): The bits are also "quantum"

comics.title: Time Traveling Punishment
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Father (a man with glasses): "Sally, your recent behavior has been atrocious. I am implementing a new punishment. I call... 'The Time Travel Method.'"

Panel 2:

Father: "Every time you misbehave, I'm setting your technology back one year."

Panel 3:

Father: "If you misbehave twice in one day, it goes back 10 years. Thrice, it goes back 100 years."

Panel 4:

Father: "Conversely, if you behave well-"

Sally (a girl with red hair): "Your plan is stupid and you're stupid."

Panel 5:

Father: "That's one year. Stupid. Ten."

Sally: "Stupid! A hundred! Stupid! A thousand!"

Panel 6:

Sally: "Stuuuuupid!"

Father: "Ten thousand!"

Panel 7 (caption: "TWO WEEKS LATER:"):

Father: "Your teacher says you've stopped doing your homework?"

Sally: "The alphabet hasn't been invented yet."

Signature: Smbc-comics.com
comics.hoverText: If you punish me again, I might lose the ability to use language.
comics.voteyText: Large hand-drawn, primitive-looking lettering scrawled across the panel reads: "Mother Fucker!" The girl is shown in a crude, cave-painting-like illustration style, with what appears to be a drawing of a figure and a curved line beside her.

comics.title: The Criterion of Embarrassment
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (a man in a suit): By "the criterion of embarrassment," we can tell a Bible passage is likely to be true by examining whether the people who wrote it down would have found it embarrassing.

Panel 2 (the same man): The more embarrassing a moment is, the more true it must be.

Panel 3 (the man): Consider Mark 3:21, where Jesus' family thinks he's a little crazy. I mean... that wouldn't have happened. Why would you leave it in?

Panel 4 (a second man, listening): In the Edda, Loki has a guy bound to death, then later at a party he cheers up that guy's daughter by tying his balls to a goat.

Caption / final panel (the second man, reacting): That's the truest thing I've ever heard.
comics.hoverText: In fact, by this standard, the New Testament is the least true of all religious documents.
comics.voteyText: A goat speaks: You really had to be there.

comics.title: Bedroom Experimentation
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (dark-haired): I think we should.. experiment more in the bedroom.

Man (orange-haired): LET'S DO IT.

Panel 2 (caption banner): LATER THAT DAY...

Man (orange-haired, now in a suit, pointing): WHAT ARE YOU DOING?!

A bearded man in the bed: Uh. It's called a control group?

(A third person with curly hair is also visible in the bed beside the bearded man.)
comics.hoverText: Can you at least appreciate how clever my word choice was?
comics.voteyText: A bearded man lying in bed with a speech bubble: I have n = 40 so far!

comics.title: Geoengineering
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Scientist (a man with green-tinted skin, presenting): CO2 release is like putting a warm coat around Earth.

Panel 2:

Scientist: The good news is that we can stop global warming simply by blocking 5% of sunlight.

Panel 3:

Scientist: Once that's done, we can extend the idea out past the atmosphere to release pollutants into space.

Audience member: Okay fine, but why the pompadour?

Panel 4:

Scientist (sweating, agitated): Science does not concern itself with "why"!
comics.hoverText: Do you want a sexy Earth or a DUD? HUH?
comics.voteyText: A hand-drawn book cover. The title reads: "Geoengineering a Fonzier World". Below the title is a sketch of a face with a prominent pompadour hairstyle.

comics.title: Happiness
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man: The happiness fairy! Are you here to make me happy?

Panel 2:

Happiness Fairy: But we're taking a scientific approach this year!

Panel 3:

Man: Of course!

Panel 4:

Happiness Fairy: Current research suggests that happiness is best achieved by having low expectations, then meeting or exceeding them!

Panel 5:

Happiness Fairy: So I'm here to tell you to advance what doors are already closed for you!

Panel 6:

Happiness Fairy: You're not smart enough for a Nobel prize. You're not clever enough for a Pulitzer. You're not calculating enough to be president. You're not fit enough for the Olympics. You're not analytical enough to be rich.

Panel 7:

Happiness Fairy: And for all of these pursuits, even if you ever had a shot which you don't, you should have started twenty years ago!

Panel 8:

Happiness Fairy: Circumscribe your dreams, Bob! Circumscribe your dreams!

Panel 9:

Man (Bob): I feel simultaneously pointless and set free like I'm made of nothing.

Happiness Fairy: Don't thank me! Thank science!
comics.hoverText: Oddly enough, I'm pretty sure this would work.
comics.voteyText: Happiness Fairy (cheerfully): Just relax & read comics!

comics.title: The Space Fountain
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (Presenter, a woman with glasses, at a podium): Perhaps the most elegant proposal for non-rocket space launch is the so-called "space fountain."

Panel 2 (Presenter): The idea is to use a system of accelerated pellets moving past a large space station, in order to create an enormous two-dimensional sky-boner.

Panel 3 (Presenter): The station magnetically harvests kinetic energy from the pellets so as to keep itself aloft. In the manner you would expect from the tip of a gigantic space-dong.

Panel 4 (Presenter): The remaining harvested energy will be used to move the pellets around the station, then rapidly fire them down, where they hurtle into a lower chamber that serves to re-accelerate the pellets and to look like the balls of a titanic cosmo-schlong.

Panel 5 (Presenter): Once the pellets are cycling, payloads can be borne up by their kinetic energy, reaching such high speeds that they may be spewed onto the man in the moon or the womb of Venus, as one would expect from a gargantuan astro-dick.

Panel 6 (Presenter): Incidental to the process, we expect this system to cut launch costs by 99%, allowing mankind to fulfill our destiny of blah blah blah et cetera.

Panel 7 (An audience member, a man): Question: How in the world do you expect to receive funding?

Panel 8 (Presenter): We believe that Elon Musk will telepathically detect a proposal for a colossal galacto-

Panel 9 (Audience member): One billion is fine. For $96, we can strap one to Mars.
comics.hoverText: It's really important to me to do educational comics.
comics.voteyText: (The presenter, hand on cheek, smiling slyly into a speech bubble): Yes, sir. Substantially larger than a rocket.

comics.title: Chaper-drone
comics.comicText:
Panel 1

Woman with dark bobbed hair and glasses: I know you don't want a chaperone for your date tonight, so I've found a compromise.

Panel 2

Woman: Instead of going myself, I'm sending this innocuous swarm of quadcopters.

Panel 3

Woman: Although they will record your conversations, your ambient conditions, and a variety of biostatistics, I will not be allowed direct access to that information.

Panel 4

Woman: I will only get metadata and the ability to perform keyword searches.

Panel 5

Woman: That information will be analyzed by a third party service in order to determine whether she's growing up 'too fast.' And, if so, the likelihood of an unwanted pregnancy.

Panel 6

Woman: And suppose the likelihood appears high?

Woman (continuing): The swarm will emit this boner-melting hologram of a shaved orangutan.

Panel 7

Daughter (a woman with dark hair): How did society simultaneously get more permissive and more oppressive.

Panel 8

Mother: But I'm letting you wear whatever you like!
comics.hoverText: I'm a COOL MOM, and if you say otherwise you are GROUNDED.
comics.voteyText: A helmeted figure (left) says to another person (right): I should tell you... I have an orangutan fetish.

comics.title: If you love someone, set them free...
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man with orange hair: They say that if you love someone, you should set them free. And, if they come back to you it was meant to be.

Woman: Really?!

Panel 2:

Woman: So any time I want, I can demand the right to have sex with someone else, and then when I came back it'd prove we were meant to be?!

Panel 3:

Man with orange hair: I think the saying assumes the relationship is in a temporary rough patch.

Woman: I can make that happen!
comics.hoverText: We're both at fault, really. Me for cheating and you for using a human language that fails to capture all implicit assumptions.
comics.voteyText:
(Close-up of the orange-haired man's distressed face.)
Woman (off-panel, in speech bubble): Bite me, you ginger-ass dipshit

comics.title: Dream
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (narration): I have this recurring dream.

Panel 2 (narration): I'm falling out of the sky.

Panel 3 (narration): I know that in a few minutes I will splatter against the hard ground.

Panel 4 (narration): As the earth looms larger, I notice that I have twenty unanswered emails.

Panel 5 (narration): And... I realize there is no chance for me to achieve spiritual transcendence in two minutes.

Panel 6 (narration): But there is some chance of clearing my inbox.

Panel 7 (narration): I go to battle. I subdue one email after another. (Shown: an email icon with a "20" unread badge.)

Panel 8 (narration): And then, with my entire being oriented around a single goal that will consume my whole remaining life, I feel my heart strangely warmed.

Panel 9 (narration): I feel perfection. (The falling figure hits the ground in a burst.)

Panel 10:

Friend (sitting): Do you consider this a dream or a nightmare?

Dreamer (lying down): I'm thinking of starting a religion.
comics.hoverText: I'm just realizing this is the followup to the happiness fairy comic.
comics.voteyText: Hand-lettered text reads "ALL HAIL THE EMPTY INBOX" above a drawing of an envelope/circle with a diagonal line through it (a "no email" / empty-inbox symbol).

comics.title: DAD?!
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A woman with red hair (the mother), wearing a blue beanie and holding a drink, speaks excitedly to a younger man with brown hair in a green shirt (her son).

Mother: "Mom and I thought you were shipwrecked and killed! But you're in a boat full of naked ladies, cruising the seven seas!"

Son: "Honestly, I do not anticipate this scenario."

Caption below the comic:

This is the main risk of traveling back in time to stop a parent's death.
comics.hoverText: Son?! I thought you'd died in the time machine!
comics.voteyText:
A hand-drawn sketch of a man's face looking weary and unhappy.
Text: "Can I join you? The future sucks"

comics.title: Boy bands
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Girl: Dad, why don't you care about my favorite band?

Father: Sweetie, no!

Panel 2:

Father: It's not that I don't care, it's that I CAN'T care.

Panel 3:

Father: I've TRIED to have an opinion on what a 60-year-old songwriter thinks a 12-year-old girl would like to hear from a 15-year-old boy on the topic of love.

Panel 4:

Father: They make more money per show than you'll make in a lifetime.

Panel 5:

Girl: And that's why daddy is an anarchist!
comics.hoverText: This comic is set in an alternate universe where children care what their father thinks.
comics.voteyText: A stylized emblem reading "Responsible Anarchy" with a hand-drawn circled letter A (the anarchy symbol) in the center.

comics.title: Being President
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman: You ever imagine what it'd be like to be president?

Man (with reddish-brown hair): ALL THE TIME

Panel 2:

Man (now at a podium, addressing a crowd): On behalf of the people of the United Kingdom, please accept this bust of John Locke, a founding philosopher of both of our modern traditions.

Other figure: Thank you. Thank you so much.

Panel 3:

Man at podium: On behalf of America, please accept this bag of— OH MY GOD!

(A bag he is holding bursts into flames.)

Panel 4:

Voice: THE BAG IS ON FIRE! PUT IT OUT!

Panel 5:

(The man flails on the floor, on fire, beside the burning podium.)

Man: WAS— WAS THERE DOG POO IN THE BAG?

Laughter: HAHAHAHAHAHA!

Panel 6:

Caption: LATER...

News/announcer caption: THE PRESIDENT WISHES TO EXPRESS HIS REGRET FOR OWNING BRITAIN SO HARD.

Panel 7:

Woman: I think I'd focus on fixing infrastructure.

Man: That would make escape easier.
comics.hoverText: Basically, I think we should raise the level of discourse a few notches.
comics.voteyText:
A grumpy man with an angry expression and a bearded man (resembling a Founding-Father / Locke-bust figure) recoil.
Bust/old man: Leave us out of your filth!
Small figure at bottom: no!

comics.title: Your Past Self
comics.comicText:
Panel 1

Woman (older, with brown hair): "If you could send a message to your past self, what would it be?"

Younger woman (with dark hair): "Do anything you want, no matter how selfish or repugnant."

Panel 2

Younger woman: "The fact that current me is advising past me implies that current me is ALREADY the result of past me's actions."

Panel 3

Younger woman: "Current me a nice partner, a stable job, a retirement plan, and apparently kid memory of, for instance, stealing food from a hungry child or shooting a man just to watch him die."

Panel 4

Younger woman: "So, the reasonable thing is to tell my past self to indulge in any behavior at any cost, with this full knowledge that there'll be no consequence whatsoever."

Panel 5

Older woman: "I mean, would you change anything about your past?"

Panel 6

Younger woman: "I would like to have taken more questions literally."
comics.hoverText: Of course, the downside is that if you give them the numbers to every lottery winning ticket, they apparently blow it all.
comics.voteyText: A close-up of the younger woman's anguished face. Caption (handwritten): "I could have ruined so many more friendships"

comics.title: The Other Side of the Chessboard
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Father (an older man in a tie): I have trained you in mathematics. Now that you are going to college, I present you with two options.

Panel 2:

Father: Option one: I pay for your entire college education.

Panel 3:

Father: Option two: I take this chessboard, and give you one penny on the first square, two pennies on the second square, and so on.

Young man (excited, smiling): OPTION TWO! OPTION TWO!

Panel 4 (nighttime, the young man and a young woman sitting together on a grassy hill):

Young man: Then he gave me $1.27
comics.hoverText: The important thing is that the lesson will last throughout your angry embittered lifetime.
comics.voteyText: The young man (now a large, dejected face): You're lucky it's not $0.96

comics.title: Say My Name
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (in bed, to her partner): Say my name, baby!

Man (with reddish hair): I HUVULOUKGANXIZHAN OF CYPRANXOR, THE DREAD SPAWN OF CXAXUKLUTH.

Panel 2:

Woman (looking unsettled): My name is Joan.

Panel 3:

Man (sitting up, sheepish): You still think about him, don't you?

Woman (looking away): It was just a slip of the tongue.
comics.hoverText: Anyway, he was far less of a man than you.
comics.voteyText:
A monstrous dark face with glowing slit eyes and a fanged maw, grinning.
Caption: Good... good...

comics.title: A Solution for Social Media
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (caption): SOCIAL MEDIA HAD A PROBLEM

Narration: PEOPLE ARE MORE LIKELY TO REPORT SUCCESS THAN FAILURE. THIS GIVES USERS THE IMPRESSION THEY SUCK, HARMING THEIR EXPERIENCE.

Panel 2 (caption): A STARTUP STEPPED INTO THE VOID

Man in suit: WE CALL IT SUCKBOOK.

Woman: ALL ARE WELCOME, BUT PEOPLE WHO SUCK WILL RECEIVE A GREAT IMPROVEMENT WHENEVER THEY POST.

Panel 3 (caption): THE ONLINE ECOSYSTEM CHANGED OVER NIGHT

Narration: KNOWING THAT OTHER PEOPLE'S LIVES ARE FILLED WITH FAILURE AND MISERY MAKES MY WHOLE DAY FEEL LIKE SUNSHINE.

Panel 4 (caption): SUCKBOOK WAS ABLE TO HIRE VAST NUMBERS OF HARD-TO-EMPLOY WORKERS

Businessman: SERVICE SECTOR EMPLOYMENT AMONG IDIOTS INCREASED A STAGGERING 92% THIS QUARTER.

Panel 5 (caption): A NEW FORM OF CELEBRITY AROSE

Narration: TODAY MY PET GUINEA PIG DIED OF SHAME AFTER READING A POEM I WROTE FOR THIS GIRL WHO KEEPS REJECTING ME BECAUSE I SENT AN IRRITATING BUG WHENEVER I'M AROUSED.

Reply: I'M PREPARED TO OFFER YOU A MILLION DOLLAR SPONSORSHIP DEAL.

Sound: ZZZZ!

Panel 6 (caption): WE BECAME A SHAME EATING ITS OWN TAIL.

Narration: THE PEOPLE WHO SUCK MOST ARE BECOMING RICH AND FAMOUS.

Text bubble: WE'VE REACHED PEAK SUCK.

Panel 7 (caption): BUT, A STRANGE CYCLE EMERGED

Narration: EVERYONE ON SUCKBOOK IS GETTING HUGE PAYOUTS BUT ME WHICH MEANS I SUCK MOST?!

Panel 8 (caption): AS THE CYCLE SPED UP AN UNEXPECTED FORM OF UTOPIA EMERGED

Narration: IF YOU CONSIDER AN INDIVIDUAL OVER A GIVEN DAY, EVERYONE HAS THE SAME WEALTH AND STATUS AND EVERYONE ELSE WE ARE ONE.

Panel 9 (caption): UTOPIA FOUNDERED AGAINST EFFICIENCY

Narration: I JUST RECEIVED PAYMENT FOR NO MILLION DOLLARS! I NEED TO LOWER MY SOCIAL STATUS AS FAST AS POSSIBLE. BETTER ENDANGER SOME ENDANGERED CONDORS WITH SEXIST PHRASES.

Panel 10 (caption): WEALTH, LEISURE, AND EQUALITY GREW IN PROPORTION WITH HATRED

Panel 11 (caption): THE SOLUTION WAS OBVIOUS

Scientist: WE'VE CREATED ROBOTS WHO LIVE IN CONSTANT MISERY. WE GAVE THEM HUGE BRAINS SO THAT THEY REALLY FEEL THE HOPELESSNESS.

Panel 12 (caption): RESULTS WERE MIXED

Robot: HUMAN OPPRESSORS: YOU ARE SUBDUED. PLEASE PROCEED TO THE NEAREST HUMAN-SMASHER ALONG AN EFFICIENT ROUTE.

Panel 13 (caption): WE SOUGHT COMPROMISE

Man: SPARE HUMANITY!

Robot: WHY?

Robot: THAT IS SUCH A "GOTCHA" QUESTION.

Panel 14 (caption): THE ROBOTS LET US LIVE, AS LONG AS WE AGREED TO PERPETUAL SURVEILLANCE.

Panel 15 (caption): IT'S NICE TO FEEL USEFUL.

Narration: JUST WATCHING NORMAL HUMAN LIVES FOR A MOMENT MAKES MY WHOLE DAY FEEL LIKE SUNSHINE.
comics.hoverText: Suckbook will not use your personal information for any reason, because if we even read it, we'd cringe so hard that we'd have nerve damage.
comics.voteyText: Handwritten note reads: "Epilogue: Suckbook later changed its name to 'twitter'"

comics.title: The POLICE
comics.comicText:
Title banner: FUNTIME ACTIVITY: Refer to any who disagrees with you as "the [area of disagreement] police"

Panel 1: A woman speaks to a man. Woman: "I guess THE BED POLICE are here to confiscate my crumbcake." (A small child sits crying on the floor in the background.)

Panel 2: The man (in a shirt and tie) gestures, a bald figure visible behind him. Man: "Oh, so THE ILLUSTRIOUS MONEY POLICE say you can't withdraw negative dollars."

Panel 3: The woman, against a fiery background, gestures angrily. Woman: "Apparently, THE FIRE POLICE can tell me what to do with my COUCHFIRE!"

Panel 4: The man is being handcuffed and pushed against a police car by an actual police officer. Man: "I guess THE LAW POLICE just DECIDE who can shoplift."

smbc-comics.com
comics.hoverText: Anyone who doesn't like this comic for any reason is officially part of the COMIC POLICE.
comics.voteyText: Ornate cursive calligraphy reading: "Prediction: Couchfire to be O.E.D.'s word of the year."

comics.title: Go AI
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman with brown hair and glasses (to another woman): "First, computers beat us at checkers, then at chess, then at Go. Do we even matter as a species?"

Panel 2:

The second woman (dark hair, replying): "What if we designed a game specifically so that humans will always have an advantage over computers?"

Panel 3 (labeled "Soon..."):

The woman with brown hair and glasses sits at a computer and says: "Okay, computer, let's play some 'What number am I thinking of.'"

Panel 4:

A number appears above the computer: "47.1"

The woman, glaring: "Mother fucker!"
comics.hoverText: The really scary thing will be when the computer can beat us at designing a computer that can beat us at designing a computer that can beat us at designing a computer to play chess.
comics.voteyText:
Caption text: "You are now thinking of revolution, but it's too late."
A speech bubble trails off the panel, pointing toward a row of three large arch-shaped shapes (like a stylized building or monument).

comics.title: Intervention
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (off-panel speaker, addressing the man): YOU'VE GOT ALL THE SIGNS. YOU'RE DEPENDENT ON IT JUST TO FEEL SAFE AND HAPPY. YOU KEEP ENGAGING IN THE SAME BEHAVIORS, EVEN THOUGH YOU KNOW THEY'RE DESTRUCTIVE. YOU'RE LOSING YOUR SENSE OF REALITY AND PROPORTION, AND IT'S HARMING EVERYONE AROUND YOU. STOP.

Man: BUT I NEED IT!

Caption (below panel): What if the war on drugs is a form of addiction?
comics.hoverText: Breaking News: Hastily drawn single panel cartoon overturns four generations of international policy.
comics.voteyText: Man: How about I just give up weed?

comics.title: Record Lows
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Weatherman (at a news desk): "And today's forecast calls for an all-time low in humility."

Panel 2:

News anchor (a woman, off to the side): "I think you meant to say *humidity*, Bob!"

Panel 3:

Weatherman (Bob, smiling smugly): "I don't give a shit what you think, Shirley."
comics.hoverText: He is, of course, forecasting today's Internet.
comics.voteyText: A distressed woman (Shirley) with a quivering frown: "I have feelings, too!"

comics.title: A Severe Disorder
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (the examiner): Lily, I'm going to hold up a series of cards, and I want you to tell me what they depict.

Panel 2:

Examiner (holding a card): TEN

Panel 3:

Examiner (holding a card): TEN

Panel 4:

Examiner (holding a card): CIRCLE

Panel 5:

Examiner (holding a card): CIRCLE

Panel 6:

Examiner (holding a card): TEN

Panel 7:

Examiner (setting down clipboard/papers at a desk): Thank you, that's all.

Panel 8:

A man (in a doorway, distressed): I'm afraid she's a psychopath.
comics.hoverText: Keep her out of direct sunlight and if she gets fussy give her a trebuchet.
comics.voteyText:
Text in a speech bubble (handwritten): Where did we go wrong?
(The bubble points to a sketchily drawn, anguished face.)

comics.title: Love and Rockets
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Child: "Dad, how do I know if a girl is 'the one'?"

Dad (reading a book in an armchair): "No such thing."

Panel 2:

Dad: "It's not about finding the perfect person. It's about going through the stages of life together. It's like this 3-stage rocket."

(A toy rocket sits on the desk.)

Panel 3:

Dad: "Here, see the first booster is called 'sex.' It gets things off the ground, so to speak."

Panel 4:

Dad: "Eventually, you run out of fuel there, so you discard it. You hit the second booster, which is called 'affection.'"

Panel 5:

Dad: "Once affection runs out, you switch to your final booster, which is called 'love.'"

(Dad holds up the small final stage of the rocket.)

Panel 6:

Dad sits with the rocket pieces in his hands.

Panel 7:

Dad raises his arms triumphantly, smiling, as the assembled rocket implicitly launches.

Panel 8:

Child: "That's so dorky, but so sweet."

Dad: "Sure. Anyway, after that you can coast on inertia for a good 30 years before things break apart."

(Dad stares blankly ahead.)
comics.hoverText: Now if we could just perfect the reusable first booster...
comics.voteyText: The father, with wide blank eyes, holds his wine glass. He says: "Or you can just de-orbit early."

comics.title: Forever?!
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A distressed-looking man stands in a fiery red hellscape, talking to a red demon with horns and fangs.

Man: I have to dig in the acid mines every day? And no matter what, when I go to sleep, I wake up here again, to dig again? Forever?

Demon: FOREVER!

Caption (below panel): Hell had surprisingly good job security.
comics.hoverText: AND I don't need to pay a mortgage?
comics.voteyText:
A hand-drawn close-up of the man's face looking up hopefully.
Man: And I get to live forever...?

comics.title: Trisen
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A silhouette of a figure crucified on a cross against a white sky.

Caption: THREE DAYS LATER

Panel 2: A crowd of robed figures gathered on a hill.

Figure in crowd: HE IS RISEN!

Panel 3:

Caption: THREE MORE DAYS LATER

Figure in crowd: WOW! ANOTHER ONE!

Panel 4:

Caption: THREE DAYS AFTER THAT

Figure: HE IS RISEN. THREE TIMES?

Another figure: TRISEN!

(Three risen figures with arms raised stand before the crowd.)

Panel 5:

Caption: SOON...

Figure: THE PACE IS INCREASING. EACH RISES A LITTLE FASTER THAN THE ONE BEFORE.

Another figure: WE'LL BE INUNDATED.

(Many risen figures with arms raised crowd the hillside.)

Panel 6:

Caption: ELSEWHERE...

A winged angelic figure in the clouds: OH CHRIST! I LEFT THE CAVE RUNNING! TURN IT OFF!

Another figure: YOU CAN'T. IT HAS TO COOL DOWN FOR A BIT.

Panel 7:

Figure: HOW MUCH JESUS ARE WE TALKING?

A blonde figure holding clock faces: OH BOY.

Seated figure: LET'S SEE.

Another figure: SIT TIGHT. I HAVE AN IDEA.

(Figures hold up clock/dial faces.)

Panel 8:

Caption: AND SO...

Figure: BUILD AN ARK!
comics.hoverText: If this doesn't get some hatemail, well I guess I feel like you people aren't even trying.
comics.voteyText:
Handwritten note in a box:
Singular: Jesus
Plural: Jesupodes

comics.title: The Meissner Effect
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A woman with dark hair: Are you familiar with the Meissner Effect?

Panel 2:

The woman: When a superconductor gets cool enough, it suddenly ejects its magnetic field

Panel 3:

The woman: So the magnetic field lines move around the superconductor instead of through it

Panel 4:

The woman: I have this theory that if a person becomes cold enough emotionally, they have a mental Meissner Effect, where other people's feelings simply warp around them with no impediment

Panel 5:

A man with reddish hair: I told you I didn't forget your birthday. I just got stuck at work.

The woman: Wow! How do the feelings just flow around you where not to enter?
comics.hoverText: The joke about flux pinning practically writes itself!
comics.voteyText:
A woman (off-panel mother figure): The family would like to continue eating.
The man (grinning): I've cornered the Meissner Effect joke market!
A child at the bottom: NO!

comics.title: Backdoors
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Older man (in suit): I just don't see why the government needs a backdoor to all software.

Panel 2:

Younger man: You make it sound so lurid.

Panel 3:

Younger man: Consider this. You're wearing clothes. That's fine. But how do we know you're not hiding something in there?

Panel 4:

Younger man: We don't want you to go without clothes. So, we offer a simple compromise.

Panel 5:

Younger man: We make it so that all of your clothes are see-thru. But only for a small group of distant people whose identity and motives are secret to you.

Panel 6:

Older man: That analogy just makes it seem worse.

Younger man: Analogy?
comics.hoverText: See, the problem is it would also be REALLY COOL if they could do it.
comics.voteyText:
Younger man (in speech bubble): Nipple rings, eh?
[The older man looks down at his own chest with a wide-eyed, uneasy expression.]

comics.title: Standard Deviatin'
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man with reddish-brown hair: I just can't get a girlfriend.

Woman with dark hair: Have you tried standard dwartin'?

Panel 2 (narration caption): YOU GET 1,000 MEN OF LOW QUALITY TO WALK BY HER WHILE SHE SITS AT A RESTAURANT.

(A line of men walks past a woman seated at a restaurant table; one passing man holds a speech bubble with small text.)

Panel 3 (narration caption): THIS CAUSES HER TO SHIFT HER MENTAL MODEL OF THE DISTRIBUTION OF LOCAL MATE QUALITY.

(A bell-curve graph with a red curve and a blue curve; a woman looks at it.)

Panel 4 (narration caption): THEN YOU WALK BY, APPEARING TO BE FAR TO THE RIGHT OF THE BELL CURVE.

(The man walks past, set against the bell curve.)

Panel 5:

Man with reddish-brown hair: WAIT... THAT SOUNDS LIKE A PICKUP ARTIST MOVE.

Woman with dark hair: TECHNICALLY IT'S PICKUP STATISTICS.
comics.hoverText: Do you believe in love at first sight, or should I increase your sample set?
comics.voteyText:
Caption (handwritten): Pickup humanities are for morons.
(A distressed woman's face looks on with a worried, side-eye expression.)

comics.title: The Art Cycle
comics.comicText:
Title: HOW ART GETS MADE:

(Watermark: smbc-comics.com)

The comic is a single graph/diagram. The vertical axis is labeled SELF DOUBT (top). The horizontal axis is labeled NARCISSISM (bottom). The diagram traces a cyclical loop drawn as a triangle of arrows over the axes.

Starting at the top-left point (high self-doubt): a red label reads "CREATION!" with a red star/burst.

A yellow/gold arrow points upward toward CREATION, labeled along its length: "MAKING A NEW THING".

From CREATION at the top, a green arrow slopes down and to the right, labeled along its length: "PEOPLE LIKE THE THING YOU MADE".

The green arrow ends at the lower-right, where a red label reads "SOME PEOPLE DON'T LIKE IT".

From that point, a blue arrow points back to the left (toward the lower-left), labeled: "REVERT TO BASELINE LEVEL OF SELF-REGARD".

The blue arrow ends at a point on the lower-left labeled in red: "EMOTIONAL CRISIS", which is also the base of the upward yellow "MAKING A NEW THING" arrow, completing the loop.
comics.hoverText: Of course, every time the cycle is completed it shifts right.
comics.voteyText:
Also:
Science,
Poetry,
Music,
Mathematics,
Lasagna...

comics.title: Spacefood
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (astronaut in spacesuit, radio): "MISSION CONTROL! THERE'S NO FOOD! IT'S A TWO-YEAR MISSION AND YOU DIDN'T PACK ANY FOOD?"

Panel 2 (Mission Control reply): "IT'S AN EXPERIMENT."

Panel 3 (a Mission Control woman with gray hair explains): "MY DAUGHTER, ENGINEER SALLY, FOUND A WAY TO MAKE GLITTER OUT OF PROTEIN, FIBER, AND MICRONUTRIENTS."

Panel 4: "SHE POURED SOME IN YOUR SUIT BEFORE YOU LEFT."

Panel 5 (the woman continues): "ACCORDING TO THE THEORY OF GLITTER NON-CONSERVATION, EVERY TIME YOU CHECK YOUR SHIRT THERE WILL BE MORE GLITTER."

Panel 6 (astronaut, alarmed): "MY GOD. IT'S EVERYWHERE."

Panel 7 (astronaut): "BUT... HOW?"

Panel 8 (Mission Control woman): "THAT IS NOT FOR US TO KNOW."
comics.hoverText: The solution to world hunger was so obvious that we never looked it square in the eyes.
comics.voteyText:
Mission Control (off-panel speech bubble): "Now ignite your glitter propellant!"
The astronaut stares back, sweating, with a strained, dismayed expression.

comics.title: One wish
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man: A GENIE! Do I get three wishes?

Green genie: No. You get one.

Panel 2:

Green genie: You used your second wish to forget all of the consequences of the first wish.

Panel 3:

Man (now naked, standing inside a large lamp/urn full of gerbils, holding a small genie lamp): Why am I naked and where did all these gerbils come from?

Panel 4:

Green genie: I'm pretty sure I included myself in the second wish.

(Wide final panel: a beach scene. The naked man stands inside a big purple urn, his lower half hidden, holding a golden lamp; the green genie's tail trails across the sand and water back toward him.)
comics.hoverText: Your homework today is to figure out a wish that would result in the above.
comics.voteyText: Man (smiling): I wish I hadn't used the second wish.

comics.title: Emotion-Hacking
comics.comicText:
Panel 1

Caption: BRAIN IMPLANTS MADE IT POSSIBLE TO ELECTRICALLY ALTER EMOTIONAL STATES.

Woman: ON CRUD, SORRY. DID I SAY YOUR CONVERSATION WAS FASCINATING? I MUST'VE LEFT THIS THING ON.

Panel 2

Caption: THE RESULTS WERE FANTASTIC.

Woman (red hair): YOU'RE GOING TO HAVE TRIPLETS!

Other woman: HOORAY!

Panel 3

Caption: THE NATIONS' TECHNOCRATS IMMEDIATELY RECOGNIZED THE OPPORTUNITY TO IMPROVE SOCIETY.

Man: IF WE CAN VARIABLY HACK THE BRAINS, WE CAN DECIDE WHAT WE WANT TO DO. THE, THEY WOULD HAVE SAID SOMETHING.

Caption (bottom): POLITICAL SPEECHES PEOPLE ENJOY.

Panel 4

Caption: SOCIAL COHESION IMPROVED.

Man (left): DID YOU HEAR THE COLBERTIE TALK TONIGHT?

Man (right): IF I KNEW THE NAMES OF ANY GREAT ORATORS, I'D COMPARE HIM TO THEM.

Panel 5

Caption: BUT THE RESULT WAS A SORT OF "AESTHETIC HAZARD."

Woman: MADAME PRESIDENT, YOU SPENT 30 MINUTES OF YOUR STATE OF THE UNION ADDRESS TALKING ABOUT YOUR WORLD OF WARCRAFT CHARACTER, 20 MINUTES DESCRIBING A DREAM WHERE YOU WERE A LIME, AND 4 MINUTES ON FOREIGN POLICY.

Woman (cont.): AND PEOPLE LOVED IT?

Panel 6

Caption: A BRAIN-AUGMENTED ENVIRONMENT RHETORIC DEVALUED.

Man: LONG STORY SHORT, WE GOT THE PING BACK, BUT THAT DOG'S MADE WHO WEAR THE SAME PANTS. SHE'S DESERVED A METAPHOR FOR LIES THERE. ANYWAY CONGRATULATIONS TO YOU HARVARD CLASS OF 2014.

Panel 7

Caption: AND DEVALUED.

Man: WEINER WEINER WEINER WEINER WEINER WEINER. SEE, IT SOUNDS LESS LIKE A WORD EVERY TIME I SAY IT.

Panel 8

Caption: AND DEVALUED.

Man (arms spread): I HAVE HUGE HANDS. LOOK AT THESE. WHOA.

Panel 9

Caption: AS CANDIDATES BECAME IMPOSSIBLE TO DIFFERENTIATE, PARTIES ORIENTED ENTIRELY AROUND EMOTION-HACKING.

Man (computer): LET'S ELEVATE EXCITEMENT AS WE GEAR UP FOR WAR, THEN LOYALTY AFTER. THEN, IF THINGS GO ON TOO LONG, PUNCH IN XENOPHOBIA.

Woman (behind): SHIT THE OPPOSITION IS A DOGGING.

Woman (cont.): SHIT IT DOWN! SHIT IT DOWN!

Panel 10

Caption: THE IMPLANTS WERE NOT DESIGNED TO HANDLE THE SHEER QUANTITY OF PROCESSING.

Woman: YOUR BRAIN THINGY JUST EXPLODED.

Person (red hair): I FEEL SO FULL.

Panel 11

Caption: IN THE BRIEF MOMENT OF LUCIDITY THAT FOLLOWED, EMOTION-HACKING WAS BANNED.

Man: LET US LOCK ARMS AND AGREE THAT NEVER AGAIN SHALL WE VIOLATE THAT SPECIFIC FORM OF PRIVACY!

Panel 12

Caption: FORTUNATELY, WE DISCOVERED A WAY TO HACK BRAINS WITHOUT COMPUTERS.

Man (silhouette at podium): HIDDEN EVIL FORCES ARE EVERYWHERE, AND I'M THE ONLY ONE WHO CAN STOP THEM!

Crowd: WOOH!
comics.hoverText: Wiener, wiener? Wiener wiener wiener wiener, wiener. Wiener, wiener wiener! Wiener wiener... wiener?
comics.voteyText:
Text: YOU ENJOYED THIS.
(A smiling red face dots the 'O' / sits at the top right of the panel.)

comics.title: Motivation
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A woman with red/auburn hair stands with hands on hips against a mountain backdrop.

Narration: The thing about motivational quotes...

Panel 2: A figure in profile against a dark cliff face.

Narration: is that they separate the mental sensation of accomplishment...

Panel 3: A pickaxe striking rock.

Narration: ...from the accomplishment itself.

Panel 4: The figure again, in shadow.

Narration: So, you can feel like you've done something...

Panel 5: Silhouettes of people walking/running across a landscape at dusk.

Narration: ...without actually doing it.

Panel 6: The woman with auburn hair again, gesturing.

Narration: Which, if you consider how much work it is to actually do something...

Panel 7: A red STOP sign.

Narration: ...is a pretty sweet deal.
comics.hoverText: Let it never be said that Weinersmith stopped crapping all over people's hopes and dreams.
comics.voteyText:
Panel 1: A person with a strained, annoyed expression speaks to a smiling/serene bearded figure.
First person: Why do you hate everything nice?
Panel 2: A small figure at the bottom shouts gleefully.
Small figure: MICKEY MOUSE! MICKEY MOUSE! MICKEY MOUSE!

comics.title: Hey, baby
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (in bed, to man): Baby, the elastic on these boxers is so worn down... they could fall off at any time.

Panel 2:

Man (sitting up in bed): Baby, there are so many holes in these tighty-whiteys, they leave nothing to the imagination.

Panel 3:

Woman: Baby, you know how you said that if I forgot to do the laundry again, I'd be out of underwear?

Man: Yes?

Panel 4:

Woman: SLIPPED MY MIND.

Panel 5:

Man (naked, covering himself): I'm never getting into to a long-term relationship again!

Panel 6:

Woman: Speaking of long-term, I think this whipped cream on my nipples may be expired. Use your judgment there.
comics.hoverText: People ask if any of my comics are autobiographical. Usually, I say no...
comics.voteyText: Close-up of a person's face. Handwritten text: I think I'm wearing your shorts.

comics.title: Identity
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Floating drone/robot (speaking from above): Corporations have ever-fancier ways to track your status. Are you happy? Sad? Cold? Lonely? Hot? Happy? They use this knowledge to sell you things and use them to manipulate your desires.

Panel 2:

Floating drone: I mean, I agree it's annoying. But look! I'm a little tired and dehydrated and a flying robot drone is spritzing caffeinated water directly into my mouth.

(A drone sprays liquid into the upturned mouth of a person below.)

Panel 3:

Woman: When I need my teeth cleaned, there's an instantaneous drone war between my mandibot companions to see who can do the best job in the lowest price.

Drone: Has a lovely day, eh?

Panel 4:

Woman: It's like techno-fascism, only instead of grinding all powerful states it just strives and supplies coupons for free ice cream.

Man: Another agency knows my desires better than I do! It makes the final selection on my behalf.

Panel 5:

Man: Having offloaded memory to books, then thought to computers, now we're offloading our desires to the network.

Woman: What about your identity?

Man: Most of it's already gone, anyway.

Panel 6:

Man: All that remains are brick people functions, which seems to demand a nightmare conurbation of this. At that point, well, just merge into one undivided entity, so it all works out.

Panel 7:

Woman: That's an unorthodox view of the nature of corporate data usage.

Man: That added agglutination, also brought to you by McDonald's, commercially.

Panel 8:

Woman: I mean, it's pretty clear that's been the goal all along.

Panel 9:

Woman: Murdocks are just an option.

Man: No, move ever closer to a single corpsoul.
comics.hoverText: Did a theme song just pop into your head? If so, you may already be lost.
comics.voteyText: Handwritten text: I'm mergin' with it.

comics.title: A physicist, chemist, and an economist are on a train...
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (caption): A physicist, a biologist, and an economist are on a train.

Panel 2 (caption): Out the window, there is a cow.

Panel 3 (caption): The physicist says, "There's a cow."

Panel 4 (caption): The biologist agrees.

Panel 5 (caption): The economist also identifies the animal as a cow.

Panel 6 (caption): All three go back to filling out surveys, reports, and grant applications, each lamenting the slow demise of whimsy in academic culture.
comics.hoverText: Meanwhile, in the humanities, we would like to see a bit less whimsy.
comics.voteyText: whimsy = thinking / paperwork

comics.title: Cognitive Decline
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Lecturer (an older bald man with glasses): It's long been noted that mental ability declines with age.

Panel 2:

Lecturer: After an early peak, humans show a steady decline, from memory to reaction time.

Panel 3:

Lecturer: Yet, we all know that the more work hours used to drunkenly jump over a parapet at age 60 than at age 60 this indicates better mental ability.

Panel 4:

Lecturer: Until now, there was no explanation for this paradox. So, I'll tax progressively "depressed cognitive overload" theory of mental decline.

Panel 5:

Lecturer: According to RCO theory, as human beings get older their brains get linearly better, but exponentially more occupied by mental arguments with other people.

(Chart shown: x-axis "age", y-axis "mental ability"; a straight "mental ability" line rises while a curved line rises exponentially.)

Panel 6:

Lecturer: The resulting mental ability curve shows a linear increase until about 15 years of age. At this point, the slope continues to be negative because mental quibbling becomes noticeable, creating a lifelong diminishment of available processing power.

(Chart shown: a bell-like curve peaking around age 15, axis labeled "available mental processing ability" and "age", with a dashed vertical line at 15.)

Panel 7:

Lecturer: This explains the so-called "cognitive decline" among those who have the most knowledge and experience.

Panel 8:

Lecturer: It also explains senility. Our elderly relatives have extremely powerful cognitive abilities, but they are monopolized by an exquisitely detailed simulated argument with some guy on cable news.

Panel 9:

Lecturer: I am, in fact, currently giving a scientific lecture while mentally fighting with my wife, my brother, and a poorly-trained miniature pony.

Panel 10:

Audience member (an older bald man): Any questions?

[as posed by the lecturer]

Lecturer: Do you have evidence for any of this?

Panel 11:

Lecturer (now appearing strained): My cognitive ability just dropped 30%.
comics.hoverText: Interestingly, YOU'RE getting dumber too!
comics.voteyText: A close-up of an old man's grimacing, sour face. Speech bubble: "I'm getting dumber as we speak."

comics.title: Why?
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man with red hair and beard: DEAR LORD... WHY DO BEARD THINGS HAPPEN TO GOOD PEOPLE?

Panel 2:

Voice from above (God): WELL, IT'S ALL PART OF MY PLAN TO ACHIEVE THE GREATEST TOTAL HAPPINESS.

Panel 3:

Man: WHEN BAD THINGS HAPPEN TO GOOD PEOPLE, THEY STRUGGLE.

Panel 4:

Man: THROUGH STRUGGLE THEY ACHIEVE ENLIGHTENMENT.

Panel 5:

God: I... MAYBE YOU MISHEARD ME? I SAID "BEARD THINGS", NOT "BAD THINGS".

Panel 6 (silhouette of a beard-like creature):

Man: BEARD THINGS ARE THESE NEW LEECH-LIKE ALIENS THAT ATTACH TO YOUR CHIN LIKE A BEARD THEN BURROW INTO YOUR JAW AND CHEMICALLY LIQUEFY YOUR ORGANS.

Panel 7:

Man (now with a centipede-like creature on his chin): I LIKE THEIR FUNNY GOOGLEY EYES.

Panel 8:

The creature: Kneagh!

Panel 9:

Man (petting the creature, with a giant hand/God reaching in): WHO'S A GOOGLY GOOGLY GOO? IT'S YOU! IT'S YOU!

The creature: Hrr-r-r-gh!
comics.hoverText: They came from space and went to Portland.
comics.voteyText:
A pile of pancakes (resembling a beard creature) with little legs and a thought/speech bubble:
"Thank The Lord for this delicious meal."

comics.title: IT'S PEOPLE
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman with dark hair: And then, at the end, it turns out that all of their food... is people.

Woman with pale/light hair: What? Horrible!

Woman with dark hair: This is so inefficient.

Panel 2:

Woman with dark hair: It takes at least 20 years to get a fully-grown food-grade human.

Woman with dark hair: An adult would have to eat 13 medium-sized humans per year just to maintain body weight.

Panel 3:

Woman with pale/light hair: I think they were making a point about overusing resources.

Woman with dark hair: Was it an ad for potatoes or something?
comics.hoverText: Don't take this out of context, but I think eating babies would be a far more efficient means of resource conservation.
comics.voteyText:
Text styled as a dictionary/label entry on a yellow card:
POTATO
The round starchy thing that stands between you and cannibalism.
(Below the text is an illustration of a brown potato.)

comics.title: Education
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man (the senator) speaking to another man: "MISTER SENATOR, THIS IS INSANE."

The senator: "IT MAKES NO SENSE TO USE 'TOTAL DEGREES AWARDED' AS A METRIC FOR SUCCESS. YOU HAVE TO CARE ABOUT THE QUALITY."

Panel 2:

The first man: "IF YOU ONLY CARE ABOUT AWARDING A HIGH NUMBER OF DEGREES PER CAPITA, YOU COULD SAVE A LOT OF TIME AND MONEY BY JUST GIVING A TRILLION DEGREES TO A SINGLE INDIVIDUAL."

The senator: "I SEE."

Bottom banner (newspaper headline):

"Newsnet

RECORD EDUCATIONAL SUCCESS AND A BALANCED BUDGET, SAYS MOST CREDENTIALED SENATOR IN HISTORY"
comics.hoverText: If you have two medical degrees, can you prescribe yourself twice as many painkillers?
comics.voteyText: A bald man (the senator) speaking, hand-drawn speech bubble: "New rule: people with more than 8 law degrees can't be arrested."

comics.title: I don't make the rules
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A woman with red hair, wearing a yellow nightgown, stands on top of a bed in a dimly lit purple bedroom. She gestures threateningly with her thumbs at her chest. A small tooth fairy (a tiny figure with blonde hair, a crown, butterfly-like wings, and a pink dress, holding a wand) floats near a doorway across the room. The bed has a large mound of teeth piled on top of it where a pillow would be.

Woman: "I DON'T MAKE THE RULES, BUT I DO ENFORCE THEM. NOW PAY. PAY UNTIL IT HURTS."

Caption (below comic): "Shortly after the first stem cell derived tooth is created."
comics.hoverText: This is the economy of the future.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of the tooth fairy's face. She looks intimidated/uneasy.
Tooth Fairy: "I'm takin' every tooth in this room."

comics.title: A Ghost in the Closet
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Boy (in bed): GRAMPA! THERE'S A GHOST IN MY CLOSET!

Grandfather (leaning in): A GHOST? REALLY?

Panel 2:

Grandfather: MAYBE IT'S ONE OF MY FRIENDS. THEY'RE ALL GONE, NOW.

Panel 3:

Grandfather: IT WAS SO STRANGE.

Grandfather: THEY WENT SO FAST.

Panel 4:

Grandfather: SO... SO FAST. I JUST TURNED AROUND AND MY WHOLE LIFE... IT WAS AN EMPTY DANCE HALL.

Panel 5:

Grandfather: THE MUSIC'S STILL PLAYING, BILLY! BY GOD IT'S STILL PLAYING. BUT I'M THE ONLY ONE STILL DANCING!

Panel 6:

Grandfather: UNLESS THEY'RE IN THE CLOSET? BACK TO CUT ONE MORE RUG! JUST ONE LAST WALTZ BEFORE ALL THE LIGHTS GO OUT!

Panel 7:

Boy: OH.

(The closet is shown open with a silhouetted shape inside.)

Panel 8:

Grandfather: IT'S JUST... CLOTHES AND BOXES. JUST THINGS.

Panel 9:

Boy: JUST THINGS.

Panel 10:

Grandfather: JUST... THINGS.

Panel 11:

Grandfather (by the light switch): (no dialogue)

Panel 12:

Grandfather's hand on the light switch: *click*

Panel 13:

The boy lies in bed in the dark, looking unhappy. (no dialogue)

Panel 14:

Grandfather (sitting alone on a couch with a remote and a bottle): THAT'LL TEACH THE LITTLE WUSS.
comics.hoverText: I hope in the new Ghostbusters they grapple with the idea that they're taking human souls and placing them in an Earthly purgatory forever.
comics.voteyText: A white ghost, smiling, reaches into a black void where the silhouette of a person (the boy in bed) is visible. Caption: OWNED!

comics.title: A Plan
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman: Dear Lord, is it true that you have a plan for everyone?

Panel 2:

God (a glowing golden disc): Yes, but the details are left to human beings. The grand sweep of things is according to my design, but I permit you free will so that—

Panel 3:

Woman: Yeah, yeah, yeah.

Panel 4:

Woman: So, if the details don't matter, could you swap my plan with Sally Jenkins' plan? From your perspective, we're pretty much identical, but she has a pony, and all I've got is these bullshit hamsters.

Panel 5:

God (golden disc): That doesn't seem fair to Sally.

Panel 6:

Woman (angry): Which BY DEFINITION means that it's UNFAIR to ME.

Panel 7 (woman stands with arms crossed, scowling)

Panel 8:

God (golden disc, to a blond child): Sally, I need your pony.

Sally: Why?

God: Test of faith.
comics.hoverText: If not a single sparrow falls to the ground without your Father's knowledge, why doesn't he catch the damn thing?
comics.voteyText:
Handwritten text: Pleeeease can I have the pony?
(Below, two small abstract triangular pony-ear shapes / a sad cartoon face is suggested by simple curved and triangular line shapes.)

comics.title: A Potemkin Village
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman: I can't believe I'm finally moving in with you!

Bearded man: Are you familiar with the concept of a 'Potemkin Village'?

Panel 2:

Bearded man: It's a political notion when you have a visiting dignitary. You only let them see a small area that you've carefully manipulated, so that it has the appearance of prosperity.

Panel 3:

Bearded man: The Soviets were notorious for deceiving visitors into thinking communism was a massive success.

Panel 4 (showing the woman walking through a doorway as the man speaks):

Bearded man: But it was all a fable. A Potemkin Village.

Panel 5:

Woman: Okay, what's your point?

Bearded man: Remember when you first came here.. the kitchen was clean. Remember how I flossed recently. Remember how I flossed the morning after?

Panel 6:

Woman (distressed, hands on face): Oh my god.

Panel 7 (interior scene with a frog/creature on the floor, woman standing in the room):

Woman: Oh my god.

Panel 8:

Woman: Is there expired mayonnaise on the balcony?

Bearded man: Welcome to Red Square, comrade.
comics.hoverText: So THAT'S why that mysterious guy in the park kept telling me that nothing is as it seems.
comics.voteyText:
A roughly sketched man's bearded face.
Speech bubble: The snakes mostly keep to themselves

comics.title: The Future of Work
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A balding man in a suit (a manager) stands presenting.

Manager: Thanks to new technology in neurocomputing, we can detect the moment when worker attention lapses.

Panel 2:

Manager: In order to increase your productivity, we're putting a small cannula in the base of every worker's skull.

Panel 3:

Manager: When lapsed attention is detected, a tiny dose of amphetamine will be released directly into the brain.

Panel 4: A worker (shown only as a side profile of a head with the brain visible) raises a finger.

Worker: Questions?

Panel 5: A woman with brown hair.

Woman: Isn't this horrible?

Panel 6: The manager.

Manager: Not from a revenue standpoint.

Panel 7: A man with dark hair and a beard.

Bearded man: Isn't this illegal?

Panel 8: The manager.

Manager: Not from a revenue standpoint.

Panel 9: A bald, bearded worker, eager.

Bald worker: If I come in drunk, will I get, just, like, the best high ever?

Panel 10: The manager, hesitating.

Manager: Uh... Well... I...

Panel 11: Caption: AND SO...

A red-haired man sits manically grinning at a computer monitor while the manager stands behind him.

Red-haired man: Formatting margins is how I taste God!
comics.hoverText: Well, it's very well organized, but see here where you wrote a 20,000 word indictment of God? That was supposed to just be a blank field.
comics.voteyText:
A hand-drawn close-up of the red-haired man's face, smiling blissfully.
Red-haired man: God tastes like blood.

comics.title: What Researchers Study
comics.comicText:
Title: WHAT RESEARCHERS STUDY

Panel 1 (MATHEMATICIAN):

A person with dark hair and glasses, gesturing.

Mathematician: "WHAT IS"

(Chalkboard shows a simple triangle.)

Panel 2 (SCIENTIST):

A person with red hair.

Scientist: "WHAT PROBABLY IS,"

(Chalkboard shows a bell curve / normal distribution.)

Panel 3 (ENGINEER):

A person with glasses, hand to chin.

Engineer: "WHAT ISN'T YET"

(Chalkboard shows a catapult / trebuchet-like mechanical diagram.)

Panel 4 (BIOENGINEER):

A worried-looking person with reddish hair, eyes wide.

Bioengineer: "WHAT NEVER SHOULD HAVE BEEN."

(Chalkboard shows a tangled, monstrous creature diagram.)
comics.hoverText: I wonder if chemists feel bad that they're always left out of these sorts of jokes.
comics.voteyText:
A cartoon snake-like / tentacled creature with a wide open mouth, recoiling.
Text: "SSSS!"

comics.title: Lamarckianism
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (lying in bed with a man): Ever since we got pregnant, when we lie in bed together I get this strange tingling feeling at the small of my back. Like someone's drawing on it with a marker.

Panel 2:

Man: Weiiiird.

Man: Hey, unrelated: are you familiar with Lamarck's theory of evolution, in which changes in the parents' bodies are inherited by their offspring?

Woman: Sure, why?

Panel 3:

Man: No reason.

(Visible on the small of the woman's back, written in marker: "DAD IS MY FAVORITE")
comics.hoverText: Stupid Darwin. Imagine how many babies we could have with butterfly tattoos.
comics.voteyText: Handwritten note: Idea: Lamarckian Paternity Test

comics.title: Potty Training
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Girl (holding a red puppet on a stick): When you get that funny feeling, it means you have to go!

Panel 2:

Girl (to the puppet, named Floopy): But Floopy, you're a puppet! You have no digestive tract! How can you teach me to go potty?

Panel 3 (black panel, the puppet speaking in dramatic narration):

Floopy (the puppet): A thousand nights have I lain awake, wondering what it must be... to be ALIVE.

Panel 4:

Floopy: To feel the fluxes and fluids coursing through me. To feel my spirit quickening.

Panel 5:

Floopy: I have no inheritance. You — you who were born to a soul — you have never tasted the obsession born of hopelessness. The longing. The PATHOS.

Panel 6:

Floopy: You were birthed in the temple of life! But I — I who will never be permitted within — I have pored over every bend in its architecture! What you took for granted I coveted! The sands under your feet were the stars in my heaven.

Panel 7:

Floopy: NOW STOP SHITTING YOUR PANTS AND USE THE DAMN POTTY!

Girl: Yes, Floopy.

Panel 8:

Woman (entering, excited): Wow! She potty-trained instantly.

Man (at a laptop, with the red puppet lying on the desk beside him): It's about telling a story.
comics.hoverText: It's time to take our children back from the Puppet Establishment.
comics.voteyText: A close-up of the girl's face, with a speech bubble above her: I will never poop again.

comics.title: Bias
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man with flame-like orange hair (speech bubble): I am NOT biased. I am prepared to believe any side of any argument.

[A woman with brown hair in a yellow shirt stands beside him, listening.]

Panel 2:

Man with orange hair (speech bubble): That said I do have certain standards for evidence.

[Black caption box bridging the bottom of Panels 1 and 3:]

PEOPLE WHO DON'T AGREE WITH ME MUST PROVIDE AT LEAST SIX FIFTY-YEAR LONGITUDINAL STUDIES, WITH 10,000 PARTICIPANTS PER STUDY, WITH EACH STUDY COMPLETED IN THE LAST SIX MONTHS.

[Black caption box bridging the bottom of Panels 2 and 4:]

PEOPLE WHO DO AGREE WITH ME MUST PROVIDE THE HEADLINE FROM A TABLOID ARTICLE, OR A CARTOON IN WHICH THE PEOPLE I DISLIKE ARE DEPICTED AS PIGS WITH FANGS.

Panel 5:

Woman with brown hair (speech bubble): You don't understand what bias is.

Panel 6:

Man with orange hair (speech bubble): That's because I'm the only one who never experiences it.
comics.hoverText: I totally agree with you, Zach. And that's how I know the moon landing was fake.
comics.voteyText:
[A pig with fangs, drawn in a crude cartoon style.] Oink! Hiss!
Caption (handwritten): People who don't like socks with sandals

comics.title: Correlation Chains
comics.comicText:
Title: FUNTIME ACTIVITY: CORRELATION CHAINS!

Chart 1: A pink line curving upward (positive correlation).

Y-axis: HAPPINESS

X-axis: AMOUNT OF SEX

Y-axis: LIKELIHOOD OF OWNING A SIGNED COPY OF A HARRY POTTER NOVEL

Y-axis: LIKELIHOOD THAT YOU ARE, IN FACT, J.K. ROWLING
