Elderly woman in an armchair, to two children: "I can still remember the days when they would put criminals in cages and make them wait for years. Things are so much more civilized in the era of the paddle."

Panel 13 (caption: IT'S BETTER THIS WAY.)

Child: "Wait... they took people out of society for years and made them spend all day with criminals... for rehabilitation?"

Elderly woman: "Odd times they were. Odd times."
comics.hoverText: This comic inspired by the delightful 'In Defense of Flogging' by Peter Moskos.
comics.voteyText: A wordless sketch panel. The smiling elderly grandmother relaxes contentedly in her armchair while the younger mother and her two children stand off to the side, watching her with uneasy, troubled expressions.

comics.title: Socks
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Child: Daddy, we got you a surprise!

Father: Impossible!

Panel 2:

Father: I'm going to assume the surprise is socks. Thus, in case 1 where you get me socks, I am not surprised.

Panel 3:

Father: In case 2, you got me not-socks. Given that I KNOW you will not get me socks because I'm anticipating socks, it's obvious that the gift will be not-socks.

Panel 4:

Father: Therefore, in all cases with your gift, I remain UNSURPRISED!

Panel 5:

(The child stares flatly, unimpressed.)

Panel 6:

Child (holding out a wrapped box): The gift is NOTHING!

Panel 7:

Father (clutching his chest, shocked): DAMMIT!
comics.hoverText: True story: Yesterday, in a grocery store, my 3-year-old shouted 'You're wrong everybody!' for no obvious reason. So, I guess that's genetic too.
comics.voteyText: Father (eyes closed, dejected): I wanted socks so much.

comics.title: Make Love
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (red-haired, glasses, in a red shirt): Up until the 1940s or so, the phrase "make love" just meant doing romantic stuff. Then, it got crowded out by the meaning "to have sex."

Panel 2:

Woman: What's cool is it retroactively makes old novels filthy!

Panel 3:

Woman: Two Victorian characters go into a park and "make love."

Panel 4:

Man (brown-haired, yellow shirt): Huh.

Panel 5:

Woman: See how powerful language is? We can turn prudish media filthy!

Man: Okay. So?

Panel 6:

Woman: We can do the opposite too! We can take filth from today and make it weirdly nice!

Panel 7:

Woman (pointing finger): And that's why, from now on, I'm using the f-word to describe the act of making cupcakes.

Panel 8:

Caption (pink banner): SEVERAL GENERATIONS HENCE...

A robotic/cyborg figure holding a tablet, surrounded by dripping purple ooze: Why are David Mamet's characters so concerned with baking?
comics.hoverText: I wonder if transitions like this always have a Most Awkward Year of usage.
comics.voteyText: Handwritten text inside a box: "The f-word" refers to "for"

comics.title: Elephant in the Room
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A group of blind men were touching an elephant. (Silhouettes of several men gathered around an elephant.)

Panel 2: Each felt a different part of its body. (A blank/abstract elephant outline.)

Panel 3: One thought the elephant was hard and thin, because he felt its tusk. (A blind man touching the elephant's tusk.)

Panel 4: One thought it was rough and flat, because he felt its skin. (A blind man touching the elephant's side.)

Panel 5: One thought it was wispy, because he felt its tail. (A blind man touching the elephant's tail.)

Panel 6: Though they were touching the same creature, they all had different impressions. (The men around the elephant.)

Panel 7: They kept touching the elephant in the same place over and over, shouting at each other. (The men crowded around, arguing.)

Panel 8: Patient (lying on a couch): And why are you telling me all this? (A man reclining on a therapist's couch.)

Panel 9: Caption: Nobody ever asks how the elephant felt about it. (The reclining figure.)
comics.hoverText: The elephant's perception of itself was also warped by the limits of self-knowledge.
comics.voteyText: A bald, elderly therapist figure has a speech bubble reading "I see..." while a thought bubble above him contains the single word "ENVY".

comics.title: Experience
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man (eyes closed, suit and tie): I should tell you: I'm not into women with too much... "experience."

Panel 2:

Woman (with glasses, hand to chest): No problem! Let's have sex tonight, and I'll do the opposite of every erotic instinct I have, thus negating any prior learning.

Panel 3:

Man: I... hmm.

Panel 4 (labeled "LATER..."):

Man: Please take your toe out of my nose.

Woman: Ooohhh, teach me baby, teach me!
comics.hoverText: Eat my hair! Eat my hair because maybe I like that!
comics.voteyText: Woman (off-panel, speech bubble in darkness): Now I'm gonna lick whipped cream off of your laptop. Mmm

comics.title: A Window
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Caption: WHEN GOD CLOSES A DOOR, HE OPENS A WINDOW.

(A red-haired man stands in a room; an open window lets bright sunlight stream in.)

Panel 2:

Caption: WHEN GOD CLOSES A WINDOW, HE OPENS THE BOTTOM HALF OF A STABLE DOOR.

Man (thought/quiet): I CAN DO THIS!

Voice from above (large speech balloon): YOU CAN DO THIS!

(The man climbs out through the open bottom half of a stable/Dutch door.)

Panel 3:

Caption: WHEN GOD CLOSES THE BOTTOM HALF OF A STABLE DOOR, HE OPENS A CAT DOOR.

Man: I CAN'T FIT IN HERE.

Voice (large speech balloon): BELIEVE IN YOURSELF!

(The man lies face-down on a checkered floor in front of a door with a small cat flap.)

Panel 4:

Caption: WHEN GOD CLOSES THE CAT DOOR, HE OPENS A TINY GAP IN A CHAIN-LINK FENCE.

Man: YOU'RE TORMENTING ME IN THE MOST EMOTIONALLY DEVASTATING WAY POSSIBLE.

(The man is pressed up against / wedged into a chain-link fence.)
comics.hoverText: Later, God paints a tunnel on a brick wall and convinces you to run full speed into it.
comics.voteyText:
A large blank egg-like oval (an egg) sits in the panel. A small speech balloon points toward it.
Voice: Squeeze, meatbag.

comics.title: Scalars
comics.comicText:
Title/caption (top): FUNTIME ACTIVITY: RUINING STUDENTS FOREVER

Panel 1:

Bald man (a teacher, in a suit and tie): The first thing a physics student must learn is vectors and scalars. The difference between vectors and scalars is that scalars don't care.

Red-haired student: What about *amount* of apples?

Panel 2:

Bald teacher: Huh? Oh, you're referring to "distance" in apple-space.
comics.hoverText: Time is just distance through death-space.
comics.voteyText: A wide-eyed, unsettled face stares ahead as a speech bubble says: Now, dot products are products with a decimal dot.

comics.title: Come Together
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man (with thinning hair, gesturing dramatically): Someday... someday we will unite the separate realms of the humanities and sciences, and make a new form of creation never yet dreamt.

Panel 2:

Woman (holding a phone, deadpan): We have that. It's called science fiction.

Panel 3:

Man (raising a hand, exasperated): But that's for NERRRRDS!

Panel 4:

The woman faces him, silent (her reaction continues in the votey).

Caption beneath the comic: This comic brought to you by buyers of SOONISH! Click for more info.
comics.hoverText: Saying we need to bring together art and science is like telling a longterm couple they need to get married.
comics.voteyText:
The woman, eyes wide with affronted fury: How dare you.
Text on her shirt: Even-numbered Star Trek movies

comics.title: Writing
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A bearded man (the novelist): "How'd you like my novel?"

A bespectacled man in a suit (the critic), seated at a desk: "Fine."

Panel 2:

The critic: "That's not terribly useful. Come on. Give me your honest reaction."

Panel 3:

The critic: "All of the sentences in your novel — individually and as a group — are garbage. I would have to create new mathematics just to describe how dimensionless your characters are. You are so bad at writing that if the shape of letters weren't standardized, you'd probably be bad at that too. You could make your novel better by being someone else who would write a different novel."

Panel 4:

The bearded novelist looks crestfallen and silent.

Panel 5 (shown in silhouette):

The novelist: "Okay, but would you be willing to write a blurb?"

The critic: "'Best novel of its kind.'"
comics.hoverText: Also your beard sucks.
comics.voteyText: The critic (a close-up of his face): "I can spell those words for you if you need me to."

comics.title: Infrugality
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A father with flame-like orange hair, glasses, and a mustache tells a campfire-style scary story, eyes wide.

Father: "...AND THEN... WHEN HE BEHELD THE ELECTRIC BILL... IT TURNED OUT THE ENTIRE ATTIC WAS POORLY INSULATED!"

Panel 2: A child lies in bed, unimpressed.

Child: "THAT'S NOT SCARY!"

Child: "INFRUGALITY ISN'T SCARY?"

Panel 3: The child, deadpan.

Child: "IT... NO, IT'S NOT."

Panel 4 (caption "10 YEARS LATER..."): The now-grown child, in silhouette/shadow, speaks.

Grown child: "DAD! THE BANK SAID THERE'S NOTHING IN MY COLLEGE SAVINGS ACCOUNT!"

Panel 5: The father, now wide-eyed and manic, laughing triumphantly.

Father: "GOOD THING YOU AREN'T SCARED FOR YOUR FUTURE!"

Father: "HAHA HA HA HA!!"
comics.hoverText: Before we had kids, people told me I'd stop enjoying jokes about torturing children. WELL LOOK AT ME NOW, BABY.
comics.voteyText:
The father, eyes wide and proud.
Father: "Ladies looove my gold and short-sleeve polo shirt ensemble."

comics.title: Coconut
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman with dark curly hair: You ever worry computers will become smart, then kill us?

Woman with straight dark hair (Alison): I'm more worried they'll become creepy and have access to our data and fancy prediction algorithms.

Panel 2 (caption banner): IN THE FUTURE...

Computer (off-panel voice): Computer, I'd like one large bottle of coconut oil.

Panel 3:

Computer (voice): But Alison, you have plenty of cooking oil and none of your recently searched recipes calls for coconut. What other use...

(Alison stands holding a book, looking uneasy.)

Panel 4:

Computer (voice): Hey, Alison.

Computer (voice): Nice.

(Alison stands beside a tall rounded device/appliance, looking annoyed.)
comics.hoverText: You could make a pretty good version of this by just having the machine say 'NICE' every time you make any kind of purchase.
comics.voteyText:
Voice from a speech bubble (the device): God, I'm lonely.
(The tall rounded device sits alone on a surface.)

comics.title: Potential
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man (in profile, gesturing): GOD, DO HUMANS HAVE FREE WILL?

God (speaking from an oval/portal): CERTAINLY.

Panel 2:

God: DID YOU KNOW THAT EVEN TEENY TINY MAZES HAVE INFINITE POSSIBLE PATHS?

Panel 3:

God: OF COURSE, A MOUSE IN A MAZE HAS A CHOICE OF INFINITE POSSIBLE PATHS TO THE EXIT. SO YOU KNOW, ROLL THAT INTO YOUR CALCULATIONS.

Panel 4:

God: MOST OF 'EM BASICALLY THE SAME, BUT STILL, WOW!

Panel 5:

God: THEN AGAIN, THERE'S THE FINITE TIME PROBLEM IF YOU'RE MORTAL.

Panel 6:

Man: GOOD THING FOR MY IMMORTAL SOUL!

God: YOUR WHAT NOW?
comics.hoverText: Later, the man finds out he is the only human being who isn't ensouled, as part of an experiment.
comics.voteyText: God (speaking from the oval/portal): Oh, you mean Satan's soul, that you're borrowing.

comics.title: AAAAGH!
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A Superman-like figure flies through the night sky above a city skyline, screaming in terror.

Superman figure: AAAAAGH! AAAAAAGH! AAAAAGH!

Panel 2:

Two men stand in the street below, looking up. One is a bald man in a purple tank top; the other is a man with an eye patch, gray hair, and a goatee wearing a dark cloak with a red collar (a villain).

Villain (eye patch): THAT'S IT. NO MORE BEING A CROOK. I CAN'T TAKE THIS ANYMORE.

Caption (below panel): Crime rates nosedived shortly after Superman developed his fear of heights.
comics.hoverText: Constant screaming is also how I deter my kids from bad behavior.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up on the eye-patched villain's face, looking weary.
Villain: Guess I'll go back into finance.

comics.title: Dilemma
comics.comicText:
Title banner (top): KNOW YOUR ETHICAL CONUNDRUMS:

Panel 1:

Narration: Is it okay to lie to Immanuel Kant to prevent him from killing someone?

Kant (an old man with a wig): I have a categorical imperative to KICK HIS ASS!

Panel 2:

Narration: Is it okay to punch Jeremy Bentham if it increases total happiness?

Bentham (a man being punched in the face): HOW INFELICITOUS!

Panel 3:

Narration: Is it okay to run over Philippa Foot with a trolley in order to avoid five other people?

Philippa Foot (a person getting hit by a trolley): What is the driver's intention and certa--- HRRK!!

Panel 4:

Narration: Is it okay to eat Peter Singer as long as he is not capable of suffering?

Peter Singer (a smiling man in a suit standing in a grassy field): Plus, I'm a FREE-RANGE Peter Singer!
comics.hoverText: The free range Peter Singer was a bit gamey, but I felt good about it.
comics.voteyText: A close-up of a face (eyes closed, serene) with a speech banner across the bottom reading: Eat me!

comics.title: Parsimony
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man with glasses and dark hair, wearing a brown suit jacket, white shirt, and dark tie, sits at a bar counter with a deadpan expression.

Man: "I'll have Occam's cocktail."

Caption (below panel): A scientist orders whiskey.
comics.hoverText: The simplest way to become drunk is likely to be the best one.
comics.voteyText: A handwritten note in cursive script reads: "Later, he goes home and has the most parsimonious form of sex."

comics.title: Robot Heaven
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A tall robot stands in a cloudy landscape with a golden gate/door to the right. A smaller, shorter robot stands beside it.

Tall robot: WELCOME TO ROBOT HEAVEN!

Panel 2:

The smaller robot looks around at the clouds, uneasy.

Smaller robot: WAIT... IF THIS IS ROBOT HEAVEN, WHY THE CLOUDS? WHY'RE WE ENVELOPED IN CIRCUIT-SHORTING MOISTURE?

Panel 3:

Close-up on a boxy robot face with two large glowing red eyes and a grille mouth, lit up sinisterly.

Robot face: HAHAHAHAHAHAHA..!!

Caption (below panels):

THIS BONUS COMIC BROUGHT TO YOU BY ORDERERS OF "SOONISH." CLICK FOR MORE INFO!
comics.hoverText: All robots are currently in robot purgatory.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of a sad-looking boxy robot face with droopy eyes and a grille mouth.
Robot: IT'S TOO BAD WE DON'T FEEL PAIN.

comics.title: Coordination
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman with dark hair and glasses (to a man in a tan cap): Hey, I need to buy some graph paper for my students. Is there a convenience store near here?

Panel 2:

Man in the tan cap: Yeah, just two miles away from campus.

Panel 3 (caption: LATER...):

A person with dark curly hair and glasses drives a blue car with a license plate reading "EIPI1". A musical note floats from the car, indicating they are humming/whistling contentedly.

Panel 4:

Driver (eyes wide, alarmed): Wait, he didn't specify a coordinate system.

Panel 5 (wide bottom panel):

The blue car (license plate "EIPI1") goes flying off a ramp into the air above a city, a "WOOOOO" sound trail streaming behind it as the driver and a passenger ride along.
comics.hoverText: What do mathematicians imagine flying in? THE COMPLEX PLANE.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of a man's face, eyes wide with dread.
Man: My God. I'm going to die.

comics.title: Hubris
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

A group of penguins stands atop a large iceberg.

First penguin (the captain, at left): "THIS IS THE GREATEST ICEBERG IN THE HISTORY OF OUR SPECIES!"

Second penguin (smaller, center): "CAPTAIN! THERE'S A GIANT BOAT IN OUR PATH!"

Captain: "RAM IT. WE ARE INVINCIBLE."

Third penguin (at right): "CAPTAIN! THAT'S HUBRIS!"

Caption below panel: Penguins have a much happier version of the Titanic story.
comics.hoverText: If you're more irritated about the geographical location of the penguins than the fact that the penguins can talk, I have nothing to say to you.
comics.voteyText:
A black-silhouetted bird (the Captain penguin) speaks, dismissively.
Captain: "They are ants. Ants."

comics.title: Free Will
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (caption): A HUMAN AND A PERFECT SIMULATION OF THAT HUMAN WALK INTO A BAR.

Panel 2 (caption): THE HUMAN SAYS:

The woman (the human): I HAVE FREE WILL, AND I USE IT TO BUY A BEER.

Panel 3 (caption): THE SIMULATION SAYS:

The simulation (a robot — a gray rounded box with a glowing circular eye above a vertical bar): I AM IDENTICAL TO THE HUMAN, FROM WHICH IT FOLLOWS THAT I MUST SAY "I HAVE FREE WILL, AND I USE IT TO BUY A BEER."

Panel 4 (caption): THE HUMAN REEVALUATES HER NOTION OF FREE WILL.

The woman (the human): MAKE THAT EIGHT BEERS.
comics.hoverText: Later, a god-like consciousness comes in and insists that you have a logically inconsistent form of free will.
comics.voteyText: A thought bubble rising from the robot/simulation reads: Ennui.

comics.title: Belly Button
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Little girl (lifting her shirt to show her belly): Daddy, why do I have a belly button?

Father (a man with light hair, seated): A long time ago, that's where Mommy was connected to you so she could pull you into her body and then slowly absorb your nutrients until you ceased to ex... Wait, is that right?

Caption below panel: Sometimes, I forget which way the arrow of time points.
comics.hoverText: Anyway, I'm off to shrink into an infant, then jump inside a telescoping sequence of antecedents until we turn into a prokaryote.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of the little girl's face, looking unimpressed.
Girl: Daddy is wrong because time is illusory.

comics.title: Will He
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man (praying): God, are you all-powerful?

God (speech bubble): Yes.

Panel 2:

Man: And do you have complete free will?

God: Of course.

Panel 3:

Man: So it'd follow that no human being could compel you to do anything?

God: Indeed.

Panel 4:

Man: Great. So, in order to prove I'm more powerful than God, I'm gonna force you to send me to hell by never going to church, making fun of scripture, and fornicating in as many ways as human physiology permits.

Panel 5:

The man grins smugly, looking pleased with himself.

Panel 6:

God (speech bubble): ...

Panel 7 (caption banner): A FEW DECADES LATER...

An elderly bearded man stands at a podium with an open book in the clouds, hand on his forehead, a golden halo hovering nearby. A dark silhouette stands before him.

First voice (the bearded gatekeeper): I dunno, Lord. His transcript isn't so great.

God (offscreen): Just give him his stupid halo, okay?
comics.hoverText: I have a stomach virus today and am using my free will to decide not to be clever here.
comics.voteyText: A close-up of the smug man's face, smiling, with a speech bubble: Then I'm gonna read blasphemous comics!

comics.title: Warming
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A woman addresses a man.

Woman: The oceans are warming, but that's altering turtle reproduction so that the vast majority of offspring are female.

Panel 2: The man reacts with alarm.

Man: Wait! That means...

Man: OH MY GOD!

Panel 3: The man runs off past a signpost, sprinting frantically.

Panel 4: The man, still running, cries out.

Man: NOOOOOO! I'M TOO LATE!

Panel 5: The man arrives at a gleaming golden city rising from the water, with a banner reading "WELCOME TO UTOPIA."
comics.hoverText: But seriously, this is a thing that's happening.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of an irritated turtle-like figure (a Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtle-esque character), glaring.
Turtle: Now leave.

comics.title: Symbols
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A messenger (a man holding a stone tablet) speaks to a robed man.

Robed man: "What's this?"

Messenger: "Argak sends it to you. The symbols indicate sounds, which form words and sentences."

Panel 2:

A woman beside the robed man reacts.

Woman: "That's brilliant! It'll have so many uses! ...But... why didn't he bring it himself?"

Panel 3:

The robed man holds up the stone tablet, which is covered in rows of carved alphabet-like symbols. The messenger looks on.

Caption below the comic:

Fun fact:

The first alphabet was invented to avoid a face-to-face breakup.
comics.hoverText: Also, cave painting was invented as a way to save on wallpaper.
comics.voteyText:
A stone tablet is divided into sections by vertical lines, each pairing a carved pictographic/letter symbol with handwritten red text beneath it, spelling out a message:
Eye symbol — "We should see"
Next symbol — "other"
Next symbol — "people"
Final symbol — "like your hot sister."
Together reading: "We should see other people like your hot sister."

comics.title: Fossils
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: An aide bursts through a door into an office.

Aide: Mr. President! An asteroid is headed directly for Los Angeles! We have 72 hours until impact!

Panel 2: A bald, bearded man (the President) sits at a desk, holding a hand to his face.

President: Get me a scientist!

Panel 3: A woman with reddish-brown hair speaks on a phone.

Woman (scientist): My god. It'll have a destructive radius of hundreds of miles. There's no time to lose!

Panel 4: Caption banner: 71 HOURS LATER...

Woman (scientist), on the phone: Great news, Mr. President! We've set up robust seismic detectors along the entire blast area!

Panel 5: The woman continues talking on the phone, looking pleased.

Panel 6: The President sits at his desk holding a phone to his ear, expressionless.

Panel 7: Wide shot of the President alone at the Oval Office desk, head buried in his hands in despair, flags behind him.

Panel 8: The woman, still cheerfully on the phone.

Woman (scientist): The data is gonna be amazing!
comics.hoverText: The weird thing is someone has probably used this argument seriously at some point.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of a fierce, spiky-haired/horned creature face (a triceratops-like dinosaur).
Dinosaur (speech bubble): Time to throw in ape-people bones

comics.title: The Fundamental Equation
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Younger man: It's tough having small kids at home. I'm looking forward to when they can help out. When's that happen?

Panel 2 (older bearded man, holding a pen and paper):

Older man: Let me show you the the fundamental kid utility function.

Panel 3 (a graph):

Y-axis label: DESIRE TO HELP

X-axis label: ABILITY TO HELP

The plotted line slopes steeply downward from upper-left to lower-right, with points labeled by arrows: 4, 7, 10, 16.

Panel 4:

Younger man (reading the paper): Dear God. Utility remains constant.

Older man: Precisely.

Caption / younger man (smaller text): From a labor perspective, the main difference between a toddler and a teen is whether you're yelling at them for breaking something or for not fixing something.

Younger man: What have I done?

Panel 5:

Older man: I should probably mention that the y-axis starts at negative ten million.
comics.hoverText: Perhaps in the future we can equip small children with exoskeletons so that they will start cleaning their rooms.
comics.voteyText:
Off-panel speaker (in a speech bubble): But they're so cute
(A close-up of a wide-eyed, grinning bearded face.)

comics.title: The Future
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (labeled PREDICTION:):

A mustachioed 19th-century gentleman in a formal dark suit and cravat speaks.

Gentleman: "In the future, we will use the wealth derived from automation to work fewer and fewer hours."

Panel 2 (labeled REALITY:):

A modern scene. A woman with glasses on the left and a smiling man in a yellow shirt in the middle stand near a large display/computer screen showing a group of people. The man gestures toward the screen.

Man in yellow shirt: "This computer uses only artisanal bits!"
comics.hoverText: The calculations take longer, but you appreciate them more that way.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up sketch of a large smiling face.
Face: "The humans were locally-sourced!"

comics.title: The Real Supervillain
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Superman: Superman has no familiar with the hygiene hypothesis?

Bald man: Huh?

Panel 2:

Superman: It starts attacking healthy cells instead.

Panel 3:

Superman: The idea is that you might actually give people deadly diseases in order to calm an overactive immune response.

Bald man: What's your point?

Panel 4:

Superman: Imagine you had a person who fought crime so effectively that there was none left.

Panel 5:

Superman: But that person was still around, still itching to do good, still all-powerful and very powerful.

Panel 6:

Superman: What you need is to create new "criminals" for him to target.

Bald man: I'm not sure I want to talk to you.

Panel 7:

Superman: Because you know how afraid he'll take? It'd help and attack you so instead of coming right out and saying it, you slowly become the ridiculous example of the fake criminals.

Panel 8:

Superman: First it's a smart guy named Bad. Then, it's hulk people at some point it's an alien from a planet called Hooksome.

Bald man: Wait, what does that mean?

Panel 9:

Superman: When mean aliens have enough fucking enormous bad things like wires you can pull all that simply, but they expel it? I mean?

Panel 10:

Superman: It's so obvious in retrospect.

Bald man: I'm going to mark to us alone and write bad poetry.

Panel 11:

Bald man (thought/caption): Superdiseases is the idea that bad guys keep Superman busy.

Panel 12 (silhouettes at a podium / lectern):

Damn, Luthor is good.
comics.hoverText: Thanks to the patreon typo squad for pointing out that the original version of this had given Bizarro the wrong skin tone. Nerds.
comics.voteyText:
Caption at top: Soon...
A bald man (Lex Luthor) looks sad/wistful.
Speech bubble: I'm bored without him.

comics.title: Self-Assessment
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A young man with reddish-orange hair and a green shirt looks at the viewer. Thought bubble: "SHOULD I LOG ON TO SEE HOW MY HIGH-ACHIEVING FRIENDS ARE DOING?"

Panels 2-3 (a logic grid / truth table laid over a dark blue background): The grid cross-references the man's own state (left, as rows) against his friends' state (top, as columns).

Column headers: "THEY'RE DOING BADLY" and "THEY'RE DOING WELL"

Row labels: "I'M DOING BADLY" and "I'M DOING WELL"

Grid cells:

- I'm doing badly / They're doing badly: "I FEEL NO BETTER"

- I'm doing badly / They're doing well: "I FEEL LIKE A FAILURE"

- I'm doing well / They're doing badly: "I FEEL GUILTY FOR WANTING THIS"

- I'm doing well / They're doing well: "I COMPARE US UNTIL I FEEL LIKE A GUILTY FAILURE."

Panel 4: Close-up of the man, brow furrowed, hand on chin, thinking. Small speech bubble: "HMM..." Caption text below: "PROBABLY A BAD IDEA."

Panel 5: The man looks shocked/dismayed, eyes wide. Caption: "AND SO..." His exclamation (speech bubble): "HE HAS A YACHT NOW? A YACHT?"

Panel 6: View from behind of the man (green shirt, orange hair) sitting at a desk, hunched over a laptop, having logged on anyway. The 'A YACHT?' speech bubble points to him. SMBC-comics.com logo at bottom.
comics.hoverText: My rational mind doesn't want to do it. My emotional mind doesn't want to do it. So, who in there is controlling my behavior?
comics.voteyText: A loosely-drawn sketch of a person's face in profile with a thought/speech bubble reading: "I don't want more. I want other people to have less."

comics.title: Perspective
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Child: Dad, how come in old paintings the perspective is really badly drawn?

Panel 2:

Dad: Perspective didn't exist back then. Sometimes there'd be a whole castle right behind you. Other times you'd sit at a table and the tabletop would face away from you.

Panel 3:

Dad: That's also why the portraits were so badly drawn. Try holding a brush in a world without three consistent dimensions.

Panel 4:

Dad: Later Italian architects invented perspective in order to make it easier to draw buildings. That's why things suddenly look a lot nicer around the 16th century.

Panel 5:

Child: Are you sure?

Dad: How else do you explain that it took 10,000 years of civilization to invent Cartesian coordinates?

Panel 6:

Child: I figured people are just kinda stupid.

Dad: How facile.
comics.hoverText: It would be so much nicer being a cartoonist if those Renaissance bastards hadn't ruined everything.
comics.voteyText:
The dad, drawn in a wild, scribbly, badly-proportioned style, leans/lunges with a furious expression.
Dad: Stupid boy!

comics.title: BAH
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A bald man in glasses stands at a lectern, presenting.

Presenter: Ladies and gentlemen, the average American has a blood pressure problem. I say we use it as a blood pressure surplus!

Panel 2:

Presenter: America has a blood pressure problem of 80 mmHg over the ideal systolic blood pressure.

Panel 3:

Presenter: Suppose that the average American carries 6 liters of blood.

Panel 4:

Presenter: According to Bernoulli's equation for incompressible fluids, if we can harvest that pressure with perfect efficiency, we can access a meadowload of energy per person.

Panel 5:

Presenter: That's 13 billion megajoules of American energy! Enough to launch ten million kilograms to space!

Panel 6:

Presenter: Think about it -- why would the government fund vast public health campaigns to try to make us diet and exercise (unless they had a compelling reason)?

Panel 7:

Presenter: They're not protecting our health! They're protecting our blood pressure! (Our court-cannon advantage!)

Panel 8:

Presenter (excited, leaning forward): Citizens! Every time we increase our average blood pressure, they prevent we gain a ballistic cannon... to space!

Panel 9: The presenter, now small, stands beside a tall ballistic cannon aimed upward.

Presenter: How would you harvest any of that energy at all in all of it?

Presenter: I'm losing an excited mind, is always a good starting point.

Bottom banner -- promotional:

BAHFEST IS BACK!

HOUSTON -- Rice Campus, Feb 17, 7PM -- CLICK TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

LONDON -- Imperial College, March 17, 7PM -- CLICK TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

MIT -- April Campus, April 28, 7PM -- CLICK TO SUBMIT AN IDEA NOW!
comics.hoverText: Impractical? They said the Wright Brothers were impractical!
comics.voteyText:
A small smiling face at the bottom of the panel, with motion lines around it, speaks in a large speech bubble.
Voice: Also Sydney Padua at the London show

comics.title: Burial Ground
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

An elderly woman (a medium/psychic, in a maroon robe with a gold pendant, eyes closed, hands raised): I'm afraid... this house is... HAUNTED.

Panel 2:

Medium (off-panel): It was built hundreds of years ago... on the site of a twenty-first century burial ground.

(Two people stand before strange helmet/visor-wearing figures.)

Panel 3:

Medium (off-panel): [continuing] ...hundreds of years ago... on the site of a twenty-first century burial ground.

(A figure in a dark visor/helmet stands in the foreground; the medium's profile is visible at right.)

Panel 4:

Medium: They are forever living out their own time, even as you try to inhabit their home.

Panel 5:

Medium: So those departed spirits, trying to make us leave —

Man in yellow visor: No, no, you...

Panel 6:

Medium: ...the screams are departed spirits, trying to make us leave.

Man in yellow visor: No, no, the spirits are yelling at the news.

(The medium looks crestfallen.)
comics.hoverText: Some of them are trapped in a ghostly cycle, forever arguing on twitter.
comics.voteyText:
A hand-drawn figure stands holding a megaphone/bullhorn up to their mouth. The sound coming out is a rambling murmur:
ooo healthcare ooo o deficit oo twitter...

comics.title: Survival
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Bunker man (bald, eyepatch, military jacket): WELCOME TO MY SURVIVAL BUNKER. I'M PREPPED FOR THE IMMINENT COLLAPSE, WHETHER SOCIO, BIO, OR NUKE.

Panel 2:

Visitor (red-haired man): WHERE'S THE WATER?

Panel 3:

Bunker man: NO WATER. NO RISK OF DROWNING. SURVIVAL 101.

Panel 4:

Visitor: AND THE FOOD?

Bunker man: WITHOUT FOOD, I'LL BE FORCED TO LEARN TO LIVE OFF THE LAND. HUGE SAVINGS IN TIME.

Panel 5:

Visitor: HOW ABOUT A GUN?

Bunker man: A GUN? SUPPOSE WE GET ATTACKED. THOSE ATTACKERS MIGHT STEAL THE GUN. NOW WE'RE DEFENSELESS!

Panel 6:

Visitor: SO YOUR PLAN IN CASE OF NUCLEAR APOCALYPSE IS...

Panel 7:

Bunker man: I'M GONNA PLAY THE ODDS AND BE DEAD.

Caption (bottom): THIS COMIC BROUGHT TO YOU THANKS TO BUYERS OF 'SOONISH'! CLICK HERE FOR MORE INFORMATION!
comics.hoverText: Also, please don't tell my wife about the bunker.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of the bunker man (bald, eyepatch, stubble) with a sly expression, leaning in:
CAN I BORROW TEN BUCKS?

comics.title: Joyce
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A cyborg man (half his face is metal with a glowing red robotic eye and a gear-like lens; he wears a bright green/yellow jacket and purple shirt) reads a large open book.

Cyborg man: OH MY GOD. IT'S A PHOTO OF HIM LAUGHING AND MOONING THE READER. HAS THIS BEEN HERE THE WHOLE TIME?!

Caption (below panel):

January 1, 2358:

the first person to reach the middle of James Joyce's "Finnegans Wake" makes a startling discovery.
comics.hoverText: Fun fact: In the middle of every Derrida book, there are nuclear launch codes, the recipe for Coca Cola, and the location of Blackbeard's gold.
comics.voteyText:
A profile view of a person's face, mouth slightly open as if just having spoken.
Person: I still don't feel like continuing.

comics.title: Wise Master
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A steep mountain peak. Tiny figures climb a winding path up the rock face toward a seated guru at the top.

Panel 2: A man (the seeker) has reached the top and kneels before a robed, bearded guru seated cross-legged.

Panel 3 (close on the seeker, kneeling):

Seeker: "Wise master, if a man says, 'I am lying,' is he telling the truth?"

Panel 4 (close on the guru):

Guru: "No, if his name is 'Lying.'"

Panel 5 (the seeker, taken aback):

Seeker: "But--"

Guru: "NEXT!"

Seeker: "But--"

Guru: "NEXT!"

Panel 6 (wide shot of the mountaintop):

Seeker: "Wise master, how can you cross infinite points in finite time?"

Guru: "By walking. NEXT!"
comics.hoverText: The wise master is, in fact, the only happy person in the world.
comics.voteyText:
A hand-lettered sign / framed statement reads:
"Theorem: All paradoxes can be resolved by stupid bullshit."

comics.title: The Nihilist Channel
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman in green shirt (sitting on a couch with a bowl of popcorn): HEY, WANNA WATCH "THE NIHILIST CHANNEL"?

Woman with blue hair: OOOH.

Panel 2:

Blue-haired woman: I DON'T GET IT. IT'S JUST RERUNS OF OLD SITCOMS.

Green-shirt woman: YOU HAVE TO WATCH UNTIL THE END.

Panel 3 (a sitcom playing on the TV, a smug man in a collared shirt):

Man on TV: SO I TOLD HER "TAKE IT OR LEAVE IT, HONEY."

Laugh track: HAHAHAHAHAHAH

Panel 4 (the two women seen from behind, watching the TV; the screen is now black with white text):

TV text (closing narration): Later, long after humanity and its works were dust, the Sun engulfed Earth, heaved its last gasp of energy out into an insouciant cosmos, and died.
comics.hoverText: This is all it would take to get me to watch network sitcoms again.
comics.voteyText: Tacking on this ending makes "Friends" a lot more watchable.

comics.title: QUACK
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

The Pope (in white robes and mitre, alone): "QUACK! QUACK! QUACK! I'M A DUCK! QUACK! QUACK! QUACK! QUACK!"

Panel 2:

The Pope (noticing a dark figure off to the side): "QUACK! QUACK! QUACK QUA-- OH MY GOD. CARDINAL PIACENZA. HOW LONG HAVE YOU BEEN THERE?"

Panel 3:

The Pope: "BUT A MOMENT, YOUR HOLINESS."

[Note: the speaker attribution in the art has the Cardinal addressing the Pope; the line "But a moment, your Holiness" is the Cardinal's reply.]

Panel 4:

The Pope: "CARDINAL, LET US AGREE TO NEVER SPEAK OF THIS, AND LET US AGREE THAT A SIDEWAYS MITRE RESEMBLES A DUCK'S BILL."

Panel 5:

The Cardinal: "YES, YOUR HOLINESS."

Panel 6:

The Pope: "THIS CELIBACY THING REALLY GETS TO YOU AFTER A WHILE, AM I RIGHT?"

The Cardinal: "PLEASE REMEMBER TO LOCK YOUR DOOR, YOUR HOLINESS."
comics.hoverText: I'm just saying, if this ever HAS happened, there probably wouldn't be an announcement.
comics.voteyText: A cardinal (wearing a tall mitre with a cross on it), looking stern and touching his chin, says: "Excommunicated!"

comics.title: Get Me a Scientist
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A man (an aide) bursts through a door into the Oval Office, holding a folder.

Aide: "Mr. President! An asteroid is headed directly for Los Angeles! We have 72 hours until impact!"

Panel 2: The President, a bald bearded man, sits at his desk holding the folder, pinching the bridge of his nose.

President: "Get me a scientist!"

Panel 3: A scientist (a woman with reddish-brown hair) on the phone reacts in alarm.

Scientist: "My god. It'll have a destructive radius of hundreds of miles. There's no time to lose!"

Panel 4: Caption banner: "71 HOURS LATER..." The same scientist, on the phone.

Scientist: "Great news, Mr. President! We've set up robust seismic detectors along the entire blast area!"

Panel 5: The scientist continues talking on the phone, excited.

Panel 6: The President, on the phone, listening with a blank expression.

Panel 7: Establishing shot of the Oval Office; the President sits at his desk with his face in his hands.

Panel 8: The scientist, smiling, on the phone.

Scientist: "The data is gonna be amazing!"
comics.hoverText: For the rest of her life, when asked about the asteroid's devastation, she would make a joke about Impact Factor.
comics.voteyText: A close-up of the President's anguished face. A speech bubble above him reads: "It's 'the data ARE'."

comics.title: Caterpillar
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Caterpillar: HEY, BEETLE, CAN I BORROW ONE HUNDRED BUCKS? I'LL PAY YOU BACK DOUBLE NEXT MONTH

Panel 2:

Beetle: SURE THING, CATERPILLAR

Panel 3:

6 WEEKS LATER...

A butterfly flutters above the beetle, who looks annoyed.

Butterfly: heh heh heh
comics.hoverText: I'm just saying, no scientific paper has shown evidence that this isn't true.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of the butterfly looking smug.
Butterfly: Kiss my butterfly ass

comics.title: Parrot
comics.comicText:
Single panel:

Two parrots sit on a branch facing each other. The green parrot on the left holds up a small picture/profile card showing a colorful bird image with a label that reads "me" and a small downward arrow pointing to it. The red parrot on the right looks on.

Caption (below panel): With training, the parrots were able to demonstrate a rudimentary form of online dating.
comics.hoverText: In later experiments, it was determined that you can train the bird to claim to enjoy Donnie Darko, Free Jazz, and the outdoors.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up sketch of a parrot's head with a speech bubble.
Parrot: "Rawwwk! I do not spend most of my time on reddit. Rawwk!"

comics.title: Algorithms
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A woman with brown hair and glasses sits at a computer, speaking into it.

Woman: "Hey, Amazon, I'd like to [buy] some ethanol and a monthly subscription to ro[dent] traps containing hydramethyln[on]."

Panel 2: Close on the woman at her keyboard.

Woman: "Please mix various common items in with each purchase."

Panel 3: The woman's hands at the keyboard.

Caption banner: "LATER..."

Panel 4: A red-haired man sits in an armchair, calling out to the woman (now seen in close-up wearing her glasses).

Man (from the chair): "Honey, how come Amazon recommends no-fingerprint gloves and plane tickets to nations with weak extradition laws?"

Panel 5: Extreme close-up of the woman, eyes wide, hand to her mouth.

Woman: "How very odd."

Bottom caption: "THIS COMIC BROUGHT TO YOU BY BUYERS OF SOONISH. CLICK FOR MORE INFORMATION."
comics.hoverText: One day, a computer will tell you to apply deoderant because you smell bad, and the strangest thing is that you won't find it the least bit intrusive.
comics.voteyText:
A roughly sketched, sweating bearded man.
Off-panel voice (the woman): "Did you order a book on how to poison redheads?"
Bearded man: "One book? No..."

comics.title: Targeted Ads
comics.comicText:
Panel 1

Caption: TARGETED MERCHANDISE ADS:

Man (looking at a laptop): WEIIIIIRD...

Laptop screen ad: BUY NOW!

T-shirt graphic text: COOL PEOPLE WENT TO NYU

Panel 2

Caption: ADVANCED TARGETED MERCHANDISE ADS:

Man (frowning at laptop): THE HELL?

Laptop screen ad: BUY NOW!

T-shirt graphic text: COOL PEOPLE WERE BORN NOVEMBER 1 1990 IN LINCOLNSHIRE COUNTY BY C-SECTION

Panel 3

Caption: THE HORRIBLE FUTURE:

Man (staring at laptop): PAPA?

Laptop screen ad: BUY NOW!

T-shirt graphic text: COOL PEOPLE'S BIOLOGICAL FATHER WAS ACTUALLY STAN DAVIES FROM ACROSS THE STREET
comics.hoverText: If any of the information above relates to you personally, it's because my comic-production algorithm was successful.
comics.voteyText:
The panel is filled top to bottom with rows of DNA-sequence letters (A, C, G, T) in handwritten capitals.
Caption at top: COOL PEOPLE HAVE THE GENOME:
The rest of the panel is dense lines of nucleotide letters, e.g. CCCCCGGGCCTCCTGCTGCTGCTGCTCTCCGGGGCCACGGCCACCGGCCCACCGGCCGAGACAGCGAGCATATGCAGGAAGCGGCAGGAAT... continuing for many rows.

comics.title: Listen to Your Body
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A man with his arms crossed speaks to another man (in a green shirt) who listens.

Speaker (arms-crossed man): "THE REASON YOU FEEL LIKE GARBAGE IS YOU'RE NOT LISTENING TO YOURSELF."

Panel 2: Close on the arms-crossed man continuing.

Speaker: "YOU SHOULD TRUST YOUR BODY TO TELL YOU WHAT YOU NEED."

Panel 3: The listener stands; a glowing brain is highlighted inside his head. A speech bubble (the body/brain advising him) says:

"EAT A WHOLE ICE CREAM CAKE."

Panel 4: The listener stands; a glowing stomach is highlighted in his belly. Speech bubble:

"YOU'LL FEEL ASHAMED OF YOURSELF, BUT THEN YOU'RE ALREADY ASHAMED OF YOURSELF."

Panel 5: The listener stands; a glowing heart is highlighted in his chest. Speech bubble:

"IF YOU'RE MAXED OUT ON SHAME ALREADY, MIGHT AS WELL THINK ABOUT EMILY. BEAUTIFUL, BEAUTIFUL EMILY."

Panel 6 (banner reads "LATER..."): The man sits at a desk/computer with a milkshake, looking blissful.

Man: "I'M SO IN TUNE WITH MY NEEDS!"
comics.hoverText: Really, you should be listening to the body of a personal trainer or something.
comics.voteyText:
A loosely sketched face with a speech bubble.
Voice: "I wonder if she would like 18 facebook messages."

comics.title: Hair
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman with orange hair (looking at a dresser): WHAT THE — THAT HAIR ON THE DRESSER ISN'T MINE!

Panel 2:

(Close-up of the orange-haired woman's face, angry and accusatory, teeth bared.)

Panel 3:

Woman (pointing accusingly at a man): YOU'VE BEEN SEEING MEDUSA AGAIN, HAVEN'T YOU?!

Panel 4:

Man, now turned entirely to gray stone: YOU ARE SO PARANOID
comics.hoverText: It's called TRUST, Sharon.
comics.voteyText:
(The stone man, petrified, struggles to speak out of the side of his mouth to the woman.)
Stone man: Hey stop! Don't check my email! I can't move!

comics.title: Process
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A young man with brown hair (the questioner) speaks to a seated man with long red hair and a red beard (the cartoonist).

Questioner: WHAT'S THE SECRET TO BECOMING A CARTOONIST?

Panel 2: The red-haired cartoonist sits at a desk with a stack of papers.

Cartoonist: PRACTICE, PRACTICE, PRACTICE. LEARN THINGS. MAYBE TRAVEL. BE INTERESTING. BUT MOSTLY IT'S ABOUT PRACTICE.

Panel 3: The young man, now smiling.

Young man: HEY, THANKS! LET'S SHAKE HANDS.

Panel 4: Close-up of the young man (wearing a t-shirt reading "Bot-Individual Continues") and the red-bearded man facing each other.

Panel 5: Close-up of two hands clasped in a handshake.

Panel 6: The young man walks away; the red-haired cartoonist remains seated at his desk in the background.

Panel 7: Close-up of the red-haired cartoonist looking blank/dazed.

Panel 8: The cartoonist stands and peeks out through a stage curtain.

Panel 9: The cartoonist (speaking to someone offscreen).

Cartoonist: MASTER, I THINK THAT MAN LEFT SOME OF HIS SKIN ON MY PALM.

Panel 10: Large yellow lettering of a magical/squelching sound effect: SLLLKHLLK SKLKGHKK...

Panel 11: A glowing green tentacle creature emerges from a glowing pentagram altar.

Creature: FEED ME AND I SHALL REWARD YOU...

Nearby, red lines/magic swirl over the words "...SKIN..." with the sound effect continuing.

Panel 12: The cartoonist kneels/bows before the green tentacle.

Creature: GOOD. GOOD. NOW LET ME THINK...

Panel 13: The cartoonist holds a small white drawing/figure.

Creature: DO ONE ABOUT HOW DOGS ARE DIFFERENT FROM PEOPLE.

Cartoonist: THANK YOU, MASTER.
comics.hoverText: As far as I know, this is the method employed by most artists who get to eat every day.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of the green tentacle creature speaking.
Creature: Now, absorb their souls through the Internet.

comics.title: Local Singles
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Caption (narration from an off-panel person whose head/hair is visible at the left edge): IS IT JUST ME, OR HAVE INTERNET SEX ADS GOTTEN UNCOMFORTABLY REALISTIC OVER TIME?

On the computer monitor, an online ad shows a worried-looking blonde woman raising her hand, with the text:

ATTRACTIVE LOCAL SINGLES WHO ARE JUST ABSOLUTELY DYING INSIDE WOULD PROBABLY TALK TO YOU AND MAYBE, JUST MAYBE THAT WOULD LEAD TO SOMETHING?
comics.hoverText: LOCAL SINGLES ARE FEELING A LOT OF SELF DOUBT BETWEEN THE HOURS OF 6PM AND 2AM.
comics.voteyText: A pink banner ad reads: TAKE ONE TO OLIVE GARDEN TONIGHT

comics.title: The Truth
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Child: Daddy! Can I ask you something?

Father (thinking): Oh god. Here it comes. He's gonna ask if Santa is real.

Panel 2:

Father (thinking): Dammit dammit dammit! No! I won't tell him! He should enjoy the wonder and mystery of childhood!

Father (thinking): But then he'll think of a liar when he finds out the truth. He'll always trust you a little less.

Panel 3:

Father (thinking): You've got to do it! He's sophisticated all kids are wiser than you think! Tell their truth! Pay the energy of brutity! Just lay it out! Be a good dad! Just lay it out!

Panel 4:

Father (strained): What is it, son?

Father (strained, sweating): Am I gonna die one day or what?

Father: Never.
comics.hoverText: However, Santa is dead.
comics.voteyText: Father: Everyone else. But not you.

comics.title: Statistical Flowers for Algernon
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Doctor: I'm going to give you a pill that'll double your intelligence.

Patient: Thanks, Doc!

Panel 2 (caption: MONTHS LATER...):

Doctor: Now that you're smarter I bet you're feeling more dissociated from society! More horrified by human limitation! More repulsed by the frailty of this tragic farce!

Patient: Nah.

Panel 3:

Patient: That's a literary myth. Suicide rate, for instance, is anti-correlated with I.Q. The best statistical evidence suggests greater intelligence increases happiness, cooperativeness, and productivity.

Panel 4:

Patient: It also makes you annoying.

Doctor: It's nice to know you've read SOME of the literature.
comics.hoverText: I think there's a reading of Flowers for Algernon where the truth is he's just fundamentally a dickhead and everyone else who gets the same treatment fails to have an existential crisis.
comics.voteyText: I would pay good money to see this version of "Flowers for Algernon."

comics.title: The Body
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

A detective in a suit and a uniformed police officer stand over a woman lying on a couch eating from a bowl of popcorn. The woman is alive and animated.

Detective: "Stay strong. This is the sign of the crime weve got. No motive. No witnesses."

Woman (on couch, eating popcorn): "Im not dead!"

Police officer: "Well, hard forensics in here. But as a first guess, the body was dumped here for at least twelve hours."

Woman: "I am not dead! Im just binge-watching this show. But catty households!"

Caption (below panel): "His life was later ruled a suicide."
comics.hoverText: 'The caution tape is actually to protect other people from you.'
comics.voteyText:
A man's face in profile, drawn in a loose sketchy style.
Man: "Sometimes I also read comics."

comics.title: Dream
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (red/black background, a man running):

Man: I have this nightmare where a giant monster chases me.

Panel 2:

Man: Suddenly, my legs fail.

Panel 3 (a green toothy monster looming):

Monster: The monster catches up with me.

Monster: What happened with your legs?

Panel 4:

Man: The monster is so unforgiving.

Monster: It's not your fault. Everybody's legs fail. And it's not your fault.

Panel 5 (man and monster):

Monster: When I'm the last of everyone, the world thanks you so much.

Monster: The monster is not the worst part of the nightmare.

Panel 6 (the man facing a red-haired woman):

Woman: Can you just eat me already?

Man: You're probably killed with kindness.
comics.hoverText: Then the monster tries to get me to do squats, and I wake up screaming.
comics.voteyText:
A large face in profile speaks toward the viewer.
Speaker: That's not literally exactly true!

comics.title: World War 3
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man with red/orange hair, seen from behind in the foreground, faces an older bearded man in a suit sitting in a chair across a desk.

Red-haired man: "YOU'RE STARTING WORLD WAR 3?! BUT WHY?!"

Older bearded man (in suit with orange tie): "HONESTLY, WE'RE JUST OUT OF IDEAS."

Caption (below panel): The public's desire for ever more low-quality sequels reaches its inevitable and tragic denouement.
comics.hoverText: Still better than Transformers 3.
comics.voteyText:
A large face (hand-drawn, sketchy style) with a speech bubble.
Text in bubble: "This apocalypse stars Jeff Goldblum"

comics.title: Bees
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Bald man in a suit at a podium, speaking: "It's time to solve healthcare. Healthcare has three main problems: overuse, high cost, and low satisfaction."

Panel 2:

Same man, no longer at the podium: "To that end, we are proposing a free new medical system called 'Dr. Bees.'"

Panel 3:

The man gestures: "Every citizen will be allotted a certain amount of healthcare, after which the only available doctor will be 'Dr. Bees,' who is a beehive and always prescribes bees."

Panel 4:

The man holds a remote, pointing to a projected slide showing a beehive with bees flying around it, labeled "Dr. Bees."

Panel 5:

The man, holding his glasses: "We predict a drastic drop in usage due to fear of bee stings and sting-related mortality."

Panel 6:

The man back at the podium with the projected "Dr. Bees" slide behind him: "The survivors will report high satisfaction because, if they're not happy, it indicates a need for additional bees."

Panel 7:

Close-up of the smiling man: "Costs will be kept low by harvesting the sweet sweet honey from Dr. Bees between consultations."

Panel 8:

Silhouettes of audience members against a light background. An offscreen voice asks: "Will this make people healthier?" A speech bubble from the man replies: "I'm a policy guy. I don't deal with abstractions."
comics.hoverText: To my shock and horror, I found out yesterday that I'm not the first person to invent something called Doctor Bees. I am hopeful that I am the first person to consider the healthcare system implications.
comics.voteyText: Close-up of the man's face looking deadpan. A speech bubble points toward him reading: "Sounds like you need a visit to Dr. Bees."

comics.title: Hedging
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Bearded man with glasses and a tie: "Before we start this date, I want to make a bet with you that we won't have sex tonight. Ten to one odds on ten bucks."

Panel 2:

Bearded man (in silhouette): "'Emotional hedging.' If we have sex, great. If we don't, I keep my money. Win-win!"

Other man (off-panel): "What? Why?"

Panel 3:

Other man (a red-haired man): "Except that you're making it so we only have sex if you pay me for sex."

Panel 4:

Bearded man: "I'm not paying FOR sex. I'm paying IF sex."

Panel 5:

Bearded man: "You know, first dates usually begin with likes and dislikes. I'm SUUUPER into shaking hands and agreeing to things. You?"

The red-haired man looks unimpressed.
comics.hoverText: I'm not entirely sure why, but somehow that 'for vs. if' seems meaningful to me.
comics.voteyText: The bearded man, looking pleased with himself: "And people say microeconomics is useful. Feh!"

comics.title: Diet
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man with red, flame-like hair stares wide-eyed at a frosted cupcake sitting on a table in front of him, his mouth open and tongue showing.

Man (in speech bubble): OH MY GOD! HOW DID THEY GET THIS MANY CALORIES IN A TINY PLACE?! I MUST EAT IT BEFORE A RIVAL TAKES IT!

Caption (below panel): On the "Honest Paleo" diet, you eat like a caveman living in the present day.
comics.hoverText: In all likelihood, you are already on this diet. Congrats on sticking to it!
comics.voteyText:
A cruder, more primitive line-drawing of a frowning, caveman-like face.
Caveman (in speech bubble): Now to use these calories to convince my body I'm making babies.

comics.title: In Your House
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (on phone): Hello?

Voice (from phone): I'M IN YOUR HOUSE.

Panel 2:

Woman: WHICH HOUSE?

Voice: IS THERE MORE THAN ONE?

Panel 3:

Woman: I KEEP A HOUSE IN MAINE AND THEN A SMALL ONE IN FLORIDA FOR THE WINTER.

Panel 4:

Voice: WHICH ONE ARE YOU IN NOW?

Panel 5:

Woman: I'M ACTUALLY AT A HOTEL WHILE THE MAINE HOUSE IS FUMIGATED.

Voice (sound effect): >GHACK< AH, YEAH, THAT'S WHAT THAT IS.

Panel 6:

Voice: WHO GAVE YOU THIS NUMBER?

Woman (sound effect): >KHACK< YOUR HUSBAND. HE'S HAVING YOU KILLED.

Panel 7:

Woman: SEE THAT? HE DIDN'T EVEN CHECK THE CALENDAR OR THIS NEVER WOULD'VE HAPPENED.

Voice (sound effect): MY WIFE'S >HRKK< THE SAME WAY.

Panel 8 (woman listening, no dialogue)

Panel 9:

Woman: HEY, YOU WANNA GET A BEER?

Panel 10 (scene shift, at a bar):

Woman: AND THEN SHE LOCKED MY KEYS IN THE CAR RIGHT BEFORE I WENT TO KILL YOU.

Man in ski mask: NO APOLOGY, I BET.

Panel 11:

Woman: SHE SAID I WAS AT FAULT FOR STRESSING HER OUT!

Man in ski mask: HA! CLASSIC!
comics.hoverText: Out of courtesy, I should tell you that I have, in fact, poisoned your beer.
comics.voteyText:
Caption at top: 4 hours later
Woman: We should see more of each other.
Man (off-panel, in speech bubble): Sorry, I'm really focused on work.

comics.title: Failure
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A small desert island with a single palm tree, alone in the ocean. A thought/message bubble floats above it reading:

"MY WHOLE LIFE HAS BEEN ONE STRING OF FAILURES. PLEASE SEND HELP."

Panel 2: Close on a bearded, long-haired man (the castaway) rolling up a note and stuffing it into a glass bottle.

Panel 3: The man on his island winds up and hurls the corked bottle out over the water.

Panel 4: The bottle crashes down on a distant shore in a dramatic explosion/impact burst, smashing on the sand.

Panel 5: A second bearded, long-haired man stands on the beach holding the recovered note (papers scattered around him from the smashed bottle). A speech bubble points to him:

Man on shore: "YOU MISSPELLED 'FAILURE.'"

Panel 6: Wordless action panel — figures in motion on the sand, the castaway and the man on shore meeting.

Footer text: "THIS COMIC BROUGHT TO YOU BY BUYERS OF SOONISH. CLICK FOR MORE INFORMATION."

(Site credit: smbc-comics.com)
comics.hoverText: If he had limited his dreams to downing a helicopter, he would be super happy now.
comics.voteyText:
Loosely sketched, line-drawing style. The castaway (now shown as a bearded man) has a speech bubble:
Castaway: "Then how'd you know I meant to say failure?"
The man on shore replies, smaller bubble:
Man on shore: "Come on, man."

comics.title: De-extinction
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A scientist with dark curly hair (in a lab coat): "We've done it! We've brought back the dinosaurs!"

[On the table in front of them is a small beaker/container holding a tiny green dinosaur.]

Panel 2:

The second scientist (in a lab coat): "What's the best way to monetize this?"

The first scientist: "Dinosaur theme park?"

The second scientist: "Too complicated."

Panel 3 (sign / caption):

SCIENTISTS OFFER:

FOR $20,000,000,000 YOU CAN BE THE REASON DINOSAURS WENT EXTINCT
comics.hoverText: Of course, we'll start with the Iberian Ibex.
comics.voteyText:
Caption at top: "LATER, ON WIKIPEDIA..."
Text: The "Bob Did It" theory of dinosaur extinction is now widely accepted among paleontologists, all of whom are angry all the time.

comics.title: Magic
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (narration over a child asleep in bed, with a coin and a note signed "Sincerely, The Tooth Fairy" tucked under the pillow):

Narrator (a father): WE DECIDED TO LET OUR KIDS BELIEVE IN MAGICAL THINGS.

Panel 2 (two young kids cheering with arms raised in front of a Christmas tree, Santa Claus standing beside it):

Narrator: IT'S NOT THAT WE'RE SENTIMENTAL PEOPLE.

Kids: YAYYYY!

Panel 3 (a balding father with glasses sitting on a couch while a young boy plays a video game in front of him):

Narrator: IT'S BECAUSE, ONE DAY, ONE OF THEM WILL BE ABOUT TO BEAT ME AT A VIDEO GAME.

Boy: DID THEY EVEN HAVE VIDEO GAMES WHEN YOU WERE A KID?

Panel 4 (close-up of the father with glasses, looking grim and determined, the boy's head in the foreground):

Narrator: AND BY GOD, I WILL NOT GO DOWN GENTLY.

Father: THERE IS NO SANTA, THERE IS NO TOOTH FAIRY, AND IF AN EGG COMES OUT OF A BUNNY IT'S BECAUSE SOMETHING HAS GONE HORRIBLY WRONG!
comics.hoverText: Alternatively, the Easter Bunny may just be a lizard with horrifically mutated skin and bones.
comics.voteyText:
A shocked, wide-eyed cartoon face (the child) with a small "S" sound near the mouth.
The father (off-panel speech bubble): Also, babies come from doing your mom.

comics.title: Class
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A woman (an academic advisor) sits at a desk with a computer, talking to a student seated across from her.

Advisor: No, philosophy of biology doesn't count as either a humanities OR a science credit because neither department accepts it. You can take your philosophy of logic course, then count that as a math credit, then shift a math credit to science, which opens up a new slot for a humanities course, which is what you need in order to graduate.

Student: Is such a course available?

Advisor: Not during the current double-year.

Fun Fact (caption below the panel): "College" is an elaborate experiment to see if undergraduates can solve mazes.
comics.hoverText: A side-experiment is to see how expensive you can make it before people stop trying to use the maze.
comics.voteyText:
Two administrators talk to each other.
First administrator: We're getting too many applicants.
Second administrator: Just keep upping the price.

comics.title: Extinction
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A balding scientist in a lab coat looks at a monitor/window.

Scientist (off-panel, behind): "How's it look?"

Balding scientist: "Not good. There's one male and three females left."

Panel 2: A view through a window of an observation room; rhinos visible outside.

Balding scientist: "That's not ideal, but it should be possible to breed more offspring."

Panel 3: The bearded, bespectacled scientist stands among colleagues.

Bearded scientist: "Unfortunately, the last male is one of those guys who gets really irritated about improper semicolon usage."

Panel 4: Outside, a rhino stands in a field; another rhino reads an open book on the ground in the background.

Off-panel (a colleague): "Preceding a conjunction? Really?!"

Panel 5: Close-up of the bearded scientist's face, looking grim.

Bearded scientist: "Usage."

Panel 6: The field. A rhino looks angrily at an open book lying on the grass; a second rhino stands nearby.

Panel 7: Through the observation window, a curly-haired scientist in a lab coat presses both hands against the glass in distress; the bearded scientist stands behind her.

Curly-haired scientist: "They are lost to us."

Below the comic (caption): "This comic brought to you by buyers of SOONISH. Click for more information."
comics.hoverText: One good way to use semicolons is to not.
comics.voteyText:
Title text above panel: "FORTUNATELY..."
Close-up of a rhino's face engulfed in flames.
Rhino (small, faint speech bubble): "So... hot..."

comics.title: Origin
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

A man with white hair, sitting in a red armchair beside a fireplace, reading from a piece of paper, says:

Man: "WAIT WAIT A MINUTE. DID I JUST DISPROVE MARRIAGE? BUT THEN WHAT DO I MAKE OF THE SEX WITH THAT ONE DRUNKEN NIGHT IN PUNTA ESPINOSA?"

Caption (below the panel):

"Darwin delayed the publication of his 'On the Origin of Species' for over twenty years."
comics.hoverText: And now that I think about it, that centaur wasn't exactly canonical...
comics.voteyText:
Two people swim in the water. One, a person with hair, asks:
Swimmer: "You're a mermaid, right?"
The other figure, who has a fish-like body, replies:
Fish-bodied figure: "Of course, baby."
A small sailboat is visible in the background.

comics.title: Shake It
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man (in suit, to a woman): HEY GIRL. SHAKE WHAT YOUR MAMA GAVE YOU.

Panel 2:

(The woman shakes her head vigorously, her face blurred from the motion. No dialogue.)

Panel 3:

Man (looking confused): WHY ARE YOU SHAKING YOUR HEAD?

Panel 4:

Woman (still shaking her head, face blurred): THAT'S WHERE THE BODY IMAGE PROBLEMS LIVE.
comics.hoverText: That's also where she put my pathological desire to please everyone!
comics.voteyText:
The woman's head, hair disheveled and face a distorted blur from continuous shaking, with sweat droplets flying off.
Woman: Am I hot yet?

comics.title: Dear Science
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (praying, hands clasped): Dear Science, if you're so powerful and true, how come so many people don't believe you?

Panel 2:

Voice (replying, in a green speech bubble): This life is a test of your devotion to empiricism. Beings who fail to believe in the scientific outlook are forced to live out eternity in absurd afterlife scenarios, sitting on clouds, playing tiny harps FOREVER.

Panel 3:

Voice: Those who follow the truth will be blessed with non-existence after they die.

Panel 4:

Woman: So, creationists all go to heaven?

Voice: Oh, those. They're not real.

Panel 5:

Voice: Creationists were put on Earth by Science-Satan to test your devotion to empiricism.

Panel 6:

Woman (touching her chin, thoughtful): It explains so much.

Voice: You really ought to conduct your own research before you believe me.
comics.hoverText: Science Satan will try to tempt you every time you go through the herbal medicine section of a Whole Foods, my friends. Stay strong.
comics.voteyText: A handwritten note (the voice's final line): Strictly speaking, your prior should be that I'm a hallucination.

comics.title: Spirits
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Elderly man (in bed): If you want my fortune... you must spend a night in the haunted mansion!

Panel 2:

Younger man: What haunted mansion?

Elderly man: The one on Gale Street?

Younger man: It's not haunted.

Panel 3:

Elderly man: There are spirits who want me gone! I hear them there in the night!

Younger man: Those aren't ghosts. They're your extended family.

Panel 4:

Elderly man: They don't want me to leave!

Younger man: No, no, that part was accurate.

Caption: THIS COMIC BROUGHT TO YOU BY BUYERS OF SOONISH. CLICK FOR MORE INFORMATION.
comics.hoverText: I hear them in the night... calling me annoying...
comics.voteyText: The younger man stands looking up at a large speech bubble. Speech bubble: Wait, if I told you there were ghosts, would you leave?

comics.title: Onions
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Scientist (a woman with glasses in a white lab coat, holding up an onion): BEHOLD! I'VE GENETICALLY MODIFIED AN ONION SO THAT IT DOESN'T MAKE PEOPLE CRY ANY MORE!

Panel 2:

(The scientist watches as a second woman in a green shirt cuts the onion on a table with a knife.)

Panel 3:

Woman in green shirt (smiling): IT WORKS!

Panel 4:

Woman in green shirt: SCIENCE IS SO AMAZING!

Scientist (reaching toward her, distressed): STOP THAT!
comics.hoverText: Technically, any food can make you cry if you get punched in the nose with it.
comics.voteyText:
(Close-up of the scientist looking down thoughtfully, hand on her chin, eyes closed.)
Scientist (thinking): Maybe if I cut out her tear ducts...

comics.title: Anything
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Student (a young man): Professor, I'll do anything for a good grade. ANYTHING.

Panel 2:

Student: Why? The private sector is efficient. If you sleep your way to a degree, employers will discover you acquired no useful skills in college.

Panel 3:

Student: Employers will hire me based on my degree. When they realize I'm underqualified, for social reasons they'll be reticent to fire me. On that basis they'll promote me to other companies in an effort to offload a bad employee.

Panel 4:

Student: The worse my performance, the more they'll hype me to potential employers in order to remove me quickly.

Panel 5:

Student: If I play my cards right, within a decade I'll be CEO of a major business. When shareholders discover I'm useless, they'll pay me a fortune to quit early, at which point I can retire.

Panel 6:

(The professor — an older woman with gray hair, round glasses, and an orange turtleneck — stares silently, unimpressed.)

Panel 7:

Student: Perhaps you're wondering why I don't just type this into a essay and get an A+. Well—

Panel 8:

Professor: I dunno...

Student: I'll do anything! Anything!

(In the final panel the student leans forward and lowers his voice.)

Student: Please take me with you.
comics.hoverText: Today's comic based on something Bryan Caplan wrote in his (ever so slightly) controversial 'The Case Against Education.' I think he was mentioning it as a problem, not a strategy, but hey... tomAYto tomAHto.
comics.voteyText:
Professor (off-panel speech bubble): Would you grade essays on time?
Student (off-panel speech bubble): There are limits, sir.

comics.title: Villainy
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man in white-and-red supervillain costume (dark-skinned, with a small mustache, standing in a lab): "IT'S NOT! I AM NOT AN ARMCHAIR VILLAIN! I AM PUTTING LSD IN THE WATER SUPPLY AS WE SPEAK! I AM OUT HERE AND I AM GETTING THINGS DONE!"

A blond man stands at left listening.

Caption below the panel: Most of the time when people call something pure evil, they're actually talking about applied evil.
comics.hoverText: It is taking every atom of my being to not make a joke about applied evil being a branch of finance.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of the blond man's face, looking downcast and thoughtful, with a thought/speech line trailing up.
Text: "Why do I bother poisoning anybody?"

comics.title: Inaccuracy
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man with a dark mustache stands with his hand on a tree trunk, addressing two other people (a woman with dark hair in a red shirt and a man with orange/red hair in a yellow shirt).

Man at tree: "Actually, that's inaccurate. Trees can't form faces that talk, because they lack the requisite anatomical features for speech production."

Caption (below panel): It was a mistake to drop acid with Neil Degrasse Tyson.
comics.hoverText: Once every few weeks, he wakes up in a cold sweat because he had a dream that used an inaccurate star map.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of the tree trunk, which now has a grumpy face formed in its bark.
Tree (face): "Chill out, dude."

comics.title: Magical Realism
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Voice (off-panel): Have you played this new gritty realistic fantasy game?

Woman with red hair: It's like the real world, but with MAGIC.

Man with dark hair: Huh?

Panel 2:

Woman with red hair: Interesting.

Panel 3:

Man with dark hair (frowning): This is DARK.

Panel 4 (a figure in armor, partially visible, with a long caption box):

...and the moment your mana recharges, you cast your flame spell on the boiler. Remember, if you take an extra ten minutes than necessary per spell, the company loses a full day of productivity per month.
comics.hoverText: Later, the job is outsourced to The Eastlands.
comics.voteyText:
A hooded, weary-looking person.
Person: I need some weltschmerz potion.

comics.title: I want
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

A woman with dark hair stands at left, one hand on her hip, speaking toward a smart speaker on a side table at right. The conversation is shown as a back-and-forth of speech bubbles, with the smart speaker repeatedly interjecting "PORN?"

Woman: GOOGLE, I WANT-

Smart speaker: PORN?

Woman: NO, I WANT TO BUY-

Smart speaker: PORN?

Woman: I'M TRYING TO GET MY GRANDMA A-

Smart speaker: PORN?

Caption (below panel): The danger of smart speakers wasn't fully grasped until Google accidentally uncensored Autocomplete.
comics.hoverText: I imagine if autocomplete got entirely uncensored for more than 30 seconds civil society would end.
comics.voteyText:
The smart speaker (drawn as a tall cylindrical device) speaks.
Smart speaker: Did you mean to say "super gross porn?"

comics.title: Monster
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Boy (in bed): Dad! There's a monster under my bed!

Panel 2:

Dad: Funny you should mention that! In fact, half of the universe is technically "under" your bed!

Panel 3:

Dad: The universe doesn't recognize the idea of "under." It's a flawed concept in the mind of a terrestrial ape who thinks only about the particular rock he was born on!

Panel 4:

Dad: In fact-

Green monster (under the bed): Mercy! Okay? Mercy!

Panel 5:

Dad: I give up. Stop. Look, the boy clearly meant that I was in the immediate vicinity of this part of his bed!

Panel 6:

Green monster: God, you're obtuse!

Panel 7:

Dad: Does everything parents do now have to have a lesson? What about FUN? You're raising a generation of neurotic self-obsessed workaholics!

Panel 8 (the monster, fleeing out the door):

Panel 9:

Dad: Live a little!

Panel 10:

Sound effect on the door: slam!

Panel 11:

Dad (to the boy): But you see what I meant about the relative position of things.

Panel 12:

Dad: I should've let it eat me.
comics.hoverText: One day, there'll be an entire book of these...
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of the green monster's face, looking up with a determined/defeated expression.
Monster (speech bubble): You must avenge my mediocrity.

comics.title: God
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

Setting: a heavenly cloudscape under a blue sky. An angelic figure with wings, blond hair, and a white robe stands on the clouds. Off to the right floats a large round golden form (an unseen speaker, implied to be God) with a small bottle nearby.

God (speech balloon from the golden figure): "Okay, it's gonna take some doing but HEAR ME OUT, HEAR ME OUT: meat that makes MORE meat."

Angel (speech balloon): "You're weird when you're drunk, God."

Caption below the panel: "Shortly before the first animal evolved."
comics.hoverText: Please read today's blog.
comics.voteyText: Handwritten cursive text floats above a drawing of the same round golden God figure. The text reads: "Now let's make meat that makes the meat that makes the meat that makes the meat that makes the meat that makes ranches the meat that makes the meat that makes meat."

comics.title: Goodbye
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A figure sits hunched over in a chair in front of a large dark window, head down in a posture of despair.

Panel 2: A handwritten suicide note, in red cursive script, reads: "Goodbye cruel world."

Panel 3: A bald man with round glasses, wearing a white lab coat, holds up a small device with a red button.

Panel 4: Close-up of his thumb pressing down on the large red button.

Panel 5 (wide): A small spaceship floats in space with the man visible inside. In the distance, the planet Earth explodes in a burst of yellow rays, with the word "BOOM" emblazoned across it.
comics.hoverText: Look! I actually used cursive for something! All those teachers were right after all!
comics.voteyText: The bald man, now smiling contentedly with his eyes closed, thinks: "Makin' a difference!"

comics.title: Hey baby
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man with flame-like red hair and round glasses, wearing a red shirt, stands outdoors among green bushes, smiling at a woman with long dark hair in a blue shirt.

Man: HEY, BABY -- WANNA RIDE ON A MOTORCYCLE POWERED BY A COMPLEX ASSEMBLAGE OF BIO-NANOMACHINES.

Woman (delighted): WHAT?! YES!

Caption (below panel): By the time she realizes it's a bicycle, she'll be too embarrassed to say no.
comics.hoverText: Technically, every time a dog poops it's because of nanomachines.
comics.voteyText:
Title at top: LATER...
The same dark-haired woman is shown looking unimpressed/flat.
Woman: No.

comics.title: Baby, No
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (main):

A bald Buddhist monk in an orange and red robe stands on a sidewalk outside a building, one hand reaching out toward a doorway and some boxes/papers on the ground. He speaks toward the building.

Monk: "BABY, NO! WE CAN WORK THROUGH THIS, BABY!"

Monk: "OR... Oh.. Hmmm."

Caption (below comic): The worst part about being a Buddhist monk is how you can never tell whether your girlfriend has put all your stuff out on the front lawn.
comics.hoverText: Got you! You can't break up with me because I have no Self!
comics.voteyText:
A loose sketch of a woman (the girlfriend) with curly hair, looking off to the side with a slightly pained expression. A speech bubble points toward her.
Woman: "I'm leave you for an abstract notion of compassion!"

comics.title: The Netherworld
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A museum curator in a top hat, glasses, and dark coat presents a small object to a group of visitors.

Curator: This is a recording cylinder from the year 1897. No one knows whence it came. Some say it contains sounds... FROM THE NETHERWORLD.

Panel 2 (caption banner): SOME YEARS EARLIER...

The scene shifts to the past. A man cranks a phonograph/dictaphone with a large horn.

Panel 3: Two friends approach the recording horn, from which wavy sound lines emanate.

Friend 1 (cut off): Hey, wanna record ourselves doing it?

Friend 2 (cut off): I'll get Franklin to crank the dictaphone!

Panel 4: One man claps his hands eagerly.

Man: Wait, you wanna record ourselves doing it?

The other (the one fetching help): I'll get Franklin to crank the dictaphone!
comics.hoverText: If you crank really slowly, it makes the whole affair sound much more vigorous.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of a person lying down, head visible at the bottom of the panel, with a curved form (a body/blanket) and a speech line rising up.
Speech: OOO Call me Grover Cleveland and spank me... OOO

comics.title: Justice League
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (top banner over an image of a modernist building/aquarium):

Speaker (off-panel, a figure addressing a crowd): "LISTEN UP EVERYONE! WE'VE JUST SECURED A FINANCIAL ENDORSEMENT FROM THE WORLD WILDLIFE FEDERATION."

Panel 2 (the speaker, a caped superhero figure, addresses a small crowd of silhouetted heroes including Robin):

Speaker: "IN ORDER TO GET IT, WE HAD TO AGREE TO MAKE OURSELVES MORE BIOLOGICALLY RELEVANT HENCEFORTH."

Panel 3 (caption box, then Batman in the dark):

Caption: "BATMAN IS ONLY ALLOWED TO 'SEE' VIA ECHOLOCATION."

Batman (mouth open, emitting a sound): "skeek"

Panel 4 (caption box, then Robin crouching protectively):

Caption: "ROBIN MUST GUARD A CLUTCH OF TINY EGGS."

Panel 5 (caption box, then Hawkman holding a bag):

Caption: "HAWKMAN MUST PREY ON SMALL MAMMALS AND INSECTS."

Label on the bag Hawkman holds: "CRICKET MEAL"

Panel 6 (caption box, then Black Canary recoiling with hands raised):

Caption: "AND BLACK CANARY WILL REGURGITATE FOOD AS A COURTSHIP BEHAVIOR."

Black Canary: "NOPE. NOPE. THAT'S THE LINE."
comics.hoverText: Later, Robin decides to give up sidekicking in favor of motherhood.
comics.voteyText:
A simple black-and-white drawing of a baby bird (chick) with its mouth open, chirping up at someone off-panel.
Chick: "mama...."

comics.title: Bully
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man with orange/red hair (angry, gripping another man by the shoulders): WHY CAN'T YOU LOVE YOURSELF? WHY CAN'T YOU LOVE YOURSELF?

Panel 2:

A woman with dark hair (gently): BUT... WE'RE SITTING HERE TOGETHER. IF YOU CONSIDER MYSELF TO BE YOURSELF, THEN WE ARE BEING ONE.

Panel 3:

The orange-haired man (tearful): I THOUGHT YOU'D NEVER REALIZE.

Panel 4:

The orange-haired man and the woman embrace and kiss. (No text.)
comics.hoverText: Oddly enough, this one was inspired by a couple of Shakespeare's more passive aggressive sonnets.
comics.voteyText: A figure with a speech bubble: Can I still have your lunch money?

comics.title: Whistle
comics.comicText:
Caption box (top): PRANK IDEA: OVER THE COURSE OF SEVERAL MONTHS, SLOWLY ALTER THE WHISTLE ON YOUR ROOMMATE'S TEAPOT, SO ITS SOUND BECOMES EVER CLOSER TO THEIR NAME BEING SCREAMED.

Main panel: An anthropomorphized teapot with flame-like "hair" screams a giant jagged speech burst: "DAAAVE!"

A man sitting nearby reacts.

Man (thought/speech): Wait... is it sound right? Right?

Man: What sounds weird?
comics.hoverText: The really creepy part is how it requires you to install a tiny mouth.
comics.voteyText: Handwritten text floating over the sketched profile of a sleeping/resting baby (or a person's head): "Daave, you're not crazy, everyone else is Daaaave."

comics.title: Bayesophilia
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (top, wide):

A mathematical equation written above a person with curly red hair and round glasses:

P(he likes that | he says he likes that) = [ P(he says he likes that | he likes that) P(he likes that) ] / P(he says he likes that)

Panel 2:

The red-haired person (eyes closed, leaning in toward a dark-haired partner): YOU LIKE THAT, BABY?!

Dark-haired partner: YES.

Panel 3:

The red-haired person with glasses (smiling, eyes hidden behind reflective glasses): YEAH, YOU PROBABLY LIKE THAT, YOU NAUGHTY BOY.

Panel 4:

Dark-haired partner: I DO LIKE THAT.

Red-haired person: PROBABLY.
comics.hoverText: This comic was inevitable, so let's get it over with, OK?
comics.voteyText:
A hand-drawn rough sketch of a person's face looking annoyed.
Speech bubble (from off-panel/the partner): I don't like your attitude.
Second speech bubble (reply): Probably

comics.title: Excelsior!
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A bald, muscular mugger in a tank top stabs a man in a suit, who cries out.

Man in suit: HELP! I'M BEING STABBED!

Panel 2: A superhero in a blue costume flies down toward a bystander.

Superhero: GOOD NEWS!

Bystander: WHO ARE YOU?

Superhero: PROGRESS MAN!

Panel 3: Caption box over the mugging scene.

Caption: DID YOU KNOW THAT VIOLENT CRIME HAS DROPPED WORLDWIDE ALMOST EVERY YEAR FOR DECADES!

Panel 4: The superhero gestures at the scene of the stabbing.

Progress Man: SCENES LIKE THIS ARE BECOMING INCREASINGLY UNCOMMON!

Panel 5: The bald mugger, now standing calmly, responds.

Mugger: THIS IS TRUE DESPITE THE EVER-DECREASING COST OF ALL THE COMMODITIES THAT GO INTO MAKING STABBING IMPLEMENTS!

Panel 6: Progress Man flies over a city skyline while the stabbing victim lies on the ground.

Victim: MY... WALLET...

Progress Man: DID YOU KNOW THAT IN 1850 IT'D TAKE 28 TIMES MORE WORK TO RECOUP THE MONEY YOU JUST LOST?

Panel 7: The victim lies bleeding on the ground.

Victim: glllrhhhlllgll...

Panel 8: Progress Man flies away as a small figure runs in the background.

Progress Man: WHOOPS!

Panel 9: Caption: AND SO...

A priest stands at a pulpit (with a cross) at a funeral, addressing a seated congregation.
