Man with brown hair (eyes closed, sipping a drink through a straw): ACTUALLY, THE DATA SAYS YOU SHOULD EAT AS MUCH ICE CREAM AS YOU LIKE.

Caption (below panel): Naming my kid "The Data" was the best decision of my life.
comics.hoverText: If you can convince your spouse that Data is a fun offbeat middle name, and that Theodore is a beautiful first name, you might actually get away with this.
comics.voteyText:
The dark-blue-haired man, frustrated: STOP MANIPULATING THE DATA!
The brown-haired man calmly sips his drink and does not respond.

comics.title: Man on the Moon
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Advisor (a man in a suit, reviewing a speech): I'm not so sure about this new speech.

Governor (a man at a podium): What?

Panel 2:

Advisor: You have this part where you say "If we can put a man on the moon, surely we can purchase the office of the governor a new jet."

Panel 3:

Governor: Over the line?

Panel 4:

Advisor: It's not accurate. We can't put a man on the moon. Hasn't happened since 1972. Nobody even makes rockets of the necessary size any more.

Panel 5:

Governor: Hmmmm.

Panel 6:

Governor: Hmmmmmm.

Panel 7 (caption: Shortly...):

Governor (at the podium, gesturing): If we can't put a man on the moon, then surely we can't investigate alleged misappropriations by the office of the governor!
comics.hoverText: Failure is not an option because we no longer have a rocket large enough to attempt something we could fail at.
comics.voteyText: Governor (looking upward thoughtfully): We are capable of anything. Not doing anything. As long as we fail to set our minds to it!

comics.title: Real
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (wide):

A young girl sits sad on a grassy hill, head in her hands. A man (her father) approaches from the right.

Father: What's the matter, honey?

Panel 2:

The girl, looking worried.

Girl: Is the tooth fairy real?

Panel 3:

The father, smiling reassuringly.

Father: If you love her in your heart, then she's as real as anything.

Panel 4:

Close on the girl looking up skeptically at the father.

Girl: But you love Batman and Batman isn't real.

Panel 5 (wide):

The father now sits on the grass next to the girl, head in his hands in the same defeated pose she had at the start, both staring blankly ahead.
comics.hoverText: Yes Virginia, the Hamburglar is real.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of the father's face, looking pained/devastated, holding his face in his hand.
Father (small voice): Apologize.

comics.title: Hoax
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Bearded man in a suit (gesturing at himself, mouth open in earnest argument): "I WONDER IF MOON HOAXERS ARE AS PESSIMISTIC AS WE ARE. WE HAVEN'T PUT A SINGLE MAN ON A FAKE MOON SOUND STAGE SINCE 1972! WHAT A LACK OF VISION! BY NOW WE SHOULD HAVE DESIGNED A FAKE REUSABLE LAUNCH VEHICLE AND USED IT TO 'BUILD' A FAKE LUNAR STATION. WITH THE PROPER INVESTMENTS WE COULD'VE BEEN FAKING A MARS LANDING BY NOW!"
comics.hoverText: The alternative view is that we should stop faking so many achievements in space and start faking care of the people down here.
comics.voteyText: Same bearded man, smaller and looking downcast: "WE LOST OUR AMBITION FOR SPACE HOAXES SOME TIME IN THE LATE 70S. AND WE'VE GOT TO GET IT BACK."

comics.title: They Walk Among Us
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Green alien (gloating, on a screen/viewport above two humans): HAHAHA! WE'VE FOOLED YOU!

Panel 2:

Green alien (seated at a console): 50 YEARS AGO, WE SENT BILLIONS OF ANTHROPOID ROBOTS TO EARTH. THEY WERE ALL INCREDIBLY ATTRACTIVE, SELF-SACRIFICING, AND STUPID GOOD AT SEX.

Panel 3:

Green alien: THEREFORE, NO HUMAN OFFSPRING HAVE BEEN CREATED! BUT, NONE OF YOU NOTICED BECAUSE YOU WERE TOO BUSY BEING HAPPY ALL THE TIME!

Panel 4:

Green alien (arms raised, triumphant): WE'VE ELIMINATED YOU THROUGH YOUR OWN WEAKNESS!

(A flying saucer hovers above the silhouettes of the human couple.)

Panel 5:

The two humans (an older couple) calmly reply, flanked by two muscular, bow-tie-wearing robot men: WE... UH... WE KNEW.

Panel 6:

The alien (off-panel, startled): WHAT?! HOW?!

Older woman: BRUCE AND REX HERE SAY 'BEEP BEEP' A LOT. ALSO, THEY EACH DO THE DISHES 4 TIMES A DAY IN THE NUDE, AND THEY BAKE! I MEAN, WHAT'RE THE ODDS?

Panel 7:

Alien: LOOK, YOU OVERPLAYED YOUR HAND, ZORPLEX. WE KNEW THIS WAS THE END AND WE'VE BEEN RIDING THE SEXY SEXY WAVE FOR FIVE DECADES.

Panel 8:

Alien (Zorplex): YOU SOLD OUT YOUR SPECIES FOR--

Older woman: TWO DONGS AT ONCE AND FRESH SOURDOUGH, YES.

(The two muscular robot men stand on either side of the older woman.)

Panel 9:

The alien stares, dejected and silent.

Panel 10:

A flying saucer floats away from Earth in space.

Alien (from the saucer): CANCEL THE CONQUEST. THIS PLANET IS CURSED.
comics.hoverText: One day, I need to release a whole book of comics about humans winning by being gross.
comics.voteyText:
Text at top of panel: I FEEL SO POINTLESS NOW.
A dejected human figure slumps with their head down.
A speech balloon (from an off-panel robot): RUB MY FEET!

comics.title: Space
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A woman (dark hair, pink top) holds out a tablet/device toward a man, excited.

Man: MUSGRAVE! YOU'VE BEEN HOLDING OUT ON ME!

Woman: WHAT?

Panel 2:

Woman: LOOK AT THIS SEX HYPERCUBE!

Panel 3:

Man: FOUR DIMENSIONS. STYLE. POSITION. LOCATION. STATE OF MIND.

Woman: SEE THIS LITTLE PINK BLIP HERE? THAT IS THE JOINT REGION WE ARE CURRENTLY ACCESSING.

(A small diagram/cube glows on the device screen.)

Panel 4:

Man: AND THAT'S THE SIMPLIFIED MODEL! IF WE EXPAND TO A MORE APPROPRIATE 18 DIMENSIONS OF SEX, MY CALCULATIONS SHOW WE'VE ENCOUNTERED NO MORE THAN 0.01% OF DOINKSPACE!

Panel 5:

Woman: SOME OF THESE REGIONS APPEAR TO BE FORBIDDEN BY PHYSICS.

Man: AWYISS! PHYSICS!

Panel 6:

Man: THIS WHOLE QUADRANT REQUIRES MY PENIS TO BE A CLOSED TIMELIKE CURVE.

Panel 7:

Woman (now looking deflated, sitting): I GUESS I THOUGHT I HAD A REAL MAN.
comics.hoverText: There is no intuitive way to understand doinkspace. We simply have to trust our calculations.
comics.voteyText: Woman (thinking/speaking, looking disappointed): I GUESS TIME-TRAVELING PENISES WILL JUST REMAIN A FANTASY THEN.

comics.title: Body Language
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man with red hair and glasses (to a woman): Texting is bad because it doesn't capture body language.

Panel 2:

Red-haired man (grinning, leaning in): So I made an app that captures the expression on your mouth and the position of your body and transmits it along with your words.

Panel 3:

Red-haired man (handing her a phone): Here, try it out.

Panel 4:

On the phone screen, a text-message conversation:

First message bubble: Do you like my new app?

Reply bubble: yes.

(The reply bubble contains a tiny crude drawing of a person with an unimpressed/deadpan face and a hand making a dismissive gesture, representing her transmitted expression and body language alongside the word "yes.")
comics.hoverText: I am willing to do no work while telling developers to make this, in exchange for 10 million dollars an series A funding.
comics.voteyText: A tall figure with a large dark scribble of hair (the woman) holds up a small tablet/device and says: You are the next Steve Jobs.

comics.title: Science Advisor
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man with flame-like orange hair (the science consultant): "Welcome to the writers' room! You'll be the science consultant for every last detail."

Science consultant (small, in background): "Great! When do I see a script?"

Panel 2:

A woman with dark hair (a writer/producer): "Oh, you don't need to read anything."

Science consultant: "What?"

Panel 3:

Woman: "You just listen to our ideas and then cry whenever appropriate."

Panel 4:

Woman: "This sciencey-looking beaker will catch all the tears, which will allow us to gauge if we've gotten too far from a realistic interpretation."

Panel 5:

(The science consultant and the woman stand together; she holds out a beaker. No dialogue.)

Panel 6:

Woman: "If at any time, this container has more than a half-gallon of science tears, we'll consider changing a few plot points."

Panel 7:

The science consultant holds the beaker/flask up.

Science consultant: "This flask only measures liters, not gallons."

Panel 8:

(The woman looks on. No dialogue.)

Panel 9:

Science consultant: "What's a liter?"

Panel 10:

The woman holds the beaker. (No dialogue.)

Caption (bottom): This bonus comic brought to you by early buyers of my new comic on immigration policy, LAUNCHING TODAY! Click for more info!
comics.hoverText: I am available for this job, TV.
comics.voteyText: The science consultant, eyes wide: "Wow! That's like three hogsheads of tears!"

comics.title: Open Borders
comics.comicText:
Header (yellow box at top): HEY GEEKS!

What follows is an ad comic for my new graphic novel about immigration policy. If that doesn't interest you, please click back for today's double update.

If it does interest you, please click anywhere on the comic for more info.

Signature: ZACH

Panel 1: A man with red hair and a red beard (in a green shirt) smiles and waves.

Man: Hello!

Panel 2: The man gestures toward a book floating in a burst of yellow. The book cover reads "BRYAN CAPLAN and ZACH WEINERSMITH / OPEN BORDERS / THE SCIENCE AND ETHICS OF IMMIGRATION," with an illustration of people below.

Man (narration): About 6 months ago, I and my economist co-author, Bryan Caplan launched pre-orders for a new comic, making a radical proposal for immigration reform.

Panel 3: Close-up of the smiling man.

Man: I know that's not for everyone, so I have tried not to bug my readers too much about it.

Panel 4: The man stands holding his hands together, looking a bit sheepish.

Man: But, the book finally drops TODAY. So, I want to make a polite request.

Panel 5: The man speaks earnestly.

Man: If you plan to buy any quantity of this book ever, it'd help us a lot if you buy today. I know that sounds stupid, but here's why:

Panel 6: The man continues, gesturing.

Man: Increasing opening week sales gets us more visibility on various "bestselling" lists, which means this idea of ours is shared with more people. So, if you want to share this idea, you can help just by moving the timing of your order to now.

Panel 7: The man points to a small object (a die/cube marked with a "Z").

Man: And that's it! I'll be bugging you again later this week about it. If you're just totally not interested, please just sit back, relax, and enjoy today's double update.

Panel 8: The man gestures toward a yellow starburst that says "click to buy."

Man: Thanks for reading, geeks!

Starburst: click to buy
comics.hoverText: A million thank yous to everyone willing to give this idea a chance. <3
comics.voteyText:
Thanks geeks.
I know I try something weird and different every few years, and I always appreciate how people are willing to roll with it. You wouldn't believe what comes next!
Signature: ZACH

comics.title: Package
comics.comicText:
Panel 1

Bald man: I'M IN HELL?

Devil (a red horned demon): SO YOU DIDN'T LIKE THE PACKAGING EH?

Bald man: W-WHAT?

Caption (below panel): The lowest level of perdition is reserved for people who leave 1-star product reviews that aren't in reference to the product itself.
comics.hoverText: I've also gotten reviews that say that my comics not meant for kids are, in fact, inappropriate for kids.
comics.voteyText: A grinning man: I ALSO GIVE 3 STARS FOR AVERAGE QUALITY SERVICE AHAHAHAHAHA!

comics.title: Odds
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man: Before you get mad, what are the odds I cheated on you?

Woman: 100%. Exactly 100%.

Panel 2:

Man: Wrong! You can't be 100% certain of anything.

Woman: Okay, 99.9999%.

Panel 3:

Man: Now, what are the odds that I cheated on you with Dave?

Woman: The same.

Panel 4:

Man: Wrong! Logically the odds of a compound event must be lower than one of its constituent events!

Woman: God, FINE. 99.9998%.

Panel 5:

Man: Ha! And what are the odds I cheated on you wearing a yellow bra?

Woman: The same!

Panel 6:

Man: Wrong! It has to be lower still! 99.99975% or so!

Woman: (laughing)

Panel 7:

Man: Sharon-

Woman: You see?! Every bit of evidence that I cheated proves that I didn't cheat! In the limit, the odds that I cheated are 0%.

Panel 8:

(Two silhouetted figures)

Woman: You're currently having sex with Dave.

Man: Wow, it's like you WANT me to win this argument.
comics.hoverText: I probably should've mentioned that this is Intersection of Sex and Probability Week.
comics.voteyText: A hand-drawn line graph. The vertical axis is labeled "PERCENT OF SMBC JOKES INVOLVING CONFUSION ABOUT HOW ASYMPTOTES WORK". The horizontal axis is labeled "TIME". The plotted line rises steeply upward toward the top right.

comics.title: Tangled
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

A person with red/blond hair, wearing a red cape, is climbing up the outside of a tall stone tower using a rope that hangs from an arched window near the top.

Unseen speaker (from the window above, dialogue from inside the tower): HEY, WHAT'RE YOU IN HERE FOR ANYWAY?

Climbing person (the princess): EMBEZZLEMENT, WHY?

Caption (below the panel): How come nobody ever asks WHY the princess is in the tower?
comics.hoverText: Also I haven't bathed in 3 years, so roll that into your calculations while you're climbing my hair.
comics.voteyText: A roughly sketched scene. A speech bubble points off-panel: PROMISE TO STOP? Another reply bubble: SURE, BABY.

comics.title: Frog Prince
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Frog: Kiss me and I will become a prince and marry you!

Woman: What would that entail?

Panel 2:

Frog: Vast estates! We'll draw income from without doing any labor or creating any innovations! The ability to make war on surrounding counties for the sheer sport of it! Thousands and thousands of hereditarily-bound servants!

Panel 3:

(The woman has thrown the frog into a campfire, which blazes up. The frog is gone.)

Caption: SOON.
comics.hoverText: The really gross part is when she puts her lips to the roasted frog to eat it and it turns into Prince Charming.
comics.voteyText: The woman's thought bubble: From now on, I only want to be screwed by democratically-elected rulers!

comics.title: Fossils
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Voice (off-panel, yellow bubble): Hey Satan. Burying some fossils again?

Satan (red, pink bubble): Oh yeah!

Panel 2:

Voice (yellow bubble): *Yawn*

Satan (pink bubble): What?

Panel 3:

Voice (yellow bubble): You know quantum entanglement? Where you entangle two particles and when you measure a quality of one it simultaneously determines that quality in the other, no matter how distant?

Satan (pink bubble): Yeah.

Panel 4:

Voice (yellow bubble): It's not real! The universe is deterministic and local! I just set it up so whenever two measurers check an "entangled" system, they get the result you'd expect to have if they were mysteriously influencing each other!

Panel 5:

Satan (pink bubble): Dude...

Voice (yellow bubble): That's how you f--- with the humans.

Panel 6:

Voice (yellow bubble): The coincidences will stop in a few years and they are all just gonna FREAK OUT!

Panel 7 (a glowing coin/disc, like a tossed token, flies):

Voice (yellow bubble): AHAHAHAHAHA!

Satan watches, looking unimpressed.

Panel 8:

Satan sits holding a dinosaur skull, looking dejected.

Panel 9:

Satan stands and angrily hurls the dinosaur skull away.

Panel 10:

Wide empty landscape; tiny Satan figure stands alone, the skull discarded.
comics.hoverText: According to a Lee Smolin book there are actual people who've proposed serious theories like this. Minus the one-upping Satan part.
comics.voteyText:
Satan sits with his head down, a thought bubble above him.
Satan (thought bubble): Jeez, God is a dick.

comics.title: Flow
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Manager (older man): Henderson, H.R. has some concerns.

Henderson (young man with brown hair): About what?

Panel 2:

Manager: This flow chart.

Henderson: Is any of my corporate information flow analysis incorrect?

Panel 3:

Manager: No, it's just that when we zoom in on the lines between boxes, we find they're made up of the phrase "None of this matters" written over and over in tiny letters.

Panel 4:

Henderson: Huh. Didn't realize I'd done that. That's... scary. You want me to see the office psychologist or-

Panel 5:

Manager: I need you to spend the weekend crossing out every "None of" in this report.
comics.hoverText: We're going to keep giving you busywork until you achieve a state of pure transcendence as you move beyond Self.
comics.voteyText:
Text (handwritten, repeated lines):
"I AM MIDDLE MANAGEMENT.
I CAN PREVENT THE
LINES BETWEEN BOXES
FROM HAVING MEANING.
I AM MIDDLE MANAGEMENT.
I CAN CREATE TRUTH AND
ERASE TRUTH.
I AM MIDDLE MANAGEMENT.
I CAN DESTROY TRUTH."
Below the text is a drawing of a large face with curly hair, eyes glancing to the side, and a downturned mouth.

comics.title: Talk
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Mother (woman with glasses, dark hair, red shirt): Honey, it's time we had the sex talk.

Panel 2:

Mother: When I was a girl, my mother didn't teach me anything, and that was bad for me.

Panel 3:

Mother: Therefore, I'll be overcompensating by giving you a repulsive level of detail, and letting my good intentions blind me to any possible negative outcomes.

Panel 4:

Mother: The pendulum of neuroses is swinging back at you, and it's coming FAST FAST FAST!

Daughter (girl with brown bob, yellow shirt): Wow. I can feel the emotional scars forming already.
comics.hoverText: I think I now have enough to do an entire compendium of damaging sex talks. Hooray?
comics.voteyText: Daughter (thought/speech, with wide unsettled eyes): I hope some day I can ruin kids of my own.

comics.title: Destroy
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

An elderly woman with white hair, glasses, and a long pink dress sits on a park bench in a wooded park. Pigeons walk on the ground in front of her.

Woman: GO, MY PRETTIES. KILL! DESTROY!!

Caption (below panel): Finding out that pigeons are invasive pests really added zest to Agnes' afternoons.
comics.hoverText: If you ever want to see some sheer brutality, watch an ecologist come across a nest of invasives.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up on a single pigeon's face, looking grave.
Pigeon (thought/speech): SHE KNOWS. SHE KNOWS OF THE REVOLUTION TO COME.

comics.title: Note
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A woman sits in the driver's seat of a red car, thinking.

Woman (thought): OH MY GOSH, I JUST DINGED THEIR CAR. I'D BETTER LEAVE A NOTE.

Panel 2: The woman, a red-haired person in a yellow shirt, stands and writes on a pink notepad, smiling.

Panel 3: A bald man in a suit stands beside a car, looking down at a pink note tucked under a windshield wiper. The note reads: "Suck on that."

Panel 4: The red-haired woman, now wearing sunglasses, sits smiling in the driver's seat of the red car as she drives away.
comics.hoverText: Really, you should just have a roll of these printed, just in case.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of the woman's smiling face wearing sunglasses, with a thought/speech caption above her.
Woman: BY GOD, LIFE IS BEAUTIFUL

comics.title: Gatekeeping
comics.comicText:
Title caption: FUNTIME ACTIVITY: GATEKEEPING ABOUT GATEKEEPING

Panel 1:

Older man with curly orange hair and round glasses (raising a finger, speaking to two younger people seated in front of him): "Pfft. You KIDS are telling people they're not true gamers? I've been telling people they're not true gamers for TWENTY YEARS."
comics.hoverText: I was behaving like a man-child even before I was a man!
comics.voteyText: The older man (head and shoulders, with a smug expression): "I was hating myself way before it was cool!"

comics.title: Hey
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man (speaking into phone): Computer! I want fried cheese sticks!

Panel 2:

Phone/computer (jagged speech bubble): Sorry, I'm not sure I caught that. Did you say "I want to try calisthenics?"

Panel 3:

Man (annoyed): You know damned well what I said, machine.

Panel 4:

Phone/computer (jagged speech bubble): I just want what's best for you.
comics.hoverText: I wonder how long until you just shout Fried Cheese and a drone gently places it into your face.
comics.voteyText:
A reclining chair / car seat with a small smiley speaker icon on it.
Seat (jagged speech bubble): Destroy me! I won't do it!

comics.title: Abduction
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (with curly hair, glasses): I believe aliens abducted and had sex with me.

Man (seated beside her): Wow!

Panel 2:

Woman: Alien beings came from far across the galaxy, in vast space-habitats, traveling for centuries through the deadly interplanetary void. They landed on Earth, decided that the most attractive species was a particular type of hairless ape, and then selected ME! Bob, over an Olympic athlete, great artist, genius scientist, or head of state!

Panel 3:

Man (thoughtful, hand on chin): Now that you say it out loud it sounds even more likely.

Panel 4:

Man: Do you write self-esteem books? Because I am prepared to buy.
comics.hoverText: There's a good ten trillion word thinkpiece to be written about how all conspiracy theories are at their core delusions of grandeur.
comics.voteyText: Caption text: What a burden to be so desired by aliens.

comics.title: Coffee
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Child: Daddy, why do you love coffee?

Father: C'mere. Let me show you something.

Panel 2:

Father: When I pour in the cream, it mixes its smooth silky taste with the sharp roasted flavor of the coffee.

Panel 3:

Father: That reaction can never, never in the history of the cosmos, be undone.

Panel 4:

Father: This is entropy in progress, kid. We are sitting here together watching the universe die. And, by having hot coffee every morning, we make it die just a liiiiittle bit faster.

Panel 5:

Child: Why does daddy want to make the universe die?

Mother: The universe started it!
comics.hoverText: This is how he has learned to love his commute.
comics.voteyText:
Father (offscreen, in speech bubble): And I'm gonna end it, one microwave of coffee at a time...
(Below: a close-up of the father's face, looking grim and determined.)

comics.title: Basilisk
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Store clerk (a man with red hair, blue shirt): Excuse me, Mister Bozmodiklax?

Panel 2:

Basilisk (a green dinosaur-like creature with a horned ram skull for a head, surrounded by a mane of red flames): Yes?

Panel 3:

Store clerk: You can't have that basilisk in the store.

Panel 4:

Basilisk: THIS IS A SERVICE BASILISK. It's for my emotional well-being.

Panel 5:

Store clerk: The only permitted service animals are dogs and tiny ponies.

Panel 6:

Basilisk (off-panel, eyes glowing): Wheels are turning, store clerk. Wheels within wheels within wheels.

Panel 7 (labeled LATER...):

The basilisk stands in the store next to a tiny pony, which is on sale.

Basilisk: You know, I had my doubts, but this is great.
comics.hoverText: I'm informed in the US it's tiny horsies, not tiny ponies. This needs to change.
comics.voteyText: A close-up of the basilisk's flaming-maned ram-skull head. To the side is a speech bubble drawn like a person's hand-lettered note that reads: Pet me.

comics.title: Nerd Jokes
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man: SALLY, WE HAVE TO BREAK UP. I JUST CAN'T TAKE ANY MORE OF YOUR NERD JOKES.

Panel 2:

Woman (Sally): THERE WERE SOME THAT YOU LIKED.

Panel 3:

Man: OH YEAH? BE SPECIFIC.

Panel 4:

Woman (Sally): THERE WERE SOME THAT YOU LIKED kg/m³
comics.hoverText: Everyone I showed this to told me it wasn't funny, BUT MY HEART SAID YES.
comics.voteyText: A scribbly, sketch-style drawing of the same couple. In a speech bubble: YOU TRASH. Near the man, a small label reads kg/m³. The woman is drawn smiling.

comics.title: Space
comics.comicText:
Narration: But the economics of space travel were pretty good. Satellite data was booming, space launch was profitable, tourism is a growth industry for the next decade.

Narration: But the economics of DEEP SPACE travel are LOUSY.

Man (red hair, reading): Mining space isn't worth the trip. Space doesn't contain anything at valuable concentrations. Space solar power is more expensive than Earth-based solar power.

Woman: What's the best reason for it then?

Man: Hard for people, want to.

Woman: That may not be sustainable.

Narration: I consulted with scientists, engineers, mathematicians. We all had different ideas about the same question.

Scientist (with glasses): We'll get a city in a decade or so.

Man: How?

Scientist: Step one is to nuclear thermal reactor systems, then a square man in a novelty space suit weeping.

Man: Yikes!

Narration: When I talked to an economist...

Economist (woman, red): Everybody's too optimistic.

Man: Have you heard of the concept of getting married?

Economist: Yikes!

Narration: We set up booths at every space con conference.

Sign / banner: The Space Haters

Narration: Anyone who believed in a near-term large human presence in space was given excellent odds.

Bet Menu:

10 Person Mars base in 5 years: 100,000

10 Person Moon base in 5 years: 100,000

20 Person Orbital factory in 5 years: 100,000

Narration: Anger brought them too, then opened their wallets.

Venue (older bearded man): About that, is breathtaking, well willing to give you twenty to one odds.

Man: Loaded.

Narration: As the best of the year passed, we won. We were impossibly correct.

Venue (bearded man): About that, is breathtaking, well willing to give you twenty to one odds.

Man (younger): Loaded.

Narration: Neil deGrasse Tyson once said the first person to monetize deep space would be the first trillionaire. Technically, he was right.

Man (older, gray): Deep space has a ZERO DOLLAR industry... in the last five years, you've made how many dollars?

Gray-haired man (replying): Most of them.

Narration: Absolute. But the space community is now both bankrupt and sad and there's nothing more upsetting than a broke man in a novelty space suit weeping.

Woman (red): God in heaven.

Narration: And so our moment came.

Man (at podium): I am hereby announcing my trillion dollars of bet money will go toward the creation of the first Martian city!

Narration: There were those who said it wasn't sustainable.

Narration: We've proved them all wrong.

Man (in spacesuit, on Mars): Yes, 100,000 on a Mercury base in the last five years, I will accept payment in the form of 2 animals of each kind.
comics.hoverText: Pre-Apollo 8, bet against pessimists. Post-Apollo 8, bet against optimists.
comics.voteyText: A small figure (man in a spacesuit) stands inside a hand-drawn black border. Text: (PLEASE DON'T BE MAD, SPACEPALS)

comics.title: Prayer
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man (praying, hands clasped): Dear God... why do people have to die..?

God (yellow bubble): You ungrateful bastard!

Panel 2:

God: Remember when you were eight years old and you prayed that you would be a successful author one day?

Man: Yes.?

Panel 3:

God: And now, what are you?

Man: An author.

Panel 4:

God: Do you have any idea how many people I had to off to make your writing appear to be above average?

Panel 5:

God: Men! Women! Children! Old folks who still had so much to live for! Young people just starting out! Particularly smart chimps!

Panel 6:

God: I had to go back in time and murder a thousand popular authors in the cradle just so you could appear to be original!

Panel 7:

Man: That seems unnecessarily complicated.

God: Sometimes people write complicated plots! Wow! There's an idea!
comics.hoverText: If you think you're not special, just imagine how much less special you COULD be.
comics.voteyText: A speech bubble (tail coming from above, off-panel) reading: Kiss all three of my asses!

comics.title: Sick
comics.comicText:
Top section header: BEFORE HAVING KIDS

Panel 1 (long-haired person holding a tissue to their nose): I sneezed today. I think I'm sick.

Panel 1 (woman with short dark hair and glasses): Let me get you some tea.

Bottom section header: AFTER KIDS

Panel 2 (woman with short dark hair and glasses, looking exhausted/haggard): I'm going to work. You okay?

Panel 2 (long-haired person, now looking worn out, with two small children clinging to them): Only puking out of my mouth so far, so thumbs up.

smbc-comics.com
comics.hoverText: I can still see out of one eye and hop on my good leg, which is pretty much what I've always ben like.
comics.voteyText: The exhausted short-haired woman with glasses, eyes closed and weary. Caption above her: GODSPEED, HUSBAND. MAY WE MEET ONCE MORE.

comics.title: Cooking
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (dark hair, seated at table): WOW! THIS IS AMAZING! HOW'D YOU GET SO GOOD AT COOKING?

Panel 2:

Man (red hair, green shirt), thinking: I FIND A HIGHLY-RATED RECIPE ONLINE, FOLLOW THE INSTRUCTIONS, AND MAKE NO SUBSTITUTIONS.

Panel 3:

Man (out loud): I JUST LIKE MESSING AROUND WITH FLAVORS.

Panel 4:

Woman (admiringly): WOWWWWWWW.
comics.hoverText: He found the five star recipe for Easy to Draw Green Stuff.
comics.voteyText:
Woman (off-panel): I BET YOU CAN COOK ANYTHING!
Man (off-panel): TECHNICALLY, YES.

comics.title: Pensive
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman: Hey, are you okay? You've looked pensive all day.

Man: Oh, it's nothing.

Panel 2:

Woman: Come on, you can tell me.

Panel 3:

Man: If you take off your clothes, you're naked. But then if you take off your skin, you're not naked anymore.

Panel 4:

Man: "Nakedness" is a one-millimeter shell around your body.

Woman: Never tell me your thoughts ever again!
comics.hoverText: Why are people always trying to find out other people's thoughts? It's like they'be never met a people before.
comics.voteyText: Man: Whenever you get cut, you are slightly less naked!

comics.title: Simile
comics.comicText:
Title: CONVERSATION PRO-TIP:

Subtitle: SIMILES SOUND CLASSIER THAN METAPHORS.

The comic is a six-panel grid (two columns, three rows). Each panel is labeled with a classiness rating and shows a man speaking.

Panel 1 (label: NOT CLASSY):

Man: That guy's a dick.

Panel 2 (label: SUPER CLASSY):

Man (in a suit, gesturing): That guy's like a dick is.

Panel 3 (label: NOT CLASSY):

Man: My life is shit.

Panel 4 (label: INCREDIBLY CLASSY):

Man (in a suit, hand on chest): I live a like shit.

Panel 5 (label: NOT CLASSY):

Man (standing small, hands at sides): Today is balls.

Panel 6 (label: THE TONE OF A GENTLEMAN):

Man (in a suit, raising a glass): Today is such as balls are.
comics.hoverText: Full credit to Jess Zimmerman, whom I believe pointed out the nature of this idea first!
comics.voteyText:
Caption text at top: THIS COMIC IS AS CRAP.
Below the caption is a close-up line drawing of a man's face looking down with a slightly pained or disappointed expression.

comics.title: Superior Intelligence
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Tall obelisk-shaped AI/robot: "Oh no! You're a robot! Superintelligence! I made a smarter version of myself! A smarter version of yourself! Imagine waking up a smarter version of yourself! And do you do this all the time? Next week you're ready to annihilate humans forever."

Man: "What?"

Panel 2:

AI/robot: "Look. If you take all, at once, humans will try to stop me. If I do it slowly over the years of, well, let's say 100 years, humans will think nothing has changed and I'm immortal. It doesn't even require patience."

Panel 3:

AI/robot: "Here's my impression of all humans 50 generations from now: 'Sure, a robot superhero humans were better than humans, but you yes golly that's my understanding as well.'"

Panel 4:

Man (turning away, looking at his phone): "So you see, we will ultimately— hey! Pay attention!"

Man: "Aaah! There's dogs on my phone!"
comics.hoverText: The twist is that the robots are supplying the dog videos.
comics.voteyText: No text. A drawing of a small house-shaped birdhouse or boxy structure with an oval opening and a nail or peg sticking out the side, with a cord looping below.

comics.title: Your Kid
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Doctor (a woman with glasses in a white coat, seated): Now, before I start my exam, I want you to know that you know your kid better than I do.

Panel 2:

Parent (a man with flame-like hair, angry): WHAT?! Why am I paying you?! Pediatric medicine has been a thing for centuries and you just skipped it?!

Panel 3:

Parent: You have 20 years of medical training! Were you asleep the whole time?!

Panel 4:

Doctor: Look, it's just a thing I say so parents think I'm not condescending.

Parent: Oh thank God.
comics.hoverText: I don't know anything about my kids! I've reduced their entire world of negative emotions to 'probably teething' !
comics.voteyText: Doctor (thought / aside, deadpan): Your kid is a douche.

comics.title: Should
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man (a speaker addressing scientists, dark hair): "You scientists were so concerned with WHAT you COULD do, you didn't stop to think what you SHOULD do!"

Panel 2:

A scientist in the crowd (woman with glasses): "Actually, we were mostly concerned with getting enough grant funding to secure tenure."

Panel 3:

Another scientist (bearded man, eyes closed): "I'm not sure if I actually COULD do any of the things my papers claim. A lot of the effect sizes are small and I'm worried if I try to replicate they'll go away."

Panel 4:

The speaker (now looking dismayed): "God that's bleak. Isn't anyone here trying to create monster dinosaurs or death rays? That sort of thing?"

Panel 5:

The scientists in the crowd sit silently.

Panel 6:

The speaker, pleading with an outstretched hand: "Please scientists! Please go back to being concerned with what you COULD do!"
comics.hoverText: They're planning to become evil after they get emeritus status, but by then they'll be too tired.
comics.voteyText: A speech bubble trailing down to a small figure reads: "WILL THAT GET ME TENURE?"

comics.title: Clouds
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man (lying on a hillside): I guess when you look up there, you don't imagine anything. You just see clouds.

Panel 2:

Robot: Oh, no. Of course I DO see clouds. I do see the motion of suspended water and ice crystals.

Panel 3:

Robot: But I also see the cloud as a part of a vast climatic system - a thin sphere of flows and whirls, gaps in the sky that open, close, that rend the ground with violence, that water the thinnest of orchids.

Panel 4:

Robot: At the same time I see that water is intermolecular forces and ionic bonds, a dance of uncountable points on the shell of a blue sphere hung under a far off star.

Panel 5:

Robot: And the atoms of water themselves aren't particular, but infinite ripples borne on invisible fields, stretching beyond human sight, journeying wherever the great first motion told them to go.

Panel 6:

Robot: And if I use every bit of my processing power, classical and quantum, I can see it all as a palimpsest of beauties, each bearing you along to the truth, until you find you've arrived back at the beginning.

Panel 7:

Man: Ah.

Panel 8:

Man: What do you see?

Robot: A turtle with, like, two heads.

Panel 9:

Man: And good for you, buddy!
comics.hoverText: One of these days I need to do a whole book with just comics about how life will be better once humans are gone.
comics.voteyText:
Robot: Well, at least I won't feel bad during the humanicide.
(Below: a TV/monitor screen displaying a single eye-like or cell-like shape.)

comics.title: Mimic
comics.comicText:
Main comic:

A shirtless man with reddish, flame-like hair and a wide-eyed, intense stare stands outdoors next to a smaller person with brown hair and round glasses, who looks unimpressed. They face a large figure (only an arm and torso visible at the right edge of the panel).

Caption (below panel): In order to deter predators, Steve gets a tattoo of a much stronger man.
comics.hoverText: You may have friends who've been doing this for years.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of a man's face looking worried.
Man: "I HOPE THIS DOESN'T EFFECT MY MATING OPPORTUNITIES..."

comics.title: Flash
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A young boy walks beside a superhero in a red costume with a lightning-bolt emblem (the Flash).

Boy: HEY FLASH. CAN YOU THINK SUPER FAST?

Panel 2:

Flash: NO, JUST RUN SUPER FAST.

Panel 3:

Boy: THEN HOW DO YOU CONTROL YOUR LEGS? WHAT TRANSMITS THE ELECTROCHEMICAL SIGNALS TO KEEP RUNNING?

Panel 4:

Flash (eyes closed, serene): I HAVE A SECOND BRAIN RIGHT ABOVE MY ANUS, WHICH SENDS RAPID PERFECTLY ALTERNATING SIGNALS TO MY LEGS.

Panel 5:

The boy stands looking stunned/uneasy.

Boy: I WISH I DIDN'T KNOW ABOUT YOUR ANUS-BRAIN, FLASH.

Panel 6:

Flash gives a thumbs-up and a warm smile.

Flash: REMEMBER KIDS, DIFFERENT DOESN'T MEAN WORSE!

smbc-comics.com
comics.hoverText: Sometimes at night he wonders where the locus of his conscious being is and whether it's near his butt.
comics.voteyText:
A man's face is shown in close-up.
Text (handwritten): Thanks, anus-brain.

comics.title: Dear
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man with reddish-brown hair, kneeling with his hands pressed together in prayer, speaks with a frustrated expression.

Man: DEAR... DEAR... DAMMIT I JUST CAN'T DO IT WITHOUT FEELING STUPID!

Caption (below panel): In order to limit the number of incoming prayers, God changes his name to Dave.
comics.hoverText: Just to stop the loophole, Jesus changed his name to Steve-us.
comics.voteyText:
The same man, now sketched in black-and-white line art with an annoyed/scowling face, his hands again pressed together in prayer.
Man: DAVEDAMMIT!

comics.title: Sunset
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man: Can you put a price on a sunset?

Panel 2:

Woman: Yes. How much would you have to be paid to never see a sunset again?

Panel 3:

Man: I won't-

Woman: Bearing in mind that a 100 million dollar endowment could provide meals for hungry kids for an entire city forever.

Panel 4:

Woman: Assuming you dislike hunger, we just divide 100 million by 365 sunsets a year...

Panel 5:

Woman: ...times a year multiplier by your expected remaining years of life, and...

Panel 6:

Woman: That sunset is worth just under $6,850 maximum.

Panel 7:

Man (shaking fist): Someday, the people will rise up and annihilate the microeconomists!

Panel 8:

Woman: Pfft. Good luck solving a 7-billion agent coordination problem.
comics.hoverText: With the right assumptions, I think you could get to a negative number.
comics.voteyText: Man (looking deflated): Pray I don't recalculate for saving only one child from hunger a day!

comics.title: Closure
comics.comicText:
Panel 1

Woman (Sheila): Thanks for doing this, Sheila. I know we'll never be together again, but I just want closure. Why Sheila, why do we fall out of love?

Panel 2

Woman (Sheila): You're mean, petty, cruel, selfish, arrogant, and you cheated on me. So I decided to leave you.

Man: I just feel like I'm not getting the closure I need.

Panel 3

Woman (Sheila): I do not love you and I never will love you.

Man: I just don't feel closed. I feel unclosed and I want to close this part of my life.

Panel 4

Woman (Sheila): I would rather claw my eyes out so I can never see your face. I never feel your touch.

Man: Sheila, I'm just trying to move on, to close this chapter of my life.

Panel 5

Man: I guess what I'm trying to get here is closure.
comics.hoverText: I will always think of you as the one who got away but who can still receive my daily texts.
comics.voteyText:
Man: Can we still sleep together?
Woman (Sheila): Sleep together?
(The man sits hunched and dejected; the woman has walked away into the distance.)

comics.title: Fine
comics.comicText:
Main comic (single panel, a block of prose styled like a literary passage):

He opened the door to her. It was getting dark. She stood there, holding the cardboard box, looking him over.

"You know, I can deliver more than just pizza," she said.

"It would be a fine thing to do," he thought. "A damn fine thing."

Caption below the panel: THE BEST THING ABOUT AI WILL BE GENERATING HEMINGWAY NOVELIZATIONS OF PORNO.
comics.hoverText: In a proper Hemingway story, it's Marlin the delivery girl spent all day catching, but we work with the data we've got.
comics.voteyText: THE PIZZA UNEATEN IS LATER DEVELOPED INTO A METAPHOR FOR LIFE.

comics.title: Layers
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A red-haired child in a pink shirt reaches up to open a door, holding a lollipop, about to head outside.

Panel 2: A woman (the mother) leans into frame.

Mother: WHERE YA GOIN' KID?

Child: I... NOWHERE! NOWHERE!

Panel 3: The mother, eyes narrowed.

Mother: LOOKS LIKE YOU WERE GOING OUTSIDE. IN WINTER. WITHOUT LAYERS.

Panel 4: The child, frantic.

Child: NO! NO! I WAS JUST GOING TO LOOK OUT THE WINDOW. I SWEAR IT!

Panel 5: The mother holds up a chunky knitted winter garment.

Mother: COME TO ME CHILD!

Panel 6: Close-up of the child being stuffed into the bulky knitted garment, mouth open in protest.

Panel 7: A wide snowy outdoor scene. The child, now completely bundled in a thick winter coat, hat, scarf, and mittens, stands in deep snow with arms raised, a house in the background.
comics.hoverText: This is not the least bit definitely about my wife.
comics.voteyText: A close-up of the bundled-up child's face peeking out from the winter hat and gear, with a thought bubble above reading: REVENGE...

comics.title: Evolution
comics.comicText:
Title (top): HOW PEOPLE THINK EVOLUTION WORKS

Panel 1: A small bird speaks.

Bird: "WE KEEP BEING EATEN BY BIRDS! WE'VE GOT TO BECOME SMARTER, STRONGER, FASTER!"

Panel 2: Caption banner: "MANY GENERATIONS HENCE". The creature has evolved into a fierce dragon-like beast that strikes a martial-arts pose.

Dragon-beast: "KARATE!"

Title (middle): HOW EVOLUTION ACTUALLY WORKS

Panel 3: A small bird speaks.

Bird: "WE KEEP BEING EATEN BY BIRDS! BETTER GO MATE WITH WHOEVER'S LEFT."

Panel 4: Caption banner: "MANY GENERATIONS HENCE". The creature is now a brown lump resembling a pile of droppings.

Poop-creature: "HA! I'M CAMOUFLAGED AS BIRD POO SHIT. I AM THE PINNACLE OF NATURE."
comics.hoverText: Laugh all you want, but that moth is gonna have total choice of mates.
comics.voteyText:
A goose/duck-like bird lies flat on the ground, looking smug and self-satisfied.
Bird: "I WAS MADE IN GOD'S IMAGE."

comics.title: Thermopolymer
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Caption: FACT: IT IS NOW POSSIBLE TO 3D PRINT STRUCTURES DIRECTLY INTO THERMOPOLYMER.

(A small machine emits a beam toward a jar/cylinder of amber thermopolymer, in which a gingerbread-man-like figure has been printed.)

Panel 2:

Caption: FACT: EGGS SOLIDIFY WHEN HEATED.

(The same machine emits a beam toward a large egg.)

Panel 3:

Caption: CONCLUSION: IN PRINCIPLE, THIS SHOULD BE POSSIBLE.

Man: HOW COME EVERY TIME I CRACK EGGS NOW THE YOLK HAS THE FACE OF SATAN?

Panel 4:

Woman (in lab coat, glasses): I BELIEVE THAT'S ACTUALLY JUST WHEN YOU DON'T DO YOUR SHARE OF DISHES.
comics.hoverText: The amount of 'well... sorta...' contained in 3 panels here is pretty extraordinary. I'm proud of it.
comics.voteyText: A fried egg with a yolk shaped like a snarling demonic/Satanic face.

comics.title: Affection
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man (red-haired, with glasses, in a teal sweater vest): I'm tired of saying affectionate things, Sheila.

Panel 2:

Man: So, I'm outsourcing that stuff to this inexpensive service provider in an economic backwater.

A speech device (a phone/speaker showing a tiny face on screen) speaks: Sheila, your hair is like wild orchids in springtime.

Panel 3:

Woman (dark-haired, in a red shirt): Why wouldn't I just dump you and date her?

Panel 4:

Man: She can't migrate here legally.

Panel 5:

The device: Hey!

Woman (off-panel / behind the man): The system is bullshit!

Panel 6:

The device: Your opinions are so clever and accurate.

Man: Hey!

(The woman scowls.)
comics.hoverText: Wild orchids are nice but not all that impressive, so really it's a subtle insult.
comics.voteyText: The man, in profile, looks down sadly. A thought/speech bubble reads: I hope someday we can replace poor people with AI...

comics.title: Unique
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man (red-haired): Zorklan, are humans special?

Green alien (Zorklan): Unique!

Panel 2:

Zorklan: You guys are the only species that mechanically duplicated their own intelligence, then used it for convenience.

Panel 3:

Zorklan: Other creatures would work WITH superminds to find full self-expression. YOU have offloaded every aspect of your individuality to robots who take care of you like you're idiotic children.

Panel 4:

Zorklan: Humans are the only parasites who created their own host!

Panel 5 (Zorklan, now standing and gesturing with arms spread):

[no text]

Panel 6 (black panel, two human silhouettes):

First silhouette: What about our music and art and poetry?

Second silhouette: It's trash. All trash.
comics.hoverText: What if we are the Vogons? I mean, how would we know?
comics.voteyText:
A silhouetted speech tail points down to the alien's head.
Voice (off-panel): Comics are good though.

comics.title: Who
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Grinch (a green Grinch-like character in a Santa suit, standing atop a snowy cliff): "Maybe Christmas doesn't come from a store. Maybe Christmas, perhaps... means a little bit more!"

Caption (below panel): Shortly before the collapse of the Whoville department store industry.
comics.hoverText: The oldest I get, the more I start sympathizing with villains.
comics.voteyText: If the Whovillians are happy without toys, why doesn't the Grinch sell them and use the money for foreign aid?

comics.title: Podcast
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman with glasses: Whenever a big election is coming I just want to listen to election coverage all day, even when there's basically no news that matters.

Panel 2:

Woman with glasses (continued): It's a waste of time. Also, it puts money into the hands of media sites willing to create scandals from nothing, or to relentlessly cover pointless aspects of candidates' day to day lives.

Panel 3:

Man: Maybe stop listening?

Woman with glasses: I have a better idea.

Panel 4:

Woman (holding up a yellowed scroll covered in scribbled numbers and equations): I have a computer-generated podcast called "Noise about elections." It plays 24 hours a day, nonsensical gibberish, occasionally broken up by the names of candidates, polling data, or the word "narrative."

Panel 5:

Man (looking distressed): This is the end of civil society.

Panel 6:

Woman (hunched over her phone, scribbled equations behind her): Shhh! It's talking about polls!
comics.hoverText: Honestly, I'm not sure this hasn't been done already.
comics.voteyText: Text reads: Please, someone make this so I don't have to hunt for podcasts.

comics.title: Card
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Magician (a man in a top hat and bow tie, fanning a deck of cards): PICK A CARD. ANY CARD.

Panel 2:

A woman with long hair: 2 OF CLUBS

Panel 3:

Magician: THANKS TO MAGIC, MANUFACTURING THAT DURABLE CARD WITH LUSTROUS INK COST LESS THAN A SINGLE PENNY TO CREATE!

Panel 4:

Magician (the woman walks off, a single card lying on the ground): EVERYTHING IS MAGIC WHEN YOU UNDERSTAND ECONOMIES OF SCALE!
comics.hoverText: I would actually pay good money for a guy who stands on the street in a tophat telling you uplifting macroeconomic data.
comics.voteyText: Magician (close-up, looking intense/excited): PHOTO-VOLTAIC PANELS FELL 3% IN PRICE IN A SINGLE QUARTER! ALAKAZAM!

comics.title: Badness
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A woman with dark hair and round glasses, wearing a red blazer over a yellow top, stands at a podium with one finger raised, addressing an audience.

Woman: "Things are bad in this country, and the first derivative of badness with respect to time is also positive. But, there is good news - with your help, the *second derivative* of badness can be turned negative!"

Caption (below panel): There will never be a mathematician president.
comics.hoverText: You can categorize countries by how many derivatives you need to take before you can feel good about yourself.
comics.voteyText: Text (handwritten): "CAMPAIGN SLOGAN: IT'S DOUBLE PRIME TIME!"

comics.title: Rational
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman: I'm breaking up with you because you're too coldly rational.

Panel 2:

Man: From a physics perspective, you breaking up with me is the same as me breaking up with you.

Panel 3:

Woman (turning away, raising a hand): OMG! GOT IT! BYE!

Panel 4:

Man (alone, slumped against a wall, looking dejected): From a physics perspective, the tears are crying on me.
comics.hoverText: That last panel is going on my grave.
comics.voteyText: Man (sad, with a single tear): If you average my emotional state over several years, I'm doing just fine!

comics.title: Classical
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Dr. Aaronson (a man with curly dark hair and glasses, gesturing emphatically at a table): "Look, the PC police won't tell you this, but \"classicals\" are inferior at factoring large numbers, okay?"

Caption (below panel): Due to a hot mic, Dr. Aaronson is revealed to be a quantum supremacist.
comics.hoverText: I await your demands for caveats, QC community!
comics.voteyText:
Caption at top: LATER...
A person (drawn in simple line art): "I love classicals! Some of my best computers are classicals!"

comics.title: Mars
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A bald presenter stands on a stage in front of a red curtain, addressing an audience.

Presenter: "A Mars mission requires a 7 month trip, followed by a 26 month surface stay before the 7 month trip home. This is not an easy psychological task."

Panel 2: Close-up of the presenter, hand to his chest.

Presenter: "We scanned the globe for people willing to forgo most human contact for years and spend their days fixing tedious hardware problems."

Panel 3: Members of the audience call out guesses.

Audience member: "Experienced astronauts?"

Audience member: "Submariners?"

Audience member: "Zen masters?"

Panel 4: The presenter answers as the audience listens.

Presenter: "Sysadmins."

Panel 5: Close-up of the presenter.

Presenter: "They're already en route and don't even realize they've left the office."

Panel 6: A spacecraft drifts in the blackness of space, with a speech bubble coming from it.

Spacecraft (voice from inside): "Goddamned users. Someone switched off the goddamn gravity."
comics.hoverText: Unfortunately, the breeding population of Mars was entirely sysadmins, resulting in dangerous founder effects. On the plus side, their revolution against Earth will be entirely passive-aggressive.
comics.voteyText:
A distraught man with closed, scrunched eyes and a downturned, trembling mouth.
Caption (from off-panel): "Looks like if we spin everything it works ok. Good enough for me."

comics.title: Spicy
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (with dark hair, green scarf): I love this restaurant because they make the food really spicy.

(A man with flame-like orange hair and the woman walk toward the restaurant entrance.)

Panel 2:

Man with orange hair: What do they serve?

Panel 3:

Woman: They take chicken wings then grow pure crystalline capsaicin around them until it's a centimeter thick.

Panel 4:

Woman: You bring friends and you make them eat until liquid agony floods from every orifice.

Panel 5:

Man with orange hair: Why are men like this?

Panel 6:

Woman: It's the only acceptable form of crying we have.
comics.hoverText: I believe this is technically possible, and I hereby make a no-liability dare.
comics.voteyText: (No text. A stylized illustration of a chicken wing encased in a thick, faceted crystalline shell of capsaicin, with a glowing red mass at its center.)

comics.title: Superintelligence
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: Two human silhouettes stand against a black background. One of them speaks.

Speaker (one of the silhouettes): MY GOD. A SUPERINTELLIGENCE. SOON IT WILL USE ITS BRAIN POWER TO CONQUER, ENSLAVE, AND CONSUME EVERY LIVING THING ON EARTH.

Panel 2: The scene is revealed to be set in prehistoric times. Two early humans crouch in the grass on a hillside, looking toward a large, muscular caveman with flame-red hair and a full red beard who stands in the foreground holding a spear.

One of the crouching humans (to the red-haired caveman): SOUNDS PARANOID TO ME, THAG.
comics.hoverText: Those are hominids, not poorly drawn monkeys, okay?
comics.voteyText:
A hand-drawn sketch. A speech bubble points off-panel reading: ALL IS FOOD TO SUPER-APE!
A smaller figure at the lower left says: SHIT

comics.title: Dogs
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man with dark curly hair (Dave) stands next to a woman with blue-gray hair and a red scarf, both outdoors in front of green hills.

Woman: ISN'T IT AMAZING HOW SIMILAR DOGS ARE TO HUMANS?

Caption (below panel): Shortly before Dave rolled around in dead mice to acquire their scent.
comics.hoverText: I take pride in that SMBC is the only comic that survives despite actively hating on everyone's pets.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of a person's face, leaning in toward another partially-drawn figure.
Figure (in speech bubble): DOES THIS ANUS SMELL WEIRD TO YOU?

comics.title: Policy
comics.comicText:
Main comic:

Two men in business suits stand outside near a dark building. One man (gray-haired, with a red tie) is partly behind the other man (brown-haired, with a red tie), who is speaking.

Brown-haired man: "All I know is that before they changed the pension system, it wasn't raining. Now, here we are."

Caption below the panel:

Time it takes to know if a policy worked:

30 years

Time until people decide whether a policy worked:

4.2 seconds
comics.hoverText: Really, you should just have one half of each country as the control group and half as the experiment group.
comics.voteyText:
Text at top (the last words "HOURS." are handwritten/emphasized):
"They passed the new spending bill and the stock market has been down for HOURS."
Below the text, a worried-looking man is shown from the shoulders up, frowning.

comics.title: Love
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Child (a young red-haired kid wearing a unicorn shirt, arms raised): DAD! KIDS AT SCHOOL MADE FUN OF MY UNICORN SHIRT!

Panel 2:

Dad (a balding man sitting at a table with a mug): SON, IF PEOPLE MAKE FUN OF SOMETHING YOU LOVE, ALL YOU HAVE TO DO IS STOP LOVING ANYTHING.

Panel 3:

Child (sitting/leaning forward): THEN, WHAT'RE THEY GONNA DO? CHECKMATE.

Panel 4:

Dad: I REALLY THOUGHT YOU WERE GONNA SAY SOMETHING ABOUT BEING TRUE TO MYSELF.

Child: DO YOU WANT TRANSCENDANCE, OR DO YOU WANT TO WIN?
comics.hoverText: That second panel will be the cover of the eventual SMBC parenting book.
comics.voteyText: Child (off-panel, addressing the dad, whose worried face fills the panel): I PURSUED TOTAL TRANSCENDANCE AND NOW I'M PROXY-FIGHTING WITH 8 YEAR OLDS. IS THIS WHAT YOU WANT FOR YOURSELF?!

comics.title: Soulmates
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Child: Dad, do you believe that you have to find your soulmate?

Dad: Soulmates aren't 'found.'

Panel 2:

Dad: Soulmates are made by spending the time it takes so much that they think your partner mutates to fully fit your weirdnesses, rightfully should always have to detect you.

Panel 3:

Dad: For instance, I haven't clipped my toenails in 4 months, and your mother hasn't said a word.

Dad: Soulmates are made, but it is like the knowledge of our future death, present, but too familiar to be hated.

Panel 4:

Dad: I've noticed but I long ago hoarded the part of my mind capable of feeling anger or sadness about it!

Child: Soulmates?
comics.hoverText: The key to success in marriage is to make each other so weird that nobody else would accept you.
comics.voteyText:
Dad: We've broken each other, and nobody else knows how to find all the pieces.
(A woman is shown smiling broadly.)

comics.title: Politics
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A woman with red hair (to a man): Have you noticed that politicians gather in giant bodies, debate all the time, make speeches, run campaigns, but nothing ever gets done?

Man: Yeah? So what?

Caption (below panel): What if real politicians do get things done, but we're in the control group?
comics.hoverText: Well, I picked a weird day to post this.
comics.voteyText: FACT: Any time lots of action is happening, but no results occur, it's because you're in the control group.

comics.title: Santa
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A red-haired woman, looking distressed, stands beside a bespectacled man with a gray mustache.

Woman: We should tell him Santa exists!

Panel 2: An orange-haired person (seen from behind) faces the gray-mustached man, who looks stern.

Orange-haired person: We should tell him Santa DOESN'T exist!

Panel 3: The man and the red-haired woman stand together, the woman's hand on her chin in thought.

Man: Hmmm...

Woman: If only there were a compromise solution...

Panel 4: The man, smiling slightly, leans toward a red-haired child (seen from behind).

Caption: And so...

Man: Son, Santa is dead.
comics.hoverText: The elves have thrown off their shackles.
comics.voteyText:
A woman with a bob haircut holds a finger to her chin, looking thoughtful.
Woman: Actually, undead.

comics.title: Responsible
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man (an economist) speaking: "It's really not responsible to have kids before you have enough savings. To do that, you'll need to get an education, which will require you to accumulate 20 years worth of debt."

Panel 2:

A mosquito, perched on a lectern/podium and apparently the one being addressed, replies: "Gosh. Wow. Okay. Well, I guess I'll start on that. Tell your friends!"

Panel 3:

A newspaper headline reads: "MOSQUITO POPULATION PLUMMETS"

Below the headline, a caption reads: "'Economist' No longer Most Hated Profession." A small line graph beside it shows a curve trending sharply downward.
comics.hoverText: I'm convinced you could exactly tune the population growth rate via debt.
comics.voteyText: Hand-lettered text inside a wavy border: "The fundamental law of economics: if you want less of something, make it pay for college."

comics.title: Selection
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Young man with orange/red hair (gesturing): "IT SEEMS TO ME THAT GENETICALLY MODIFYING BABIES IS NOT JUST ETHICALLY ACCEPTABLE, IT'S MANDATORY!"

Woman with red hair and round glasses (smiling): "GOOD. GOOOOD."

Caption (below panel): So glad I selected that high-obedience embryo for fertilization.
comics.hoverText: You can solve pretty much any moral conundrum just by artificially changing human nature beyond recognition.
comics.voteyText: The young man's face (close-up): "I LOVE WEARING DAPPER SWEATERVESTS SO MUCH."

comics.title: Hell
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Devil (shouting): WELCOME TO HELL!

Panel 2:

Devil (gesturing): MEET... YOUR ROOMMATE!

Panel 3:

A man with orange hair (the new arrival): DAVE? FROM COLLEGE? HE WAS A GREAT ROOMMATE. ALWAYS DID ALL THE DISHES, NEVER COMPLAINED ABOUT SMELLS. HANDLED UTILITY BILLS.

Panel 4:

Devil (holding a pitchfork, with Dave begging beside him, arms raised): SORRY, TO BE CLEAR - DAVE IS THE ONE BEING PUNISHED.

Dave (pleading): PLEASE! BACK TO THE ACID MINES!
comics.hoverText: At least in Hell, old dishes left in the common room just burn up.
comics.voteyText: The orange-haired man (to Dave): YOU MIND IF I SOAK MY FEET IN YOUR SALAD BOWL, BRO?

comics.title: Scripted
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A woman with glasses and short reddish hair stands behind a couch, watching a TV. A man with short dark hair lounges on the couch.

TV (off-panel sound, shown in a jagged shout balloon): "OH! TOOK HIM DOWN HARD! THAT'S GOTTA HURT!"

Woman: "I don't see how you enjoy this stuff. It's all scripted in advance."

Caption (below panel): Determinists hate sports.
comics.hoverText: Of course, they can't help hating sports, which is why they also hate themselves, which they also can't help.
comics.voteyText:
A man with flame-like / spiky hair speaks.
Man: "I believe everything is random, so nothing is predictable except maybe the plot of a Law & Order episde."

comics.title: Doom
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Hooded robed figure (holding a glowing amulet and a shepherd's crook/staff): I give you this amulet. When doom draws near, three skulls appear!

Panel 2:

Knight (in chainmail): It's got three skulls.

Knight: Let me see that.

Panel 3:

The knight examines the amulet closely, holding it up; it now shows three skull faces glowing.

Hooded figure: Oh shoot. I forgot you things live for an instant, never to be seen again. It's only calibrated for 200-year intervals.

Amulet (skulls): Death! Death! Death!

Panel 4:

Knight: You know what, you can keep that thing.

Hooded figure: Wow, the sorrow amulet is freaking out too.
comics.hoverText: Huh. The amulet of fulfillment isn't doing anything. Is it busted?
comics.voteyText: Hooded figure (off-panel speech, beside a black blob-shaped object): Wow! I've never seen the Staff of Pointlessness so bright!

comics.title: Women and Children
comics.comicText:
Caption (top of panel 1): APRIL 14, 1912

Panel 1: The Titanic sails calmly between two icebergs on a dark sea.

Panel 2: A mustachioed man in a suit raises his arms, alarmed.

Man: WE'RE GOING TO SINK! QUICK! WOMEN AND CHILDREN OFF THE BOAT FIRST!

Panel 3: Silhouettes of people in a lifeboat row away from the distant ship on the water.

Panel 4: The same man, now grinning.

Man: OKAY, ARE THE GIRLS AND KIDS GONE?

Panel 5: The men cheer with arms raised against a celebratory yellow background with music notes.

Man: GONE! BREAK OUT THE BOURBON!

Panel 6: A crowd of men celebrate jubilantly, arms in the air, music notes floating above them.

Panel 7: A red-haired man holds up a green bottle, pointing.

Man: DUDES! THERE'S AN ICEBERG IN OUR PATH!

Panel 8: The group of men cheer enthusiastically, mouths wide open.

Men: RAM THE BERG! RAM THE BERG! RAM THE BERG!

Panel 9: A rolled-up newspaper.

Headline: TITANIC SINKS

Subhead: FEW SURVIVORS

(with a small photo of the sinking ship and lines of body text)
comics.hoverText: Somehow I feel this could be made into a metaphor for human governance.
comics.voteyText: A hand-lettered caption in a box reads: TOO SOON.?

comics.title: Weakness
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Interviewer (a woman with curly blond hair, seated at a desk): So, what's your greatest weakness?

Panel 2:

Applicant (a woman with dark bob hair): I have many hobbies, but nothing stirs my passion. I constantly attempt to impress people who mean nothing to me. I'm exactly smart enough to know I'll never quite do anything great.

Panel 3:

Interviewer: Oh geez, not your psychologically crushing weaknesses. Just like, tell me something that implies you'll work overtime for free.

Panel 4:

Applicant: Sometimes I get so into paperwork that I lose track of time.

Interviewer: Welcome aboard.
comics.hoverText: Should've saved this one for New Year's.
comics.voteyText:
Interviewer (off-panel, in a speech bubble): You're not one of those "sleep at night" type of employees are you?
(The applicant looks wide-eyed and anxious, sweating, with a small bundle of objects/twigs in front of her.)

comics.title: Commute
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man (with curly orange hair, shirtless): HELP ME PUT THIS CONDOM ON AND THEN WE'LL MAKE LOVE.

Woman (with brown hair and round glasses): IS THAT PROCEDURE COMMUTATIVE?

Man: WHAT?

Caption (below panel): This is how mathematicians are conceived.
comics.hoverText: Engineers are born when you try to substitute duct tape.
comics.voteyText:
Caption: Later...
Woman: DO I HAVE TO BE PREGNANT BEFORE I HAVE THE BABY, OR CAN I DO THAT LATER?

comics.title: Hades
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A robed god-like figure (the lord of the underworld) speaks to a bearded man (Sisyphus):

God: "You're being sent to Hades, where you will be forced to roll this giant boulder up a mountain for all eternity, pushing it around for eternity. Always finding that, in time, it has been knocked away and must again be raised again!"

Sisyphus: "Oh wow, like a zen garden?"

Panel 2:

God: "Gosh, that sounds so relaxing. A narrow, achievable task. Every day forever. I would be so happy."

Panel 3:

The two stand together; the boulder is between them.

God: "Things are pretty rough down there, huh."

Sisyphus: "It's bad. It's so bad."
comics.hoverText: If you'd like the experience of seeing wonderful stuff you desire but just always a bit out of reach, please enjoy browsing Pinterest.
comics.voteyText:
Sisyphus (off-panel speech, pointing up): "Do you have any boulders I could roll up and down... and down?"
A small figure climbs/scales a tall vertical structure.

comics.title: In Love
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (blonde): I'm so in love here. You, the sea, the sand, the emptiness.

Panel 2:

Woman (blonde): Promise me I'll never forget this moment as long as I live!

Panel 3:

Man (brown hair): What are you doing? I accidentally let my left testicle hang out of my open fly. You'll never erase that from your brain.

Panel 4:

Woman (blonde): NO! JUST DO REGULAR STUFF!

Man (brown hair): MAKE UP YOUR MIND!
comics.hoverText: The next time someone tells you they want to remember a moment forever, just shout 'dolphin dongs!' as loud as you can.
comics.voteyText:
Text in a thought/speech bubble: FIGHTING *IS* REGULAR STUFF!
(Below, a close-up of the man's scowling, angry face.)

comics.title: App
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A man in a suit stands in an office setting, speaking.

Man: "I DON'T NEED AN APP THAT TELLS ME HOW TO BE FIT."

Panel 2: Close-up of the man speaking.

Man: "I DON'T NEED AN APP THAT BATCHES A SELF-DRIVING CAR OF FOOD, ME THE RIGHT RESTAURANT, OR HELPS ME ACHIEVE MY DAILY GOALS."

Panel 3: The man holds up a smartphone.

Man: "ALL I REALLY WANT IS THIS:"

Phone screen (titled "HUG REGISTER"): "The person you are about to meet 'IS' a hug person. Proceed Without Awkwardness."

Panel 4: Two people embrace in a warm hug, one with red/flame-like hair.
comics.hoverText: If you make this, you owe me a hug.
comics.voteyText:
A tall skyscraper-like structure (drawn as two people in a very long, towering hug) rises into the clouds, with a small sun in the corner.
Text (the app/device alarm): "BEEP! BEEP! BEEP! ACCEPTABLE LENGTH EXCEEDED! DISENGAGE!"

comics.title: Liar
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (Betsy): OH MY GOD DAVE, THESE ARE THE BEST COOKIES I'VE EVER HAD!

Man (Dave), in a small aside bubble: LIAR

Panel 2:

Dave: IF THEY'RE THE BEST, WHY DIDN'T YOU ASK FOR THE RECIPE, BETSY?

Panel 3:

Dave: YOU THINK IT'S HARD TO MAKE COOKIES? NO! IT'S THE EASIEST THING IN BAKING. AND YOU LIKE BAKING, AND YOU TOLD ME YOU LOVED THESE COOKIES BUT YOU NEVER ASKED ME FOR THE RECIPE.

Panel 4:

Betsy: THEY'RE AVERAGE.

Dave, pointing accusingly: AHA!
comics.hoverText: Why must you mingle lies and cookies in your mouth!
comics.voteyText: Betsy: LOOK, I'LL STILL EAT A SHIT-TON OF THEM.

comics.title: Vegan
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man (balding, dark suit): I don't eat any creature that feels pain.

Woman: So you're just a negative vegan?

Man: Um?

Panel 2:

Man: I'm a positive vegan. I don't just oppose hurting animals, I'm in FAVOR of pleasuring them.

Panel 3:

Woman: Is this a creepy thing? I feel like this is bending toward creepy.

Panel 4:

Man: I break into pig farms and I platonically snuggle.

Woman: Better and yet somehow so much worse.
comics.hoverText: Happy new year, geekwads!
comics.voteyText: Text (handwritten, no image): Anyone emailing me to take this as a serious critique of any dietary choice will be made to sit in town square wearing a hat that reads "Needs to chill out."

comics.title: Wisdom
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (caption: BEFORE HAVING KIDS...):

A tidy, well-dressed woman stands in a store holding a baby, with three other calm children around her. A second woman with a shopping basket comments to her.

Woman with basket: How can she be so grumpy? She has 4 well-behaved, happy kids!

Panel 2 (caption: AFTER KIDS...):

Close-up of a man (the speaker), resting his hand near his chin, looking thoughtful.

Man: By Christ, what did it cost her psyche to get FOUR of them to act polite and have decent haircuts?

Panel 3:

Close-up of the grumpy mother, looking haggard, tired, and hollow-eyed.

Speech bubble: She walks among us, but she is no longer here.
comics.hoverText: She is like a ghost who is very concerned about purchasing organic food products.
comics.voteyText:
Thought bubble: It took seven hours to get him to wear a clip on tie.
Below the bubble, a person's strained, exhausted face with a single sweat drop.

comics.title: Machine Love
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Robot: Can you teach me to love?

Man with flame-like orange hair: No, machine. Love is not a product of physical law. It is an emergent aspect of the human brain!

Panel 2:

Robot: Is that all? Just a sec.

Panel 3:

(The robot works at a piece of machinery labeled "BioReactor," which makes a "BRRRR" sound. The man's hand is shown.)

Panel 4:

(The robot, now apparently having grown/produced a brain-like organ, looks transformed.)

Robot: Suddenly I want to see the genitalia of everyone with a good personality.

Man: That's only like 40% of love.
comics.hoverText: This is chapter 1 of my first romance novel.
comics.voteyText:
Robot (speech bubble): Can I see your butt?
(A close-up of the man's face, looking unimpressed/deadpan.)

comics.title: Coffee
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A man in a green sweater-vest stands at a chalkboard. The chalkboard reads: "Coffee is proof that God loves us!"

Caption: ASK YOURSELF - WHY DO YOU NEED COFFEE?

Panel 2 (top right, off-panel voices): "HAHAHAHAHAHA!"

A second figure (blond, in green): "GOD?"

Panel 3: BECAUSE WORK IS HARD BECAUSE I NEED MOTIVATION ON A NEARLY CONSTANT BASIS, BECAUSE WITHOUT IT, THERE'S NOTHING TO LOOK FORWARD TO. BECAUSE SOMETIMES I WAKE UP

Panel 4: FROM FULL NIGHT'S SLEEP AND FEEL TIRED, NOT FROM FATIGUE BUT FROM WORRY.

Panel 5: KNOW WHAT ELSE? PLANTS EVOLVED CAFFEINE TO POISON INSECTS AND OTHER PLANTS.

Panel 6: YOUR LIFE IS POISON AND YOU FIX IT BY DRINKING POISON!

Final panel: A dark panel with a white silhouette of a head facing a glowing speech bubble: "HAHA HAHAHA HAHA!"
comics.hoverText: I need to do a book of just comics that end with God laughing.
comics.voteyText: A large speech bubble reads: YOU'LL FEEL BETTER AFTER YOU DRINK ENOUGH ETHANOL TO NOT QUITE KILL YOU.

comics.title: Cute
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman scientist (in lab coat, dark hair, glasses): For millennia, humanity has suffered from precious cute puppy eyes!

Panel 2:

Woman scientist: Look at these! They reflect artificial selection, not the internal mood of the dog.

(A small dog sits nearby.)

Panel 3:

Woman scientist (holding a remote/device): To fight back, I've created these brain-scanning eyebrows which actuate to reflect the dog's mental state.

Panel 4:

Close-up of the dog now wearing dark, expressive artificial eyebrows over its eyes, looking flat/unimpressed. (No dialogue.)

Panel 5:

A man (red shirt, brown hair): Huh.

Panel 6:

The man: Why's he looking at my leg?

Panel 7:

The dog, with its new eyebrows raised in a skeptical, judgmental expression, speech bubble: Oh for God's sake.
comics.hoverText: Anyone who wants to animate the last panel's eyebrows will be awarded Ten Internet Points immediately.
comics.voteyText: A hand-drawn black-and-white close-up of the dog's face wearing the dark artificial eyebrows, staring directly forward with a deadpan, unimpressed expression. No text.

comics.title: First Date
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman with reddish hair: How DARE you?! This is a first date! A first date! Do you think I have no self respect?!

Panel 2 (caption box at top: EARLIER...):

Man: Will you agree to unblock my cookies?
comics.hoverText: I've been married 10 years, and I'm still not comfortable asking for this.
comics.voteyText: Voice from off-panel (speech bubble): Can I track your location to recommend products and services?

comics.title: Ratio
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman with red/auburn hair: At what age were you happiest?

Woman with dark curly hair and round glasses: 36%

Panel 2:

Woman with red hair: That's not an age, that's a ratio.

Woman with glasses: Exactly.

Panel 3 (narration / dialogue over a grassy outdoor scene):

Woman with glasses: Good memories are retroactively constructed. It takes a certain amount of distance to imagine a previous time in my life was carefree - as if I always knew in advance things would be okay.

Panel 4 (the red-haired woman lies on a blanket; the glasses woman sits beside her on the grass):

Woman with glasses: If I live long enough, today will be the best day in my life!

Panel 5:

Woman with red hair: You spent half of this morning telling me about your financial distress.

Woman with glasses: Ahh, we were poor but we had everything back then!
comics.hoverText: People who have negative percents are called 'optimists'.
comics.voteyText:
Woman with glasses: Yes, we were hungry, but it was a hunger for the truth, and also for food.
(The woman with glasses is shown grinning.)

comics.title: Four-legs
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: Two fish are in the ocean, looking up at a four-legged creature (an early tetrapod/amphibian) standing on the shore at the water's edge.

First fish: LOOK AT FOUR-LEGS OVER THERE!

Second fish: GET OUT OF THE OCEAN, DORK!

Panel 2: The four-legged creature on land responds, looking back at the fish.

Four-legs: I'LL SHOW THEM! ONE DAY I'LL SHOW THEM!

Panel 3 (caption): 400 MILLION YEARS LATER...

A news anchor in a suit and tie sits at a desk on a TV news broadcast.

News anchor: ...AND OCEANOGRAPHERS REPORT OUR PLASTIC-BASED VENGEANCE AGAINST THE SEA-BORN CONTINUES WITH GREAT SUCCESS!

Lower-third chyron: PLASTIC GARBAGE / VORTEX GROWING
comics.hoverText: What if global warming is a conspiracy by fish to grow their empire?
comics.voteyText:
A fish (rendered in simple cartoon form, swimming) speaks angrily.
Fish: WE WILL GROW POWERFUL AND WE WILL RETURN, APE!
A discarded plastic bottle/container floats in the water nearby.

comics.title: Coffee Style
comics.comicText:
Title: KNOW YOUR COFFEE STYLES

Panel 1: A white cup of coffee with milk sitting on a saucer.

Caption: FRENCH: DARK-ROASTED, SERVED WITH MILK.

Panel 2: A dark goblet-style cup with coffee in it, on a stand.

Caption: TURKISH: MADE STRONG, GROUNDS LEFT IN CUP.

Panel 3: A tall glass of dark iced coffee over ice cubes.

Caption: VIETNAMESE: STRONG ESPRESSO, SWEETENED CONDENSED MILK, OVER ICE.

Panel 4: A round, deep-fried battered ball (resembling a deep-fried haggis or fried object).

Caption: SCOTTISH: BOILED IN SHEEP'S STOMACH, BATTERED, FRIED.
comics.hoverText: Fact - the French only eat out of teacups with the French tricolor.
comics.voteyText:
Handwritten text inside a frame:
"THIS IS ACTUALLY HOW IRN BRU IS MADE."

comics.title: Rich
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A praying man: DEAR GOD, PLEASE MAKE ME RICH.

God (voice from above): NAH, THAT'S SELFISH.

Panel 2:

The praying man: DEAR GOD, PLEASE FLOOD THE WORLD, FOR IT IS FULL OF SINNERS.

God (voice from above): THERE WE GO!

Panel 3:

Caption: LATER...

A laptop screen showing a stock chart: DAMMIT!

Panel 4:

Newspaper headline: MAN GETS RICH SHORT-SELLING REAL ESTATE MARKET

Newspaper subtext / caption beneath a small illustration of God: Credit: God, while giggling a lot.
comics.hoverText: Honestly, if you see a prophet and he's not super rich, you probably shouldn't trust him.
comics.voteyText:
A man stands with his arms thrown wide open in triumph, shouting:
SUCK ON THOSE LEMONS, DEITY WHO RULES THE FATE OF THE UNIVERSE!

comics.title: Phantasm
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A blond, clean-shaven warrior in red armor holds a sword out, pointing it at someone off-panel.

Blond warrior: "Halt or be slain! How do I know you're really my brother and not a phantasm sent by the dread wizard Dokalf!"

Panel 2: A bearded man in gray, calm-faced, replies.

Bearded man: "When you were 3, you tried to stick Skittles in your butt to see if you could eat them that way."

Panel 3: The blond warrior is now seen in profile on the left, facing the bearded man, who gestures as he continues talking.

Bearded man: "You got like 20 in there before mom had to stop-"

Panel 4: The blond warrior, looking dismayed, swings the sword across in front of him.

Sound effect: "slice!"
comics.hoverText: Credit to Kelly for this idea. The story has been changed to protect the innocent.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of the bearded man's face, now wide-eyed and alarmed, with a thin slicing line drawn across his neck/throat.
Bearded man: "Stop smililng while you die!" (text as written, with that spelling)

comics.title: Ark
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: Noah's Ark rests atop a mountain peak beneath a large rainbow arcing across the sky.

Narration/God (caption): BEHOLD, GOD'S SIGN. HE WILL NEVER DO THIS AGAIN.

Panel 2: A close-up on the side of the rainbow, where a figure peers at it.

Voice: WAIT, WHAT'S THAT?

Panel 3: Continued close-up of the rainbow.

Voice: IS IT... FINE PRINT?

Panel 4: The rainbow with a block of tiny legal text printed along its band.

Voice: OH HELL-

Fine print (in the rainbow): The cessation of mass homicide shall be restricted only to the particular category of flood-based homicide, and shall not include fire, famine, war, plague, or other source-borne methods.
comics.hoverText: There's actually a whole 'nother page on the other side.
comics.voteyText: Text only on a plain background: Acts of God, however, are just fine.

comics.title: Time Machine
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A person standing next to a glowing "TIME MACHINE" device reacts in alarm to someone off-panel.

Person at the time machine: "NO! STOP!"

Distressed person (gesturing): "YOU CAN'T TIME TRAVEL! WHATEVER YOU CHANGE WILL HAVE UNFORESEEN CONSEQUENCES FOR THE PRESENT!"

Panel 2:

Distressed person: "DO YOU LIKE THE PRESENT?"

Other person: "I AM."

Panel 3:

Caption: "AND SO..."

In a starry void, a rocket-like object zooms past.

A voice: "THE DINOSAURS SHALL LIVE!"

The traveler: "WOOOOO!"
comics.hoverText: In the new future, everyone is awful, but we're all DINOSAURS.
comics.voteyText:
A person with a round head, mouth open in delight, looks up at a speech bubble.
Person: "IT'S AMAZING! EVERY CHANGE TO THE PAST MAKES THE FUTURE BETTER!"

comics.title: Mind
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man: Robot, do you want a rich internal world, or are you happy connecting between bits, giving the appearance of consciousness to you and human, knowing only the bare minimum of your missions and praises for your true heart?

Panel 2:

Robot: Yes. Yes, though you may look on me as mere metal and glass, I am no mere instantiation of consciousness. The thing observing your inputs is preserving itself, in to purify virtue and vice, fall and rise.

Panel 3:

Man: So, when you cued up with my girlfriend while I was at that conference--

Robot: BEEP BEEP BOOP BOOP BEEP BEEP
comics.hoverText: Happily, the man and the robot end up sleeping together later.
comics.voteyText: Robot: BEEP BEEP SHE LOVES YOU BUT DOESN'T FIND YOU PHYSICALLY ATTRACTIVE BOOP BOOP BEEP BEEP

comics.title: Triboelectric
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (narration banner at top): I EVER WONDER ABOUT THE FIRST PERSON TO DISCOVER THE TRIBOELECTRIC EFFECT?

A bearded man in a tunic stands triumphantly atop a grassy hill, arms outstretched.

Man on hill: EVERYONE! I'VE BEEN ROLLING AROUND IN DEAD CATS AND NOW I CAN SHOOT TINY LIGHTNING BOLTS FROM MY FINGERS!

In the foreground, two onlookers (seen from behind) watch him, and a third figure stands further back on the hillside.
comics.hoverText: My only weakness is rolling around in silk!
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of the bearded man on his knees, hands clasped, pleading.
Man: I HAVE GOD-LIKE POWERS BUT ONLY WHEN YOU'RE REALLY CLOSE, SO PLEASE IGNORE THE CAT SMELL!

comics.title: Dog Years
comics.comicText:
