Young man (shouting): I HATE your generation!

The older man peers out from behind a tall chair, looking back.
comics.hoverText: Maybe movies about angry men without morals just got crowded out by news opinion shows?
comics.voteyText:
Young man (continuing to shout): No supper until you admit that all of my problems are due to the behavior of the previous generation!
The older man looks exasperated/deadpan, hand on chin.

comics.title: Impact
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman: Why the codpiece?

Bald man: I live every day like it might be my last.

Panel 2 (narration over an asteroid hitting Earth):

Man (narrating): Imagine this. Asteroid smashes into Earth - ash blankets the sky, trapping all surface life in a layer of soot and powdered glass.

Panel 3 (narration over a barren landscape):

Man (narrating): Eons hence, aliens come. See what happened. Begin the archaeological work.

Panel 4 (narration; two aliens excavating a plaster cast of a body with a prominent codpiece):

Man (narrating): They make castings of the gaps where corpses once lay. And BAM!

Alien: Wow! What a huge wiener!

Panel 5:

Woman (worried): Why do you care? You'll be dead.

Panel 6:

Bald man (clasping hands, blissful): I'll be watching from heaven!
comics.hoverText: While some stare at their feet, others see over the horizon.
comics.voteyText: Angel (the bald man, now winged and haloed, peering down through clouds): So huge.

comics.title: Bottom
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Child: Mom, why do women have bigger bottoms than men?

Mother: To stop predators.

Panel 2:

Mother: When attacked, women shed their excess buttocks, increasing their speed while distracting predators.

Panel 3:

Mother: Later, they consume extra calories to regenerate their defense system.

(The child sits at a laptop.)

Panel 4:

Child: Why don't men have that?

Mother: Men are expendable. That's evolution.

Panel 5:

(Silhouettes of the child and mother.)

Child: It's been a while since you've had a predator attack, huh.

Mother: Boys are expendable too.
comics.hoverText: Later, as a punishment, she gives him the sex talk.
comics.voteyText:
Mother: I will sit on you, child. Sit on you until you die.
(A worried, sweating face.)

comics.title: AI
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A person (off-panel, speaking from the left) gestures at a glowing egg-like AI device on a desk.

Person: DAMMIT! THIS AI SYSTEM IS CRAP!

Panel 2:

A tiny humanoid figure stands beside a larger glowing egg-shaped AI unit.

Person: IT KEEPS INCORRECTLY CLASSIFYING OPINIONS AS FACTS, LUST AS LOVE... HELL IT THINKS THINGS THAT RHYME ARE MORE LIKELY TO BE TRUE!

Panel 3:

A man with red/orange hair sits at the desk near a glowing egg device.

Person: WHAT KIND OF TRAINING DATA DID IT HAVE?

Second speaker (pink speech bubble): MOSTLY INTERNET. TONS AND TONS OF INTERNET.

Panel 4:

The red-haired man and the small figure look at the glowing egg AI device, which now displays a small page/screen.

Person: JESUS, BUT... WAIT, THERE'S NO DATA HERE. JUST METADATA.

Second speaker (pink speech bubble): IT ONLY READS HEADLINES.
comics.hoverText: I don't know why, but I find it really funny to draw naked vacuous humans.
comics.voteyText:
A hand-drawn black-and-white panel showing a tall rounded figure (the AI unit) with a single eye.
Speaker: YOU CAN ACTUALLY CORRUPT MOST OF ITS DATA JUST BY MAKING IT SCARED.

comics.title: Shift
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Green alien: Why is it that every part of the universe is running away from every other part?

Man: That's just you.

Panel 2:

Man: There's not.

Panel 3:

Man: Your planet is belonging to it. Every direction. Do you think we want our kids running up with this?

Green alien: Then why did you come with the ray from planet Zorblax?

Panel 4:

Green alien: We're criminals, and this is a punishment.
comics.hoverText: Why do you think those Roswell aliens decided to crash?
comics.voteyText:
Text in speech bubble (from offscreen): Please kill us.
(The speech bubble trails down to a sad-eyed alien/monster figure.)

comics.title: Drugs
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man in a hat and trench coat, leaning in like a stereotypical drug dealer, approaches a young person.

Man in hat: Hey kid, you wanna buy some drugs?

Kid: What kinda drugs?

Panel 2:

The man in the hat explains, looking earnest.

Man in hat: Drugs that people need to live, but which are difficult to make generic versions of, and over and over we have patents for trivial incremental improvements.

Panel 3:

The kid responds calmly.

Kid: We can change whatever we like.

Panel 4:

The kid screams in horror, mouth wide open.

Kid: AAAAAAAAAA
comics.hoverText: One day, we will look on the street dealers of insulin as heroes.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up on the dejected man in the hat, looking down sadly.
Man in hat: Why don't kids want my insulin?

comics.title: Condescension
comics.comicText:
Title panel: NEW MODES OF CONDESCENSION -FOR- MODERN LIFE

Panel 1 (header caption): ASSUMING YOUR OPPONENT'S PERSPECTIVE IS ACTUALLY A SEX THING.

A man with curly blue hair (to a woman): "Ah, so what you're saying is you have a neoliberalism fetish. Hey, as long as it's consensual, you do you."

Panel 2 (header caption): DATA-AUGMENTED CREDENTIALISM

A balding man (to a woman): "Yes, that about as much insight as I'd expect from a person whose university acceptance rate was 63.1% during their first year of enrollment."

Panel 3 (header caption): ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE THAT IDENTIFIES WHAT SOMEONE IS TALKING ABOUT AND READS A RELEVANT WIKIPEDIA ARTICLE TO THEM SLOWLY

An AI/robot voice: "Staaatiiistiiiiics issss aaaa braaanch offffff maaathemaaaaatics."
comics.hoverText: It's not me insulting you, it's the program I wrote that actively targets people like you.
comics.voteyText:
A disembodied voice in a speech bubble: "I just don't want to have to explain it to my children."
(Below the bubble is a drawing of a person's head with curly hair and a downturned mouth.)

comics.title: Past
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Dark-haired man (interviewer/older figure): Are you ever embarrassed by the views and actions of past you?

Younger man with light hair: Of course.

Panel 2:

Younger man with light hair: That's power! Present me is the past me of the future me! If I know in advance I'll be ashamed of this era in my life, I have the freedom to do anything I like!

Panel 3:

Younger man with light hair: I'll be mortified about this time whether it's spent grasping for corporate promotion or living a bohemian life of bad poetry and sexual misadventure, so CLEARLY I should do the second thing!

(The dark-haired man stands in the background looking unimpressed.)

Panel 4:

Caption banner: 20 YEARS HENCE...

The light-haired man, now older, lies sunbathing on a beach towel by the shore.

Thought/caption (pointing to him): Past me was a goddamned genius.
comics.hoverText: Rejection of the purple turtleneck for a speedo was also a wise decision.
comics.voteyText:
Handwritten text inside a wavy black border:
Why am I the only cartoonist who regularly uses "hence"? Do better, internet.

comics.title: Before
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (title bar): BEFORE KIDS

Man with red hair, standing in a grocery store freezer aisle, a yellow "SALE!" tag visible on the shelf: "My God, who buys microwave burritos? They come out like red hot cardboard with frozen beef jerky inside."

Panel 2 (title bar): AFTER KIDS

The same man, now with long unkempt hair and a full beard, looking haggard and holding a microwave burrito up to his face: "My God! These are the exact diameter of my food-hole!"
comics.hoverText: If you don't cook it, it's a frozen dessert!
comics.voteyText: The bearded, exhausted man continues, gazing at the burrito: "It's a hole cylinder... filled with eat-stuff!"

comics.title: Problem
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man: Sally, before we go to bed, I need you to know that... I'm a post-mature ejaculator.

Panel 2:

Woman (Sally): Wait?

Man: I will orgasm very quickly, but not for a decent sex due to the last time I had sex.

Panel 3:

Woman (Sally): Look, it's not a problem. You don't have to make up weird excuses.

Man: I have lasted YEARS at this point. YEARS!
comics.hoverText: There's pre and post, but what's in the middle? Entremature? Mesomature?
comics.voteyText: Man: If you average in my pre-pubescent years, I can go very long indeed.

comics.title: Preference
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Girl (red hair): Mom, how do I get a boy to like me when he doesn't even know I exist?

Mom: Money.

Panel 2:

Mom: Evaluate your relative social status. Survey him for the strength of his preference for someone of equal social status. Do a little math and you arrive the minimum cost he'd be willing to accept in exchange for dating you.

Panel 3:

Girl (off-panel, in silhouette/shadow): I'm just as good as he is! He should want me because of who I am!

Panel 4:

Mom (in doorway): Grow up and accept the importance of allocative efficiency, kid!
comics.hoverText: Somewhere out there, and economist doesn't see what the joke is.
comics.voteyText: A man (off-panel speaker, smiling): I actually have a fetish for 4s.

comics.title: Oak
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (top):

Woman (holding a leaf): HOW DO YOU KNOW THAT'S AN OAK LEAF?

Older man (wide-eyed, sweating): WELL IT'S GOT AN OAKY-LIKE... OAKSOME... OAK...NESS.

Panel 2 (bottom): A line graph. The vertical (y) axis is labeled "ABILITY TO EXPLAIN HOW YOU IDENTIFIED A SPECIES." The horizontal (x) axis is labeled "KNOWLEDGE OF NATURE." The curve is a bell curve: it starts low, rises to a peak in the middle, then falls back down low at high knowledge.
comics.hoverText: Like look at these leaves. 14 oakitudes, minimum.
comics.voteyText: (TAXONOMISTS ARE UNNATURAL FREAKS)

comics.title: Interesting
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man with orange hair: What an interesting nose.

Woman: Huh?

Panel 2:

Man with orange hair: Classically aquiline, yet without the coldness of sculpture.

Woman: What are you doing?

Panel 3:

Man with orange hair: I'm anti-negging. I'm dropping offhand comments about your appearance to build up your self esteem until you realize you're out of my league.

Panel 4:

Woman: You... wow. That is so kind.

Man with orange hair: Stop! I wanna be single so I can game all weekend again!
comics.hoverText: In the first draft of this I called anti-negging 'pozzing,' which apparently would've been in colossally poor taste.
comics.voteyText:
Voice (in speech bubble, from off-panel): You're so wonderful and smart and pretty! Please internalize all of this!
(A close-up of a face crying, tears streaming down, mouth turned down in distress.)

comics.title: Ships
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man with dark hair: The Trojan War was pointless.

Bald man: Why?

Panel 2:

Man with dark hair: There's no way Helen of Troy was that attractive.

Panel 3:

Man with dark hair: You got, what, 500,000 Greeks back then? She's the hottest person among 500,000?

Panel 4:

Man with dark hair: That's like saying she's the prettiest girl in the middle third of Idaho.

Panel 5:

Man with dark hair: In fairness, the thousand ships her face launched were pretty small by tonnage. The prettiest girl in Boise could probably get a medium-sized modern destroyer going.

Panel 6:

(The two men look at each other; no dialogue.)

Panel 7:

(The dark-haired man and another man face each other; no dialogue.)

Panel 8:

(The two men stand together; no dialogue.)

Panel 9:

Man with dark hair: My god, the future is going to have discussions like this about us, isn't it?

Bald man: That's why we need a nuclear war.
comics.hoverText: If you go back 100,000 years, being able to launch a wooden dinghy is pretty much the best you can hope for.
comics.voteyText:
Caption (in a thought/word balloon shape): The future looks bright as uranium!
(Below, a rhinoceros is drawn with simple lines.)

comics.title: Mood
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (lecturer at a podium, presenting to an audience):

Lecturer: Visual signals take the fewest steps, generally taking the longest time. They use up to 15 seconds to process.

Panel 2:

Lecturer: Sound is faster, but to convey a complete thought generally takes the longer time. Tones, words and images take time, but with visual stimulus.

Panel 3:

Lecturer: The other senses are slower still. Touch, you have to find the limbs and so forth. Taste, way to kill the mood. You must create a mood-killing sound first. Smell can deliver mood-cognition in under 10 milliseconds.

Panel 4:

Lecturer: After an extensive search of possible signaling devices, it is possible that its possible to accelerate the playback of these effects, to arrive at a recognizable signal in under 1 millisecond.

Panel 5 (an audience member raises a hand):

Audience member: Any questions?

Audience member: Couldn't you do something better than this 15th century tactic?

Panel 6 (lecturer at podium):

Lecturer: Sorry, folks. But this symposium is no longer sexy.
comics.hoverText: Bless you, patreon typo squad. You are the sexiest of symposia.
comics.voteyText: [No text. A close-up illustration of a person's lower torso/hips from behind, wearing a dark grey skirt/jacket hiked up, exposing dark maroon underwear, with a long pointed object protruding from beneath the clothing.]

comics.title: Zorgax
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: Two green aliens stand among a group of humans. One alien, addressing the other, gestures toward something off-panel.

Alien 1: WHAT THE HELL IS THIS, ZORGAX?!

Panel 2: The second alien (Zorgax) explains.

Zorgax: THAT'S A "SCARE-HUMAN." YOU GUYS KEEP GETTING INTO THE HUMAN-FOOD BINS, SO WE PUT THIS UP TO FRIGHTEN YOU AWAY.

Panel 3: A crude humanoid mannequin is mounted on a tall stick/pole, like a scarecrow. The first alien looks up at it.

Alien 1: IT'S JUST A MANNEQUIN ON A STICK.

Panel 4: An alien sits in a chair/seat, viewed from behind, pressing a button on a device.

Sound effect: boop

Panel 5: Close on the mannequin-on-a-stick (the "scare-human"), now seen near an alien.

Mannequin (activated, speaking): WE SHOULD DISCUSS OUR RELATIONSHIP STATUS.

Panel 6: The crowd of humans reacts in terror, fleeing.

Humans (shouting): SCATTER! SCATTER!
comics.hoverText: Just to be clear, the drawing in panel 5 does not want to talk about your relationship. Please proceed to the end of the comic.
comics.voteyText:
A human figure stands with a small device/communicator near their chest. A speech bubble points away from them.
Speech bubble: CAN. I. BORROW. MONEY.

comics.title: Unique
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

An older man with gray hair and glasses sits beside a woman with reddish-brown hair.

Man: "People want to know what makes humans unique. But, every animal is 'unique' by some definition. Every animal can do SOMETHING no other animal does."

Panel 2:

Man: "So you can pick all sorts of arbitrary human behaviors, categorize them as a human speciality, and technically not be wrong."

Panel 3:

Woman (offscreen, in shadowed silhouette): "So that's what your lecture today is on?"

Man: "Well, sorta."

Panel 4 (captioned "SOON..."):

The man stands at a lectern in front of a red curtain, gesturing to an audience. He now has dramatic, jagged lightning-bolt-shaped sideburns.

Man: "Man is the only species that can grow lightning bolt sideburns!"
comics.hoverText: Sorry, no, chimps can't shave themselves. Deal with it.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of the man's face showing his lightning-bolt sideburns.
Voice (from a speech bubble): "Gaze in despair, dolphins!"

comics.title: Love
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Little girl (excited): MOMMY I'M GONNA MARRY BILLY!

Woman (the mother, with flowing reddish-brown hair and glasses): OH?

Panel 2:

Little girl: HE HAS FOUR HUNDRED AND SEVEN POKEMON CARDS! I COUNTED THEM!

Caption (below, narration): Later, Ellen married for love, which is fleeting, instead of the solid reliability of very rare cards. She has never had a moment of joy since.
comics.hoverText: Imagine having to lay abed night after night, knowing that you'll never have any first edition holofoils.
comics.voteyText:
Speech bubble (from an unseen speaker): I CHOOSE YOU, BOBBY. BUT IT IS TOO LATE.
[The panel shows a sketchy, indistinct figure/blob hunched over, suggesting a defeated or collapsed figure.]

comics.title: Giants
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A woman with brown hair, wearing a red blazer over a yellow top, stands at a podium with one finger raised, mid-speech.

Woman: "IF I HAVE FOUND MORE BULLSHIT, IT IS BECAUSE I HAVE SWUM IN THE SEWERS OF GIANTS."

Caption (below panel): At the keynote speech for the Skeptics Hall of Fame.
comics.hoverText: I hereby release this to anyone wanting to be as condescending as I am.
comics.voteyText: (THIS SHOULD EXIST, AND ALSO THERE SHOULD BE A YEARLY EVENT WHERE MEMBERS TRY TO CONVINCE EACH OTHER IT DOESN'T EXIST)

comics.title: Surprise
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman with dark hair: One day next week I am going to surprise you with sex.

Man with reddish hair: That's impossible.

Panel 2:

Man: It can't be Saturday next week because by midnight Friday I'll KNOW it's coming Saturday.

Panel 3:

Man: Having eliminated Saturday, I know it can't be Friday because I'd know it was coming on midnight Thursday.

Panel 4:

Man: It follows that you cannot surprise me with sex! Your logic destroys itself!

Panel 5:

Caption: THE FOLLOWING SATURDAY...

(The woman sits alone on a bed at night in her underwear, looking at her phone.)

Panel 6:

(Close-up of a hand holding the phone, showing a text message.)

Text message: I'm doing your best friend.
comics.hoverText: The so-called Surprise Test Paradox can be resolved by delivering it one second after midnight on the last day of the week.
comics.voteyText: Speaker (off-panel / the woman): Heh. I just got it.

comics.title: Pareto
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man (sitting on a couch, thought): I've done it.

Panel 2:

Man (thought): I've reached total Pareto-dismality. Everything is as bad as it can conceivably be. Any action I take will make things no worse.

Panel 3:

Man (thought): I could sit on this couch motionless for a week, drinking cheap vodka and watching cartoons and I would either be better off or the same!

Panel 4:

(The man, viewed from behind / slumped in the chair. No text.)

Panel 5:

(Close-up of the man's tired, deadpan face. No text.)

Panel 6:

Man (thought): God, life is wonderful.
comics.hoverText: Of course in real life there wouldn't be pants.
comics.voteyText: Thought bubble (the man slumped at the bottom of the panel): Now that hope has died, I can watch the news in peace.

comics.title: Nature
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: Two people stand beneath a large old oak tree.

First person: It's amazing just how many life forms live on, in, and around just one old oak. How they all work together to form a system.

Second person: We have so much to learn from nature. Things like...

Panel 2 (caption): Eating the weak...

(A predator stands over a prey animal's carcass.)

Panel 3 (caption): Fighting so that you can claim the most females...

(Two horned animals lock horns.)

Panel 4 (caption): Poisoning soil so your neighbor can't grow...

(A lone tree on barren, poisoned ground.)

Panel 5 (caption): Paralyzing other creatures and using their still-living bodies as incubators for offspring...

(A wasp-like insect.)

Panel 6: The enthusiastic man (with one finger raised) and his companion stand in the grass.

Companion: I meant the tiny percent of nature that isn't horrible!

Enthusiastic man (both fingers raised, eyes wide): Circle of liiiiiiiiife!
comics.hoverText: Nature doesn't exactly want you dead, but it certainly doesn't want you alive.
comics.voteyText:
A speech bubble pointing off-panel, with a person's face in the lower right.
Voice (off-panel): But animals never make war, except for the ones that do.

comics.title: Salt
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A robed figure (resembling God or an angel, all in white) speaks to a bearded man in robes against a backdrop of fiery destruction with meteors falling from the sky.

White-robed figure: "NO! SHE LOOKED BACK AT THE MAYHEM AND DESTRUCTION OF SODOM AND GOMORRAH, EVEN THOUGH IT PROVIDED NO ADDITIONAL RELEVANT INFORMATION! NOW SHE IS 100% SALT!"

Caption (below panel): What if the story of Lot's Wife was actually a homily about avoiding cable news?
comics.hoverText: I used to watch a lot of news and commentary until one day I tried to tally up what I had learned during a month of it and found the quantity of facts could fit on a postage stamp.
comics.voteyText:
A thought bubble rises from a person's head (shown from behind/side, resting their chin).
Thought: "IF ONLY SHE'D FOCUSED ON INTERNET COMICS."

comics.title: Flood
comics.comicText:
A man with orange/red hair kneels with his hands clasped in prayer, talking to God. The man's lines appear in white speech bubbles; God's replies appear in yellow speech bubbles with purple borders.

Panel 1:

Man (praying): Dear God, did the flood kill any babies?

God: Ho yeah!

Panel 2:

God: Look, babies are bastards. They scream all night. They crap their pants. They would kill you for a cookie. It's a no-brainer.

Panel 3:

Man: That's not where I saw you going with that.

God: Humans are bad and I like when they suffer.

Panel 4:

Man (looking up, shrugging): Then why'd you make us?

Panel 5:

God: Does watching reality TV make you happy?

Man: No.

God: But you watch it.

Man: ...Yes.

Panel 6:

God: You are made in my image.

God (silhouetted figure): Aw hell.
comics.hoverText: Kelly told me the first two panels were a bit much, but so far I haven't been struck by lightning, so I think we're good.
comics.voteyText: God (in a yellow speech bubble): I hear dramatic violins whenever you suffer.

comics.title: Pre
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (to child): They call them "the post office" because POST means "after" and people get your letter AFTER it's sent.

Panel 2:

Woman: This is a PRE office. You get stuff BEFORE people send it.

Panel 3:

Woman (reading a card with hearts on it): Oh wow! What a beautiful Mother's Day card! So thoughtful of future-you to send something for once!

Panel 4:

Child (annoyed): Ok, got it. Will do.

Panel 5:

Child: Wow. Time traveling passive-aggression.

Woman (holding the card): You'll thank me when you're younger.
comics.hoverText: In real life, the kid would assume this was all real and feel very proud of making the card.
comics.voteyText:
The card reads, in handwriting:
Dear Mom,
I appreciate all the stuff I appear to find stupid and/or incredibly boring.

comics.title: Oats
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man: Before we go to bed, you should know I've... sown some wild oats.

Panel 2:

Man (distressed, to a woman named Sally): Invasive oats from Australia. They're crowding out habitats for native mice.

Panel 3:

Man (anguished, mouth wide open): Millions of mice, Sally, crying out in hunger as their babies gnaw upon seeds their teeth cannot crack!

Panel 4:

Woman (Sally): I... well... have you stopped doing that?

Man: Don't try to change me, baby.
comics.hoverText: If you're married and have kids, you can say 'I've sown some domesticated oats.'
comics.voteyText: Woman (thought/caption): I was hoping "Hitler of mice" was your fetish.

comics.title: Nudge
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A red, bird-like dinosaur aide holding a folder addresses a green tyrannosaur president.

Aide: "Good news President Rex! The asteroid will miss us by over 300,000 miles."

Panel 2: The green tyrannosaur president, looking concerned.

President Rex: "But the emergency asteroid deflection program was going to put huge funding in a bunch of swing states!"

Panel 3: President Rex, leaning over a desk, in a scheming pose.

President Rex: "What if we keep this quiet and send out some spacecraft for a liiiiittle nudge. What's the worst that could happen?"

Panel 4: President Rex grinning.

President Rex: "Great idea, small cold-adapted mammal!"

Panel 5: A small, scruffy brown mammal stands on a checkered floor.

Mammal: "It's all upside, Mr. President!"
comics.hoverText: Someone on patreon pointed out that the small mammal sure looks like the infamous hedgefox of comics past, which makes perfect sense in context.
comics.voteyText:
A disheveled, primitive mammal speaks toward an unseen figure, a thought/speech bubble fading above.
Mammal: "Your kind shall be eliminated."

comics.title: To the Moon
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Speaker (a man at a podium, gesturing): "If we can put a man on the moon, why can't we do this? I'll tell you why: because the moon landing was the result of a unique and unlikely convergence of geopolitical and technological factors. I mean, what are the odds that'd happen for us?"

Caption below the comic: "I'm no longer allowed to give motivational speeches."
comics.hoverText: Nothing will ruin space for you like reading the political history of how decisions were made.
comics.voteyText:
Handwritten text: "MOST ENDEAVORS FAIL. WHY NOT ENDEAVORS TOO? VORS FAIL. WHY NOT OURS TOO?" (the writing trails off into scribbles)
Below the text is a small sketch of two cartoon figures embracing.

comics.title: Sue
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Son: PAPA! WHY DID YOU NAME ME SUE?!

Panel 2:

Father: I GAVE YOU THAT NAME TO MAKE LIFE HARD. SO YOU'D GROW UP TO BE STRONG AND WISE. I SEE I HAVE SUCCEEDED.

Panel 3:

(No dialogue. The son holds a hand of playing cards.)

Panel 4:

(No dialogue. Another man, sweating, holds a hand of playing cards.)

Panel 5:

Son: SO...IT WAS TO HELP ME.

Father: YES. IT ALSO WORKED FOR... YOUR BROTHER.

Panel 6:

Father: TINKERBELL VON SPHINCTER-NUGGETS.

Panel 7:

(No dialogue. The son looks at another man, the father's speech bubble tail trailing in from off-panel.)

Panel 8:

(A muscular man reveals his bare chest and holds up a pink book titled "Quantum Mechanics for the Smart". A large round belt buckle is at his waist.)
comics.hoverText: I tried to read that book but there are too many numbers at not enough pictures.
comics.voteyText:
Father (off-panel speech bubble): OF THE VERMONT VON SPHINCTERS.
(The father stands in a wide-brimmed hat, scratching/stroking his stubbled chin, looking down thoughtfully.)

comics.title: In Charge
comics.comicText:
Panel 1

Man with shaggy dark hair, beard, and round glasses: What if I told you the entire world is run by a tiny financial and technological elite.

Panel 2

Woman with short blue hair (relieved, smiling): Oh thank GOD.

Panel 3

Woman: Oh that is such a relief. SOMEONE is in charge.

Man (leaning in, grinning): Let me finish! They're baby-eating alien reptile ultra-satanists!

Panel 4

Woman: But they're in charge, right? Someone's in charge?
comics.hoverText: Thanks, ultra-satanist reptiloids!
comics.voteyText: Woman (off-panel speech, anxious close-up of her face): They need more babies to eat? I know a guy...

comics.title: Dox
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Caption (header bar): DOXXING: RELEASING PRIVATE INFORMATION ONLINE.

(A man with brown hair sits hunched at a desk, snarling intensely at a computer monitor.)

Panel 2:

Caption (header bar): PARADOXXING: PROVING SOMEONE'S NON-EXISTENCE.

Woman with dark hair (gesturing): The fact that reality seems real is proof that it isn't real because most things that seem real are illusions.

Bald man (facing her): That's some real shit.

Panel 3:

Caption (header bar): ORTHODOXXING: GETTING SOMEONE TO JOIN A SMALL INSULAR RELIGIOUS COMMUNITY.

Man with a black hat, beard, and sidelocks (Orthodox Jewish appearance): The community spirit is incredible but I miss bacon.
comics.hoverText: Wait, the guy in panel 1, why aren't his fingers touching the buttons of the mouse?
comics.voteyText: (HETERODOXXING IS CONVINCING SOMEONE THEY'RE ATTRACTED TO THE OPPOSITE SEX.)

comics.title: Marriage
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

A woman with gray/black hair in a teal shirt sits across from a man with red flame-like hair and a long red beard. They are mid-argument.

Woman: BUT I HATE YOU.

Man: LOOK, I NOT ONLY HATE YOU, I HATE THE CHILDREN TOO. NOBODY SAID THIS WAS GOING TO BE EASY, BUT IF WE HIT THREE MORE MONTHS, WE GET THE BRONZE LOVE EAGLE.

Woman: FINE. FINE.

Caption (below panel): A lot of divorce could be prevented by merit badges.
comics.hoverText: If you made it the least bit social you could complete end divorce and also happiness.
comics.voteyText: A wordless image of the "Bronze Love Eagle" — a heart-shaped, eagle-like figure cast in bronze/gold, shown striding forward on two legs with wings and clawed feet, its body and a wing rendered as heart shapes.

comics.title: Bastardry
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (caption above a bald speaker at a lectern):

Speaker: During the last several centuries, humanity has gone from seeing itself as the highest life, as the spark of the divine, to being a particular species of ape molded only by the struggle for survival.

Panel 2 (caption above a chart):

Speaker: During the same period, a metric I call "general human bastardry" consisting of per capita incidence of war, genocide, slavery, and so on has declined in concert.

(The chart is labeled "Bastardry" on the falling curve and "Self-Hate" on the rising curve.)

Panel 3 (caption):

Speaker: The inescapable conclusion is that human self-hatred is the driving force behind building a more just and peaceful world.

Panel 4 (caption):

Speaker: Therefore the quickest means by which to achieve utopia would be a crash program to not only display but promote the ugliest, most debauched and degraded view of human nature.

Panel 5:

Speaker: Any questions?

Panel 6 (audience member silhouette raising a question):

Audience member: Have you heard of Facebook?

Speaker: Yes! Why do they keep sponsoring me?
comics.hoverText: Once neuralink is piping twitter directly into our collective amygdala, we will enter the perfect anxiety-based Utopia.
comics.voteyText: No, the perspective isn't off in panel 4. The guy has a third arm coming out of his belly button.

comics.title: Raisin
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (with reddish hair): God, why do people have to die?

Second voice (off-panel, dark): Nobody dies.

Panel 2:

Second voice (in a dark, void-like panel): Maybe this confusing? Imagine a big cake. In the cake there are beings. Every being has a beginning part and an end part.

Panel 3:

Woman: You guys act like the raisins so smug just because they don't encourage the entire cake, but they're there. Just finite and in particular regions of the cake!

Panel 4:

Dark void voice: Are you silent because you understand me?

Woman: I'm irritated at being compared to dried fruit and also could I have a longer raisin please?
comics.hoverText: Now you have ONE MORE reason to hate raisins.
comics.voteyText: Woman: Also I dunno what the cake is a metaphor for, but can I eat the cake?

comics.title: Fast
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A man in a flat-brimmed hat speaks to a younger red-haired man as a large dark-cloaked figure looms in the foreground.

Hat man: "That's Tex. They say he's the fastest gun in the West."

Panel 2: The flat-brimmed-hat man continues, the looming figure (Tex) seen from behind.

Hat man: "Faster'n light. Causin' spacetime to loop in on itself, violatin' the natural order o' things, so as effects precede causes!"

Panel 3 (yellow background): A close-up of Tex, a mustachioed man in a cowboy hat, turning his head.

Tex: "You talkin' about me?"

Panel 4: The hat man answers as Tex points at him.

Hat man: "Yeah I'm talkin' about you. So what?"

Tex: "Pistols at 20 paces!"

Panel 5 (red background): Close-up of the hat man, glaring angrily.

Hat man: "When?"

Panel 6: Tex (foreground, in profile) faces the hat man, who now stands holding a bleeding wound in his chest. The red-haired man stands beside him.

Tex: "Yesterday."
comics.hoverText: I am prepared to license the movie rights to this comic, ONLY to directors prepared to keep every last plot hole.
comics.voteyText:
Extreme close-up of the hat man's shocked face, mouth open.
Hat man: "SHIT!"

comics.title: Lumpy
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Robot (doctor): I'm sorry ma'am, I don't know how to tell you this, but... where your brain should be, there's just a pile of lumpy jelly.

Panel 2:

Woman: That is my brain. That's what brains are.

Robot: Okay, ma'am, that's fine. Whatever you "think."

Panel 3:

Robot: I'm just going to do a quick mental acuity test. What's 14233*11899992?

Panel 4:

Woman: Can I have a pencil?

Robot: We're gonna go ahead and take out the lumpy thing, juuust in case.
comics.hoverText: You can take it home in a jar to show your baby meats!
comics.voteyText: "SMBC morphed into pro-robot propaganda so gently that no one noticed until it was too late."

comics.title: Before
comics.comicText:
Title banner (Panel 1): BEFORE INTERNET

Panel 1:

Child (a boy with orange hair): "WHEN I GROW UP, I WANNA BE A COW!"

Man (in suit with glasses, red tie): "HAHAHAHAHA!"

Title banner (Panel 2): AFTER

Panel 2:

Child (the same orange-haired boy): "WHEN I GROW UP, I WANNA BE A COW!"

Man (same man, now with a flat, resigned expression): "YEP. THERE ARE PEOPLE INTO THAT. YOU DO YOU."
comics.hoverText: The really interesting question is whether the Internet drove this or whether a subset of all populations were suppressed cow-people.
comics.voteyText: The man (close-up, looking uneasy/sweating): "YOU... HAVEN'T BEEN LOOKING AT MY BROWSER HISTORY, HAVE YOU?"

comics.title: Clean
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man (offscreen/asking): What are you doing?

Woman (with dark hair): Achieving perpetual cleanliness.

Panel 2:

Woman: If I attach an elastic band to everything in my life, it will automatically return to its proper place once I'm finished with it.

(A bespectacled man with a mustache stands in the background.)

Panel 3:

Mustached man: You could just, like, neaten up once in a while.

Panel 4:

Woman: Come closer, father.

Panel 5:

Mustached man: What the-

Panel 6:

(No dialogue. The mustached father is yanked violently across the room by an elastic band attached to him, flying through the air toward the woman, who stands scowling in a doorway.)
comics.hoverText: I will do anything to have a clean office except cleaning.
comics.voteyText:
(No dialogue. A red splat fills the panel beside the woman's face.)
Sound effect: SPLAT!

comics.title: Center
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man with combed-back hair: Hey Steve, how do you stay so upbeat?

Second man (red-haired): You gotta look out for number one, you dig?

Panel 2:

Red-haired man: Personally, I'm found a lot of peace in always myself the absolute rule-er, center of every issue.

Panel 3:

Red-haired man: Like a waiter, I slide. I go straight to thanks. I personally maintain as a maximum and admirable goal, which is being calm and remunerative.

Panel 4:

Red-haired man: When someone else is unhappy, I assume they blame me and that an argument so I can enjoy both the personal indignation and the eventual apology.

Panel 5:

First man: When I hear about bad news in therapy contexts I consider myself solely responsible for their suffering and as their only potential savior.

Panel 6:

Red-haired man: I believe that's called insanity.

First man: Yes that is what everyone else seems to save.
comics.hoverText: This comic is about me. ME!
comics.voteyText: First man (face shown close up, frowning): And only I can save them.

comics.title: Precision
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (Doctor, standing, addressing seated patient): In the laboratory, we are going beyond personalized medicine. We not only analyze your genetic and epigenetic and metabolic profile, we know how you interface with society and how that causes wider effects.

Panel 2 (Patient, seated): That's the future, but I've just got a migraine.

Panel 3 (Doctor): According to our social analysis, you're one of those people who shares lots of incorrect statistical information in the form of poorly-compressed memes.

Panel 4 (Doctor): Society would be better off with you incapacitated, and your suffering would be emblematic of a world where justice reigns.

Panel 5 (Doctor, handing over pills): These salt-pills will worsen your symptoms, and that's bad.
comics.hoverText: I could live with all the bigotry and ignorance, but must they have jpeg artifacts?
comics.voteyText: (A character with a sly, wide-eyed expression speaks.) With a little luck, you might die!

comics.title: War
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Person (off-panel, red-haired): Why can't we be more like other animals? You know, other animals never make war.

Woman with grey hair (red shirt, white round glasses): Oh, sure they do. Chimps do it. Ants do it.

Panel 2:

Grey-haired woman: Some ants not only war against other ants, they take captives as slaves!

Panel 3:

Grey-haired woman: No, war isn't special to us. What IS special is PROXY wars.

Panel 4:

Grey-haired woman: You never see a group of chimps funneling sticks and stones to a distant tribe of chimps to help them fight a third group of chimps in order to thwart the ambitions of a fourth group of chimps who are supplying sticks and stones to the third group of chimps.

Panel 5:

Grey-haired woman (arms raised): THAT is the province of MAN.

Panel 6:

The red-haired person (off-panel): Somehow I hate us even more.
comics.hoverText: I am the first to propose this theory and I encourage someone else to do all the legwork then name it after me.
comics.voteyText: (NOTE TO SELF: APPLY FOR GRANT TO DETERMINE IF DOLPHINS CAN BE MADE TO FIGHT PROXY WARS)

comics.title: Spooky
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A blonde, frightened-looking angel with white feathered wings stands amid clouds, raising her hands nervously. Floating beside her is a large round golden cracker (a saltine/Ritz-style cracker with fork-hole dots around the edge).

Angel (speaking upward, off-panel): GOD... THIS PLACE IS SUPER SPOOKY...

Angel (to the cracker): IT G-G-GIVES ME THE C-C-C-CREEPS, AZRIEL!

Caption (below panel): Technically, Heaven is haunted.
comics.hoverText: Why are disembodied souls scarier than animated meat?
comics.voteyText:
A loosely sketched scene: the golden cracker (drawn in orange outline) on the left faces a sketchy blue-outlined human figure on the right.
Cracker (speech bubble): BOO!

comics.title: Lingerie
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man (shirtless, dark hair) lies in bed. Caption/dialogue: "The ideal lingerie is made of the smallest possible underwear mass."

Panel 2:

The man stands gesturing toward a woman with reddish hair who holds a metallic device. Man: "Therefore I have constructed this 'Positive Buoyancy Thong' made entirely of an opaque fog of hydrogen emitted from concealed cartridges on your thigh and armpit."

Panel 3:

The man's hand presses a control. Speech bubble: "Activate!"

Panel 4:

The woman is now covered by a fluffy pinkish cloud of fog around her chest. Sound effect: "ffff!"

Panel 5:

The woman, draped in the fog, looks unimpressed. Woman: "I could just be naked?"

Panel 6:

The man, looking earnest. Man: "But where is the mystery?!"
comics.hoverText: Technically, when nude, we all wear a lingerie of dead skin.
comics.voteyText: Caption only (no characters): "(The minimum possible lingerie involves manipulating the Higgs field)"

comics.title: Seasonal
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A fishing boat is out on the water near a rocky shore.

Panel 2: On a beach, small pumpkins with stick-like legs scurry across the sand. A man's voice cries out.

Man (off-panel): MY GOD, THEY'RE BACK. BACK AGAIN! RUN CHILDREN! TRY TO STAY AHEAD!

Panel 3: The pumpkins swarm across the beach as more emerge from the water.

Panel 4: Two men stand on the shore. One older man (with a beard, holding a knife) and a younger man (aiming a rifle) prepare to fight.

Older man: TO EVERY THING...

Panel 5: Close-up of the older bearded man speaking grimly.

Older man: ...THERE IS A SEASON.

Panel 6: The younger man fires the rifle.

Sound effect: BANG

Panel 7: A pumpkin recoils, struck.

Panel 8: Nighttime exterior of a CAFE. Two patrons sit at an outdoor table. A lit window sign reads: PUMPKIN SPICE LATTES ARE BACK! Pumpkins are visible in the window display.
comics.hoverText: Of course, in modern times, most pumpkins are farmed.
comics.voteyText:
A diagram of a to-go coffee cup with three labeled layers, arrows pointing to each.
Labels (top to bottom): foam, espresso, blood.

comics.title: Neural
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Caption (pink banner): IN THE FUTURE:

Two young people (off to the side, laughing): HA! WE PRANKED YOU!

An elderly woman (gray hair, round glasses, red top): WHAT?

Panel 2:

The two pranksters (one in orange, one in red): WE HACKED YOUR NEURALINK! NOW, IN ALL YOUR CHERISHED MEMORIES OF YOUR DEAD HUSBAND, HIS FACE IS A *BUTT*!

Panel 3:

The elderly woman: HANK?

Panel 4:

The elderly woman's memory: a man in a suit at the beach kneeling on one knee, but his face is replaced by a butt.

The man (in the memory): YOU ARE THE AIR I BREATHE, MARSHA. MARRY ME.

Panel 5:

The elderly woman, looking distressed: SON OF A BITCH!

The two pranksters in the background, laughing.
comics.hoverText: See, the future is also going to be awful in ways you DIDN'T expect.
comics.voteyText:
A memory bubble showing a butt with a speech bubble.
Voice from the memory: SHE'S SO BEAUTIFUL, MARSHA. SHE HAS MY EYES!

comics.title: Slug
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (dark hair, red shirt): Billy! Don't pour salt on that slug! It's mean!

Billy (boy with orange hair, holding a salt shaker): Actually, scientists haven't confirmed that I feel pain. I might just be a stimulus-response machine that's attempting to avoid damage. Salt away!

(A slug sits on the ground nearby.)

Panel 2:

Woman: But you can talk. That means you can think.

The slug: Thinking just makes me want the salt more, kids!
comics.hoverText: People kept saying YESTERDAY's comic was dark, but at least it had a butt in it.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up on the slug's face, looking up with wide eyes.
The slug: Salt me, children!

comics.title: IUT
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (labeled "NORMAL KID"):

Off-panel voice: CLEAN YOUR ROOM!

Child (with messy hair, looking annoyed): I DON'T WANNA

Panel 2 (labeled "FUTURE MATHEMATICIAN"):

Off-panel voice: CLEAN YOUR ROOM!

Child (same kid, gesturing matter-of-factly): I'VE PROVEN THE EXISTENCE OF CLEAN ROOMS. SOMEONE ELSE CAN MOP UP THE DETAILS.

Small text near the child: ZQ EUT
comics.hoverText: People are still debating whether the shirt is funny.
comics.voteyText: Close-up of an adult's lower legs and feet wearing slippers, standing on a floor.

comics.title: Wise
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A bearded advisor or tailor in a cloak gestures toward the king, presenting something unseen.

Advisor: "My lord, this clothing is only visible to the wise."

The King (a bald, bearded man): "I shall wear it on my next parade!"

Panel 2: The naked king stands on a balcony before a crowd, confetti falling, as he shows off his "clothing" during the parade.

Panel 3: Caption (top): "IN A NEARBY LIBRARY"

A hooded figure peers out from a small stone window/dungeon-like opening, speaking wistfully.

Hooded figure: "I wish I could see the king's raiment..."
comics.hoverText: I'm really happy with how the ruffles on the collar came out in panel 2.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of the hooded figure's bearded face, continuing the verse in a speech bubble.
Hooded figure: "Yet here poor fool for all I've read I cannot see the royal head."

comics.title: Bayesian
comics.comicText:
Panel 1

Woman with glasses: I'm a strict Bayesian.

Panel 2

Man: Wait... like you use Bayesian statistics?

Panel 3

Woman with glasses: No. I mean sometimes I change my opinion, and when I do I feel like it's the result of math.

Panel 4

Man: That sounds like normal reasoning plus unwarranted confidence.

Woman with glasses (pointing at him): I am adjusting my priors about you, sir.
comics.hoverText: Oh God, is this the one that finally delivers the hatemail?
comics.voteyText:
Speech bubble: I like you very much but also *slightly less*
(A close-up of the woman's face, looking unimpressed/deadpan.)

comics.title: Easter Bunny
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman with dark curly hair (agitated): OH GOD. OH MY GOD. THE EASTER BUNNY. IT'S A MAMMAL THAT LAYS EGGS.

Red-haired woman: SO?

Dark-haired woman: IT'S A MONOTREME, JENNY. A MONOTREME.

Caption below panel: Cloaca.
comics.hoverText: Okay, it's not the right time of year for this joke, but the caption is universal.
comics.voteyText: (THIS CAPTION IMPROVES ANY NEW YORKER COMIC)

comics.title: Death
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman with red hair (standing): Our lives have become dull and repetitive. Our love has cooled and cooled until it has finally congealed into a polite mutual acknowledgment, bereft of surprise or joy or hope.

Woman with black hair (reclining on a couch): Oh absolutely.

Panel 2:

Red-haired woman: But whaddya gonna do?

Red-haired woman: I think we should live our current lifestyles but imagine our mutual disregard is a fetish dynamic we're playing out 24 hours a day.

Panel 3:

Black-haired woman: That doesn't interest me personally, but I'm prepared to pay lip service to your desires in slowly diminishing quantities over the next two weeks in the hopes that you lose interest.

Panel 4:

Red-haired woman (leaning on the black-haired woman): So hot.

Black-haired woman: Right on, babe.
comics.hoverText: Life is kinda like the movie Saw, only there aren't any riddles to solve.
comics.voteyText: In a hand-drawn style, a man's face with closed eyes and a flat expression. A speech bubble above him reads: YOU ARE GROUNDED!

comics.title: Strings
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man: The proof of Riemann's hypothesis is trivial.

Panel 2:

Man: Step then. Write it down and claim your fields medal.

Girl (a blonde child): I don't have the solution -- that's the point. I'm just saying the solution is trivial.

Panel 3:

Man: Think about the space of all possible proofs. There are infinite proofs. All of which are just stepping of little squiggles. It follows that there's some point where there is some other proof that is both longer and has more complicated squiggles.

Panel 4:

Man: Since "triviality" is always a relative quality you can make a proof trivial just by looking a harder one. Thus relative to that one, the original proof is trivial. And thus we have shown that all proofs are trivial, including this one.

Girl: That seems... non-obvious.

Panel 5:

Man (standing on a cliff, gesturing across to another cliff): Actually everything is obvious.
comics.hoverText: I think God permitted infinities just to permit stupid proofs.
comics.voteyText: The one downside is that the answer is approximately infinity characters in length.

comics.title: Interesting
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A woman with dark hair (sitting at a table across from a man) asks her date.

Woman: So what are your hobbies?

Panel 2: The man answers earnestly.

Man: I run up to strangers, crying, shout "I forgive you, but I can never forget" and run away.

Panel 3: Close-up of the woman, looking unsettled / unimpressed.

Panel 4: The conversation continues, shown as silhouettes of the two facing each other.

Woman: It said on your profile you like interesting men?

Woman: That was code for educational attainment.

Man (small text): Ahhhhh.
comics.hoverText: Now please parrot some professor's opinion about Foucault.
comics.voteyText: A hand-drawn sketch of a man's face with flame-like / wild hair, paired with handwritten text above it reading: "I forgive you. But I can never forget."

comics.title: True Love
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Ghost woman (a green-skinned female ghost with long pale hair, haunting the woods): "...BUT MY TRUE LOVE NEVER CAME! AS I WEPT IN THE DARKNESS, A TREE FELL UPON ME. THAT WAS FORTY YEARS AGO, BUT STILL, I HAUNT THESE WOODS."

Panel 2:

Man (off-panel/listener): "WHO WAS THE TRUE LOVE?"

Ghost woman: "LEWIS G. BURLINGATE"

Panel 3:

Man: "LEWIS?! LEWIE BURLINGATE? HE'S STILL ALIVE! GOD. LEWIE? HE'S 58 AND STILL CRUSHES A SIX PACK OF COORS 3 DAYS A WEEK. LITERALLY CRUSHES AGAINST HIS FOREHEAD. THE YOUNG GUYS THINK IT'S HILARIOUS, BUT GEEZ. HE SHOULD BE WITH HIS KIDS MORE. HOLD UP I'LL FISH HIM OUT OF THE PUB."

Panel 4:

(The man waves his hands excitedly; an older man with gray hair appears, gesturing with both hands raised.)

Panel 5 (caption: "SHORTLY..."):

The older man (Lewis): "SALLY! SALLY, I NEVER FORGOT!"

Ghost woman: "MY NAME IS ELIZABETH."

Panel 6:

Lewis: "CAN GHOSTS DO SEX?"

Ghost woman (looking dismayed): "MAYBE I'LL BECOME A DRYAD."
comics.hoverText: Have you noticed the ghosts who sit around pining for their true loves are always under the age of 25?
comics.voteyText: The ghost woman (now a vague white blob shape): "BOY I REALLY DODGED A BULLET WHEN I DIED YOUNG."

comics.title: Relationship
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman with orange/red curly hair (standing): "Our lives have become dull and repetitive. Our love has cooled and cooled until it has finally congealed into a polite mutual acknowledgment, bereft of surprise or joy or hope."

Woman with dark hair (reclining, eyes closed): "Oh absolutely."

Panel 2:

Dark-haired woman: "But whaddya gonna do?"

Red-haired woman: "I think we should live our current lifestyles but imagine our mutual disregard is a fetish dynamic we're playing out 24 hours a day."

Panel 3:

Red-haired woman: "That doesn't interest me personally, but I'm prepared to pay lip service to your desires in slowly diminishing quantities over the next two weeks in the hopes that you lose interest."

Panel 4:

Dark-haired woman (eyes closed): "So hot."

Red-haired woman: "Right on, babe."
comics.hoverText: This seemed way more funny and less depressing in the script stage...
comics.voteyText:
Red-haired woman (speech bubble): "Watch this sexy move where my very inertness becomes a form of aggression."
(The woman is shown lying down, eyes closed, motionless.)

comics.title: Tube
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Interviewer (a woman with glasses and dark hair, in a maroon blazer): WHERE DO YOU SEE YOURSELF IN FIVE YEARS?

Panel 2:

Applicant (a bald man in a suit): AS A SORT OF COMPLEX TUBE THAT MOVES THROUGH THE WORLD, ENCOUNTERING NUTRIENTS WHICH IT USES TO REPAIR THE TUBE FOR AS LONG AS IT CAN UNTIL THE TUBE FALLS APART.

Panel 3:

Interviewer: AND WHY DO YOU WANT TO WORK HERE?

Applicant: BETTER NUTRIENTS TO SUSTAIN THE TUBE. IMPROVE THE TUBE. FIND WOMAN-TUBE AND BREED MORE TUBES.

Panel 4:

Interviewer: WOW, I REALLY APPRECIATE YOUR HONESTY MISTER JANSEN.

Applicant: ALL IS STRUGGLE AND DEATH.
comics.hoverText: You will be supervising a team of unhappy tubes.
comics.voteyText: Interviewer: I THINK WE HAVE A SPOT FOR YOU IN HUMAN RESOURCES.

comics.title: Death
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man (in a suit, distressed): Death?! You can't come for me! I have 4 children and my wife can't take care of them all herself! So many beautiful people depend on me!

(A robed, skull-faced figure of Death stands holding a scythe.)

Panel 2:

Death: Heaven is real. You're going there. We have booze.

Panel 3:

Man (face lit up with joy, shouting): FUCK MY SHIT UP!
comics.hoverText: I'm noticing all these depressing comics got drawn just prior to the election...
comics.voteyText:
Man: Does heaven have boobs?
Death: Oceans, bro.

comics.title: Prayer
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (praying): Dear Satan, please bring us a vaccine for-

God (interrupting, in a yellow speech bubble): WHOA, hey, sorry, God here. You sure you wanna go with Satan?

Panel 2:

God: Bro, there is literally a pestilence upon the land. You got like billions of people praying every night for the health of loved ones and then WHAM - pestilence.

Panel 3:

God: Okay but you're gonna go with Satan? You're gonna spend infinite time in hell.

Panel 4:

Woman: Think of all the added people going to hell because they're committing all the sins born of poverty! If Satan comes through, I lose one infinity of time, but millions of infinities are spared!

Panel 5:

God: See this is EXACTLY why I made it so you can't add and subtract infinities.

Panel 6:

Woman: Would you PLEASE stop interrupting so I can pray to Satan!
comics.hoverText: Oddly enough this was drawn just about a week before the Pfizer vaccine.
comics.voteyText: A small horned/devil-like figure says: I hear you, humanity, and I empathize.

comics.title: Prize
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

An elderly man with a white beard, glasses, and a dark suit stands at a podium, holding up a gold medal/coin.

Man: "We are announcing a new category of Nobel Prize: for discoveries about the origins of war. Only one will be minted, and you can only get it by taking it from whoever has it now."
comics.hoverText: This trophy is just emblematic. The actual prize you need to capture is the Near East.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of a man looking strained/angry, with a speech bubble above him.
Man (thought/speech): "Cooperating to make more prizes is against the rules!"

comics.title: Rational
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (with brown hair): Do you think humans are rational?

Man (in a suit): Well "I" certainly am.

Panel 2:

Man: Except when hungry, sleepy, fatigued, sick, sad, drunk, overworked, underworked, anxious, stressed, bored, when I miss my coffee, when I have too much coffee, when I browse the internet, when I see the ocean, when music is on, when something bad has happened, when something good has happened, and when it's morning, night, early afternoon, or any time during winter, fall, or late spring.

Panel 3:

Man: Outside of that I'm a cold-hearted calculating MACHINE.

Panel 4:

Woman: So... when exactly do you feel rational?

Man (now as a silhouette): Any time you ask me my opinion.
comics.hoverText: I was feeling especially rational when I made this observation.
comics.voteyText: FACT: ASTERISKS ARE A *PERFECTLY ACCEPTABLE* FORM OF EMPHASIS.

comics.title: Nietzsche
comics.comicText:
Caption (top): PHILOSOPHY TIP: ABOUT HALF OF NIETZSCHE'S APHORISMS READ LIKE A TECHNICAL SUMMARY FOR A STANDUP COMEDY ROUTINE

Panel 1: A mustachioed man (styled as Nietzsche) stands at a microphone on a brick-walled stage, performing standup to an audience.

Nietzsche: "Insanity in individuals is something rare -- but in groups, parties, nations, and ages, it is the rule."

Panel 2: Close-up of Nietzsche at the mic, gesturing.

Nietzsche: "One does not hate as long as one disesteems, but only when one esteems equal or superior."

Panel 3: A woman in the audience laughs.

Audience member: "So true! It's so true!"

Panel 4: Nietzsche continues his set.

Nietzsche: "Man wishes woman to be peaceable, but in fact woman is essentially unpeaceable, like the cat, however well she may have assumed the peaceable demeanor."

Panel 5: The audience roars with laughter.

Audience laughter: "HAHAHAHAHAHA"

Panel 6: Close-up of a grinning, satisfied Nietzsche.

Nietzsche: "The fellows know of what I speak!"
comics.hoverText: Later, the joke was on him!
comics.voteyText:
Nietzsche (to the audience, pointing): "This lady in the front row has assumed the peaceable demeanor despite being by nature unpeaceable, am I not right, sir?"
(Below: two audience members in the front row look up at the towering figure of Nietzsche on stage.)

comics.title: Prize
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Auctioneer (a man in a suit and fedora holding a microphone): ALL RIGHT, DO I HAVE $100,000? YES, IN THE BACK. $100,000. DO WE HAVE $200,000? ALL RIGHT, GOING FOR $200,000! DO WE HAVE $500,000? IMPECCABLE CREDENTIALS, LADIES AND GENTLEMEN. 500,000. YES! THE WOMAN IN FRONT. DO I SEE 550?

Caption: The Nobel Prize in economics should be awarded via an auction system.
comics.hoverText: Isn't the goal of prizes to maximize utility?
comics.voteyText: A bidder (a stick-figure-style face): I BED 47,000 HOURS OF MY LIFE SPENT ANALYZING HISTORICAL DATA ON MONETARY POLICY!

comics.title: Pairings
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (title card):

KNOW YOUR WINE-ANXIETY PAIRINGS

Panel 2 — SELF ESTEEM ANXIETY:

(A distressed stick figure clutches its chest and head.)

Caption: CABERNET SAUVIGNON, BECAUSE LIKE YOU IT IS HEAVY AND BITTER.

Panel 3 — SOCIAL ANXIETY:

(A stick figure frowns and looks away, arm behind its back.)

Caption: SAUTERNES, BECAUSE IT IS CLOYINGLY SWEET YET STILL UNPOPULAR.

Panel 4 — MONEY ANXIETY:

(A frowning stick figure squeezes a small object in its hand.)

Caption: ANY WINE IN A PLASTIC BLADDER SO YOU CAN SQUEEZE OUT THE LAST THREE DROPS.

Panel 5 — WORK-RELATED ANXIETY:

(A worried stick figure sits at a computer monitor.)

Caption: LIGHT WHITE WINE, BECAUSE YOU CAN SWALLOW IT DOWN FOR 8 HOURS A DAY, EVERYDAY, WITHOUT FEELING ANYTHING.

Panel 6 — EXISTENTIAL ANXIETY:

(A dark, faceless gray figure with only two eyes stares out against a black background.)

Caption: TEQUILA. IT IS NOT REALLY WINE, BUT IS ANYTHING REAL? ANYTHING?
comics.hoverText: With grief anxiety the main thing is to finish the whole bottle and realize you'll never get the same bottle of wine again.
comics.voteyText: Handwritten text: Yes. Tequila is real.

comics.title: Adult
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (caption): WHEN I WAS A KID:

Young man (pointing at a TV): Why don't people in horror movies just LEAVE the haunted house?

Panel 2 (caption): AS AN ADULT:

Older man (now with glasses, pointing at a TV): Why don't the dead pay rent if they're there all night? Mortgage ain't free, GHOST.
comics.hoverText: Imagine how rich you could get if your house were actually possessed by the spirits of murdered people?
comics.voteyText: A ghost (a simple white spectral figure with an angry frown) replies: Bro, you try getting work as an ethereal specter.

comics.title: Hot
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A glowing golden sun/orb hovers in the sky above a green landscape with a tree. A speech bubble (from God, off-panel above) says: "I CURSE YOU, ADAM AND EVE! EVER AFTER YOU SHALL BE ASHAMED OF YOUR NUDITY!"

Panel 2: A nude woman with long brown hair (Eve) speaks: "DIDN'T WORK. STILL FEELING HOT."

Panel 3: A nude man with brown hair and beard (Adam) speaks: "I'VE GOT BOOBS! HUGE SQUISHY SEX-PILLOWS!"

Panel 4: Eve, gesturing downward, says: "LOOK AT THIS DONG! IT'S LIKE AN OBELISK, MAN!"

Panel 5: The glowing orb is shown. A voice (God) says: "STOP TALKING ABOUT YOUR PRIVATE PARTS! STOP IT!"

Panel 6: Adam and Eve face each other. God says: "STOP LOOKING AT EACH OTHER! NO! NO DONGS! EACH OTHER?"

Panel 7: The glowing orb again, with a downward-pointing triangle symbol shown. Text: "=HEAVY BREATHING="

Panel 8: The orb. A voice (God) says: "I'M GONNA MAKE IT SO SEX IS HOW BABIES ARE MADE!"

Panel 9: Bottom strip with the green landscape. Small exclamations float in the air: "WOE!" and "ALAS!"
comics.hoverText: They were gonna be brought by giant birds, but nooooooo, you couldn't keep your thing in your fig leaf.
comics.voteyText: A single rough hand-drawn panel. A speech bubble (God) says: "ALSO NIPPLES WILL BE WHERE BABY FOOD COMES FROM." Below the bubble is a plain oval shape (a breast/nipple).

comics.title: Potemkin
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (showing a man into a room): WELCOME TO THE DEMO OF STEVE! DOES IT LOOK NICE? DOESN'T EVERYTHING SEEM FLAT?

Panel 2:

Man: I CAN LOOK AROUND. WHY DOES EVERYTHING SEEM FLAT?

Man: WAIT. MY GOD. ARE THESE CARDBOARD CUTOUTS OF A CLEAN ROOM?

Woman: I CAN EXPLAIN!

Panel 3:

Man (pulling back a flat cardboard panel to reveal what's behind it): LOOK AT THIS! THEY'RE PROPPED UP WITH LAUNDRY AND HOT POCKET SLEEVES!

Panel 4:

Woman: OKAY, THIS TOOK LONGER THAN ACTUALLY JUST CLEANING YOUR PLACE.

Woman: HINDSIGHT IS 20/20, OKAY?
comics.hoverText: The cheese bits from the hot pockets helps solidify the laundry as it dries.
comics.voteyText:
A single large smiling face fills the panel.
Caption: SOME OF THOSE HOT POCKETS ARE STILL GOOD.

comics.title: Fisher of Men
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A wide beach scene. A small distant figure runs across the sand toward the ocean. A small orange dot floats in the water near the shore. (No dialogue.)

Panel 2: Close on a man with reddish-brown hair, seen from the chest up against the dark water. He looks ahead. (No dialogue.)

Panel 3: The same man now in the water, holding the string of a large orange balloon that floats above the surface. (No dialogue.)

Panel 4: An underwater view. A large fish (greenish) swims at the left. On the right, a pair of legs and an arm stick up out of the water above, the man having gone under / drowned. (No dialogue.)
comics.hoverText: The balloon has two dollars in it.
comics.voteyText:
Text (in a speech bubble): "HOPE THERE'S NOT TOO MUCH MERCURY IN THEM THIS YEAR."
Below, a fish skeleton lies on the sea floor, with a fishing-line and hook trailing down toward it from above.

comics.title: Probe
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man with glasses: The Pioneer probes had a plaque attached to it identifying earth's location. They had naked figures of two naked humans.

Panel 2:

Other man (annoyed): God, it's not cool... it's the wrong message. It says they want naked humans! It says you want naked humans for an alien to be part of a threesome!

Panel 3:

Man with glasses (holding up a hand): Look!

Panel 4:

Man with glasses (presenting a whiteboard with a diagram): This is the solution to the Fermi paradox. The universe thinks we're a creepy middle-aged couple looking to double-team it!

Panel 5:

Other man: What's your solution?

Panel 6:

Man with glasses: We should send a second probe, playing it off as a drunk human dare.

Panel 7:

Other man: But what if they were going to say yes?!

Panel 8:

Man with glasses: Then we give them the night of their lives.
comics.hoverText: Come to the object at this distance from the following pulsars FOR A HOT TIME.
comics.voteyText:
Caption text: In your fantasies, you sex freaks!
Image: A naked human figure (a man) in the line-drawing style of the Pioneer plaque, standing within a doodled border.

comics.title: Evolution
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A woman with long hair stands at the end of a wooden dock, hoisting a large metal barrel over the edge toward the water. Another person stands further back on the dock watching.

Watching person: WHAT... WHAT ARE YOU DOING?

Woman: EVOLUTIONARY BIOLOGY.

Caption (below panel):

Proposal: Fill the ocean with weapons to see if anyone evolves hands.
comics.hoverText: Why don't scientists check oil spills for dolphin-made combustion engines?
comics.voteyText:
A roughly drawn man's face.
Off-panel voice: WHERE'D YOU GET THAT BARREL?
Man: COSTCO.

comics.title: Like
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man (talking upward, to God): Dear God, do you even like us?

Panel 2:

God (offscreen voice in a purple speech bubble): How can you ask me that, baby?

Panel 3:

Man: If you really liked humans, why did you put us in bodies?

Panel 4:

God (offscreen): If someone you like comes to visit, do you put them in a hotel that's leaky, smells bad, that's cramped and lonely?

Panel 5:

God (offscreen, the man listening): How in the world are you complaining? Look at what your bodies get to do! You live a life of harmony, freedom, and non-stop sexual gratification ruled by an assertive yet loving matriarchy.

Panel 6:

Man: (listening, uncertain)

Panel 7:

Man, gesturing: ...

Panel 8:

God (offscreen): Oh shit, I thought you were a bonobo. Humans don't have souls.

Panel 9:

God (now shown as a silhouetted figure): Try reading history. It's obvious.
comics.hoverText: Bonobos have souls. Chimps have half-souls. Cetaceans get a quarter.
comics.voteyText:
Text (continuing God's list of which creatures got souls): It's only bonobos, dolphins, squid, puppies, octopodes, whales, bee hives, and fairly smart robots.
(Below: a scene of a person petting/interacting with a small robot, with motion lines.)

comics.title: Law
comics.comicText:
Panel 1

Woman (an aide holding a paper): Mr. President, the era of top-down policy is over. We can now use algorithms and A/B testing to pitch millions of ideas to constituents in order to suss out the most popular proposals.

Panel 2

Woman: Coming up with our own views would be inefficient, so the algorithm randomly generates policy-sounding sentences, which voters then rate by preference.

Panel 3

Woman: Thus, we have over time evolved the single policy that nobody opposes and everyone favors.

Panel 4

Woman: Throw it on the teleprompter! I'm off to my podium!

Panel 5

The President (a man with glasses, reading from a teleprompter at a podium): And therefore we must... huh. Give all birds humanoid arm attachments so it looks like they're waving.

Panel 6

Caption: [THUNDEROUS APPLAUSE]

(A crowd cheers ecstatically.)

Panel 7

The President (smiling slightly): Wow, there's something worse than democracy.
comics.hoverText: Somewhere out there... specifically in San Francisco... someone is reading this and deciding it's a great idea.
comics.voteyText: A bird (toucan-like, with a large beak) stands on a wire, with one humanoid arm attached to its body, raised up as if waving.

comics.title: Silver Lining
comics.comicText:
Two people lie on their backs on a grassy hillside, looking up at the sky, talking.

Panel 1:

Person 1: They say every cloud has a silver lining.

Person 2: That's because of all the mercury pollution.

Panel 2:

Person 1: Your generation will probably need to do something.

Panel 3:

Person 1: I thought that was a metaphor.

Person 2: Used to be. Environmental damage has ruined a lot of our old sayings.

Panel 4:

Person 2: We used to say "there are plenty of fish in the sea."

Person 1: Meaning?
comics.hoverText: On the other hand, once there's enough orbital debris, we can go back to saying the sky's the limit.
comics.voteyText:
A person leans in close to another's face.
Speaker (in speech bubble): It's getting harder and harder for birds of a feather to flock together.

comics.title: Causal
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Daughter (off-panel/foreground): You're grounded?!

Mother: You can't ground me!

Panel 2:

Daughter: As my misgivings are the direct consequences of the fatal conditions of reality!

Panel 3:

Daughter: There is no free will! Thus, all justice is a farce! Aside that I'm a robot in a world without choice, there is no god!

Mother: Not only will you not adopt that, I'm canceling your screen time for two weeks.

Panel 4:

Daughter: But you could do otherwise!

Mother: That'd violate causality.
comics.hoverText: If you don't find this funny, blame physics.
comics.voteyText: Daughter (distraught, near tears): There dwells no justice in the house of Mom!

comics.title: Tail
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man with dark curly hair, sunglasses, and a suit holds up a handheld graphing calculator triumphantly, as if it were a phone showing off at a club.

Man: YEAH! SHAKE THAT FAT TAIL, BABY!

Caption (below panel): This is how statisticians celebrate rare events.
comics.hoverText: Suddenly regretting that I didn't make him look like Nate Silver.
comics.voteyText: No dialogue. A statistical distribution curve is drawn as a long, low-spreading shape with a pronounced long "fat tail" extending to the right. Numbers are scrawled along the bottom of the curve (resembling axis tick marks / data values, e.g. "5 2 0 8 2").

comics.title: Feelings
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (at laptop): Okay, I think I figured out how we can afford the kitchen repairs.

Man (Frank): I'm here to listen to you. To be your shoulder to cry on.

Panel 2:

Woman: What are you doing?

Frank: I read a book about how women don't like to solve problems. They just want to feel heard. And I HEAR YOU about your strong feelings.

Panel 3:

Woman: I'm not having strong feelings. I'm fixing our budget.

Frank: Nah. You're talking about the budget to CONNECT with me. To know there's a sympathetic ear for your FEELINGS about the budget.

Panel 4:

Woman: You're pissing me off, Frank.

Frank: See! I told you it was all about feelings!

Panel 5 (silhouettes):

Woman: I'm removing your $200 a month for lockpick sets and firecrackers.

Frank: But I need those!
comics.hoverText: Fortunately, she wouldn't dare touch the budget for ninja stars.
comics.voteyText: Frank: This is just as asinine as when you canceled my monthly samurai sword subscription.

comics.title: Evidence
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Flame-haired man: Why won't people accept that reptiles rule the government from Buckingham Palace?

Bespectacled man: Lack of evidence?

Panel 2:

Flame-haired man (agitated): WRONG. There's no GOOD evidence. There are pages and pages and pages of stuff people have said!

Panel 3:

Flame-haired man: If one piece of bad evidence is only as good as one-millionth of a piece of good evidence, to prove the reptile theory all we have to do is get people to say they're pretty sure it's true ten million times.

Panel 4:

Bespectacled man: You don't get gold by piling shit really high.

Flame-haired man (angry, blushing): You can't prove that!
comics.hoverText: I see this logic all over the place and it's fundamentally like saying 10,000 frogs makes one hamster, if you think of frogs as just not terribly good hamsters.
comics.voteyText:
Flame-haired man (off-panel, shouting): We just need enough so that it goes supernova.
(The bespectacled man stares blankly, sweating, saying nothing.)

comics.title: Slur
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man (speaking, gesturing): "Oh, they claim to be peaceful, but they're constantly violent! They're lazy! They're stupid! They'd rather loaf around and drink than put in a day's work! And you know what else? They treat their women like GARBAGE!"

(A second man listens beside him.)

Caption below the panel:

Any slur on a particular group is an apt description of humans in general.
comics.hoverText: Is this it? Is this where the hatemail tsunami finally hits the shore?
comics.voteyText:
Handwritten text inside a hand-drawn square border:
"I WONDER WHAT SLUR BONOBOS USE FOR US."

comics.title: Ending
comics.comicText:
Main comic:

Panel 1:

Man (bearded, with round glasses, lying in bed): "A STORY SHOULD HAVE A BEGINNING, A MIDDLE, AND AN END, BUT NOT NECESSARILY IN THAT ORDER."

Caption (below panel):

Cinema Fun Fact:

Jean-Luc Godard is lousy in bed.
comics.hoverText: In fact, sometimes the climax won't even arrive until several sequels later.
comics.voteyText: The man (loosely sketched in a rough, scribbly style) speaks again: "I KNOW YOU FEEL LIKE YOU DIDN'T ENJOY IT, BUT THE STORY IS BETTER THIS WAY."

comics.title: Suffering
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Advisor (a man holding a notepad): Terrible news, Mr. President.

Panel 2:

Advisor: We've discovered a mathematical quirk in the science of human behavior which has allowed us to completely eliminate human suffering forever.

Panel 3:

President (a balding man with glasses and a beard): Isn't that good?

Advisor: No, Mr. President.

Panel 4:

Advisor: The main philosophical objection to eating living humans is that we're capable of suffering.

Panel 5:

Advisor: Now that we have a scientific economics, the inevitable result is widespread murder-cannibalism. As we speak, people are devouring each other in the streets.

Panel 6:

President: Interesting.

Panel 7:

President: But we've eliminated suffering?

Panel 8:

President (now seated at a table holding a fork and knife): Also hunger!
comics.hoverText: If we could artificially enhance dolphin suffering, maybe we'd treat them better.
comics.voteyText:
A speech bubble reads: I am at peace with this.
(Below, two disembodied butts/figures and small sketchy human shapes are shown crawling on the ground, suggesting people on all fours.)

comics.title: Hydra
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A bearded man in a toga gestures toward a multi-headed green hydra rising from the darkness.

Bearded man: "If you once remove a head from the hydra, there grow two in its place!"

Panel 2: Two robed men (one bearded, one not) regard each other thoughtfully.

Man: "Huh. Huh."

Panel 3: A black void with several glowing-eyed, sharp-toothed hydra heads lurking. Two robed figures stand in silhouette at the bottom.

Figure: "Do you think we could catch it?"

Panel 4 (within the same dark scene):

Figure: "Why?"

Panel 5: A pink banner reads "EVER AFTER..." A modern-day father in a gray jacket stands beside a small boy.

Boy: "Dad, where does shawarma meat come from?"

Father: "Nobody knows, son. Nobody knows."
comics.hoverText: Hot dogs are made of the infinite turtles that hold up the Earth
comics.voteyText: Text only (no image): "Also hot dogs are made of sasquatch."

comics.title: Past
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man 1 (bald, with a goatee): You ever feel like you were born in the wrong era?

Man 2 (with combed-back hair): All the time, man.

Panel 2:

Man 1: Sometimes women make me think I'm living in a quaint "olde tyme" period of history. They imagine her I get kicked out of Home Depot.

Panel 3:

Man 1: I meant like... fancy outfits and horse and carriage and stuff.

Man 2: Sometimes I go in public to burn a sack of cats but instead of drawing an audience, I get kicked out of Home Depot.
comics.hoverText: I'm prepared to license this ad concept to Home Depot.
comics.voteyText:
Text (a man's outstretched arm and a security guard's hand visible): "Sir, I'm going to have to ask you to leave Home Depot."
The scene shows the back of a person's head as he is being told to leave.

comics.title: Dangerous
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (red-haired): I hear you like... dangerous men.

Man: ...maybe I do.

Panel 2:

Man: Sometimes I walk around the house just swallowing stuff.

Man: Tacks, animal hair, batteries, whatever.

Panel 3:

Man: It's hard. It's damn hard. The pain comes at night, but I push through.

Panel 4:

Woman: I guess strictly speaking what I like is men who are dangerous in a way that implies they have visible abs.

Man: You gonna eat that toothpick?
comics.hoverText: Do you like danger...ously sedentary lifestyles?
comics.voteyText: Man (close-up, frowning): What's mine is mine.

comics.title: Phallus
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Male spider: Baby, if it's okay with you I'd like to detach my phallus after we copulate in order to deny access to future mates.

Panel 2:

Female spider: Honestly that feels a little possessive.

Panel 3:

Female spider: I guess I just see our relationship as a serious one.

Panel 4:

Male spider: Also, like, this thing just pops off after sex. Evolution sucks.

Caption: EVOLUTION SUCKS.
comics.hoverText: To be clear, I know how many legs a spider has, I just haven't got a clue where they go on the spider.
comics.voteyText: Male spider: Still better than that ape thing where they stare at each other while doing it.

comics.title: Ends
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Father (a balding man with orange hair and glasses, lying in bed): Son, the most important thing in life is that you must always treat people as an end in themselves, never a means.

Panel 2:

Son (a young man with orange hair and glasses): Why?

Panel 3:

Father: People will love you for it and then you can get stuff out of them.

Panel 4:

Son: Like social stuff?

Father: Cash, boy. Cash.
comics.hoverText: Mind you this isn't true of MY actions. Just other people.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of the father's face, smiling slyly.
Father: Trust me. I am your friend.

comics.title: Market Failure
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man in a suit (the customer, standing): "Wow, a quarter a cup. What a deal!"

(A small boy sits at a lemonade stand with a red pitcher.)

Panel 2:

Boy (cheerful, to himself / aside): "My parents think I'm learning to be entrepreneurial, so they're fronting the cost of production. Sales are 100% profit for me."

(A sign on the stand reads: "Lemonade 25¢")

Panel 3:

Boy: "By flooding the market with inexpensive lemonade, I will strangle every local supplier of refreshing drinks."

Panel 4:

Boy (grinning, pointing): "With the competition suffocated, every parched tongue will make its way to Billy's Lemonade Stand. Only to find the price has been JACKED UP twentyfold."

Panel 5:

Boy (laughing maniacally): "Everyone will be too thirsty to swallow, but they'll HAVE to swallow monopoly pricing."

The customer (skeptical): "The people will rise up! We'll just drink healthy refreshing water!"

Panel 6:

Boy (scornful): "You're gonna get through your workday without sugar or artificial flavoring? Stop blowing smoke up your own ass, you old fool."

Customer (resigned, eyes wide): "All right, give me the damn lemonade."

Panel 7:

(The boy hands over a cup of lemonade to the customer.)

Boy: "Have a blessed day, sir!"
comics.hoverText: Once he has monopoly power, fresh lemons may as well not exist.
comics.voteyText: The customer, now drinking, looks down into the cup with a delighted/dazed expression: "Wow, fresh lemons!"

comics.title: Pour One Out
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (with bob haircut, addressing someone off-panel): I'm pouring this one out for you, Sally.

Panel 2:

The woman, in a red blazer, pours out a fancy box of wine. The box reads (in French): "la boîte de vin".

Panel 3:

A ghostly spirit rises from the poured-out wine.

Ghost: Boxwine? You're pouring out boxwine for me?

Panel 4:

Ghost (off-panel): You know what you were.

The woman looks down, unimpressed/sheepish.
comics.hoverText: Do you REALLY want correct French on a boxwine?
comics.voteyText:
A smiling face speaks.
Speaker: This is one level better than "le box de wine" wine.

comics.title: Conscious
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man with red hair: Consciousness is just a system observing itself.

Woman with dark curly hair: How dare you!

Panel 2:

Woman (eyes wide, alarmed): Are you saying I'm not conscious?

Panel 3:

Man: Don't you ever introspect?

Panel 4:

Woman (gripping her head, panicking): AAH! NO! AAH! I'm remembering embarrassing stuff from middle school now you son of a bitch!

Panel 5:

Woman (calmer): Okay. Phew. Okay. I think I'm back to having no complex internal sense of self.

Woman: Teach me your ways.
comics.hoverText: I just don't see why everyone's so pro-consciousness.
comics.voteyText:
Man (caption text): First step: have a phone. Second step: never stop looking at stuff on the phone.
(The woman is shown blankly looking down, presumably at a phone.)

comics.title: Surveillance
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Child (holding a tablet, addressing parents): Mom, dad, I want to show you this surveillance video of the kitchen last night.

Panel 2:

Child (narrating over the video): As you can plainly see, mom took a large bakesale cookie, intended for children, spread cream cheese over said cookie, put powdered sugar on the cream cheese, consumed the whole as if it were a liquid bolus and her neck was a vast straw, and absconded into the darkness.

Panel 3:

Mom (defensive, sweating): That's a deepfake! Don't believe it! Google can do anything these days!

Panel 4:

Mom (shouting wildly, as the father and child look on): Then explain why the cookie is gone. Sheep! You are sheep of the tech industry!
comics.hoverText: Later it turns out the Dad has masterminded everything.
comics.voteyText: Mom (shouting, single close-up panel): You're in the pocket of Big Truth!

comics.title: Trough
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Child: Dad, how come adults are all crazy?

Dad: Because they had parents.

Panel 2:

Dad: This is well-studied. In countries around the world, the lowest levels of happiness occur between the ages of 40 and 60. This is regardless of whether you have kids or not.

Panel 3:

Dad: So at the exact moment you're come to be for guidance, I'm at my lowest level of utility. You are getting all your rage- and role-modeling from people at their lifetime maximum of confusion, sorrow, and anger and everyone else is too.

Panel 4:

Child: I asked mom the same question and she said this was crazy with love for me.

Dad: Damn her.
