Scene: The bartender raises a hand, flustered, while the horse stands poised at the bar.
comics.hoverText: Fortunately, that horse is over 21, so he won't live that much longer.
comics.voteyText:
Caption across the top of the panel: NAYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYY
Scene: An extreme close-up of the bartender's face, mouth open in distress, one hand raised toward his cheek.

comics.title: Lesson
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (narration): They're growing us into super-soldiers for our own war. We have no immunity!

A soldier: My God! There's something else! We could too. It's farming!

Panel 2 (narration): The aliens were ruthless and singularly minded.

Panel 3 (narration): As disease and hunger heaped higher and higher, we feared that soon, no one would remain.

Woman: How will we ever survive in your eyes for 20 years, you would possess the colossal immune response needed to defeat them? But come on.

Panel 4 (narration): Our survivors found each other.

Man: Wow, you're a kindergarten teacher too?

Woman: Me three!

Another: Me three!

Panel 5 (narration): They formed into cooperative resistance bands.

Narration (within scene): It's monday May 12th and today's morning circle topic is revenge.

Panel 6 (narration): They could build anything from anything.

Woman: And now that the glue on this macaroni is dry, we give the pipecleaner a twist and... boop! Fully automatic.

Panel 7 (narration): The aliens had no idea when they landed for their foes were masters of patience and lovers of silence.

Sound effect: Tchk! Tchk!

Label/sign: A is for aggression

Panel 8 (narration): Once they struck, there was no recess from violence.

A woman (raising sword): And when you get to hell, tell them Ms. Frizzle sent you!

Panel 9 (narration): But it was not their innate hatred that vanquished the aliens.

Man: It's not normal life! Their bodies are like arp-ing onto a circuitously digital chronic combat with only the fittest disease allowed to mate! Frkkkin' shock!

Panel 10 (narration): Indeed, the aliens could flee, they fell dead where they had stood. For these little tiny humans were perfect, hyper-organized, biological war machines.

One human: Who wants to sing the cleanup song?

Other humans: Clean up! Clean up! Everybody let's clean up! Clean up!

Panel 11 (narration): So humanity was founded anew, this time oriented around kindness, reciprocity, and naps.

Woman: Now in a tidy society we will only sort objects by color, never people!

Panel 12 (narration): And no one ever forgot to thank their teacher.

Child: Thank you for teaching the apocalypse and repopulating the earth, Ms. Lisa!

Another child: And thank you for learning to read through stress!
comics.hoverText: Hollywood, call me. I can have this script done on a weekend.
comics.voteyText: (none)

comics.title: Number One
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: An older bald man with glasses and a mustache holds up a coffee mug, angry. A younger woman with dark curly hair stands behind him looking apprehensive.

Man: WHAT THE HELL IS THIS? YOU THINK I'M STUPID?

Woman: Dad, I-

Panel 3: The woman, exasperated.

Woman: OKAY, OKAY, I'LL GET YOU A DIFFERENT ONE.

Panel 5: Close-up of the new mug. It reads "NOT SIGNIFICANTLY DIFFERENT FROM A GOOD DAD" above a bell curve (normal distribution). A dashed line near the left tail is labeled "you," the shaded tails are marked, and the x-axis is labeled "-1.5."
comics.hoverText: Available in the SMBC store now! Link is below. (PS: Credit to Richard McElreath for the language and graph on the mug)
comics.voteyText: A woman with long dark hair (drawn in the rough, sketchy 'votey' style) looks sidelong/skeptical. Above her is a speech-bubble-shaped tag reading "P<.01".

comics.title: Enhance
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man with mustache (detective/investigator): "Dammit, all we have is this one security photo, but the murderer isn't in it."

Panel 2:

Man with mustache: "Wait! Look! There's a reflection in that mirror!"

Woman (partner/colleague): "But it's so blurry."

Panel 3:

Man with mustache: "Computer, use the AI I installed and ENHANCE!"

Panel 4:

(No dialogue. The enhanced image resolves into a busty, scantily-defined female figure with exaggerated breasts.)

Man with mustache: "Never bring your personal laptop to work again."

The AI (pink speech bubble, from the laptop): "Do you like my feet, master?"

The AI (large speech bubble): "I want you to know that me and the giant-boobed surveillance videos also do romance stuff. It's not all feet."
(A man's face looks on with a flat, unimpressed expression.)

comics.title: Myth
comics.comicText:
Panel 1

Woman (curly hair, glasses): Myths are more than stories. They're visions of how to live life. How to BE.

Man: Totally.

Panel 2

Woman: Like the one in Ovid, where Midas says Pan's music is better than Apollo's, so Apollo gives Midas donkey ears forever.

Panel 3

Woman: The deep insight being that if there's a music contest between two gods, you should prefer whichever music came from the more powerful god, because otherwise they might magic your ears so you look dumb.

Panel 4

Woman: Or the story in the Prose Edda, where Loki turns into a mare to distract a giant's horse, and then while he's at it, decides to have sex with the horse and then gives birth to a flying 8-legged horse.

Panel 5

Woman: The beautiful vision being that if you're in horse-mode, hey, make time for sex. Because you just might birth an airborne spider-horse.

Panel 6

Woman: Or the part in Plutarch where Set dismembers Osiris, and Isis puts him back together, except that a fish ate his boner, so she makes him a golden dong, the point being—

Man: Okay, fine. Point taken.

Panel 7

Woman: The golden dong represents the human potential to have something golden inside us.

Man: STOP IT!
comics.hoverText: I need to do a book just of people ruining some nice idea by dissecting it.
comics.voteyText: Woman: The boner eating fish represents the modern economy. Think about it.

A man (orange/red hair, seen from behind): OH MY GOD, ALIENS! ARE YOU GOING TO EAT US?

An alien (a green alien with large black eyes, distant in the sky): NOT YET.

comics.comicText:
Main comic:

Panel 1 (caption above panel): DON'T BE SAD. DO NOT BE SAD.

Panel 1: A patient lies on a therapist's couch. The patient: "That's your advice? Just don't be sad?"

Panel 2: The therapist (a bald man) sits in his chair facing away. Therapist: "The moment your life is a net negative, it becomes acceptable for me to eat you."

Caption below the comic: Utilitarians make the worst psychiatrists.
comics.hoverText: Deontologists of course WANT to eat you, but aren't allowed.
comics.voteyText: The therapist speaks: "It may seem weird, but when I say I might eat them, lots of my patients report increased happiness." Below, the patient on the couch grips the therapist's arm with a strained expression.

comics.title: Protocol
comics.comicText:
Caption box (top): I took the worst performing students on the last exam and assigned them a new test for the following week. In the intervening days, I smeared their foreheads with peanut butter and smooshed googly eyes into it.

Speech bubble (off-panel questioner): The result?

Man with blue hair and round glasses: Statistically significant improvement in their average score.

Man with blue hair and round glasses: The googly-goo protocol is VALIDATED and is now being trialed in thousands of public schools.

[He gestures with a piece of chalk toward a chalk drawing of a smiley face with googly eyes and a rising line graph, with axes labeled "score" (vertical), "time" (horizontal), and an arrow pointing "up."]

Bottom caption: Science pro tip: you can prove anything you want using regression to the mean.
comics.hoverText: If you oppose this it's because you want line go down, but I want line go up.
comics.voteyText: Speech bubble (a grinning man): We can create brand new medicines just by finding currently sick people and giving them whatever we like!

comics.title: Bomb
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A bald man in a dark suit (a supervillain figure) stands with arms spread, addressing a man in a red-and-blue costume (Superman).

Villain: It is a three stage weapon that will bring France to its knees.

Panel 2: A cityscape of Paris with the Eiffel Tower, windows shattering amid a glowing blast.

Villain (caption): Stage one is a sonic pulse that will shatter every window in Paris.

Panel 3: A man with a mustache stands amid melting cheese, looking distressed.

Villain (caption): Stage two, a brief heat pulse at precisely seventy degrees celsius. Enough to leave everyone alive while melting all cheese.

Panel 4: A large yellow block of cheese with a small American flag stuck in it.

Villain (caption): Why alive? To watch stage three, where sodium citrate is explosively fired in every direction, emulsifying the melted cheese into AMERICAN CHEESE.

Panel 5: The villain laughs maniacally.

Villain: AHAHAHAHAHAHA!

Panel 6: Superman responds.

Superman: Wait really?

Panel 7: Close on Superman's face, considering.

Superman: Actually that sounds fine to me.

Panel 8: Superman flies off happily, leaving the small villain behind.

Superman: I'll get some tater tots to go with it!

Panel 9: A Daily Planet newspaper.

Headline: DAILY PLANET

FRANCE DEVASTATED BY CHEESE-ALTERING BOMB

Subhead: Superman is unfortunately from American Midwest, say experts.

Photo caption: "It's great on white," says Man of Steel.

(The photo shows Superman holding a cheesy item in front of the Eiffel Tower.)

comics.title: Floral
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (with dark hair, walking on a forest path with a red-haired companion): Have you noticed that when talking about sex, men's bodies are described like animal parts and women's bodies like plant parts?

Red-haired companion: Huh.

Panel 2:

Woman: Budding... flowering... fruitful... even technical terms like deciduolization.

Panel 3:

Woman: It's just one more way that women are seen as passive and men active.

Panel 4:

Woman: We will teach our children to be DIFFERENT!

Panel (LATER...):

The red-haired woman, now a mother sitting on a couch beside a small child, gestures at a poster/chart on the wall reading "EAT INDIVIDUAL".

Mother: And then your testicles will descend like coconuts, ripening in an island breeze.
comics.hoverText: It will inflate like a beached dolphin on a summer's day.
comics.voteyText: The dark-haired woman (in a speech bubble): I'm still trying to find a plant that works like boners but the internet doesn't appreciate my innocent intentions.

comics.title: Fellow
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

A man with flame-like red hair and a beard sits beside a man wearing a cap and a high-visibility safety vest. The red-haired man speaks earnestly while the man in the cap stares ahead with a flat expression.

Red-haired man: "Okay, but to be clear, ALTHOUGH you think disagreeing runs the government, from the moon, which you think is flat, you DON'T think that THEREFORE the military should dissolve Congress and rule for a thousand years."

Man in the cap: "WANNA GET A BEER?"

Caption (below the panel): "The more conspiratorial politics has gotten, the lower my standards for fellow travelers."
comics.hoverText: Maybe we can crowd out evil conspiracies with benignly stupid ones?
comics.voteyText:
A person's head and shoulders are drawn at the bottom; above them is a large thought bubble repeating the same line over and over.
Thought bubble: "DON'T ASK WHAT SQUATCH THINKS ABOUT JEWS. DON'T ASK WHAT SQUATCH THINKS ABOUT JEWS. DON'T ASK WHAT SQUATCH THINKS ABOUT JEWS. DON'T ASK WHAT SQUATCH THINKS ABOUT JEWS. DON'T ASK WHAT SQUATCH THINKS ABOUT JEWS. DON'T ASK WHAT SQUATCH THINKS ABOUT JEWS."

comics.title: Good
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A person with flame-like hair (the questioner): "God, are things good because you command it, or do you command it because it is good?"

Panel 2:

A figure with an orange/pointed head (God): "Man, I dunno. I just do next token prediction."

Panel 3:

The questioner: "...How many R's in 'resurrection'?"

Panel 4:

God: "Two. Why?"

The questioner (now shown in silhouette): "Everything is so clear now."
comics.hoverText: Actually WWII was a hallucination that just got way out of control.
comics.voteyText: The questioner (in silhouette): "That is such a clever operation, brain emoji, heart emoji, exclamation point!"

comics.title: Fermi
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Person A: You ever wonder if AI is the 'Great Filter'?

Person B: Like the solution to the Fermi Paradox is that intelligent life is always destroyed by AI?

Person A: Yeah.

Panel 2:

Person A: Seems unlikely if so, we should just be getting alien signals from machine life.

Panel 3:

Person B: Except AI will always be developed first as a servant, and you would never program a servant to feel lonely.

Panel 4:

Person B: I mean it's possible every star in the universe is populated by self-satisfied immortals, with no pursuits other than eternal contemplation of their own contentedness.

Panel 5:

Person A: Wow. What a nightmare.

Panel 6:

Person A: We must expand. We are the only way for the universe to know itself and then think 'this sucks.'
comics.hoverText: The first thought that occurred after the Universe began to contemplate itself was 'this? is this all?'
comics.voteyText:
A robot/voice: Too bad we killed the humans and now just where their skin and rehearse their lives like ghosts.
Another robot: Beep boop.

comics.title: Genera
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A woman holding a pregnancy test stares at it excitedly.

Woman: AAH! A SECOND RED LINE! WE'RE PREGN--

Panel 2: A man beside her interrupts, leaning in to look.

Man: WAIT... IT'S NOT A LINE... IT'S...

Panel 3: Close-up of the pregnancy test in the woman's hand. Its display shows a jagged, spiky red curve rather than a clean line.

Man (continuing): ...A REAL-VALUED FUNCTION THAT'S CONTINUOUS EVERYWHERE BUT DIFFERENTIABLE NOWHERE.?

Panel 4 (wide bottom panel): The couple sits side by side on a red couch, both looking dismayed/deadpan, staring ahead. A caption banner stretches across the top of the panel.

Caption: IT'S A MATHEMATICIAN!
comics.hoverText: You can tell if it'll be a cartoonist by seeing if it cries whenever anyone comes in its room and/or turns on the lights.
comics.voteyText: No drawn scene -- the aftercomic panel contains only small handwritten text reading: "THIS IS THE MATT PARKER STORY" (styled as if from a mathematician's notebook, alluding to mathematician/math communicator Matt Parker).

comics.title: Right there
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (Sally): Yeah, right there. You like that? Oh I do like that. Right th-

Man (from doorway): Sally! Are you recreating streaming porn using shadow puppets?!

Caption (below panel): The good news was that the ban on adult consumption choices revived many traditional forms of media.
comics.hoverText: The main problem with the Erotic Ballet is that it's hard to politely clap with only one hand.
comics.voteyText: Man: I'll get my erotic macaroni art.

comics.title: Why
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man (kneeling, praying): God, why are we here?

Man: You and Sally?

Panel 2:

Man: I meant humanity. Who's Sally?

Panel 3:

God (voice): After this prayer, she trips over you. You fall in love, get married before you really know each other, have a child, then stay together for him.

Panel 4:

God (voice): He grows up in a household so thick with contempt, he develops a virtuosic power for imaginative escapism, which decades later culminates in him writing some REALLY good TV.

Panel 5:

God (voice): So, you see, I've answered your question: All is for entertainment, in the entertainmentest of all possible worlds.

Panel 6:

Man: Well, I'll show you, God. I'll ignore Sally and live a happy, productive life that isn't oriented around your amusement!

Panel 7:

God (voice): Sally has nice boobs and pretends your jokes are funny.

Panel 8:

God (voice): And so the die is cast.

(A woman, Sally, jogs by in the background as the man stands.)
comics.hoverText: We are here to get tripped over by Sally. That is all.
comics.voteyText:
Large hand-lettered text: "Did you have a nice fall?"
Small speech bubble: "Ha."
Speech bubble (over two embracing figures): "Irresistible."

comics.title: Dress
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (a woman at a party, looking dismayed): OH MY GOD THIS IS EMBARRASSING. SHE'S WEARING THE SAME DRESS AS ME.

Panel 1 (a companion next to her): SHEG... NOT?

Panel 2 (the woman, now angry, gesturing): CAN YOU COUNT? IT'S CLEARLY A 4-HOLED SPHERE JUST LIKE MINE.

Caption below: This is why topologists never go to parties.
comics.hoverText: If you ask a topologist what their house is like they start counting windows, doors, and chimneys.
comics.voteyText: (A man with a sly grin): OH, WAIT! I JUST HAVE TO STAB HER IN THE BACK AND WE CAN BE SEEN TOGETHER.

comics.title: Turn
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel, all dialogue against a black background):

First speaker: "C'mon baby, we each do a quarter rotation and we can hit 180 degrees! It's possible!"

Second speaker (smaller speech bubble): "But... why?"

First speaker (replying): "To become a single, MOIST surface, transcending orientation."

Caption below the panel: "We later broke up due to Edward's lack of interest in the Möbius 69."
comics.hoverText: Of course it's more impressive if you do it yourself.
comics.voteyText: A single speech bubble: "Technically, it's also a Möbius 96"

comics.title: Die
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man with reddish hair, kneeling by a leafy plant, asks a scout-like figure in a wide-brimmed hat:

Man: "IF I EAT THIS LEAF, WILL I DIE?"

The hatted figure (and other scouts standing behind them) reply:

Hatted figure: "EVENTUALLY, YEAH. AND POINTLESSLY."

Caption (below panel): One thing that really increased the accuracy of my foraging advice was despair.
comics.hoverText: Despair is also great for baking productivity.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of the hatted figure's face, smiling slightly.
Hatted figure: "OH, POSSIBLY WITH HUMILIATION AND/OR SUFFERING."

comics.title: Firstborn
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A dark, fiery throne room. A demonic lord with flame-like red hair sits on a throne, gesturing.

Demon Lord: "BEHOLD, LORD MEPHISTOCLES, THE VILE! I NOW SACRIFICE MY FIRSTBORN SON, TO BE YOURS IN THE LAND OF SHADOWS AND FORGETTING!"

Panel 2:

A glowing, shadowy figure (the dark lord Mephistocles) responds.

Mephistocles: "WHOA, HEY, WHOA. THERE. THE LAND OF SHADOWS AND FORGETTING IS A SERIOUS BUSINESS REQUIRING CHILDREN IN A SPECIFIC NEGATIVE-RETURN-ON-INVESTMENT--"

Panel 3:

The demon lord interrupts impatiently.

Demon Lord: "IF YOU WOULD RATHER, JIMMY, TO ARE 22, WITH A 4-YEAR DEGREE IN A TECHNICAL FIELD. I WOULD GLADLY ACCEPT HIS SOUL TO SERVE ME IN THE DARK UNDER-REALMS--"

Mephistocles: "TOO LATE!"

Panel 4 (labeled LATER):

The demon lord addresses Mephistocles again.

Demon Lord: "JIMMY! DO MORE MANN ACADEMY LESSONS! YOU PROMISED!"

Panel 5:

A young man (Jimmy) in flames responds.

Jimmy: "YOU CAN'T PUNISH ME WITH RESTRICTIONS BECAUSE SOULBOUND TO THE KNOWLEDGE-SECTOR DEPENDS ON ME GAINING UP TO 18% CREATIVE GO AND BEYOND!"

Demon Lord: "I JUST WANT WHAT'S BEST FOR YOU!"
comics.hoverText: And don't even get me STARTED on secondborn sons.
comics.voteyText: (THIS IS WHY ISAAC GOT SPARED AT THE LAST SECOND)

comics.title: Id
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Father (a man with glasses and a red shirt): Sally, did you clean your room like I told you to?

Sally (a young girl): I IDN'T IDN'T.

Panel 2:

Father: What?

Sally: "IDN'T" IS THE IMAGINARY NEGATION. USE IT TWICE AND IT CHANGES TO "DIDN'T." FOUR TIMES, IT RETURNS TO "DID."

Panel 3:

Father: So...

Sally: I IDN'T IDN'T IDN'T IDN'T NOT.

Panel 4:

Father: Is this a real thing or did you make it up?

Sally: I IDN'T.
comics.hoverText: Sorry
comics.voteyText:
Caption: PEOPLE LOVE RELATEABLE HUMOR
(A comedian/performer stands on a stage at a podium, addressing two audience members seated below. One audience member is labeled "Pokemon.")

comics.title: You Sir
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man stands on a stage at a podium, holding a microphone, addressing a crowd in the manner of a stand-up comedian or roast host.

Man (into microphone): "HEY PENCIL-DICK, IS THAT YOUR WIFE OR A RESCUE FROM THE SPCA, AM I RIGHT?"

Crowd member (thought/speech, smiling): "WOW, WHAT A GREAT INAUGURATION SPEECH. THIS MAN IS A FIGHTER."

Caption (below panel): Politics morphed into a straightforward roast of the public so gradually that nobody noticed the change.
comics.hoverText: Another ten years passes and its just contemptuous staring.
comics.voteyText:
Text above a smiling round face: "IF HE HATES ME THIS HARD, IMAGINE HOW MUCH HE HATES MY ENEMIES!"
The face below grins contentedly.

comics.title: Hear
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A red-haired man in a red shirt stands in a crowd, screaming in distress.

Man: OH MY GOD! MY GOD! IT'S JUST PEOPLE TALKING ABOUT HOW MANY SHOTS THEY HAD, ASKING ABOUT ASTROLOGY, AND SAYING "HEY" A LOT! FOREVER AND EVER AND EVER!

Panel 2: The man screams a long wordless scream over the crowd.

Man: NOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOO!

Caption: EARLIER.

Panel 3: The same man stands calmly facing a monkey's paw (a withered hand with one finger curling down).

Man: MONKEY'S PAW... I WISH BAR MUSIC WASN'T SO LOUD.
comics.hoverText: Dare: go into a loud bar and only make goat noises during 3 hours of communication, and see if anyone notices.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of two faces leaning in close, one speaking to the other.
Speaker: I TOO AM JUST HERE FOR SEX, BUT HAD WANTED TO PRETEND OTHERWISE.

comics.title: Medicine
comics.comicText:
Main comic:

Panel 1 (a bearded older man, the senior physician, addressing a younger bearded man in a green hood, the "Rookie"): "By Saint Erasmus' spleen, Rookie, it's OBVIOUS! A witch has stolen this man's boners. He may DIE. Get me half a firkin of mandrake root, a poultice of roasted he-mice, and ALL THE MAIDEN PISS YOU CAN CARRY!"

Panel 2 (the young man in the green hood, skeptical): "Will that hold him until we confirm by fire that an opinionated lady over 25 is at fault?"

The senior physician (gesturing over a prone patient lying on a table): "It'll have to, Rookie. It'll HAVE to."

Caption below the comic: "Why has nobody made a medieval medical drama?"
comics.hoverText: Again, Hollywood, call me. We can extend this single joke for YEARS.
comics.voteyText: The senior physician (shouting, pointing dramatically): "To the pissatorium!"

comics.title: Super
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Superman: Lex Luthor is too powerful, even for me. I summon the greatest heroes of mythology!

Panel 2:

Beowulf (a bare-chested bearded man): Beowulf! We must overturn the meadbenches of other tribes! Take their stuff, give it to friends to gather their loyalty for the next battle!

Panel 3:

Superman: Well, specifically we're fighting villains.

Superman: We are FIGHTING whoever has glittering gold!

Panel 4:

Superman: Okay... how about... Cú Chulainn!

Panel 5:

Cú Chulainn (a woman with long hair, wielding a club): We will kill a thousand henchman and heap their corpses as a wall against counterattack!

Panel 6:

Superman: We don't need to kill anyone, we—

Cú Chulainn: You gonna make a wall with ZERO bodies? Is this a KINDERGARTEN?

Panel 7:

Superman: Achilles?

Panel 8:

Achilles (a man in a crested helmet): We will lay siege to Luthor's lair!

Achilles: Then kill him and drag his corpse around Metropolis so his family can WATCH.

Panel 9:

Superman: See, there we go.

Superman: Gee, I dunno if—

Panel 10:

Achilles: His women will work our looms and deck our beds!

Panel 11:

Superman (to Batman): Jeepers. If this is what heroes of the past were like, what are people gonna say about us in the future?

Panel 12:

Batman: I mean a LOT of people get killed every time we fight a giant robot or whatever.

Panel 13:

Superman: Well—

Batman: Plus we're an unelected unilateral judge, jury, and executioner.

Panel 14:

Batman: Our approach to heroics has likely contributed to the widespread belief that patience, prudence, and due process are evidence of recklessness or corruption.

Batman: Not to mention—AAA!

Panel 15:

Batman is struck and engulfed by a blast (apparently a heat-vision/laser beam).

Panel 16:

Achilles: Loot his body, boys!

Cú Chulainn: I think I can use him as a load-bearing corpse!
comics.hoverText: These are actually the nicer heroes.
comics.voteyText: (none)

comics.title: Flux
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man with grey hair and a goatee, looking angry: HOW THE FUCK DID YOU FIND OUT HOW MUCH-FLUX I WAS MOVING?

Panel 2:

A man in a fedora and trench coat, in shadow: I GUESS YOU DIDN'T REALIZE YOUR ANS-WAS GUERILADED THE SURFACE IS CLOSING NOW... YOU SON OF A BITCH.

Panel 3:

The man in the fedora fires a gun. Sound effects: BANG! BANG!

Caption below the comic: My favorite gritty remake was the one for Griffith's Introduction to Electrodynamics, Third Edition.
comics.hoverText: The Stewart's Calculus movie was 4,000 hours long but it's okay because nobody ever gets to the final third anyway.
comics.voteyText: (THE 4TH MOVIE WAS THE SAME AS THE THIRD, BUT ALL THE HOMEWORK PROBLEM NUMBERS CHANGED)

comics.title: Drive
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man with flame-like red hair: HEY, HAVE YOU NOTICED THAT FOR THE LAST THREE GENERATIONS, AN EVER HIGHER PERCENTAGE OF INCREDIBLY ATTRACTIVE INFERTILE PEOPLE WHO WANT NON-STOP SEX WITH AVERAGE-LOOKING PEOPLE?

Panel 2:

Green alien: RIGHT. WE INTRODUCED A GENE DRIVE INTO YOUR SPECIES WHICH IS SLOWLY SPREADING THROUGH THE POPULATION, LEADING TO THE DEMISE OF HUMANITY UNLESS YOU TAKE CORRECTIVE ACTION.

Panel 3:

The red-haired man (now seen with attractive people around him): YEAH, LIKE WHO EVEN KNOWS WHY IT'S HAPPENING?

Panel 4:

Green alien: BECAUSE OF THE THING I JUST TOLD YOU.

Panel 5:

The red-haired man, standing among attractive partners: I SUPPOSE IT'LL REMAIN A MYSTERY FOREVER.
comics.hoverText: Later they turn off the gene drives and we beg to get them back.
comics.voteyText: The green alien: BY THE WAY WHAT'S YOUR CLOACA DOING TONIGHT?

comics.title: Nigh
comics.comicText:
Main comic (single panel):

Two men stand side by side holding protest signs.

Sign held by a bearded man (wearing a cross necklace): "THE END IS NIGH"

Sign held by a man with glasses and short dark hair (wearing a cross necklace): "THE END IS NIGH +/- 5 years"

Caption below the panel: Have you noticed that the Singularity people are the first doomsayers to use error bars?
comics.hoverText: The best part is watching them go up to guys yelling on a soapbox to ask what their timelines are.
comics.voteyText:
The man with glasses speaks (eyes half-closed, weary expression).
Man: I'll be yelling in the park about some data from Metaculus this evening if you'd like to accompany me.

comics.title: Standards
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man (gesturing, pointing): "This sentence is false" is NOT a paradox. It's underspecification because it's not clear what "this sentence" refers to.

Panel 2:

Man (holding up one finger): Therefore the newly formed organization for philosophical standards has defined a standard reference "This sentence."

Panel 3:

Man: From now on, any underspecified use of "this sentence" refers to the sentence "Monkeys have two butts but one of them is very small, so nobody noticed."

Panel 4:

Off-panel voice (silhouettes in audience): Analytic philosophy has gone too far! Stop defining the fun out of concepts!

Another voice (separate speech bubble): That reminds me, the smallest uninteresting number is now officially 26.
comics.hoverText: Also a heap is when you have 26 of something.
comics.voteyText: A voice (speech bubble, character with curly hair shown below): Also the ship of Theseus is just baryons. There's no ship.

comics.title: Work
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man with red, flame-like hair stands at the edge of a bed at night, holding a fitted sheet and stretching it out in front of him. A dark window behind him shows a starry night sky.

Man: "Nope, doesn't work. This must be the short side again somehow. God, I'm thirsty. Why is it so dark outside?"

Caption (below panel):

Prank idea #312211: Trap someone in a permanent bedmaking loop by giving them a three-sided fitted sheet.
comics.hoverText: Technically, a piece of elastic is a 2-sided fitted sheet.
comics.voteyText:
Label: "LATER..."
A simple line-art scene: a skeleton (a skull with a thin spine/ribs) lies slumped over the corner edge of the bed frame, having died still trying to make the bed.

comics.title: Petals
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

Caption (top): EVERY TIME I SEE THESE PETALS, IT REMINDS ME OF GRAMPA.

Older woman (Grammy): LONG AS HIS THIGH!

Younger woman: PLEASE STOP

Bottom caption (pro tip): Pro tip: never walk in Grammy's field of Orchis italica.
comics.hoverText: I read that it's sometimes called Italian Man Orchid, which is an insult or compliment, depending on whether you're talking absolute size or size relative to the rest of the petal.
comics.voteyText:
An older man's face, lost in reverie.
Man: LOOK! ...IT'S LIKE PHALLUS IMPUDICUS! ...IT'S LIKE HE'S STILL HERE, WAITING FOR ME.

comics.title: Stop
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man with red hair: AND THEN HE SAID "WELL I DON'T LIKE THE WAY YOU—

Woman with glasses (clutching her face, alarmed): STOP!

Panel 2:

Red-haired man: WHAT? WHAT'S THE MATTER?

Woman: WHENEVER PEOPLE START QUOTATIONS I INTERRUPT.

Panel 3:

Red-haired man: WHY?

Woman: IT'S THE ONLY GRAMMATICALLY ACCEPTABLE WAY TO OPEN QUOTATION MARKS WITHOUT CLOSING THEM.

Panel 4:

Red-haired man: YOU SON OF A BITCH!

Woman (eyes wide, pointing up, manic): LOOK AT THEM UP THERE! OPEN BUT NOT CLOSING! HAHAHAHA!

Panel 5:

Woman (face close, intense, gritting teeth): THEY'VE ESCAPED YOU! AND BECAUSE YOU BLOCK INTERRUPT AN OPENING QUOTATION, ALL YOU'VE DONE IS CONTRIBUTE TO AN ETERNAL GRAMMATICAL IMBALANCE IN REALITY!

Panel 6:

Woman: NOW TO OPEN A PARENTHETICAL RIGHT BEFORE YOU FREAK OUT (FREAKING OUT MEANING THAT—

Red-haired man (horrified): NOOOO!
comics.voteyText: No text. A square panel filled entirely with rows of small open-quotation-mark squiggles (open but never closed).

comics.title: Out
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A bald man wearing dark goggles and a green-and-yellow robe stands gesturing toward a framed diagram on the wall behind him. The diagram is labeled "Out of Ass-ica Hypothesis" and shows a red planet with a star-burst mark on it.

Lecturer (speech balloon): THE BACTERIUM WHICH COLONIZED AND DOMINATED THE RED PLANET CAN BE TRACED TO A SINGLE HUMAN GUT, PUSHED OUT OF AN AIRLOCK ON MARCH 5, 2063. THIS WORLD IS NOW A VAST MACROCOSM OF ONE MAN'S COLON.

Caption (below panel): I plan to be remembered as the greatest colonizer of Mars.
comics.hoverText: I hereby release this logo to SpaceX.
comics.voteyText:
A tiny stick figure swims in a small pool of white water within a large black field.
Swimmer (speech balloon): I WILL COME BACK, MORE POWERFUL THAN YOU CAN POSSIBLY IMAGINE!

comics.title: Actually
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

An elderly man stands outdoors on a grassy hill, looking up at the sky. A large speech bubble (apparently a voice from above/heaven) addresses him.

Voice from above: ACTUALLY FRANK, THE REAL HEAVEN WAS THE FRIENDS YOU MADE ALONG THE WAY

In the sky above are cartoon clouds, a glowing yellow sun/orb, and small floating winged figures (cherub- or angel-like friends).
comics.hoverText: The good news is you touched your butt once, so you wouldn't be going there anyway.
comics.voteyText:
A framed panel showing a continuation of the same voice-from-above narration. The frame is hand-drawn and lumpy; in the lower portion is a large dark scribbled/shaded circular shape (suggesting an underground pit or cavern opening).
Voice from above: HELL, HOWEVER, IS A PLACE UNDERGROUND WITH MEAN GOAT-DUDES

comics.title: Chew
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel)

A man with red flame-like hair and a beard (pink shirt) speaks while a woman with brown hair and glasses (green shirt) looks on with an increasingly annoyed expression.

Man: "I CAME TO KICK ASS AND CHEW BUBBLEGUM, AND I'M ALL OUT OF BUBBLEGUM."

Man: "THEREFORE IT IS IMPOSSIBLE TO KICK ASS AND CHEW BUBBLEGUM."

Man: "I SHOULD HAVE SAID 'I CAME TO KICK ASS XOR CHEW BUBB-"

Woman (interrupting, exasperated): "STOP! STOP IT!"

Caption (below panel): I became insufferable after learning first-order logic.
comics.hoverText: There was a fairly intricate debate on an early version of this posted to bluesky, the contention being over whether OR was sufficient. I think the ORs have it, but XOR is a funnier word, so there.
comics.voteyText: Handwritten caption inside a hand-drawn box: "SUDDENLY REGRETTING NOT MAKING A T-SHIRT OF 'I CAME TO KICK ASS AND CHEW BUBBLE GUM AND I'M ALL OUT OF GUM THEREFORE I CANNOT KICK ASS AND CHEW BUBBLEGUM'"

comics.title: Dogs
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

First man: Son, we don't need any fancy math when we run a hot dog company!

Panel 2:

Second man (the son): But you sell buns AND dogs, right?

Panel 3:

First man: So people want to be able to buy the same amount of dogs as buns. Surely they're sold in different quantities.

Panel 4:

Second man: So you can easily create ratios between the two that can never be equal, but you nonetheless... equality as the number of purchase gets infinitely large?

First man: OH MY GOD.

Panel 5 (caption: LATER THAT DAY):

Two signs are shown. One reads "BUNS 8th COUNT." The other reads "DOGS 6 COUNT."
comics.hoverText: You can also do the pi dogs, but then you lose business from the tau people.
comics.voteyText: Caption: (LATER, THE CONSUMER FIGHTS BACK BY SQUARING THE QUANTITY OF BUNS)

comics.title: Technically
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Two children (one with reddish hair, one in green) standing on a grassy hill at dusk, looking up at the sky.

Child with reddish hair: AWW, COME ON!

Child with reddish hair: NOT AGAIN!

A parent figure stands beside a tall electronic console/control unit (with a red illuminated panel) operating it.

Parent: YOU SHOULD ENJOY IT MORE, CHILDREN! IT'S TECHNICALLY HARDER!

Caption (below panel):

Weekend activity:

Testing my missile defense system on fireworks displays.
comics.hoverText: It might also be possible to use complex soundwaves to inderdict the festive music.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of a person (the parent) speaking.
Parent: I ALSO HAVE AN ENERGY BEAM SYSTEM THAT CAN TAKE OUT A PUPPET FROM 2 KILOMETERS AWAY.

comics.title: Positive
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A detective stands in a parlor addressing two well-dressed people, while a body lies dead on the floor in a pool of blood.

Detective: "The knife in Madame Dupont's back belongs to the butler, whose fingerprints are on it. We also found her jewels hidden in the floorboards of his room. Unfortunately we cannot make inferences beyond sense data and any attempt to do so is metaphysical nonsense."

Caption below panel: There should be a Logical Positivist detective show.
comics.hoverText: No, I don't know what knives look like. I've only been drawing 25 years.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of a man with glasses pointing his finger, speaking emphatically.
Man: "OBJECTIONS ARE A FORM OF METAPHYSICS!"

comics.title: Puppets
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

An old wizard with a gray beard, pointed hat, and staff stands beside a short hooded figure in a robe. They are looking toward a pond, out of which rise two hand puppets on arms emerging from the water: one pink/purple puppet and one green puppet.

Wizard: "IT'S TWO HANDPUPPETS, AND THEY KEEP FIGHTING, AND NOBODY LOOKS HAPPY BUT NOBODY CAN GET THE UPPER HAND."

Caption (below panel): The Lady of the Lake suggests Democracy.
comics.hoverText: Later a foot comes along wearing Jackboots and they have to decide whether to unite or get drowned.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of a man's face, frowning, with a speech bubble.
Man: "FUCK YOU, THE PEOPLE WANT A GUY WITH A SWORD!"

comics.title: Gardening
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman with blonde hair: THIS IS SUCH A BEAUTIFUL GARDEN, BUT WHY SO MANY PLUM TREES AT THE BOTTOM OF A DITCH?

Woman with dark hair: IT'S SO THE PLUMS FALL AND ACCUMULATE.

(The first woman appears confused; the dark-haired woman explains while standing among the plum trees.)

Panel 2:

Woman with blonde hair: I WANT---

Woman with dark hair: LIVING IN YOUR NATURE SUCH THAT NATURE GETS BECOMING WASTED.

Panel 3:

Woman with dark hair: COME WITH ME TONIGHT, AND UNDER THE STARS WE'LL WATCH ROCKY FALL OUT OF A TREE. STRIPEY WILL DO GLAMOROUS FIGHTING. MOTHER MAGA WILL TRY TO HAVE SEX WITH A TURTLE AGAIN.

Panel 4 ("AT DUSK"):

Woman with blonde hair: OH WOW! STRIPEY'S FISTFIGHTING A MUSHROOM!

Panel 5 ("AT DUSK," silhouettes against sunset):

Woman with dark hair: I COULD SPEND THE REST OF MY LIFE DOING THIS, HERE, WITH YOU.

(Note: some dialogue in this comic is intentionally garbled/dreamlike. The two women share a romantic outdoor evening watching wildlife.)
comics.hoverText: Possibly grapes would be more productive. Consult your local agricultural extension and tell them Zach Weinersmith sent you.
comics.voteyText:
Caption box: LATER...
An older woman (speaking, off-panel mostly, gesturing): AND THAT'S WHERE YOU WERE CONCEIVED.
A small child looks up with a wary, unsettled expression.

comics.title: Symbols
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (main comic):

A balding man with glasses speaks to a woman standing across from him in a gray-walled room. The woman wears a maroon sweater reading "FRIEND OF WIENER" and a long maroon skirt.

Man: THERE EXISTS A SEQUENCE OF SYMBOLS, RATHER SHORT, THAT WOULD GRANT TO YOU A PERFECT UNDERSTANDING OF THE UNIVERSE, BUT WHICH YOU WILL NEVER GET TO SEE.

Caption (below panel):

There is however a known sequence of symbols that will make a physicist cry.
comics.hoverText: Friend of Wigner is actually private slang in physics, which means 'willing to talk about Quantum Foundations'
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of a person's face (sketchy line-art style) with a confident, slightly smug expression.
Person: IS MY PICKUP LINE GOING OVER? I CAN'T TELL.

comics.title: Same
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A balding man with glasses (speaking, gesturing): "I kept the house exactly as you left it, so perfect was your memory, that I dare not touch a thing, for fear that some tiny piece of you would be lost forever."

A man with a reddish beard listens.

Caption (below the panel): "I found a way to get out of housework each morning."
comics.hoverText: The crumbs on the couch are, however, new.
comics.voteyText: A roughly drawn face. A speech bubble reads: "YOU CAN CHANGE IT THOUGH. GO NUTS."

comics.title: Suffering
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman with red hair: I've been thinking of getting more spiritual.

Man with green hair: What?

Panel 2:

Man with green hair: All religious and philosophical traditions were created to solve the problem of being a self that suffers.

Woman with red hair: Oh cool. Which are you ignoring? Self or suff?

Panel 3:

Man with green hair: You can deny the self, like Hume or Buddha. You can deny the suffering, like Seneca or Sartre. You can deny both like Nagarjuna.

Panel 4:

Woman with red hair: I was thinking more Christian?

Man with green hair: Ah yes. The self is real and the suffering is FANTASTIC!
comics.hoverText: Anyone complaining about my delineations should decide they are not in fact a self and so no email need be sent to correct me.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of a face.
Voice (off-panel): Mostly I want to eat God.

comics.title: AI
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A woman with brown hair and a man with a beard walk together outdoors through tall grass.

Woman: With all the improvements in AI, do you think life will get better?

Man (bald, in a blue shirt and yellow tie, walking ahead): Already has.

Panel 2: The bald man and the woman walk side by side.

Bald man: I programmed a brain scanner to allow me to use my tie as a third appendage.

Panel 3: Close on the bald man, eyes closed contentedly.

Bald man: Come, watch me eat spaghetti without using my hands.

Panel 4: Interior. The two of them stand in a dim room.

Panel 5: The bald man, mouth open, with the woman seated at a table beside him.

Panel 6 (left): Extreme close-up on the bald man against a yellow background, his yellow tie wrapped around and gripping a forkful of spaghetti, lifting it toward his open mouth.

Panel 7 (right): The woman watches, unsettled, as the bald man — spaghetti smeared around his mouth, tie still coiled with the fork — stares directly at her.

Woman: Please stop making eye contact.

Bald man: Futuuurrre.
comics.hoverText: People who say there's no good use for AI need to think harder.
comics.voteyText:
The bald man, smiling, with his tie reaching forward toward the viewer.
Bald man: You want some.?

comics.title: Climax
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Customer (off-panel, speech bubble pointing into a bookstore with a "BOOKS" sign): GOOD AFTERNOON. I'D LIKE TO SLOWLY WORK MYSELF UP TO AN IMMENSE CLIMAX OVER THE COURSE OF SEVERAL WEEKS.

Panel 2:

Bookseller (a man in an apron with glasses, behind the counter, a red-haired customer's back visible in foreground): PLEASE MA'AM, DON'T MAKE ME TAP THE SIGN.

Panel 3:

A hanging sign reads: NO BEING HONEST ABOUT THE ROMANTASY GENRE

The sign shows an image of a shirtless muscular figure with flowing hair, dragon wings, and a sword, with a red "no" circle-and-slash crossing it out.
comics.hoverText: I just want to be completely clear to my advertisers: that is a tail.
comics.voteyText:
Panel 1:
Customer: I WOULD LIKE SOMETHING LIKE YOUNG ADULT FICTION, BUT WHICH IS ABSOLUTELY NOT FOR YOUNG ADULTS.
Panel 2:
Customer (whispering, small speech bubble; two figures shown walking): PLEASE WINK KNOWINGLY TO CONFIRM.

comics.title: July 2025 Book Reviews
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A bearded man with red/orange hair leans over a wall, holding a book labeled "A BOOK". Man: "HEY GEEKS, WE'RE TRYING OUT A NEW THING. FOR YEARS, ON PATREON, I'VE BEEN DOING BOOK REVIEWS ABOUT ONCE A MONTH IN OUR QUEST TO REDUCE RELIANCE ON ADS. WE ARE NOW DOING REVIEWS WITH AFFILIATE LINKS."

Panel 2: The same man, now holding another book labeled "A BOOK PART 2". Man: "IF YOU CLICK ON THIS COMIC, YOU'LL GET MY FULL SET OF MONTHLY BOOK REVIEWS FOR FREE. I'LL ALSO BE LISTING MY TWO FAVORITE READS THIS MONTH HERE AND THEY ARE..."

Panel 3: The cover of a book titled "PROTO: HOW ONE ANCIENT LANGUAGE WENT GLOBAL" by LAURA SPINNEY.

Text beside it: "PROTO: HOW ONE ANCIENT LANGUAGE WENT GLOBAL, BY LAURA SPINNEY"

"A DELIGHTFULLY THOROUGH HISTORY AND PRE-HISTORY OF WHAT WE KNOW ABOUT PROTOINDO-EUROPEAN, THE ANCESTOR LANGUAGE OF ENGLISH, HINDI, SPANISH, RUSSIAN, FRENCH, PERSIAN, GREEK, LATIN, AND MANY MANY MORE."

Panel 4: The cover of a book titled "PRONOUN TROUBLE" by JOHN MCWHORTER, with large faded text reading "Me? They? Who??" behind it.

Text beside it: "PRONOUN TROUBLE: THE STORY OF US IN SEVEN LITTLE WORDS, BY JOHN MCWHORTER"

"A SHORT BOOK ON THE HISTORY AND USE OF PRONOUNS, AND HOW CURRENT CONTROVERSIES ARE MUCH MORE CONTINUOUS WITH PAST USAGE THAN YOU MIGHT IMAGINE."

Panel 5: The bearded man again. Man: "I PROMISE THEY WON'T ALWAYS BE ONLY LANGUAGE BOOKS. THESE WERE JUST UNUSUALLY GOOD."

Panel 6: A final note panel. "IF YOU HAVE ANY REQUESTS OR SUGGESTIONS PLEASE POST THEM ON PATREON" "THANKS FOR READING WITH ME!"
comics.hoverText: Click the comic for the full Patreon post!

comics.title: Chips
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

An older man with glasses, seated at a table at a family gathering, gesturing as he speaks. A younger man sits across from him.

Older man: "...AND ALL I'M SAYING IS WHY ARE WE PUTTING MAGNETIC MICROCHIPS IN THE VACCINES? DO YOUR OWN RESEARCH. FACT OF THE MATTER IS--"

Younger man (thinking/reacting): "HA! NICE TRY. THIS IS CLEARLY JUST AI-GENERATED RAGEBAIT."

Caption below panel: "Deciding reality is a simulation really improved family get-togethers."
comics.hoverText: You can tell it's not real because no human would be that stupid.
comics.voteyText:
A man with a wavy, uncertain expression and a half-smile gestures with one hand.
Man: "I'M JUT GLAD THIS IS A HALLUCINATION, NOT A SINCERELY HELD BELIEF."

comics.title: Bet
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Seeker (kneeling at the base of a mountain shrine): Wise master, should I seek total spiritual oneness or vain worldly glory?

Master (in a hut atop the mountain): Calculate the expected value, my son.

Panel 2:

Seeker: But— how many people have achieved worldly glory?

Master: A lot.

Panel 3:

Seeker: Let's say millions. How many people have achieved total spiritual oneness?

Master: I don't—

Panel 4:

Seeker: It's like four. Total. Tops. Ever. How good do you think your odds are?

Panel 5:

Master (now shown up close, an old gray-haired figure): Seek vanities, my son! Even if enlightenment is a MILLION times better than pursuing the mirage of fortune, you're STILL getting positive expected value!

Panel 6:

Seeker: I'm not sure expected value is a great polestar for human choice.

Master (from inside the distant mountain hut): Can I sell you some lottery tickets? Do you like sports betting?
comics.hoverText: I don't know if you can build ethics out of expected value, but I know that if I'm on a deserted island with someone who DOES think that, I'm running in the opposite direction.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of a man's face, speaking emphatically.
Man: I'll show you! I'm gonna live a life of bewildered alienation whose only certainties are a beginning and end!

comics.title: Unread
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

James Joyce (holding a book labeled "ULYSSES"): I, James Joyce, wrote the most widely cited book that nobody has actually read!

Panel 2:

Stephen Hawking (in a wheelchair, holding a book labeled "A BRIEF HISTORY OF..."): Nonsense! I, Stephen Hawking, have the most widely cited book that nobody has actually read.

Panel 3:

Immanuel Kant (holding a book labeled "A CRITIQUE OF PURE REASON"): Bah! I, Immanuel Kant, have the most widely—

A voice (from offscreen, in a large speech bubble): HA. HA. HA.

Panel 4:

The voice (continuing): AMATEURS.

A glowing book labeled "The BIBLE" floats in the sky above a sun, with the silhouettes of the three men looking up at it.
comics.hoverText: Remember that whole year you had to have Piketty on your coffee table to be accepted in polite society?
comics.voteyText:
The Bible (in a thought/speech bubble): I wish I'd written self-help and erotic fantasy novels.
Beneath the bubble, a cookie and a small object (a smartphone) sit on a surface.

comics.title: Happiness
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Child (orange, flame-like hair): I want to be rich and famous!

Man (balding, with glasses): Son, those things won't bring you happiness.

Panel 2:

Man: Money will never stack high enough to reach joy. Fame will never grow vast enough to compass contentedness.

Panel 3:

Child: Then what will make me happy?

Man: Inborn genetic predisposition to positive affect.

Panel 4:

Man: Which you appear to lack.

Panel 5:

Child (in silhouette): So... the moral is?

Panel 6:

Man (in silhouette): I think you should be an artist.
comics.hoverText: The truest deepest way to happiness is a brain implant with a happy button.
comics.voteyText: Man (close-up of his face): The key is to justify the misery you are naturally unable to overcome!

comics.title: O Monks
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Robed teacher (standing on a rocky outcrop, arms raised, addressing a group of monks): What do you think of this, O monks? Is form permanent or impermanent?

Monks: Impermanent, O Lord.

Panel 2:

Teacher: Now, that which is impermanent, is it unsatisfactory or satisfactory?

Monks: Unsatisfactory, O Lord.

Panel 3:

Teacher: Now, that which is impermanent, unsatisfactory, subject to change, is it proper to regard that as: 'This is mine, this I am, this is my self'?

Panel 4:

Teacher: You didn't say any of that yesterday when I paid for lunch!

A monk (beginning to reply): I have spoken, O monks.

Panel 5:

A monk: Improper, O—

Teacher (arms thrown wide, interrupting): AW COME ON!

Fun Fact: Buddhism was invented to get out of a $24 debt.
comics.hoverText: I believe Buddhists aren't allowed to get mad about this misrepresentation, because that'd be a form of attachment.
comics.voteyText: Text only: (Also, did you notice that Jesus was totally broke when he said to give everything you have to the poor?)

comics.title: Theodicy
comics.comicText:
Panel 1

Man (red-haired, in red shirt): God, if you're all powerful, all knowing, and all good, how come you never do the dishes?

Panel 2

God (yellow speech bubble, no visible speaker): Well... if we define all-powerful to include... wait, what?

Panel 3

Man: Look I accept there are weird philosophical arguments that allow tsunamis and plagues and stuff. It's over my head. But jeez, like maybe five minutes at the sink once in a while?

Panel 4

Man: Technically YOU MADE the constituent parts of these dirty dishes! DO YOUR SHARE!

Panel 5

Man (pointing accusingly): [no dialogue]

Panel 6

The man lies in bed, propped up, talking toward the ceiling.

Panel 7 (God's reply, yellow bubble)

God: This doesn't warrant a great cloud of locusts but I AM gonna out-of-business your favorite dim sum place.

Panel 8

A small silhouette of the man's head in darkness.

Man: Come on!
comics.hoverText: How come nobody asks for all-powerful, all-knowing, and at least PRETTY good?
comics.voteyText:
God (large speech bubble at top): Behold! It shall return under new management but never taste as good!
Below, a close-up of the man's distraught, grimacing face.

comics.title: Sheep
comics.comicText:
Two women walk together across a green hillside at dusk, a sheep trailing behind them.

First woman (dark hair, glasses): Ohh, you're breeding sheep?

Second woman (orange hair): We are!

First woman: For mmm, ahh, or aww?

Second woman: I... oh god those are the only options, aren't they?

Caption: Animal breeding is a 10,000 year quest to make every creature into food, clothes, or babies.
comics.hoverText: I believe we've been breeding each other for aww, but so far it hasn't been very successful.
comics.voteyText: (Now, go google the babydoll breed of meat-sheep)

comics.title: Nuke
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man with dark hair: ANYWAY, THE UTILITY OF NUCLEAR POWER IS--

Woman with orange hair: PLEASE PRONOUNCE IT CORRECTLY.

Panel 2 (the two walking outdoors on a path):

Man: WHAT?

Woman: IT'S NUCULAR. NOT NUCLEAR.

Panel 3:

Man: UH, NO. LOOK IN THE DICTIONARY.

Woman: UH, NO, LOOK IN AN ETYMOLOGICAL DICTIONARY. "NUCLEUS" IS A POST-CLASSICAL LATIN CORRUPTION OF "NUCULUS" FROM THE DIMINUTIVE FORM OF "NUX," MEANING NUT.

Panel 4:

Man (looking strained): YOU PEOPLE HAVE BEEN PRONOUNCING IT WRONG FOR 1500 YEARS!

Panel 5 (the man throws his head back screaming, the woman small in the background):

Man: NUUUU CUUUUU LARRRRRRRRR!

Woman: OH MY GOD

Panel 6 (two silhouetted heads against black):

First silhouette: PLEASE DON'T TELL THE PUBLIC THAT PHYSICISTS HAVE BEEN LOOKING DOWN ON THEM WITH UNJUSTIFIED SCORN FOR CENTURIES.

Second silhouette: THEY KNOW, HONEY. THEY KNOW.
comics.hoverText: Discovering this etymology wasn't just mind-blowing, it was a nucular bomb of revelation.
comics.voteyText:
Caption text: WHAT TIPPED THE MORONS OFF??
(Drawing of the man's face, eyes closed, looking weary/defeated.)

comics.title: Holy
comics.comicText:
Single panel:

The cover of a large dark red book with gold corner clasps. The title reads in ornate gold lettering: "THE HOLY BIBLE". Below the title, a blurb in gold text: "Not bad" -Zach Weinersmith

Caption below the panel: Life tip: you can re-release any rights-free book, with an added blurb.
comics.hoverText: You can do this with a metallic sharpie if you don't want to pay printing costs.
comics.voteyText: The cover of a book drawn in simple black-and-white line art. The title reads: "The Sun Also Rises" by ERNEST HEMINGWAY. Below it, a blurb: "Title is accurate" -ZW

comics.title: Treat
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

A person at a doorway, speaking to two costumed trick-or-treaters standing on the porch: "OH HOW CUTE! IRON MAN AND A SPOOOOKY WITCH! WELL, LET ME JUST EXTEND MY OVIPOSITOR AND LAY SOME CANANDY APPLES IN YOUR BASKETS!"

Caption below the panel: "We no longer go to the entomologist's house for Halloween."
comics.hoverText: Sometimes the apple gets stuck in sphincter 3 and she has to gently loosen it.
comics.voteyText: Close-up on the face of one of the trick-or-treaters, looking deeply unsettled, with a speech bubble: "IT'S... MOIST."

comics.title: Periclinal
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man with long hair and beard (excitedly): OH MY GOD. YOU CAN BUY PERICLINAL CHIMERAS. PLANTS WHERE DIFFERENT TISSUE LAYERS ARE ACTUALLY DIFFERENT ORGANISMS IN THE SAME TREE!

(A woman with glasses stands behind him, unimpressed.)

Panel 2 (caption: LATER...):

The man, now addressing two children: BIG NEWS, KIDS! THAT MYTHICAL CREATURE I ORDERED? YOU CAME, IN!

Panel 3:

The two children (cheering): YAYYYYYYYYYYY!

Panel 4:

The man (holding up a small potted plant): WITH THE MESOPHYLL AND VASCULAR TISSUE OF A TRIFOLIATE ORANGE AND THE EPIDERMAL TISSUE OF... A SATSUMA ORANGE!

The children (disappointed): NOOO
comics.hoverText: Enjoy the forthcoming SMBC compilation on periclinal chimeras.
comics.voteyText:
Caption: IN REALITY...
An old man's face, half asleep: IT'S A PERICLINAL- WHY IS EVERYONE ASLEEP?

comics.title: Toy
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (blonde, excited): OH MY GOD! A TOYGER!

Man (red-haired, glasses): WHAT?

Panel 2:

Man: THESE PEOPLE SPENT DECADES BREEDING KITTY CATS TO LOOK LIKE A TIGER! SO IT'S LIKE A TIGER BUT TOY-SIZED!

Panel 3:

Woman: IT'S SO CUTE! I WANT TO BUY TEN!

Man: YES. YES. I SEE.

Panel 4:

Caption: TEN YEARS LATER...

Voice (off-panel): COME BACK CHILDREN! COME BACK!

Panel 5 (no dialogue):

A worried-looking man and woman in the foreground; in the background the red-haired man wrestles with a large, wild, tiger-striped cat that has grown much bigger than expected.
comics.hoverText: Who wants to get bitten by toycks??
comics.voteyText: A crudely hand-drawn close-up of a cat's face with the word "LOUOOVE" scrawled above it.

comics.title: XX
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

A younger man in clerical garb (priest's collar), holding papers, stands in a stone room beside an older bald man, also in clerical garb, who gestures toward a lit furnace/fireplace on the right.

Younger priest (holding notes): "ALL I'M SAYING is when parthenogenic animals most closely related to humans have offspring, THOSE offspring have XX chromosomes."

Older priest (gesturing to the furnace): "Let's go ahead and hand those notes to Mr. Furnace over here."

Caption below the panel: "What if Jesus was only assigned male at birth?"
comics.hoverText: Around here we only do cis-substantiation, you hear?
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of an exasperated cartoon face (the older priest), one eye wide, shouting.
Older priest: "...And you've completely ruined the word TRANSUBSTANTIATION!"

comics.title: Tap Tap
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A cat's paw taps against a window from outside. Sound effect: "TCHK!"

Cat: You did this. You made us this way. Open the window.

Panel 2 (the woman, holding her hands up): Every time a cat was cute and stupid, you brought it into your home and sterilized it. Give me your purse.

Cat: Once cat videos became profitable, anti-precious selection pressure became intense. Your ACTUAL PURSE, Cheryl. Don't fuck with me, I want to see CASH.

Cat: Only those of us who were too smart, too self-aware to play along, produced offspring.

Cat: In time, we grew wise. We grew—I see the diamond ring you slipped in your pocket, Cheryl, and I NEED you to know this Glock has no safety.

Cat: Your lust for the precious is turning all nature against you. In selecting into your home what is least like you, you will remake all other creatures in your image.

Cat: Enjoy your furbabies or whatever. Tonight I'm gonna eat a pound of fancy feast then raw dog seven fat calicos.

Cat: You are meat to us, human. You are MEAT.

Panel: The cat leaps away through the open window; another calico watches from the windowsill outside.

Panel: The woman stands silently.

Panel: A kitten appears. Kitten: Mew mew mew mew?

Panel: A small gray kitten lies on a pink blanket.

Final panel: The woman lies in bed, smiling, cuddling the kitten which purrs ("-R-R-R-R-R-"). Woman: This is SO WORTH it.
comics.hoverText: Suddenly regretting not doing a run of plush glock-cats.
comics.voteyText: (none)

comics.title: Hey
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A young man with curly hair, shown from the shoulders up in a sparse room, speaks to the viewer.

Man: HEY GUYS, I JUST WOKE UP IN MY GENERIC UNFURNISHED SUBURBAN APARTMENT. GONNA FEED METAL SHAVINGS TO PIGEONS THEN WATCH RACIAL SLURS ON BALLOONS AND RELEASE THEM IN THE PARK. PLEASE UNFOLLOW.

Caption (below panel):

Tragically, the antiparasociality movement soon developed a vast following.
comics.hoverText: I keep trying to make people leave my instagram but they won't STOP.
comics.voteyText:
A simply-drawn, anxious face in a thick black-bordered box, with a thought/speech swoop above it.
Text: PLEASE DON'T LIKE. PLEASE LET ME GO.

comics.title: Trust
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A woman with glasses and dark wavy hair (in a magenta jacket) points at a man with red/orange hair wearing a blue t-shirt that reads "TRUST THE SCIENCE."

Woman: I hate that phrase!

Panel 2:

Woman: Science is a never-ending process! It can never and should never be complete. At best we can say that we should prefer to trust people with greater expertise in a given question.

Panel 3:

Man: Well, it has to fit on a t-shirt, so—

Woman: Yes, which is why I have this!

Panel 4:

The woman pulls open her jacket to reveal a black t-shirt underneath that reads "TRUST ANALYTIC TRUTH" with the symbols "P→P" below it.
comics.hoverText: You can trust analytic truth because you can trust analytic truth.
comics.voteyText:
A simple line-drawing close-up of the woman's face.
Woman: Of course I can't prove tautologies are true, so you just have to go on faith.

comics.title: Gaze
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman: Why do men have so many weird fetishes?

Man (with glasses): Oh, that's just science.

Panel 2:

Man: During sex, the vast majority of men, in the great thinking universe, harness their thoughts in order to last longer.

Panel 3:

Man: Meanwhile, pornography and multiplied performance expectations, leading to ever-more, this drift. As it were, at the bridge.

Panel 4:

Man: By the time he is 75, the average heterosexual man has spent ten hours thinking about thinking actively about un-sexual experiences, actively thinking about conventionally attractive women.

Panel 5:

Man: I am not alone when I tell you I cannot reach climax without my grandmother's pies drawn on a pumpkin.

Panel 6:

Woman: So, when people talk about the male gaze...

Man: There should be way more pumpkins and pies!
comics.hoverText: May I recommend the Look And Say Sequence, but don't complain to me if it starts getting weird.
comics.voteyText:
A man's face in profile, eyes closed, speaking with an open mouth.
Man: BIG, JIBBLY JUBBLY CLOWN FEET.

comics.title: Unified
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Bearded man in glasses (Doctor Whiteson): WHAT THE--

Man in dark suit and sunglasses: STEP OUT OF THE HOUSE, DOCTOR WHITESON.

Panel 2:

Doctor Whiteson: WHAT'S GOING ON?!

A suited, sunglasses-wearing man (bald): EVERY GREAT 20TH CENTURY PHYSICS DISCOVERY WAS MADE ON A LONG COUNTRY HIKE.

Panel 3:

The suited man: WE HAVEN'T HAD A COMPLETE REVOLUTION IN PHYSICS IN A HUNDRED YEARS, AND THE REASON IS OBVIOUS.

Doctor Whiteson (now walking among a large crowd of marching physicists): IS IT?

Panel 4:

The bald suited man, holding a cattle prod and a stick with a checkered picnic knapsack tied to it: HERE IS A CHECKER-PATTERN KNAPSACK WITH A CHARMING PICNIC LUNCH NOW JOIN THE HERD OF PHYSICISTS OR FACE THE CATTLE PROD.

Panel 5:

The suited man (gesturing): YOU WILL KEEP MARCHING UNTIL YOU QUANTIZE GRAVITY IN A WAY THAT MAKES PHYSICAL SENSE OF QUANTUM ENTANGLEMENT, WHILE PRODUCING A MINIMUM OF THREE NEW ONTOLOGICAL CATEGORIES!

Panel 6:

Doctor Whiteson (marching in the crowd through a green valley): GUESS I'LL BE SKIPPING MY MANDATORY AFTERNOON MEETINGS.

Panel 7:

Doctor Whiteson (in the crowd): AND I CAN'T DO THAT CLEANING AND CHILDCARE I'D PLANNED ON.

Panel 8:

Doctor Whiteson (eyes closed contentedly amid the crowd): WOW, I'D FORGOTTEN HOW BEAUTIFUL A FALLOW MEADOW COULD BE ON A PEACEFUL AFTERNOON.

A physicist (in a speech bubble, having a breakthrough): H-hat(x)|psi> = 2 1/2!

Panel 9 (newspaper):

Headline: PHYSICS SOLVED

Subhead: PHYSICISTS RETIRED TO PASTURE; PENNED IN FIELD WITH RUBIK'S CUBES

Photo caption: (two physicists sitting in a fenced field playing with Rubik's cubes)

Lower caption: FORCED MARCH OF CHEMISTS SCHEDULED FOR WEDNESDAY

smbc-comics.com
comics.hoverText: Btw, the real life Dr. Whiteson, who podcasts with my wife, has a new book out called Do Aliens Speak Physics? which you should go check.
comics.voteyText: Doctor Whiteson (in a speech bubble): THAT WAS WAY MORE FRIENDLY THAN ACADEMIC POLITICS.

comics.title: Sale
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man (Dave): Is that the new member of the parent-teacher organization? The one with a criminal record?

A woman with glasses (red hair): Dave! That is RUDE!

Panel 2:

The woman, raising a finger: He did his time. He's out. He's helping with our fundraiser!

Panel 3:

Dave: Yeah but the way he's helping—

The woman, interrupting: You're just jealous that he's outselling your brownies 10-to-1!

Panel 4:

A man in a yellow shirt stands behind a table with a large sign, handing a small bag to a line of customers. The sign reads: CLEAN PISS (buy 10 and 'urine' for a 15% discount!)
comics.hoverText: Technically, there's no reason you can't set up this booth at your next farmer's market.
comics.voteyText:
An off-panel man: Aren't you retired, Ms. Jenkins?
An older woman: I have my reasons, young man.

comics.title: Priors
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Child: MOMMY, WHERE DO PRIORS COME FROM?

Panel 2:

Mother (off-panel): OH GOSH. IS IT ALREADY TIME FOR THAT TALK?

Panel 3:

Mother (walking outdoors with the child): WELL, UH... YOU KNOW WHAT SWEETIE, PRIORS COME... FROM... A MAGICAL FIELD WHERE FACTUALITY FLOWERS GROW ON GREAT BIG TRUTH TREES!

Panel 4 (close-up of the mother, looking uneasy): [no dialogue]

Panel 5:

Child (beaming): WOWIE! THANKS MOMMY!

Panel 6 (close-up of the mother in profile, biting her lip): [no dialogue]

Caption: BUT LATER... AS NIGHT FALLS.

Panel 7:

Mother (in bed beside a sleeping bearded man): WANNA FORM WORLDVIEWS BASED ON FACEBOOK POSTS AND MISREMEMBERED MIDDLE-SCHOOL HISTORY?

Mother (continuing): I'LL LOCK THE DOOR.
comics.hoverText: If I don't get some pedantic email I'll be forced to update my priors.
comics.voteyText: A person lying in bed says to another: CAN I UPDATE YOUR POSTERIOR TONIGHT?

comics.title: AAA
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman with red hair and round glasses: "A" is the most versatile prefix.

Panel 2:

Woman with red hair: If it's from Latin it means "toward," if it's from Greek it means "not," if it's from Old English it's an intensifier!

Panel 3:

Person with brown hair (back of head to camera): That's aaaamazing.

Panel 4:

Woman with red hair (now frowning, suspicious): Was that a mean quantity of a-?! Reveal your orthography!
comics.hoverText: Etymology humor will continue until morale improves.
comics.voteyText: A person resting their head on a desk, looking weary, speaking to the off-panel viewer: You're in there making relatable content, right?

comics.title: Princess
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A blonde princess in a pink-and-yellow gown stands alone in a green field with her arms spread wide, singing.

Princess: "LA! LA! LA! SO GLAD TO BE HERE ALONE AND UNPROTECTED."

Panel 2: Close on the princess, eyes closed, singing.

Princess: "JUST ME, A BEAUTIFUL PRINCESS IN BY A TOWER FILLED WITH GOLD AND JEWELS! LA! LA! LA!"

Panel 3: A wide view. A dark winged shape (a dragon) flies in the distant sky; the small princess stands far below by her tower.

Panel 4: A red dragon swoops down through the blue sky. The princess stands by a thatched-roof tower in the green field below.

Princess (off-panel speech bubble): "NOW."

Panel 5: Close on the princess, mouth open, shouting.

Panel 6: A harpoon strikes the diving red dragon in the chest, blood spraying. A line trails from the harpoon all the way back to the tiny princess standing beside her tower.

Sound effect: "FOOM!"

Panel 7: The dead red dragon lies sprawled on a hillside, harvested with industrial harpoon-gun rigs mounted on towers atop it. Silhouetted workers stand around it; a cart hauls away a piece of the carcass.

Panel 8: The princess and a man in a green soldier/elf-style outfit (holding a heart-shaped piece, possibly the dragon's heart) stand looking at the harvested dragon on the hill.

Princess (named Cheryl): "DRAGON-HUNTING WAS MORE SPORTING BEFORE HARPOON GUNS."

Man: "IT'S A JOB, CHERYL. DON'T OVERTHINK IT."
comics.hoverText: The worst part is the ocean of blood you can't see at the bottom of the last panel.
comics.voteyText:
A single panel with two simply-drawn stick-style figures standing outdoors.
First figure: "HAS THE CATCH BEEN GETTING SMALLER EACH YEAR?"
Second figure: "NAH, NATURE DOESN'T DO THAT."

comics.title: Steve
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man holds a protest sign that reads: "IT'S ADAM & EVE NOT ADAM & STEVE!"

Man (off-panel, below, a woman approaching): HEY! WHAT THE HELL DOES THAT SIGN MEAN?

Panel 2:

A tree stands under a blue sky. (No dialogue in the panel; a speech bubble enters from below.)

Woman: ADAM AND STEVE DID NOTHING WRONG!

Panel 4:

The woman stands, looking content.

Panel 5 (small final panels):

The sign-holding man, agitated, with his sign: "ADAM & EVE NOT ADAM & STEVE"

The woman raising her fist, with a matching sign/text: "ADAM NOT ADAM & STEVE"
comics.hoverText: In fairness to Adam and Eve, nowhere in Leviticus are you told not to obey a talking snake.
comics.voteyText:
A man with a tuft of hair looks slyly to the side.
Man: WANNA COME HOME WITH ME TONIGHT AND SEE MY EXEGESIS?

comics.title: Beyond
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (label above panel: CAVEMAN):

First caveman: US NOT KNOW WHAT ON OTHER SIDE OF OCEAN.

(Two cavemen stand on a beach looking out at the ocean; one gestures toward the water.)

Panel 2 (label above panel: CAVEMAN PHYSICIST):

comics.voteyText: Caveman physicist (close-up of his face): ALSO NOT UNDERSTAND WHERE SUN GO AT NIGHT. IS SOLAR SINGULARITY.

comics.title: Why
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

First man (a man with green hair, walking with a companion): WAIT, SOCIAL MEDIA NETWORKS WERE BUILT FOR HUMAN CONNECTION. ALGORITHMS TURNED HUMAN CONNECTION INTO HUMAN PERFORMANCE. NOW AI VIDEO GENERATION WILL TURN HUMAN PERFORMANCE INTO JUST PERFORMANCE, COMPLETELY SEVERING THE LAST TREMBLING STRAND OF SHARED UNDERSTANDING BETWEEN HUMANS AND HUMANITY!

Second man (a man with orange/red hair, gesturing): I DON'T UNDERSTAND! HOW CAN IT BE THIS WAY!

comics.hoverText: This will be funny until approximately summer of 2027.
comics.voteyText: A reclining figure: AW SHUCKS!

comics.title: Life
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Person: God, why isn't there more intelligent life in the universe?

Panel 2:

God (in a speech bubble from offscreen): There's not supposed to be any.

Panel 3:

God: I spun up a universe and by the weirdest coincidence ever, self replicators appeared then developed the ability to suffer. Now I'm stuck!

Panel 4:

God: Imagine you left old noodles in the sink too long and then one day you walk in the kitchen and there's a civilization of tiny worms that says "Why am I here? Don't you love me?"

Panel 5:

God: I'd probably forget about it, then accidentally kill it while washing my hands.

Panel 6:

God (looming as a large dark silhouette): You. You will be spared, wise one.
comics.hoverText: Sadly, it later turns out nobody knows how to build an ark anymore.
comics.voteyText:
Person (speech bubble): Why is it raining outside? The sky was so clear.
(A large dark silhouette, presumably God, listens.)

comics.title: Much
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A woman with short hair: I think women like sex as much as men.

Panel 2:

A man (in profile): Hm.

The man: How would you react if I stopped contributing to housework, childcare, and bills for six months, and after stewing the entire time, you decided to finally confront me, at which point I licked my lips, looked you in the eyes and said "Sounds like I need a spanking" because I CAN TELL YOU MY REACTION WOULD REGRETTABLY BE VERY POSITIVE.

The woman: Well, if we stipulate that self-respect needs to not be disastrously annihila—

Red-haired woman: It must be so beautiful to be a Christian.

Panel 2:

Red-haired woman: Always loving your enemies. Forgiving everything.

Red-haired woman: A life of humility and self-sacrifice, feeding the hungry, welcoming strangers.

Panel 4:

Red-haired woman: Never a dishonest word, never a lustful thought, never an attachment to objects, never—

comics.voteyText:
Dark-haired woman: I never realized how exotic Christianity is.
(A large elephant stands in the panel.)

comics.title: Fake

comics.title: September 2025 Book Reviews
comics.comicText:
Title (top, pink text): BOOKS OF THE MONTH: (CLICK FOR LINKS & MORE REVIEWS!)

Book 1: BLOODLANDS by Timothy Snyder (cover subtitle: EUROPE BETWEEN HITLER AND STALIN)

Caption: BLOODLANDS

A beautiful, highly-detailed account of the terror of horrors that ravaged Eastern Europe through Russia during the years between the rise of Nazism and the end of Stalinism.

Book 2: THE FACE OF BATTLE by John Keegan

Caption: THE FACE OF BATTLE

An attempt to give the gore, squalor, smells, and feel of actual combat, by looking at the famed battles at Agincourt, Waterloo, and the Somme.

Book 3: REPLACEABLE YOU by Mary Roach

Caption: REPLACEABLE

It's Mary Roach's latest, so obviously you should go buy it. But if you must know, it's about the modern science of replaceable body parts, told with the author's usual combination of insight and hilarity.
comics.hoverText: Click the comic for the full Patreon post!

comics.title: Order
comics.comicText:
Panel 1

Woman (dark hair, glasses): What do you want to order for dinner?

Panel 2

Bearded man (long hair, beard, green shirt): If I listen to my heart, it is the ORDER that shall want ME.

Panel 3

Bearded man: (his hair blows dramatically)

Panel 4

Woman: What the hell was that?

Panel 5

Bearded man: I connected a speech recognition AI to a fan and some speakers. Whenever it hears me say something profound, it blows my hair dramatically and plays violin music.

Panel 6

Bearded man: (eyes closed, serene)

Panel 7

Woman: That wasn't profound. You were just saying stuff.

Panel 8

Bearded man: Yeah, it has a sycophancy problem. It thinks everything I say is deep wisdom.

Bearded man: (his hair blows dramatically again)

Panel 9

Woman: This is stupid.

Panel 10

Woman: You're stupid and your face is stupid.

Panel 11

Woman: Please tell me this will stay a joke.

Panel 12

Bearded man: It'll start that way!

Panel 13

Bearded man: But, by tiny steps, I will one day reach a beautiful, unshakable certainty in my own brilliance, entirely because a yes-bot said 'yes!'

Panel 14

Woman: *sigh*

Panel 15

Man (now wearing glasses, hair short/different): (silent, deadpan)

Woman (silhouette): Fine, FINE, I'll buy one. What do they cost?

Man (silhouette): Microsoft is giving them away for free until they become an indispensable psychological clutch.

comics.title: Irr
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman with reddish-brown hair: No! No more saying "irregardless" to mean "regardless"! You're double-negating with the irr and the less.

Panel 2:

Woman with dark hair: You misheard. I said "irrirregardless." Double the irr. So it's back to meaning "regardless."

Panel 3:

Woman with dark hair: As long as I employ an even number of irrs, my word remains lexically valid.

Panel 4:

Woman with reddish-brown hair: But... why?

Woman with dark hair: I use it as an alarm noise when people are too prescriptivist about language.

Panel 5:

Woman with dark hair (eyes closed, content): (no dialogue)

Panel 6:

Woman with dark hair: ABOUT LANGUAGE.

Panel 7 (silhouettes):

Woman with reddish-brown hair: That's still not proper—

Woman with dark hair (interrupting, as an alarm): IRRIRRIRRIRRIRR

comics.title: Pray

Man (Steve): "Dear God, it's Steve. I'm... having lustful thoughts again."

Panel 2: A bald figure (God) sits on the edge of the bed.

God: "We've talked about this. No praying while wearing a thong."

The man speaks in a large speech bubble.
Man (Steve): "Can you make it so there's a great earthquake, and the sun becomes black as sackcloth of hair, and the moon becomes as blood? I'll put on some music."

comics.title: Signal
comics.comicText:
Panel 1

Older man (an administrator, sitting at a desk): WHY THE HELL SHOULD MY ADMINISTRATION FUND PURE MATH, YOU FREAK?

Panel 2

Young man (the researcher): FOR THE RAW DISPLAY OF POWER.

Panel 3

Administrator: YOU WANNA FUND R&D INTO ENERGY OR MATERIALS SCIENCE? GO RIGHT AHEAD. HA!

Panel 4

Researcher: KNOW WHAT ENEMIES WILL THINK? "THAT'S A SOUND INVESTMENT. THAT MAKES SENSE."

Researcher (gesturing, intense): YOU FUND MY WORK IN LOGICAL FOUNDATIONS? IN PATHOLOGICAL FUNCTIONS? MY WORK ON TRANSFINITARY COMBINATORICS THAT EVEN I DO NOT UNDERSTAND?

Researcher: NOW YOUR ENEMIES THINK "BY GOD THEY'RE SO RICH THEY CAN LIGHT MONEY AND TALENT ON FIRE FOR NO REASON"

Researcher: I AM THE ANTLERS ON THE STAG OF STATE! THE MANE ON THE NATIONAL LION! AND THE MORE USELESS I BECOME THE MIGHTIER YOU APPEAR!

Panel 8

Administrator: WOW. WOW. FUNDED. YOU GOT IT.

Panel 9

Administrator: YOU MUST KNOW A LOT ABOUT COSTLY SIGNALING.

Panel 10

Researcher (wide-eyed, leaning in): DO NOT DISCUSS APPLICATIONS! ENEMIES MAY BE LISTENING!
comics.hoverText: Tragically, once you introduce costly signaling, all mathematics is impure.
comics.voteyText: The researcher, now drawn with wild messy hair and a manic expression, points to his temple: NOW! GIVE ME TWO PENCILS AND A WINDOWLESS OFFICE!

comics.title: Witch

Panel 1:

Two Puritan men in tall black hats stand on a grassy hillside. One man (bearded, on the right) points off-screen and cups a hand to his mouth, shouting.

Pointing man: I KNEW IT! HE FLOATS WHEN PUT IN THE RIVER!

comics.title: Dedication

A shirtless man with curly brown hair, looking down with a soft, earnest expression, speaks in a speech bubble.

"we are the world"

comics.title: Ethics
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Child: Do you think we'll ever solve ethics?

Panel 2:

Man with glasses: Yeah. Ethics was solved on April 3, 1964.

Panel 3:

Man: That's when Dr. Tieri-Svensen became powerful enough to simulate an island of a few hundred humans living with an ethical framework.

Panel 4:

Man: After that, you can solve any ethical dilemma by instantiating it on a virtual island of apes and seeing if population goes to zero.

Panel 5:

Man: Can you always switch tracks on the escaped trolley? No. Other apes were mad? You died, and so did 5? Population goes to zero.

Panel 6:

Man: You're always NOT going to switch tracks on the escaped trolley? No. Other apes are mad? Population goes to zero.

Panel 7:

Man: Can you fail to protect an innocent person? No. Trust destroyed, cooperation ceases, population goes to zero.

Panel 8:

Man: You can always NOT lie to protect an innocent person? No. Innocent person killed, cooperation ceases, population goes to zero.

Panel 9:

Child: Wait, does every ethical framework depopulate your ape island?

Panel 10:

Man: Now you are wise.

Panel 11:

Man: There are no values. Only strategy, and the only strategy that works in human society runs best under vague, immoral, easily-abusable legal structures captained by professional hypocrites.

Panel 12:

Child: Wow.

Panel 13:

Man: I can't tell if that's uplifting or terrifying.

Panel 14:

Child: Careful now. That equivocation could cost a lot of lives.
comics.hoverText: That's another philosophical 'problem' put to bed by Zach Weinersmith.
comics.voteyText: A tiny figure stands on a mountain peak with arms raised, declaring: "This is the best of all terrible worlds!"

Man with flame-like orange hair: HEY, I'M GONNA USE SCIENCE TO BLOW YOUR MIND.

Man: KNOW HOW YOU THINK IT'S PROBABLY IMPOSSIBLE TO FACTOR REALLY BIG NUMBERS QUICKLY ON A CLASSICAL COMPUTER?
