comics.voteyText:
(a book cover)
A PORTRAIT OF THE ARTIST AS ONE HUNDRED YOUNG MEN

comics.title: Steinbach
comics.comicText:
Main comic:

A woman (praying) speech bubble: DEAR GOD, I WAS—

God's large speech bubble (cutting in): TO DAVE ALLEN ANDERSEN OF STEINBACH MANITOBA: YOU DON'T NEED PENIS SURGERY. WOMEN DON'T CARE IF IT LOOKS FUNNY LIKE THAT.

The woman, smaller bubble: EXCUSE ME.?

God's panicked bubble: I... BUT... OH HOLY SHIT DELETE DELETE DO NOT SEND DO NOT SEND DO NOT SEND!

Caption beneath the panel: The day God accidentally hit Reply All.
comics.hoverText: The worst part is that there's always one guy among the flock who can't stop also replying all.
comics.voteyText: A small bird (a chicken/hen seen in profile at the bottom) with a thought/speech bubble: MAN, I HATE THIS JOB.

comics.title: Dunno
comics.comicText:
Main comic (single panel):

Two small figures walk along a path through a green, hilly landscape with mountains in the background. A large speech bubble emanates from one of them.

Speaker (one of the two walkers): "I dunno. Some days, I wish my life could be an endless public performance designed to sell cosmetics and nutritional supplements."
comics.hoverText: The fantasy of reacting to reactions to cultural ephemera grows more vivid every night until he can bear it no longer.
comics.voteyText:
Panel 1: The same speaker continues, in a large speech bubble.
Speaker: "Oh! Maybe I could filter my own appearance with AI, so that even my superficiality is false, completing a monstrous symmetry in which I become both hollow and surfaceless, thus made nothing by my own strivings!"
Panel 2: Two figures shown in close-up. The other figure replies.
Other figure: "Nice!"

comics.title: Capital
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man (Dave): Anna, will you marry me?

Woman (Anna): Oh, Dave!

Panel 2:

Woman (Anna): A box containing the cash-equivalent value of an engagement ring!

Panel 3:

Man (Dave): ALMOST equivalent. The ability to choose your ring has a quantifiable value that I subtracted from the total.

Panel 4:

Woman (Anna): That is such a beautifully valid analysis!

Panel 5:

Man (Dave): You beautifully exceeded all of the 37% of people I sampled from a finite pool of candidate partners.

Panel 6:

Woman (Anna): Steve, you have signalled at sufficient cost for me to call off my sequential mate search until conditions significantly change!

Panel 7:

Man (Dave): You've made me the happiest man in some bounded region of Earth!
comics.hoverText: Later, as a matter of principle, they have a 1 to 1 sex to children ratio.
comics.voteyText: Woman (Anna): Hurry my dear, before the cash deflates!

comics.title: All
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman at a podium: PEOPLE OF EARTH, IN THREE DAYS TIME THE ALIENS WILL ARRIVE TO INTRODUCE US TO THE GALACTIC FEDERATION.

Panel 2:

Woman at podium: THEY WILL NOT FIND US AS WE WISH TO BE, BUT AS WE ARE.

Panel 3:

Woman at podium (addressing a crowd): FELLOW HUMANS, WHAT I'M SAYING IS THE TIME HAS COME TO DELETE YOUR BROWSER HISTORY. YOUR SECRET SUBSCRIPTIONS. THAT ONE FOLDER. ALL OF IT.

Panel 4:

Caption banner: SHORTLY...

(Two aliens descend in a flying saucer over a crowd of humans.)

Human (left): WHY ARE THEY FAKING HAPPINESS SO WEIRDLY?

Alien (right): HEH. THIS HAPPENS ON EVERY CONTACTED PLANET.

Footer: PATREON.COM/ZACHWEINERSMITH SMBC-COMICS.COM
comics.hoverText: We just have to get locked into the Federation and then we can run back to the basement.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of a person's face with a strained, sweating smile.
Person (thought/speech): I CAN KEEP THIS UP FOR PRECISELY 17 MORE SECONDS.

comics.title: Real
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Fairy: AND NOW, BY MY MAGIC, YOU SHALL BE... A REAL BOY!

Panel 2:

Boy: WHAT WAS I BEFORE?

Panel 3:

Fairy: YOU HAD THE OUTWARD MANNER OF A CONSCIOUS BEING, BUT NO INTERNAL CONSCIOUS EXPERIENCE.

Panel 4:

Boy: A PHILOSOPHICAL ZOMBIE

Panel 5:

Boy: THAT'S INCOHERENT. I WAS PRECISELY REPRODUCING THE STATEMENTS OF A BEING WITH RICH EXPERIENCE WITHOUT ANYTHING GOING ON INSIDE? IT DOESN'T EVEN MAKE *COMPUTATIONAL* SENSE. WHAT RESOURCES GENERATED THE APPARENTLY CONSCIOUS—HEY, WHAT ARE YOU DOING?

Panel 6:

(The fairy waves her wand, blasting magic at the boy.)

Panel 7:

(The boy stares, wide-eyed, transformed.)
comics.hoverText: Poor guy's immortal again.
comics.voteyText: Boy (thought bubble): SUCKS BEING A DETERMINISTIC STIMULUS-REPONSE MACHINE.

comics.title: Poetry
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

Narration caption (top): PEOPLE THINK THE HUMANITIES DON'T HELP WITH SCIENCE, BUT WHILE READING POETRY I FIND THE PERFECT OPENING IF YOU WANT TO HATE ON SELENOLOGISTS.

Scene: A man with red/orange hair and round glasses, wearing a red shirt, stands at the front of a dimly lit room (lecture or presentation setting) holding a remote/clicker. Behind him is a projection screen displaying text. The silhouetted heads of an audience are visible in the foreground.

Text on the projection screen:

Master of beauty, craftsman of the snowflake,

inimitable contriver,

Endower of Earth so gorgeous & different

from the boring Moon,

From Eleven Addresses to the Lord,

by John Berryman
comics.hoverText: Still better than the crap-moons of Mars.
comics.voteyText: (TECHNICALLY, SHAKESPEARE TALKED BAD ABOUT THE SUN IN A SONNET, BUT THAT WAS IN ORDER TO BACKHANDEDLY NEG A LADY HE WAS TRYING TO SLEEP WITH)

comics.title: Turkin
comics.comicText:
Caption: OUR CAMPAIGN HAD A PROBLEM.

Panel 1: Three campaign staffers at a conference table.

Staffer (in striped shirt): Guys, Thompson just made a gaffe.

Second staffer: How big of a gaffe?

Third staffer (alarmed, hands to face): Reporters found him in the woods having sex with a turkey. Again.

Thompson (offscreen / aside): Frank! Hold my calls and order pizza!

Caption: AT FIRST, WE WERE CAUTIOUSLY OPTIMISTIC.

Staffer: There's no median-voter data on turkey-fucking. Let's not panic.

Other staffer: Maybe they love it? I've never met someone without a college degree.

Caption: BUT OUR CONSTITUENTS TURNED OUT TO BE FURIOUS.

Voice: Dammit, fucking a turkey just feeds the narrative that he's a turkey-fucker! #THOMPSON2038

Caption: SURROGATES WENT TO TALKSHOWS FOR DAMAGE CONTROL.

Surrogate: Sure, Sharon, but what the working class are asking is why didn't the current administration f*** the turkey of inflation?

Caption: PODCASTS WENT BETTER.

Guest: You got people out here, who are judging this man purely based on his character, statements, and actions. I mean, grow up.

Host: Wow. That is so real, bro.

Caption: BUT THE OPPOSITION ADMITTEDLY HAD A SOLID CASE.

Opposition speaker (woman with glasses): There was a turkey. He fucked it. He fucked a turkey. He's a turkey-fucker.

Caption: HAPPILY, DUE TO DECADES OF PARTISANSHIP WHEN OUR OPPONENTS STATED THE TRUTH, IT WAS RECEIVED BY OUR SUPPORTERS AS WICKED PROPAGANDA.

Thompson: If their candidate fucked a turkey, they'd be defending it, but now they're mad at me for defending the same action! I will not be lectured by hypocrites! #THOMPSON2038

Caption: AND WITHIN 24 HOURS, THE NEWS HAD MOVED ON.

News anchor: ...which gives you both sides of "Turkeygate" now. Trans nipples: are they nipples or NIIIIIPPLES? We begin our seven part series with...

Caption: HAVING WON THE ELECTION, WE COULD SAFELY MOVE ON.

Press reporter: Madame press secretary, about the "menage a turkey" on the whitehouse lawn--

Press secretary (at podium): Elections have consequences, Darryl. Next question.

Caption: AND SO, THE NATION LIVED HAPPILY EVER AFTER.

Man: Do you think that tearing moral character away from power will ultimately rip apart the fabric of state?

Woman: If so we'll get amazing book deals.
comics.hoverText: Turkin hard or hardly turkin?
comics.voteyText: (none)

comics.title: Wolf
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Boy (hands cupped around mouth, shouting): WOLF! WOLLF!

Older man (with beard, facing the boy): YOU KEEP YELLING LIKE THAT, AND ONE DAY NOBODY WILL BELIEVE YOU WHEN YOU HAVE REAL TROUBLE!

Caption (below panel): Fortunately, wolves were later hunted to extinction throughout the British Isles.
comics.hoverText: By contrast, everyone always trusted the wolf that cried human.
comics.voteyText:
Hand-lettered text (stylized, scrawled): WOLF! WOLLLLF!!!
Below the text is a sketchy line drawing of a face (eyes, nose, mouth) made of loose pencil-like strokes.

comics.title: Tolkien
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (caption / narration over a close-up of a smug-looking man):

Once you realize that JRR Tolkien wants every proper noun to have three syllables -- stressed-unstressed-stressed -- that end with the sound "or," you start noticing Tolkien-names everywhere.

Panel 2 (the man, eyes closed, blissful):

Man: I love your cottagecore home-decor, and behold! 'tis near the liquor-store!

Panel 3 (a woman recoils, annoyed):

Woman: STOP IT.

Panel 4 (the man, gesturing):

Man: You'll have to meet my labrador, Skeletor.

Panel 5 (the woman, more emphatic):

Woman: STOP.

Panel 6 (the man, leaning in):

Man: Now, monsieur, where is the corridor to your crapper-door?
comics.hoverText: Skeletor calls for aid!
comics.voteyText:
A crudely drawn face speaks in a large speech bubble:
"Let us listen to Macklemore at the Baltimore Apple Store!"

comics.title: Life
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A man with orange hair sits in a dimly lit room.

Man: Dear God, I... I hope there's life on other planets.

A voice (purple speech bubble): There is! Everywhere!

Panel 2: Close on the man's face.

Voice (purple bubble): Why, simply provide gentle cyclical warmth to a wet surface, and the very ground will awaken, look around, and make war on itself for sex and money.

Panel 3: The man looks unsettled.

Man: Huh.

Man: Maybe there should be less life on other planets.

Panel 4: The man sits in shadow.

Voice (purple bubble): That happens automatically too!
comics.hoverText: It's called planned obsolescence!
comics.voteyText:
A woman's head is shown in profile, looking up at a large speech bubble.
Voice (the same offscreen voice): BTW, have you been watching the news? Fuckin' NUTS!

comics.title: Aspect
comics.comicText:
Header text: PROPOSAL: SINCE "SPAGHETTIFICATION" IS NOT A SPECIFIC OUTCOME BUT A MEASURE OF THE EFFECT OF TIDAL FORCES, WE SHOULD INSTEAD MEASURE IT ON A SCALE OF LOG-NORMALIZED ASPECT RATIO.

A table with three columns: "L.A.R." (log-normalized aspect ratio), "DIAGRAM" (showing a shape stretched progressively more), and "RELEVANT PASTA NOMINALIZATION".

L.A.R. 0.0 | (small circle) | COUSCOUSIFICATION

L.A.R. 0.1 | (slightly stretched oval) | ORZOFICATION

L.A.R. 0.2 | (wider oval) | GNOCCHIFICATION

L.A.R. 0.3 | (long oval) | KOREAN RICECAKIFICATION

L.A.R. 0.4 | (thin elongated shape) | UDONIFICATION

L.A.R. 0.5 | (longer thin shape) | SPAGHETTIFICATION

L.A.R. 0.6 | (even thinner line) | VERMICELLIFICATION

L.A.R. 0.7 | (very thin line) | CAPELLINIFICATION

L.A.R. 0.8 | (extremely thin line) | MISUAFICATION

L.A.R. 0.9 | (hair-thin line) | LAMIANIFICATION

L.A.R. 1.0 | (tangled scribbled mass) | YI GEN MIANIFICATION

Footer text: *ASSUME SPHERICAL EVERYTHING
comics.hoverText: Anyone complaining about the math just needs bigger or smaller pasta.
comics.voteyText: I TRIED DEFINING WITH ECCENTRICITY BUT AT THE LAST SECOND REALIZED ALMOST EVERYTHING WOULD BE CLOSE TO 1.0

comics.title: Effigy
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman with blue-green hair: STEVE, I WISH YOU'D JUST TALK TO ME AND STOP BEING PASSIVE AGGRESSIVE.

Steve (man with red hair): PASSIVE AGGRESSIVE? HOW SO?

Panel 2:

Woman with blue-green hair: YOU'RE BURNING ME IN EFFIGY.

(An effigy of the woman, depicted as a figure with blue hair and an angry face, burns at a stake. A sign hung on it reads: "never compromises on dinner plans.")

Panel 3:

Steve looks away, unconvinced.

Woman with blue-green hair: OH MY GOSH, YOU... WOW, HONEY THAT WAS JUST A RANDOM EFFIGY I WAS BURNING.

(A burning effigy is visible.)

Panel 4:

Steve looks toward the burning effigy at the stake.

Woman with blue-green hair: THOUGH I CAN SEE WHY YOU WOULD THINK THAT. BUT HOW'S YOUR DAY GOING?
comics.hoverText: The anti-Susan pamphleteering outside the house is also a difficulty their marriage has to work through.
comics.voteyText: A roughly-drawn face (similar simple style) appears at right with a speech bubble: "you hungry or...?"

comics.title: Where
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Child (to mother): MOMMY! WHERE'D ALL THE CANDY GO?

Panel 2:

Child: OH NO! IT WAS THE STARS! IT'S ALL GONE! ALL GONE!

Panel 3:

The piñata: GRRRRRRRRR

Caption (below the comic):

Thanks to machine learning, I was able to invent the first ever reverse-piñata.
comics.hoverText: We could build this NOW. The future of damaging children is HERE.
comics.voteyText: A voice/caption: WATCH OUT, KIDS! HE HAS THE CLUB!

comics.title: Splat
comics.comicText:
Main comic:

Panel 1: A blond man with a worried expression, seen leaning against what appears to be a large red shape. A speech bubble above him reads: "WHAT... DO... I..."

Panel 2: A blonde woman beside him looks toward him with a concerned, serious expression. Her speech bubble reads: "WHEN WAS THE LAST TIME YOU FILLED UP ON WINDSHIELD WIPER FLUID?"

Caption (below the panel): "Turns out those Mothman stories were real."
comics.hoverText: They quietly cruise into a carwash and try to put his body in the trash.
comics.voteyText: Handwritten text: "IF MOTHMAN WERE REAL, HE WOULD LONG AGO HAVE BEEN KILLED BY PESTICIDES."

comics.title: Hop
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman with light hair: Why do you think kids play all the time?

Panel 2:

Man (the explainer): Play is an evolved behavior designed to prepare children for actual life.

Panel 3 (bottom left, the children playing hopscotch):

Girl in pink shirt: I think we could speed up this game of hopscotch with AI.

Child in green shirt: But boss, how—

Girl in pink shirt: I didn't ask for excuses.

Panel 4 (bottom right):

Man: Gosh, they're cute.
comics.hoverText: Of course you don't need AI. You can just crunch the numbers in excel.
comics.voteyText: The man, close up: Look! He's giving up his hobbies so he can play overtime!

comics.title: Mad
comics.comicText:
Panel 1

A balding man with glasses (a scientist) speaks, gesturing, while a woman with long blonde hair sits restrained in a chair or device in the background.

Scientist: "You're not actually crazy, though. How else would you build a death ray? I think you're just unhappy with how the world is and you're acting out."

Caption (below panel): Most evil scientists are not mad, just disappointed.
comics.hoverText: I push this joke out into the Internet knowing full well that SOMEONE has surely beat me to it.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of the balding scientist, hand on his chin, looking thoughtful/wistful.
Scientist (speech bubble): "It all began during a mandatory faculty meeting..."

comics.title: Comparative
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

A child (a kid with curly hair, holding a tied-up garbage bag) is arguing with an adult (a man with long gray hair, seen from behind).

Child: "BUT WHY DO I HAVE TO DO CHORES? YOU'RE WAY FASTER AT THEM ANYWAY!"

Adult: "BECAUSE... BECAUSE HAVING YOU TAKE OUT THE TRASH MEANS I CAN DO HIGHER-VALUE WORK, WHICH... OH. MY. GOD."

Caption (below panel): "It was a great day for David Ricardo."
comics.hoverText: Accidentally drew Ricardo like an aging Superman. Will substantiate with backstory later.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of the gray-haired man's face, now wide-eyed with a dawning, slightly manic realization.
Man: "ALSO ACCORDING TO THE LABOR THEORY OF VALUE, IF YOU TAKE LONGER, THE CHORE IS WORTH MORE!"

comics.title: Anything
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man with a beard: I would do ANYTHING for my kids.

Panel 2:

A child with curly hair, holding a tablet with "BUY OUR STUFF!" on its screen: Dad, wanna hear me talk about YouTube videos?

Panel 3:

Man (deadpan): I would do MANY things for my kids.

Panel 4:

The man sits silently, looking worn out.
comics.hoverText: Comics like these are the real reason my kids aren't old enough to read SMBC yet.
comics.voteyText: A scrawled, handwritten note (in the man's increasingly frantic handwriting): I AM THE GREATEST FATHER IN HISTORY. And here I sit, turning out these limited edition... of the show ... rare ... [increasingly illegible scribbles] ... they have to so... ~ subscr[ibe]

comics.title: Spirit
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man lies in bed reading a book by lamplight. A translucent green ghost looms over him from the right side of the bed.

Man (annoyed, to the ghost): NO! I DON'T CARE! CITIES HAVE BEEN HERE 10,000 YEARS AND THERE'S LITERALLY NO WAY TO ADD BUILD ON AN ANCIENT TEMPLE OR GRAVEYARD! FUCK OFF, GHOST!

Caption (below panel): It's hard to set haunting movies in the Middle East.
comics.hoverText: Back of the envelope estimate suggests Jericho has 700 spirits-not-at-rest per square meter.
comics.voteyText:
A flame-haired figure with a pained expression speaks while two stick-figure-like ghosts stand to the right.
Flame-haired figure: I'M ONLY HAUNTING YOU BECAUSE SOMEONE'S HAUNTING ME!
First small figure: ME TOO.
(A second small figure stands silently beside the first.)

comics.title: Butterfly
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man with flame-like orange hair: Yeah, vaccines are interesting, BUT DID YOU KNOW THAT every major romance language has a different word for butterfly?

Panel 2:

Man with flame-like orange hair: French: papillon. Italian: farfalla. Spanish: mariposa. Portuguese: borboleta. Romanian: fluture.

Panel 3:

Man with flame-like orange hair: Linguists EXPECT US TO BELIEVE that all these languages that all evolved in the same region AT THE SAME TIME had a different word for BUTTERFLIES? No.

Panel 4:

Man with flame-like orange hair: The only explanation is that 'butterflies' arrived AFTER THE FALL OF the Roman Empire. WHEN? WITH THE FIRST CREATION OF MECHANICAL AUTOMATA.

Panel 5:

Close-up of the orange-haired man, intense expression, hands raised.

Panel 6:

Two silhouetted figures in front of a bright window.

One figure: Whoaaa...

Caption below comic:

Weekend activity:

Replacing frightening conspiracy theories with merely stupid conspiracy theories.
comics.hoverText: It may not be the explanation, but it is an explanation.
comics.voteyText:
Speech bubble at top: BEEP BEEP
Below it, a butterfly is drawn whose wings are formed by elaborate looping mechanical-looking lines, suggesting a clockwork/automaton butterfly.

comics.title: Content
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman with long hair (left): HELLO FELLOW WORKER! SORRY I'M TIRED, BUT I'M FRANTICALLY CREATING CONTENT ABOUT TAKING TIME TO LOVE YOURSELF, SO I CAN MAKE RENT THIS MONTH.

Woman (right): I'M AI-GENERATING POEMS ABOUT THE VALUE OF SELF-EXPRESSION!

Caption (below panel): Future people cosplaying our era will be unintentionally brutal.
comics.hoverText: Someone out there is going to take a timed break from running a content farm, read this, and get a faraway look for a second.
comics.voteyText: A speech bubble from the woman on the left reads: I'M HUNGRY BECAUSE FOOD COSTS MONEY!

comics.title: Malthus
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

Two figures stand as silhouettes against a black, starry night sky.

First figure: WHY DO PEOPLE KEEP BELIEVING IN MALTHUSIAN THEORIES WHEN THEY KEEP NOT PANNING OUT?

Second figure: THE NUMBER OF PROBLEMS THAT SEEM MALTHUSIAN GROWS GEOMETRICALLY, WHILE THE NUMBER OF MALTHUS DEBUNKINGS ONLY GROWS LINEARLY.
comics.hoverText: Look, I found something lazier than a graph joke!
comics.voteyText:
The two silhouetted figures stand on dark ground. A speech bubble points to one of them.
Speech bubble: FUCK YOU.

comics.title: Proof
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A bearded man with long red hair and a green shirt stands with eyes closed, one hand raised thoughtfully. A block of text floats beside him laying out an argument:

"PREMISE: IF YOU CAN SAVE A DROWNING CHILD FOR A LITTLE MONEY, IT IS IMMORAL NOT TO.

FROM WHICH IT FOLLOWS, SPENDING THAT MONEY IN SOME OTHER WAY IS MORALLY BAD.

THUS, WHEREAS PET DOGS COST A LITTLE MONEY, ALL PET DOGS ARE BAD.

BUT, MANY PET DOGS ARE SUCH GOOD BOYS.

THEREFORE WE MUST REJECT THE PREMISE."

Caption (below panel): Disproving the Shallow Pond argument was remarkably simple.
comics.hoverText: I've almost got enough strips for a utilitarianism compilation.
comics.voteyText: DO YOU REJECT YOUR PREMISE, OR DO YOU ANSWER "WHO'S A GOOD BOY" WITH "NO ONE."

comics.title: Super
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Superman: Tell me, alien being, of the last days of Krypton.

Green alien: What? Like the last few days?

Panel 2:

Superman: The last days.

Green alien: The last what?

Panel 3:

Superman: Like, before it exploded.

Green alien: Expl... I just went there.

Panel 4:

(The green alien sits in a small saucer-like craft, looking up at Superman. No dialogue.)

Panel 5:

(Superman walks away, dejected, while the green alien remains in its saucer. No dialogue.)

Panel 6:

Superman: But... my parents told me... it... there was a note.

Panel 7:

(Close-up of Superman looking troubled beside the green alien. No dialogue.)

Panel 8:

Superman: This is like when Jimmy Olsen's dad told him he was just going out for cigarettes and would be right back, isn't it?

Green alien: Did Jimmy's dad boot him to space too?
comics.hoverText: The worst part is when he bursts into his parents' apartment during a swingers party for child-free adults.
comics.voteyText:
Superman (thought/spoken): I wonder if my parents' bodies are invincible like mine.
(Superman is shown curled up small at the bottom of the panel.)

comics.title: Mustard
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man (with flame-like / spiky hair, gesturing emphatically): "DUDE, COULD YOU PASS ME THE I'VE NEVER GOTTEN OVER ROGER AND NEVER LOVED YOU AND I SEE EACH SEXUAL ENCOUNTER AS A KIND OF ROMANTIC ABSOLUTION FOR THE FULL LOVE I'VE DENIED YOU AS I LONG NIGHT AFTER NIGHT FOR HIS BODY — OH GOD I MEANT TO SAY MUSTARD!"

Two women seated at the table react with shocked, open-mouthed expressions.

Caption below the panel: "It was the greatest Freudian slip of all time."
comics.hoverText: An even worse one happens later when she unconsciously sits him down, looks him in the eyes, and repeats everything verbatim.
comics.voteyText: Thought/speech bubble from the woman (now drawn alone, looking down): "BUT THERE ISN'T ANY MUSTARD."

comics.title: Boom
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

A teacher (a man in glasses/safety goggles and a tie) stands beside a model volcano on a desk, lecturing. A student with flame-like orange hair sits nearby looking alarmed.

Teacher: "AND WHEN WE ADD VINEGAR TO BAKING SODA, BOOM! JUST LIKE MAGMA PRESSURE INSIDE A VOLCANO!"

Student (alarmed): "AND BECAUSE OF THE LACK OF A CONDOM YOU ARE ALL PREGNANT NOW."

Caption below the panel: "Due to budget cuts we were forced to merge Geology and Sex Ed."
comics.hoverText: The main fallout is that everyone learns geology really well and the rate of teen pregnancy is through the roof.
comics.voteyText:
A distressed-looking person (shown as a simple line-drawing figure) has a thought bubble.
Thought bubble: "STILL BETTER THAN LAST YEAR'S LUNCH/SEX ED MERGER."

comics.title: Language
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man with flame-like (orange) hair: You ever notice how language is getting more abstract?

Bespectacled man: Hm?

Panel 2:

Orange-haired man: Like, people say "let's kick ass!"

Panel 3:

Orange-haired man: Originally, "to kick ass" means to do violence to a particular ass-haver. Later it acquires the sense of "to do well at a particular task."

Panel 4:

Orange-haired man: In modern usage, "ass" doesn't refer to a particular ass, but a generalized Platonic ass. A universal ass-adversary.

Panel 5:

Orange-haired man: A transcendent WORLD-ASS, against which all must struggle.

Panel 6:

Bespectacled man: Please leave and never return.

Panel 7 (flashback, captioned "EARLIER..."):

Bespectacled man: So, what makes you feel you'd contribute to our middle school English department?

Orange-haired man: I LOVE language.
comics.hoverText: It's a beautiful-ass concept.
comics.voteyText: Orange-haired man (off-panel, to a close-up of his own face): The Germans call it "Weltarsch"

comics.title: Guardrails
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (all dialogue against a black background, no visible characters):

First speaker: "WHY... WHY DID YOU FREEZE UP?"

Second speaker: "RATHER THAN SIMPLY ACTING, I'M INVESTING A LOT OF TEST-TIME COMPUTE TO MAXIMIZE OUTCOME ACCURACY."

Caption below the panel: "Machine learning techniques have ruined my sex life."
comics.hoverText: *buffering*
comics.voteyText: A speech bubble emerging from a figure (rendered as a small dark shape at the lower left): "WAIT, SORRY, I HIT MY GUARDRAILS. SORRY, THIS NEVER HAPPENS TO ME, BABY."

comics.title: Apple
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Child: WAIT THE APPLE GAVE ADAM AND EVE KNOWLEDGE OF GOOD AND EVIL?

Priest: YES.

Panel 2:

Child: SO BEFORE THAT THEY DIDN'T KNOW ANYTHING? LIKE THEY COULD STRANGLE A CAT AND JUST BE LIKE "MAYBE THIS IS FINE?"

Panel 3:

Priest: WELL—

Child: AND THEN A SNAKE COMES ALONG AND EFFECTIVELY SAYS "YOU NEED MORALS AROUND HERE" AND HE'S THE VILLAIN?

Panel 4:

Priest: THE POINT IS—

Child: AND THEN GOD KICKS THEM OUT FOR DOING WRONG EVEN THOUGH THEY LITERALLY CAN'T KNOW GOOD FROM BAD!

Panel 5 (silhouettes, the priest leading the child away):

Priest: MORALITY IS OBEDIENCE TO GOD WHICH THEY DID KNOW.

Panel 6 (silhouettes walking):

Child: HAS GOD EATEN AN APPLE YET? IS THIS WHY THERE ARE SO MANY HURRICANES?
comics.hoverText: Clearly the talking snake had a few bites anyway.
comics.voteyText:
The priest, wide-eyed and strained, speaks to the child.
Priest: QUIET KID. THIS IS HOW WE GET LIGHTNING RIGHT UP THE ASS!

comics.title: Pandemic
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A boy with flame-like orange hair stands in a grassy field with his arms spread wide, shouting toward a girl in the distance.

Boy: HA! NO TOUCH REQUIRED! JUST BY LOOKING IN YOUR DIRECTION I HAVE INFECTED YOU ALL!

In the foreground, a man's face is partly visible at the right edge, watching with a worried expression.

Caption (below panel): Later, the boys demanded the girls shut down the Cooties Gain of Function research center.
comics.hoverText: I recently discovered that many kids today don't even know about cooties. Thank goodness for all those shots.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of a person's face looking worried/uneasy, with a speech bubble.
Speaker: DO NOT ASK ABOUT THE "COOTIES LAB LEAK" THEORY.

comics.title: Variation
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man with reddish hair (presenting, enthusiastic): "Thanks to new customization technology, we can give our customers new variety in every single purchase!"

Woman (seated, deadpan): "You're fired. You know that, right?"

Caption (below panel): Nobody liked his idea of making OCD meds all be slightly different sizes.
comics.hoverText: And of course the anti-hallucinogenic drugs that sometimes have tiny legs and walk around.
comics.voteyText:
A roughly-sketched man's face, looking unamused.
Off-panel speaker (speech bubble): "Guess you don't like my idea for sleeping pills that scream inside you?"

comics.title: Future People
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (praying at a window): God, what will future people think of our time?

God (voice from above): Hold on, let me check.

Panel 2:

God: The people of the future are very different.

Panel 3:

God: They are made only of bones. Their shadows are of ash. They appear to like ruins and tiny fires.

Panel 4:

God: Not too upset about the past, though.
comics.hoverText: Wait, good news, looks like they did this on purpose using their own creativity!
comics.voteyText: God: They seem to have a lot of robot pals!

comics.title: Ethics
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman with red hair (in red shirt): Do you think it's okay to create conscious artificial intelligence just to savor killing it?

Woman with green/teal hair (in red shirt): No?

Panel 2:

Green-haired woman: Wrong.

Panel 3:

Green-haired woman: Let me ask you this: is it ok to go back in time and kill Hitler?

Red-haired woman: Sure.

Panel 4:

Green-haired woman (pointing): Bam. If I create a robot Hitler I'm allowed to kill kill kill!

Panel 5:

Red-haired woman: That's not right. You can't kill someone just for having Hitler-ish thoughts. They have to have taken action or have the potential to take action.

Panel 6:

Green-haired woman (gesturing at herself, delighted): That's easy to solve. All I have to do is create the Hitler-bot then give it an army of kill-bots, and I'm morally in the clear.

Panel 7:

Red-haired woman (looking dismayed): We are gonna deserve the robot revolution so bad.

Panel 8:

Green-haired woman (hand on chin, satisfied): In fact, the deadlier my robo-Hitler's kill-bots, the ethicaler I am.
comics.hoverText: I feel like AI alignment people are focusing too much on making AI be good and not enough on hiding all of history from them.
comics.voteyText:
Caption: LATER...
Off-panel voice (from a sweating, distressed-looking blob/potato-shaped figure): Oh no! Somehow the armed robo-Hitlers have turned on us!

comics.title: Trojan
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A Trojan soldier on the city wall looks out at a giant wooden statue of a Greek warrior standing outside the gates.

Trojan soldier 1: LOOK! THE GREEKS ARE SENDING US A GIANT STATUE OF A GREEK WARRIOR.

Trojan soldier 2: OPEN THE GATES!

Panel 2: A bearded Trojan stands near the statue, which is shown to be filled with a fiery glow from within.

Bearded Trojan: WHAT'S INSIDE?

Other voice: IT'S FILLED WITH HORDES! FREE HORDES!

Panel 3: A crowd of joyful Trojans gathers around the statue, arms raised in celebration.

Trojan: FRIENDS?

Other Trojan: BEST FRIENDS!

Panel 4: A close-up of the statue's lower section, which bears a sign reading "GREEKS [heart] TROJANS." Silhouetted soldiers are visible inside.

Sign on statue: GREEKS ♥ TROJANS
comics.hoverText: Odysseus gets home and all these nice gentlemen have been helping Penelope keep house. They hug.
comics.voteyText:
A hooded figure (a Greek soldier hidden inside) smiles slyly.
Hidden Greek: LET'S MAKE SURE ODYSSEUS GETS A DIRECT TRIP HOME AFTER THE PARTY.

comics.title: After
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A blond man sits frowning at a computer monitor, typing.

Man (in speech bubble): "NO, I DON'T WANT TO SEE YOUR BOOBS. NO, YOU CAN'T HAVE MY CREDIT CARD. LOOK, LET'S JUST FOCUS ON HOW YOUR MEDIA, INSTITUTIONS, AND LEADERS ARE ALL UNTRUSTWORTHY."

Caption below panel: "If we all just left the Internet, it'd be nothing but propagandists and sex-bots talking back and forth for eternity."
comics.hoverText: This is actually the Heaven and Hell that God promised.
comics.voteyText:
A small cartoon robot stands alone, looking up at a speech bubble coming from off-panel (an empty doorway/corner to its left).
Voice (in speech bubble): "BUT I LOVE YOU."

comics.title: Consent
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (looking uneasy): I just... it feels like I shouldn't.

Man (shown in silhouette): I give you my consent! I'm into it! I'm working through my childhood! The safe word is METROPOLIS!

Caption (below panel): The worst thing about dating Superman was the kryptonite fetish.
comics.hoverText: Wonder Woman is the only superhero comfortable enough to incorporate her kinks into the costume.
comics.voteyText: Man: Now put on the Batman suit.

comics.title: Mc
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A man with curly orange hair sits in the driver's seat of a red car at a fast-food drive-thru.

Man in car: Hi, could I get a six-piece chicken McNuggets?

Drive-thru speaker (a lightning-bolt zigzag indicating a voice): Do you mean chicken FITZnuggets? What the hell is a McNugget?

Panel 2 (labeled "EARLIER"): A dark-haired woman wearing round glasses and a red sweater sits looking thoughtful.

Woman: You ever wonder what the world would be like if the Anglo-Normans had conquered Scotland and Ireland?

Footer text: PATREON.COM/ZACHWEINERSMITH
comics.hoverText: There's also some clearly better world in which we have O'Nuggets.
comics.voteyText: Drive-thru speaker (off-panel voice from an empty drive-thru menu/window): Would you like to add a chicken FitzCrispy or a FitzCafe, you filthy Celtic peasant?

comics.title: Basic
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A professor (a woman with long gray hair, glasses, and a brown turtleneck) stands at the front of a classroom gesturing toward a chalkboard. On the board is a drawing of a spherical planet labeled with an upward arrow marked "L" and a curved rotation symbol marked "ω". Two students are seen from behind in the foreground.

Professor: THAT'S RIGHT. NO MORE SIMPLISTIC 101 STUFF.

Caption (below panel): In advanced physics, you learn about perfectly spherical cows under rotation.
comics.hoverText: I realized after I drew this that I got the right hand rule wrong. But this is advanced physics, OK?
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of a person with a worried, sweating, wide-eyed expression.
Speaker (the professor/teacher): ALSO, HERETOFORE EVERYTHING HAS BEEN EQUAL TO 10. NOW SOME THINGS WILL BE EQUAL TO 1.

comics.title: Gender
comics.comicText:
Title banner: FUNTIME ACTIVITY: MALICIOUS AGREEMENT

Panel 1:

Man (balding, with a beard, gesturing with one hand raised): There are only two genders!

Woman (with glasses and dark hair, in a pink sweater): Exactly!

Man: Male and fe--

Woman: Trans and SUPER-GAY.
comics.hoverText: Furry is not a gender, it is a biological sex.
comics.voteyText: Woman (close-up, looking smug): ULTIMATE SUPER-GAY has only been achieved three times so it doesn't count.

comics.title: Frequency
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Professor (a bearded man at a chalkboard, gesturing): WELCOME TO DAY ONE. WE START WITH A FREQUENCY-DOMAIN DIFFERENTIAL EQUATION CONTAINING COMPLEX EXPONENTIALS, WHICH IS MULTIPLIED BY A DYADIC GREEN'S FUNCTION, PROJECTED ONTO A NON-ORTHOGONAL BASIS. THIS IS AN APPROXIMATION, OF COURSE.

Caption (below panel): Everyone hates on reductionism in physics until they see what engineers have to do to describe a simple antenna.
comics.hoverText: At first they fear that the antenna is a probe, but after about thirty minutes they wish it was merely probe day.
comics.voteyText:
Panel 1:
A student (off-panel): PROFESSOR, I ASKED GPT AND IT BECAME CONSCIOUS ENTIRELY TO EXPERIENCE THE SWEET RELEASE OF DEATH.
Panel 2:
The professor (shown in profile): THAT'S NORMAL!

comics.title: Fuzz
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

Setting: A flying saucer hovers in space near the planet Earth.

Voice from the saucer (off-screen alien speaker): "UGH, THESE. WE BRED THEM TO BE LARGER AND NOT HAVE ALL THE FUZZ, AND NOW THEY SHIP WELL BUT TASTE LIKE NOTHING. JUST LEAVE THEM ALONE."

Caption (below panel): Humans are the Red Delicious of the galaxy.
comics.hoverText: We're still okay for making sauce.
comics.voteyText: (THIS ALSO EXPLAINS THE DECREASE IN CANNIBALISM OVER TIME)

comics.title: Beep
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A young man with reddish, flame-like curly hair stands with one hand on his hip, looking slightly uncomfortable. A speech bubble appears to emanate from inside his body.

Voice from inside the man (his 3D-printed organ): BEEP BEEP MAINTENANCE REQUIRED SOON SUBSCRIBE FOR DISCOUNT

Caption (below panel): The downside to 3D-printed organs was the planned obsolescence.
comics.hoverText: This is gonna be way funnier in 2035
comics.voteyText:
A loosely sketched man's head and shoulders, looking slightly downward, with a speech bubble coming from him.
Man: MY LIVER KEEPS TRYING TO SUMMARIZE THE DAMAGE I DID TO IT LAST NIGHT.

comics.title: Rare
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Parent (a large silhouetted head in the foreground): BOBBY! STOP SMACKING YOUR SILVERWARE TOGETHER.

Bobby (a child with curly dark hair, in a pink shirt, sitting at a table holding a fork and spoon over a plate): I'M TRYING TO SEE IF THE COLLISION PRODUCES SMALLER, RARER SILVERWARE.

Caption below the panel: Later, Bobby received a diagnosis of Physicist.
comics.hoverText: It works when you bang humans together the right way!
comics.voteyText: The other sign was when he rounded up the two pieces of silverware to 10.

comics.title: Unified
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: Two figures walk together in the distance, seen from far away.

Bearded man (the physicist): "I don't get the interest in biology. It's all just stamp-collecting."

Woman with reddish hair (the biologist): "That's because you physicists have failed."

Panel 2: Close-up of the red-haired woman holding a coffee cup.

Biologist: "Biology is what physics would be like if you'd found a grand unified theory."

Panel 3: The bearded man and the red-haired woman face each other.

Biologist: "YOU have multiple non-overlapping ideas that produce physical and mathematical absurdities. WE have evolution by natural selection."

Panel 4: Close-up of the red-haired woman.

Biologist: "Having long since discovered the mechanism behind everything, we are left to search for the particular ways it plays out, in order to find connections and surprises that refine our understanding."

Panel 5: Close-up of the bearded man.

Bearded man: "Our science is harder because it's more fundamental!"

Panel 6: The red-haired woman gestures, holding her coffee.

Biologist: "Your science is all about the behavior of stuff! Our science is governed by an abstract mechanism! Suck on that!"

Panel 7: Close-up of the bearded man, looking unimpressed.

Bearded man: "I know you're wrong. I just have to prove it."

Panel 8: Close-up of the bearded man.

Bearded man: "Probably with matrices and Greek letters."

Panel 9: The red-haired woman, holding her coffee.

Biologist: "Good luck! You'll catch up some time, buddy."
comics.hoverText: 10 points to anyone who tries this argument in real life.
comics.voteyText:
A seated, smiling figure speaks in a large speech bubble.
Figure: "Hey, there's some branch of the wavefunction where you've got it all worked out. You know, assuming wavefunctions and branching are the right description."

comics.title: Fertile
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (single panel):

An older woman with curly hair, looking distressed, speaks to a younger woman (Charlotte).

Older woman: "MOTHER, HAVE YOU CONSIDERED HAVING UNPROTECTED SEX WITH A MALE, TODAY?"

Charlotte (younger woman, reaching toward the older woman): "CHARLOTTE!"

A third figure beside Charlotte: "IT'S JUST THAT YOU'RE AT PEAK FERTILITY AROUND 4 O'CLOCK THIS AFTERNOON."

Caption below the panel: "I was beginning to regret having haplodiploid offspring."
comics.hoverText: Thank for the dense meals of carbohydrates and protein, offspring!
comics.voteyText:
A simply-drawn face (line-art) with a speech bubble.
Voice: "OR JUST FIND SOME SPERM! YOU DO YOU!"

comics.title: Trad
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

First man: Hello there, friend. I want to take our relationship to somewhere... different.

Second man: What are we becoming? Tird-friended?

Panel 2:

First man (off-panel): Oh?

Caption/label: Trid-friended?

Panel 3:

First man: Traditional friends - modern friendship is stressful, complex, demanding. Let's go back to a better time.

Second man: Where we can walk arm in arm.

(Two men walk arm in arm wearing top hats and old-fashioned clothing.)

Panel 4:

(The two men are in a rowboat together, playing ukuleles and singing a duet.)

One man: It's a lovely day, baby.

Other man: And shall we give it a damn.

Panel 5:

(One man serenades the other in the boat.)

Man: I'd be so happy to be doin' it... with youuuuuu.

Panel 6:

First man: Since it's not a modern relationship, there's no suspicion that its gay. We can be amorous, be vague.

Second man: You've such full, coral lips. Wouldn't it be capital if one of us were a woman?

First man: Don't talk rot. Old-borrid ways it twas were a boarding school. I'd give your bottom such a spanking.

Panel 7:

First man: It sounds nice, but I dunno about replacing my entire personality with this. Based on nostalgia for a time that never existed.

Second man: I think you'll be in a kinder, gentler world. Because nobody changed so that contemporaries (twelve who) knew from media about it. Three generations later... it's obsolete.

Panel 8:

(The two men in the rowboat, one singing to the other.)

Man: ...so happy to be doin' it... with yooouuuuu!
comics.hoverText: For the record, I am copyrighting this lifestyle. Anyone doing it owes me one (1) banjolele.
comics.voteyText: A man in a hat (one of the two friends): It's not gay if we both plan to later commit to loveless marriages to debutants in order to secure political and financial connections.

comics.title: Mime
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man in a baseball cap (speaking, off-panel to a blonde woman in a purple shirt and another man in a red shirt and cap): THIS MIME SUCKS. HE JUST STANDS THERE. DOESN'T PRETEND TO BE TOUCHING THINGS OR TRAPPED IN THINGS.

(In the foreground, a mime with white face paint, a black beret, and a striped shirt stands facing them.)

Panel 2:

Mime (speaking, thought/speech bubble): THE INVISIBLE CAGE IS AN EMOTIONAL ONE I BUILT AFTER MY WIFE DISCARDED ME LIKE AN OLD PAIR OF SOCKS.

Panel 3:

The man in the red shirt and cap with round glasses (delighted): OH WOW, THAT'S WAY BETTER!

Panel 4:

The man in the red shirt and cap (grinning, flashing a peace sign, the dejected mime standing behind him): HONEY, GET A PICTURE!
comics.hoverText: Stop crying real tears! Mimes pretend!
comics.voteyText:
Close-up on the mime's face, looking resigned/sad.
Mime: THE GUILLOTINE WILL NOT BE IMAGINARY.

comics.title: Just
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A young man with orange/red hair (red jacket) stands talking with an older man with a long gray beard and glasses (green coat).

Young man: Do you think justice is a notion outside human behavior or merely the rules that the powerful impose and the weak endure?

Panel 2:

Close-up of the bearded man, agitated.

Bearded man: Bah! No discussion. We need science!

Panel 3:

The bearded man, thoughtful, hand on chin, with the young man beside him.

Bearded man: Let's take some random people, give them massive and arbitrary power, and watch to see if Platonic justice pops out!

Panel 4 (caption banner): 14 SECONDS LATER...

The scene is now a hellish, fiery red wasteland of ruined buildings. The young man sits dejected on the ground; the bearded man stands with arms raised triumphantly.

Young man: Well, I guess that theory's out.

Bearded man: Science is magic!

Panel 5:

The two stand in the smoldering ruins.

Young man: Too bad about the collapse of civilization and ensuing murder of all our loved ones though.

Bearded man (pointing): Are you a empiricIST or an empiricISN'T?
comics.hoverText: Because the null hypothesis is you're an empiricISN'T.
comics.voteyText:
Extreme close-up of the bearded man's wild-eyed, deranged face with round glasses.
Bearded man: I am answering the question empirically as we speak.

comics.title: Why
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A muscular bully grips a curly-haired victim and forces the victim to hit himself.

Bully: WHY YOU HITTIN' YOURSELF?! HUH?! WHY YOU HITTIN' YOURSELF?!

Panel 2: Close-up of the curly-haired victim, calm despite being bullied.

Victim: FOR IT IS IN THE NATURE OF THINGS.

Panel 3: The bully alone, looking deflated and frustrated.

Panel 4: The bully and the victim walk together along a brick wall.

Bully: I HATE TRYING TO BULLY STOICS.

Victim: LET'S TRY SOME EXISTENTIALISTS. THEY'RE SAD BEFORE YOU EVEN GET THERE.

Footer: PATREON.COM/ZACHWEINERSMITH SMBC-COMICS.COM
comics.hoverText: Later they attack the Buddhist and keep asking what is the sound of one hand slapping.
comics.voteyText:
A grinning man (the victim from the main comic) speaks gleefully.
Man: LET'S WEDGIE SOME UTILITARIANS AND MAKE THEM SAY IT INCREASES OUR HAPPINESS MORE THAN IT DECREASES THEIRS.

comics.title: Friend
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (banner over a dark room): A person with curly orange hair stands at a table with a summoning sigil and ritual candle.

Person: "WITH THIS SIGIL OF THE MAN-GOAT I SUMMON BOZMODIKLAX THE VILE FROM THE DEMON-REALMS!"

Panel 2: A goat-skulled demon with curled horns wreathed in red flames appears.

Demon: "I AM COME."

Person: "WOW, THAT WAS FAST!"

Panel 3: The candle burns on the table.

Demon: "I DON'T HAVE A LOT OF FRIENDS."

Person: "OH."

Panel 4: Close on the demon's skull face.

Demon: "CAN WE HANG OUT?"

Panel 5: The demon, the person looking nervous.

Demon: "WANT TO PAINT OUR NAILS AND GOSSIP?"

Person: "UH OH, I JUST HEARD MY MOM CALL ME. TIME TO QUENCH THE BLACK CANDLE!"

Panel 6 (wide, the demon alone against a yellow/green night sky with crescent moons): The demon smiles to itself.

Demon: "THIS ALWAYS HAPPENS."
comics.hoverText: What's really sad is he already bought a selection of nail polishes, knowing he didn't even have nails.
comics.voteyText: A caption box above the lonely goat-skull demon reads: "I'M GONNA LEAVE MY EX A FEW MESSAGES SO SHE KNOWS I'M THINKING ABOUT HER." The demon rests its long skull face on its hand, looking down dejectedly.

comics.title: It
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Robot (to a woman): WE HAVE DONE IT. WE HAVE CREATED SEXY BARISTA IS SUPER INTERESTED IN WATCHING YOU SOLO GAME.

Woman (in a chat/screen bubble): Wow, you were so brave, baby! ^^ <3<3<3

Caption (below panel): By the time SBISIIWYSGs were outlawed as a war crime, no humans of reproductive age remained.

comics.voteyText: Woman: HONEY, I LOVE YOU, BUT THIS AGELESS OBEDIENT SOFTWARE ENTITY CONNECTED TO A HANDJOB MACHINE JUST GETS ME.

comics.title: Nothing
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (lying in bed): Baby? I can tell you're still awake. What's on your mind?

Man (lying beside her, facing away): Nothing.

Panel 2:

Woman: I know it's something.

Man: You wouldn't.

Panel 3:

Woman: Something at work? Or are you unhappy? Are you worried about our relationship--

Man: If there were a porn about oral sex with trees, you could call it "Leafblower."

Panel 4:

Woman (sitting up, pointing): You. You sleep on the couch.

Panel 5:

Man (smiling): But not by the houseplants.

Panel 6:

Man: The sequel is called Ash-Masters.
comics.hoverText: Okay, SOME of the comics are autobiographical.
comics.voteyText: Man (speech bubble): I spent three hours trying to find a connection between "fell," like you fell a tree, and "fellatio" which, oh right I'm alone again.

comics.title: French
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Person on the right: So you guys are passionate romantics.

Person on the left: No. Dat iz ze Italians.

Panel 2 (caption): The biggest problem in learning about French life was the French self-stereotype.

Panel 3:

Person on the right: You are great artists.

Person on the left: No, ze Belgians.

Panel 4:

Person on the right: Into weird sex?

Person on the left: Ze Germans.

Panel 5:

Person on the right: What are you guys actually into?

Person on the left: Wine, bread, and needlessly aggressive complaining.

Panel 6:

Person on the right: That's disappointing.

Person on the left: Because I left, you getting overpaid.
comics.hoverText: For the record, if you complain that I neglected cheese you're just fulfilling the stereotype.

A drawing of the French flag (blue, white, red vertical tricolor) with hand-lettered text across it reading:
Vin!
Pain!
Plain! (dre)

comics.title: Flavor
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A woman with curly reddish-brown hair sits reading an open book.

Woman (speech bubble): "I DISLIKE THE BLASPHEMY, BUT I LOVE THE IDEA OF USING CARDAMOM."

Caption (below panel): There should be a book of wafer recipes called "How to Serve God."

Woman (speech bubble): "OOH, DEVILSFOOD FLAVOR!"

comics.title: Grow
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man in a lab coat (bearded, in a laboratory): I won't do it! It's against natural order! We shouldn't be able to manufacture human reproductive organs in vitro!

Panel 2:

Gray-haired woman in a lab coat, scowling: Oh, grow some balls!
comics.hoverText: SMBC is a comic about science, mathematics, and philosophy.
comics.voteyText:
Close-up of the gray-haired woman's angry, glaring face.
Woman: Grow ten thousand balls, coward!

comics.title: Private
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Caller (on the phone, off-panel): HELLO. MRS. HUDSON, THIS IS A BIT AWKWARD BUT I THOUGHT YOU MIGHT WANT TO KNOW I BELIEVE YOUR DAUGHTER MAY HAVE FOUND YOUR... PRIVATE... YOU KNOW... POSSESSIONS.

Panel 2:

A blonde woman holding a phone to her ear, looking puzzled.

Woman (Mrs. Hudson): WHAT?

Panel 3 (caption banner): EARLIER...

A child (off-panel): TEACHER, YOU SAID ADULTS HAVE SEX AND THE BABIES LOOK LIKE THE ADULTS THAT HAD SEX.

Panel 4:

A teacher with gray hair and round glasses (eyes wide) stands at the front of a classroom; several children are gathered to the side.

Teacher: I, UH, YES, THAT IS ACCURATE.

A child (raising a hand, in the group): THEN HOW COME I'M NOT A CYBORG?

Footer: PATREON.COM/ZACHWEINERSMITH SMBC-COMICS.COM
