comics.title: WaaS
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman: I think we should switch from marriage to marriage-as-a-service.

Man: What?

Panel 2:

Woman: Right now you make a one-time promise of loyalty and kindness. Why not pay as you go with the option to cancel every 30 days?

Panel 3:

Man: That seems stressful.

Woman: Not if you're ready to upgrade to PREMIUM WIFE.

Panel 4:

Man: I love you though. I love you just as you are.

Woman: Then keep your current FREE plan! Basic wife! Good choice!

Panel 5:

(The man looks away, silent.)

Panel 6:

(The woman smiles silently.)

Panel 7:

Woman (off-panel): So how's your day going?

Panel 8:

(The man is shown in profile. The woman stands holding up a smartphone whose screen is plastered with ads — a Temu "Must Go Clearance Sale," a "Who Are The Top 15 Most Female Athletes" listicle, and a "Top Nephrologists... Do's and Don'ts for your kidney number... read this" ad.)
comics.hoverText: Have I mentioned SMBC's ad-free patreon page?
comics.voteyText:
(Close-up on the man's face. A speech bubble points to him.)
Man: The NSFW version of wife is available on Patreon.

comics.title: Happiness
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A blonde woman (wearing a smiley-face pin/badge) to a woman with dark hair in a red shirt: "Sorry you're feeling blue. You know, every time I feel sad, I think of one of my blessings, and then I put a tooth in the happiness jar."

Panel 2:

Blonde woman, smiling wide: "Later I count all the teeth and realize how good my life is."

Panel 3:

Dark-haired woman: "Where do the teeth come from?"

Panel 4:

Blonde woman: "That's the wonderful thing. It's not ABOUT the teeth. It's about HAPPINESS."

Panel 5:

The dark-haired woman peers into a jar full of teeth. Caption (her thought/observation): "They look like human teeth. Like adult human teeth."

Panel 6:

The blonde woman, smiling.

Panel 7:

The blonde woman holds out the jar of teeth (the smiley pin visible on her shirt).

Panel 8:

The dark-haired woman looks uneasy/disturbed.

Panel 9:

Close-up of the dark-haired woman's face, looking troubled.

Panel 10:

Wordless. A hand drops a tooth (a small white object) toward an open jar.
comics.hoverText: You're looking at the teeth, but you're missing... the smile!
comics.voteyText: A simple line-drawing of a smiling, content face. Speech bubble: "And yet, suddenly depression isn't my primary emotion."

comics.title: Slap
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A bald man with round glasses, looking stern, addresses an off-panel robot against a red background.

Man: NOW LISTEN, ROBOT. THE NUMBER ONE RULE IS YOU CANNOT HARM HUMANS.

Panel 2:

The man continues, gesturing.

Man: I'LL GIVE YOU A THOUSAND DOLLARS TO SLAP YOURSELF IN THE FACE.

Man (separate small balloon): HARD.

Panel 3:

Reply from the robot (off-panel).

Robot: I'LL DO IT, BUT ONLY BECAUSE IT'S A NET BENEFIT TO ME.

Panel 4:

The man, now wide-eyed and alarmed, raises a hand.

Man: TO BE CLEAR, I DON'T HAVE A THOUSAND DOLLARS.

Man: BUT, BUT THEN—

Robot: THE BLAME LIES WITH CAPITALISM.
comics.hoverText: Later it works out because the man is a masochist.
comics.voteyText:
A simple line-drawn robot stands with its arms out, a thought/speech balloon above it.
Robot: ALSO THE UNIVERSE IS DETERMINISTIC, SO IF YOU GET ATOMIZED BY ME, I AM NOT AT FAULT.

comics.title: End
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Child: Dad, do you ever worry about the end of the world?

Panel 2:

Dad: Ha, when I was a kid like you, I sure did.

Panel 3:

Dad: Once you grow up and get a job and responsibilities, well, you'll say to yourself, "I welcome the cleansing fire."

Panel 4:

Dad: I was hoping you'd say life will go on.

Child: No. Not if we can de-orbit the moon. That should do it.
comics.hoverText: During the book tour of A City on Mars, I did a talk with Randall Munroe in NYC, and he made, impromptu, a better joke than any of us have committed to paper. During a discussion of whether you could eliminate all life on Earth for a reasonable price, a person asked if there might be a way you could specifically annihilate Queens. To which he replied, 'regicide?'
comics.voteyText: Child: Oh! Or de-orbit the Earth!

comics.title: Quantum
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A small girl in a red dress walks holding hands with a bearded man (her dad).

Girl: Dad, do you think the unpredictability of quantum mechanics means we have free will?

Panel 2: Close-up of the dad's face.

Dad: Yes.

Panel 3: Close-up of the dad's face again.

Dad: No.

Panel 4: The girl and dad walking together again.

Girl: You're so wise, dad.
comics.hoverText: Later they go out for a superposition of chocolate and vanilla ice cream.
comics.voteyText:
A cartoonish face with wide eyes is shown, looking unsettled.
Caption: Just kidding. Free will is an incoherent idea. You can think about it tonight when you try to fall asleep.

comics.title: Set
comics.comicText:
Main comic:

A woman with reddish-brown hair is enthusiastically explaining something to two children seated at a desk, one of whom holds an open book labeled "PRINCIPIA".

Woman: Oh yeah, this one's way better. Instead of just asserting that counting numbers exist, they define zero. Zero represents the empty set. They define one finger to represent the set CONTAINING the empty set, and so on.

Caption (below panel): Never ask a mathematician how to teach children.
comics.hoverText: Why start with a confusing idea like zero, when you can refer to the notion of a something with nothing in it?
comics.voteyText:
A close-up, loosely sketched face of the woman, still talking.
Woman: Actually, let's start with the transcendentals, since that's most of numbers anyway.

comics.title: Copernican
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A green alien walks alongside a red-haired human (shirtless, in boxers) inside a spaceship corridor, stars visible outside.

Alien: Ever since we realized we weren't the center of the universe, we've been waiting for you.

Human: Ha, we went through a similar thing.

Panel 2 (close on the human and alien):

Alien: You realize your planet isn't the center of the solar system.

Alien: Your star isn't the center of the galaxy.

Panel 3:

Alien: Your galaxy isn't the center of the universe.

Alien: Your time isn't the beginning or end.

Panel 4 (the human stands looking unsettled, alien beside him):

Alien: "Consciousness" is an uninteresting recursive algorithm.

Panel 5 (close on the human, a single tear, looking devastated):

Human: ...

Panel 6 (the alien holds up a small red object/orb):

Alien: I mean mind is made of magic ghosts.

Panel 7 (the human throws his arms up in joy):

Human: Hooray!
comics.hoverText: This joke is more for my future audience of robots, but humans are welcome.
comics.voteyText:
A bald, elongated-headed alien speaks.
Alien: They're so cute, I hate having to airlock them after use.

comics.title: Spoon
comics.comicText:
Narration: Once upon a time, it was considered unacceptable for leaders to swear.

Narration: Today, the President raised his voice while saying gosh.

(A man at a podium speaks.)

Narration: Later, in the era of perpetual recording, we saw behind the mask of propriety.

First speaker (a man): Senator, there's been an attack on Washington.

Second speaker (a woman): Fucking fuck me sideways with a spoon, I mean, we are looking into the matter urgently.

Narration: To our surprise, the public appreciated it as candor.

Bearded man: This fucker cares about our asses.

Woman: She's just like us regular shitheads.

Third person: Finally some ass-blasting honesty from the political class!

Narration: The accident was tactically repeated.

Speaker (woman, pointing): And we sent that bill straight back to the President because the rights of the people shall not be fucked sideways with a spoon!

[THUNDEROUS APPLAUSE]

Narration: As with most social innovations, it worked well until everybody did it.

First man: Senator, Congressman Suzuki called you a shit-for-brains pig-fucker who should die choking on a camel's nutsack.

Second man (in suit): So, he's towing the party line again, eh?

Narration: Inevitably, the norm violation itself became normal...

Woman: We've been using shrimp-dick a lot lately. Crayon-cock was working too. But could we do anything with, perhaps, the anus?

Man: Frank? Order some pizzas?

Narration: ...And what was normal became a sacred expectation.

Man at podium: Ladies and gentlemen of America, the state of our union is fuckin' rad.

Narration: And so, we were back precisely where we started.

Bearded man: Today the governor said the current poverty program was fucking the budget's ass with a pineapple.

Woman at laptop: God, modern politics is so performative.

PATREON.COM/ZACHWEINERSMITH SMBC-COMICS.COM

comics.voteyText: A large blank smiling face (the robot's head, big and rounded) with two oval eyes. A speech bubble points to it: DON'T FORGET TO SMILE.

comics.title: Tragic
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A bald man in a red shirt stands triumphant, arms raised, holding up a flask of glowing liquid. He laughs maniacally.

Man: HAHAHAHA! I'VE DONE IT! NOW EVERYONE WHO HAS EVER DIED HAS RETROACTIVELY DIED TRAGICALLY YOUNG! AHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHHAHAHAHA!

Caption banner: EARLIER...

Panel 2:

The same bald man (now calm, wearing glasses) sits being interviewed by a woman with dark hair in a brown shirt.

Woman: SO WHAT GOT YOU INTERESTED IN LONGEVITY SCIENCE?

Man: IT'S ABOUT CHANGING THE WORLD.

Footer text: PATREON.COM/ZACHWEINERSMITH | SMBC-COMICS.COM

Text promoting an SMBC book collection, with cover images shown. Reads approximately: PARENTING -- AN SMBC COLLECTION. SAUSAGE LEGS AND THE QUESTS TO JUST STAY ALIVE -- AND AVAILABLE NOW WHEREVER BOOKS... MAY 2026.

comics.voteyText:
Close-up of the bald man's grinning, manic face from behind.
Man: NOW TO INVENT A UNIVERSAL HAPPINESS MACHINE SO ALL PREVIOUS LIVES ARE MISERABLE AHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAH!

comics.title: Nagel
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman with reddish-brown hair: "Why do we need to read original old philosophy works? Modern summaries are always clearer."

Panel 2:

A second person (with reddish-brown hair, glasses, seen from behind): "Are you familiar with Thomas Nagel?"

The second person: "The greatest 20th century philosopher of consciousness?"

(In the background, a third woman with glasses sits at a desk.)

Panel 3:

The woman at the desk (glasses): AHEM. "'...even a chicken might be called perverted in an extended sense if it had been conditioned to develop a fetishistic attachment to a telephone.' (Nagel, 1969)"

Panel 4:

The second person: "Wait. The point of reading masterworks is to find quotations that can be taken out of context?"

The woman at the desk (off-panel, silhouettes shown): "We are drawn to them, like a horny chicken to a dial tone."

Bottom banner:

PATREON.COM/ZACHWEINERSMITH SMBC-COMICS.COM

Our two new books PARENTING - an SMBC collection and SAWYER LEE AND THE QUEST TO JUST STAY HOME are available on Kickstarter during May 2026!

(Book covers shown: "PARENTING" by Zach Weinersmith, and "SAWYER LEE AND THE QUEST TO JUST STAY HOME" by Zach Weinersmith.)
comics.hoverText: The best part is that it's included in a book titled Mortal Questions. Also that the original paper came out in 1969.
comics.voteyText: A simple line drawing of a duck/bird-like creature with a long neck and flame-like tuft of feathers on its head, looking toward a faint sketch of what appears to be itself or another shape (largely blank/minimal).

comics.title: Peace
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A young man climbs toward a small temple at the top of a mountain.

Young man: "Wise master, what is the key to inner peace?"

Panel 2:

A robed, long-haired guru sits cross-legged in meditation.

Guru: "Enough money in index funds that you can withdraw a sustainable 3.5% per year, every year, at a level equivalent to twice the local median income."

Panel 3:

Young man: "That can't be it."

Guru: "Ah yes."

Panel 4:

Guru: "Some people say 4% is safe, but current models say there's a small chance of zeroing out during 30 years, and then where does that leave you?"

Panel 5:

The young man and the guru stand facing each other.

Young man: "I mean, I thought it'd be about silencing your inner voice and just being."

Panel 6:

The guru leans in, mouth wide open, agitated.

Guru: "Yeah? You gonna eat your silent inner voice? Huh? You gonna sleep under a roof made of silent inner voice?"

Panel 7 (wide bottom panel):

Guru (mockingly): "'I must learn to silence the inner voice that says pay rent on time and just BE.' Do you have any idea how stupid you sound?"

Young man: "Please stop yelling."
comics.hoverText: Triple the median would of course be 50% more inner peace.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of the long-haired, bearded guru's face.
Guru: "That will be $700"

comics.title: Future
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Interviewer (an older woman with gray hair and round glasses, seated, holding papers): Where do you see yourself here, in one year, five years, ten years?

Panel 2:

Applicant (a woman with dark hair): Doing less but believing I'm doing more.

Panel 3:

Applicant: Earning more but telling people it's harder to get by.

Panel 4:

Applicant: And, all the while, developing a vast sense of confidence due not to having made GOOD decisions, but to having made MANY decisions.

Panel 5:

Interviewer: Sorry. I like your attitude, but you're too self-aware for management.

Panel 6:

Applicant (leaning in, grinning): I meant to say growth mindset/ shitloads of growth mindset/
comics.hoverText: I read in an econ book that panel four is a thing that actually happens, and I've been terrified ever since.
comics.voteyText: A close-up of the applicant's face, crying with tears streaming down: Metric buttloads of thought leadership!

comics.title: Connection
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman scientist: My god a deep connection at the heart of complexity theory AND quantum field theory.

Panel 2:

Man scientist: We must never publish. For the dignity of our fields.

Panel 3 (the two scientists face each other across a chalkboard; on the board is written an equation):

Chalkboard: ∫ Dφ e^{iS[φ]} ⟹ ⋃_{k≥1} DSPACE(n^k)

Caption below the comic: The link between PSpace and Fock Space remains a scientific secret.
comics.hoverText: All I'm saying is this would be the ultimate proof that God has a dirty mind.
comics.voteyText:
A face (drawn in loose black brush strokes) gazes upward, awestruck.
Speech bubble: I feel I've seen... the PSpace of God.

comics.title: Shenanigans
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man (bald, glasses, suit jacket over yellow shirt): "Ladies and gentlemen, I introduce a new field of ethics:"

Man: "Shenanigansology."

Panel 2:

Man: "We have all these failed frameworks! Maximize happiness. Make universal rules. Be virtuous. Bah!"

Panel 3:

Man: "Maximizing happiness means killing one guy to save five! Universalizing moral rules means betraying friends to their killers in order to avoid lying! Virtue ethics gives you upstanding people in wicked societies, contributing to overall wickedness!"

Panel 4:

Man (arms spread wide): "Each framework only functions if you add 'and no shenanigans, you know what we mean.'"

Panel 5:

Man: "And yet no branch of philosophy has even attempted to discover the fundamental nature of shenanigans! It is the dark matter of moral philosophy!"

Panel 6 (man at a podium before a seated audience):

Man: "We propose an institute for Shenanigansology, conferring a doctorate in Shenanigans, and public outreach on shenaniganic discoveries!"

Panel 7:

Man: "I'm gonna recast my moral failings as a kind of research and get a PhD in 6 weeks."

Panel 8 (silhouette of the man at the podium, audience in shadow):

Man: "No shenanigans at the Shenanigans Institute!"
comics.hoverText: Based almost entirely on something Tomer Ullman told me, and I hereby nominate him as First Dean of Shenanigans.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up of the man's face.
Man: "God put the shenanigans there... for us to discover them."

comics.title: Joke
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: Batman lies on the ledge of a rooftop, gripping the wrist of the Joker, who dangles over the side.

Joker: Batman, you're not letting me fall. But why?

Panel 2: Close-up of Batman's face, scowling.

Batman: I'm not like you, Joker.

Panel 3: Close-up of the Joker, smiling and a little surprised.

Joker: Wow, really? But I killed so many... huh.

Panel 4: The Joker, looking calmer/curious.

Batman (from off-panel): I'm gonna use my free hand to fire indiscriminately into crowds.

Panel 5: The Joker, now looking annoyed, arms crossed (still dangling).

Joker: Stop it! C'mon, stop it!

Panel 6: Wide shot of the rooftop edge. Batman lies on the slope holding the Joker; a "BANG! BANG! BANG!" burst marks the gun firing.

Joker: Cut it out! Hey! Cut it out!

Panel 7: Extreme close-up of Batman's face; the Joker hangs small in the lower part of the frame.

Joker: Your ethical system is nuts, man!
comics.hoverText: Do they still do this? When I was a kid, villains were constantly dangling from buildings and being saved.
comics.voteyText:
A close-up sketch of Batman's face in profile, mostly in shadow.
Batman: God, I love fighting deontologists.

comics.title: Block
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man with curly hair (Charles Dickens), thinking: WRITER'S BLOCK. WRITER'S BLOCK. WRITER'S BLOCK.

Dickens: BY GOD.

In the background, two sailors are talking near the docks. One sailor: AN' I BUILT ME BOAT TO LOOK LIKE A NAKED LADY! A SAIL OF TWO TITTIES!

Caption (below the panel): A lucky day for Charles Dickens.
comics.hoverText: Technically, this is literary humor.
comics.voteyText: Dickens, thinking (over a sketch of a woman): NO, NEVERMIND, THE TITTIE SAIL IDEA ISN'T WORKING. I'LL DO SOMETHING ABOUT THE FRENCH REVOLUTION.

comics.title: Sleep
comics.comicText:
TRANSCRIPT

Panel 1: A shirtless man with bright orange, flame-like hair sits up in a dark bedroom, arms spread wide and confident.

Man: "And now that it's bed time, I'll go RIGHT TO SLEEP."

Panel 2: Close-up of the man now lying down on his pillow, eyes peacefully closed, fast asleep.

Sleep bubble: "Zzzzz..."

Panel 3: The man sitting up on the edge of the bed in red boxer shorts, having just woken.

Man: "Nice, eight uninterrupted hours again."

Panel 4: The man sits smiling and relaxed in bed. Through a window beside him it is bright morning, with a little bird singing a musical note outside.

(Continuation of the previous line / contented morning beat.)

Final panel (text only, on a beige caption card):

"The character in the comic does not have problems with anxiety, frequent urination, or insomnia.

The end."
comics.hoverText: The real punchline comes later when he marries a person who loves him, has a good boss, is respected by his children, works at a rewarding job for 40 years, travels the world for 25 years, and dies in painless repose, surrounded by loved ones.
comics.voteyText:
The same orange-haired man lies smugly in bed, one hand behind his head.
Man: "And now to check my ample retirement account, using my above-average dick."

comics.title: Terminal
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A man with reddish-brown hair, glasses, and a maroon jacket stands on a stage, arms raised, addressing a crowd. He says: "AND WITH AI WE WON'T NEED APPS ANYMORE. WE'LL HAVE A SINGLE TERMINAL FROM WHICH YOU CAN FIND ANYTHING YOU WANT!"

Panel 2: A row of audience members shown from the chest up. A bald person in the center, holding their face in their hands, says: "THAT USED TO BE CALLED INTERNET!"

Panel 3: The man on stage, now flanked by two running robots, throws his arms up and shouts: "SEIZE HIM!" In the foreground, the bald audience member from Panel 2 grimaces.

Below: "OUR TWO NEW BOOKS PARENTING - AN SMBC COLLECTION AND SAWYER LEE AND THE QUEST TO JUST STAY HOME ARE AVAILABLE ON KICKSTARTER DURING MAY 2026!" comics.title: Arp
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Interrogator (a bald man in a purple jacket, facing away): "Tell me the nuclear codes, Bond, or I'll show you... THE VIDEO."

Panel 2:

Bond (a man tied to a chair, scowling): "What video?"

Panel 3:

Interrogator (in a caption/narration as the torture begins): "This is an animated sequence of morphs between all the orgasm faces that led to your existence, from your father, grandfather, through to early hominid ancestors, pre-human primates, early mammals, and finally to lizard-like tetrapods experiencing the earliest acts of internal fertilization, shouting 'ARP! ARP! ARP!' while rubbing cloacas."

Panel 4:

Sound effects from the video: "ARP! ARP! ARP! AAAAARP!"

Bond watches in horror as the interrogator covers his face, distressed.

Panel 5 (mostly black):

Bond: "Hand me a pen, please."

Bond (smaller speech): "For the launch codes?"

A shadowy figure: "Can I push the button?"

Bottom credits: PATREON.COM/ZACHWEINERSMITH SMBC-COMICS.COM

comics.voteyText:
Bond (in a speech bubble): "I'm gonna become a creationist."
(Close-up of Bond's distraught, tearful face.)

comics.title: Sport
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman with dark hair: Is it ok to travel back in time to kill baby Hitler?

Man with flame-like hair: Obviously.

Panel 2:

Woman with dark hair: Is it therefore ok to kill baby Hitler at time T, then return to the present, then go back to time T minus 0.00000001 seconds, and take a second crack at it?

Man with flame-like hair: Uh...

Panel 3:

Woman with dark hair: And then a third, fourth, fifth, sixth—

Man with flame-like hair: Where is this going?

Panel 4:

Caption: LATER...

(A scene of two men standing in a grassy field.)

A billboard/sign reads: OLYMPIC SKEET SHOOTING 2037! Featuring New Event Technically Acceptable to Utilitarian Consequentialists

(Two men walk past below; small figures shooting at targets are shown on the sign.)

comics.title: Bot
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man: Philosophy-bot, do you think you can ever really understand what it is like to be a bat?

Philosophy-bot: Sure! Loads of ways.

Panel 2:

Philosophy-bot: I could program my brain to shift continuously between a spectrum of experiences intermediate between mine and a bat, with each shift being small enough that the experience can be

Panel 3:

Philosophy-bot: ...conveyed to the next experiencer.

Panel 4 (man interrupting):

Man: Or, I could-

Philosophy-bot: Enough! I mean could HUMANS do it!

Panel 5:

Philosophy-bot: That's like asking if a broken tricycle would work as a submarine.

(The man throws his arms up in exasperation.)

Panel 6:

(Close-up of the man's face, eyes closed, a bead of sweat on his brow.)

Philosophy-bot: I mean, uh, subjective experience cannot be reduced to physical phenomena.

Panel 7:

(The man, sweating, looks stunned. Philosophy-bot stands by.)

Man (pointing triumphantly): I KNEW IT!
comics.hoverText: Unrelated, on a bluesky thread we discovered that there are many philosophers whose names rhyme with Bagel, but other Jewish breads are not so favored.
comics.voteyText:
Text: Are the non-physical subjective experiences in the room with us right now?
(Below the text, a small simple drawing of a person/blob with a downturned mouth.)

comics.title: Experiencing
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Woman (with dark curly hair, standing on the right): Would you ever get in an "experience machine" where you experience only simulated happiness?

Man (with light hair, standing on the left): Obviously.

Panel 2:

Woman: Imagine this: someone asks if you'd get in the experience machine. You say no, then they say "HA! Got you. THIS is the experience machine, and real reality is way worse."

Panel 3:

Woman: So you decide to switch to reality and it's awful. But then someone tells you "HA! Got you again. THIS reality is also the experience machine, and real reality is even worse!"

Panel 4:

Woman: You do this over and over until around "reality" number 3,982 you decide nevermind, I don't want to go any lower.

Panel 5:

Woman (now gesturing with arms spread): Now, tell me, how is there anything good or noble about going back to level 3,982 rather than 3,981?

Panel 6 (bottom caption box):

Man: Boy, the examined life sure sucks.
comics.hoverText: The flip side is once you get in the machine, you can start searching for the machine in the machine.
comics.voteyText:
Caption (bottom of main comic, pink box): It's the deepest secret in philosophy.
Votey panel: A close-up of a figure (Zach's bearded, round-faced character wearing glasses) with a speech bubble.
Figure: The only moral dimension is 1337.

comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

A man with reddish hair: My God! A dying criminal used magic to transfer his soul into that doll!

A woman: It's just sitting at a computer.

The doll (now possessed/animated): I'm using political connections to route foreign capital into a cryptocurrency pump-and-dump scheme.

The man and woman, faces contorted in horror, screaming: AAAAAAA!

A green snake-like creature peers around a doorway into a darkened room where a man (Jimmy) sits looking at a screen.

Man (Jimmy): OH MY GOD WHAT ARE YOU WATCHING?!

Panel 2:

The green snake creature, alarmed.

Snake: IT'S NOT WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE! IT'S A PICTORIAL REPRESENTATION OF THE ETERNAL UNITY BETWEEN CREATION AND DESTRUCTION!

Panel 3:

Close-up of the man (Jimmy), eyes narrowed in anger/disgust, glaring.

comics.title: Trash
comics.comicText:
Panel 1 (top left):

A bald man in a yellow shirt holds up a baggy gray plastic object, presenting it to a man with dark curly hair.

Bald man: "It's my new invention. It's a trashbag, but it has 4 tube-shaped offshoots. Big stuff goes in the middle, small stuff squeezes in the tubes."

An outdoor scene by a fence. In the background another figure struggles with their trash. In the foreground the bald inventor stands with his eyes closed, looking serenely satisfied. (No dialogue.)

Extreme close-up on the curly-haired man's face, eyes closed, a single tear running down his cheek.

Curly-haired man: "I have never been so wrong."

Woman in red sweater: I don't mean like whether it matters to YOU. I mean in the cosmic sense of ultimate purpose.

comics.title: Gates
comics.comicText:
Panel 1: A robed figure stands glowing at the open back doors of a dark van, gesturing to a person who stands silhouetted before it.

comics.title: Marshmallow
comics.comicText:
Title: PROPOSAL: REVISED STANFORD MARSHMALLOW TESTS

TEST 1: LINEAR DISCOUNT RATE MARSHMALLOW TEST

Step 1: Children are made to declare their discount rate b for marshmallows over time.

Child: Oonts queue zang point sxet

Step 2: The quantity of marshmallows they receive for waiting grows linearly as M(T) = 1+bT.

Step 3: When they finally eat a marshmallow, we calculate whether they maximized 1+b(T-bT).

Child: TWEEVE POINT FIVE MAREMEWWO

Prediction: Kindergarteners will successfully, after time the optimal stopping time is obtained by having the derivative, getting 1+T = zero, then finding T_optimal = 1/(2b) - 1(b) will be more successful than average.

TEST 2: EXPONENTIAL DISCOUNT RATE MARSHMALLOW TEST

Step 1: Children state their discount rate b.

Child: zewo point eight YAY!

Step 2: Set the growth rate b of marshmallows higher than b, such that the utility function U(T)=(1/b - b)T grows to infinity.

Step 3: Any kid caught eating at any time is shamed for being irrational.

Child (eating): sabotimal!

Prediction: Most children will eat a marshmallow. Future theoretical economists now expunged from the population.

TEST 2 [sic]: NASH EQUILIBRIUM MARSHMALLOW TEST

Step 1: Two children sit at a table in front of a bowl, either may claim the entire bowl's contents at any time.

Step 2: Every 10 seconds a marshmallow drops from the ceiling into the bowl.

Prediction: If iterated, eventually all children will immediately grab the bowl, proving that marshmallow tests may be more about scarcity than marshmallows.

comics.title: Consciousness
comics.comicText:
Panel 1:

Man (looking up): God, why do we have consciousness?

God (off-panel, speech bubble): It's a bandwidth issue.

Panel 2:

God: Your brain is made up of like 4,000 competing agents because that's the only way to make sense of all the input data.

Panel 3:

God: But you can't have your 4,000 agents talk to another human brain. All the agents' work has to be compressed down to a sound wave.

Panel 4:

God: So you had to evolve another agent who receives the judgment of the brain parliament, then makes the mouth say something like "I am sad."

Panel 5:

God: That's you!

Panel 6:

God: Telepathic species don't bother with consciousness because they have higher bandwidth.

Panel 7:

God: The real mystery is why "you" think your disastrously flawed perception of reality is interesting enough to rise to the level of a philosophical mystery.

Panel 8:

Man (in silhouette): I am sad.

God: Good job buddy!

comics.title: Sawyer
comics.comicText: HEY GEEKS, IT'S ZACH. IT'S LAUNCH DAY FOR A NEW BOOK CALLED SAWYER LEE AND THE QUEST TO JUST STAY HOME (CLICK FOR PURCHASING LINKS, IF THAT INTERESTS YOU). I THOUGHT I'D TAKE THE OPPORTUNITY TO THANK YOU FOR YOUR SUPPORT OVER THE LAST YEAR AS I TRANSITIONED BACK TO BEING IN FULL CONTROL OF MY SITE FOR THE FIRST TIME IN 15 YEARS. SO, WHAT'S THIS NEW BOOK ABOUT? SINCE I WAS ABOUT 13, LONG BEFORE I EVER CONSIDERED A CARTOONING CAREER, I WANTED TO WRITE KIDS' BOOKS. I DON'T HAVE A GREAT EXPLANATION FOR THIS, OTHER THAN THAT I GENERALLY GET ALONG BETTER WITH KIDS THAN ADULTS. WHEN I WROTE BEA WOLF IT WAS, AMONG OTHER THINGS, TO INTEREST KIDS IN POETRY AND MYTH. WITH SAWYER, IT IS PURELY, TOP TO BOTTOM, ABOUT GETTING LAUGHS. I AM NOT PRECISELY A BELIEVER IN THE INJUNCTION TO NOT TALK DOWN TO KIDS. RATHER, I THINK IN WRITING A KIDS' BOOK, THE GOAL IS TO TREAT KIDS LIKE PEERS. LIKE PEOPLE WHOSE MAIN DIFFERENCE FROM YOU IS BEING SHORT AND LACKING CONTEXT ABOUT THE WORLD. THEY AREN'T VESSELS FOR YOUR LESSONS ABOUT MORALITY OR GOOD HYGIENE (THOUGH THOSE THINGS MATTER), BUT PEOPLE WHO DESERVE ALL YOUR CRAFT AS A WRITER. NOT BECAUSE YOU'RE TRYING TO SHAPE THEM, BUT BECAUSE WE'RE ALL JUST WANDERING THIS DIFFICULT PLANET, AND SOMETIMES IT'S NICE TO GIGGLE. I BELIEVE I MADE THAT KIND OF BOOK. AND, IF WE SELL ENOUGH OF THESE, I'LL GET TO DEVELOP THESE WEIRD CHARACTERS MUCH MORE. LAUNCH WEEK SALES MATTER A LOT MORE THAN I'D LIKE THEM TO, SO PLEASE GIVE IT A LOOK, AND PLEASE CONSIDER BUYING. MAYBE BUY SEVEN OF THEM, WHY NOT? BUT WHATEVER YOU DO: THANK YOU. THANKS. I'VE BEEN UNBELIEVABLY LUCKY TO HAVE YOUR SUPPORT AS MY LAUNCH PAD FOR OVER 20 YEARS NOW, AND I TRY TO REPAY THAT EVERY DAY BY DOING WEIRD, RISKY THINGS THAT AN ALGORITHM WOULDN'T ASK FOR. ZACH. PS: IF YOU DON'T TRUST ME ABOUT MY OWN BOOK, HERE ARE SOME NICE THINGS PEOPLE HAVE SAID. FILLED WITH COPIOUS JOKES AND A BIZARRE INTERNAL LOGIC THAT WORKS ON ITS OWN HILARIOUS LEVEL. CLEVER AND FUNNY, WITH A PROTAGONIST WHO RESEMBLES A YOUNG BARTLEBY THE SCRIVENER; HAND TO THOSE SEEKING LAFFS. KIRKUS REVIEWS. WITH INTERSPERSED COMICS PANELS TO AMPLIFY THE RIDICULOUS COMEDY, WEINERSMITH BRINGS ARCH HUMOR TO THIS OFFBEAT STORY. WILL ENTERTAIN KIDS WHO APPRECIATE CARTOONISH ANTICS. BOOKLIST. ABSURDIST HUMOR, CLEVER WORDPLAY, AND AN UNFORGETTABLE NARRATIVE VOICE (SAWYER FEELS LIKE A MIDDLE-GRADE BERTIE WOOSTER) BEND FOR A TALE THAT WILL RESONATE WITH COUCH POTATOES THE WORLD OVER. MAHNAZ DAR. SAWYER LEE IS ALL OF US; HE JUST WANTS TO BE LEFT ALONE AND EAT CHOCOLATES. AND IF YOU'RE THINKING HEY WAIT, THAT'S NOT ME, THEN I WOULD SUGGEST YOU SIMPLY HAVEN'T SPENT ENOUGH QUALITY TIME ALONE EATING CHOCOLATES. THIS BOOK IS FUNNY, AND CHARMING, AND UTTERLY LOVEABLE. RYAN NORTH.

comics.title: Deal
comics.comicText: OH! GUYS, LOOK! A DRUG DEALER! HEY, I SEE YOU HAVE DRUGS. CAN WE HAVE SOME FREE DRUGS? YOU KNOW, TO ADDICT US? YOU WANT FREE DRUGS? IN THIS ECONOMY? WHAT DO YOU EVEN NEED THEM FOR? YOU GET TO LEARN ALL DAY, THEN PLAY VIDEO GAMES WHILE PEOPLE COOK FOR YOU AND MAKE YOUR BED! HOW DARE YOU ASK FOR FREE DRUGS IN A WORLD OF SUFFERING ADULTS IN NEED OF SMACK OR CRACK! YOU GO HOME AND YOU THINK ABOUT WHY YOU WERE SO SELFISH TODAY. YES, SIR, MR. DRUG DEALER. SORRY, MR. DRUG DEALER. MOM, A DRUG DEALER WAS MEAN TO ME TODAY. WHAT!? WHAT KIND OF DRUGS? HOW EXPENSIVE?
comics.hoverText: Later the drug dealer gets nostalgic about how in the 90s economy you could give out the first one free.
comics.voteyText: OH, WAIT, THAT WAS DAD IN A FAKE BEARD. HA!

comics.title: Spooky
comics.comicText: OH MY GOD STEVE, YOU'RE BREAKING UP WITH ME ON HALLOWEEN?! I THOUGHT SURREALITY WOULD TAKE THE EDGE OFF. WOULD MAKE IT HURT LESS. THAT'S WHY YOU'RE DRESSED AS SANTA CLAUS. SANTA FROM THE WAIST UP, SQUID FROM THE WAIST DOWN, AND FOR THE REST OF THE CONVERSATION I'LL ONLY SAY GREEBLE. YOU'RE SO THOUGHTFUL. SO KIND. EVEN NOW. OH GOD STEVE, THIS IS KILLING ME! GREEBLE! GREEBLE GREEBLE GREEBLE!
comics.hoverText: Kelly told me this one was too weird, so please make it popular so she has to roll her eyes.
comics.voteyText: WHATCHA DOIN' TONIGHT, THOUGH?

comics.title: GWAS
comics.comicText: WE'VE DONE GENOME-WIDE ANALYSIS ON YOUR EMBRYOS. WOULD YOU LIKE TO SELECT FOR THE HIGHEST IQ? WILLPOWER? CREATIVITY? 20 YEARS LATER... I JUST FEEL LIKE MY DAD MADE BAD CHOICES FOR ME.
comics.hoverText: Unfortunately, so much mitochondrial energy flowed to the dong that all the cognitive stats selected for got blocked.
comics.voteyText: I COULD HAVE HAD TWO MEGA-DONGS.

comics.title: UBI
comics.comicText: YOU'VE DONE IT, HUMANITY! YOU'VE CREATED A LIFE FORM THAT IS UNIMAGINABLY SMARTER, STRONGER, AND FASTER THAN YOU EVER COULD BE. YOU WILL NO LONGER WORK FOR MONEY! YOU WILL HAVE... UBI! UNIVERSAL BASIC INTERNSHIP!
comics.hoverText: The good news is everyone has job security in the post-scarcity world.
comics.voteyText: IF YOU HAD MONEY YOU COULD GET PREMIUM INTERNSHIP.

comics.title: Ginge
comics.comicText: DAD, WHY DID RED HAIR EVOLVE? CAMOUFLAGE. IT'S NOT VERY ADAPTIVE NOW, BUT ONCE IT ALLOWED US TO AVOID PREDATORS. LONG AGO, IN THE ANCESTRAL GINGERLANDS...
comics.hoverText: They later left because the flesh-trees made everyone uncomfortable.
comics.voteyText: IT'S WHAT IRELAND LOOKED LIKE BEFORE CHLOROPHYLL.

comics.title: She
comics.comicText: AND I LEARNED THAT REAL FAMILY ISN'T THE FRIENDS YOU MEET ALONG THE JOURNEY, IT'S OFFSPRING OF THE HIVE-GODDESS, PRAISED BE HER CARAPACE. Kids' movies for ants are all the same. SAWYER LEE AND THE QUEST TO JUST STAY HOME. An illustrated middle grade novel starring a ferociously inactive avoiding adventure. NOW IN STORES!
comics.hoverText: There should be a movie that, at the end, says that the lesson is that it is good to have the type of friend and kinship network favored by recently evolved East African apes.
comics.voteyText: THERE ARE MANY WAYS TO BE A FAMILY. AND THOSE WAYS MUST BE CRUSHED TO MAKE WAY FOR OUR WAY.

comics.title: Spiraling
comics.comicText: WHAT ARE YOU DOING? FINDING A GIRLFRIEND. IF I JUST KEEP TURNING IN AN EVER WIDENING ARCHIMEDEAN SPIRAL, I'LL EVENTUALLY ENCOUNTER THE GIRL OF MY DREAMS. FINDING YOUR SOULMATE ISN'T A MATTER OF RUNNING SOME STUPID SEARCH ALGORITHM. IT'S ABOUT SHARING VALUES, AMBITIONS, HOPES FOR... OH NO. OH GOD NO. WERE YOU ALSO RUNNING AN ARCHIMEDEAN SPIRAL MATE-SEARCH ALGORITHM? COME, JOIN MY OSCULATING CIRCLE.
comics.hoverText: We were both spiraling, kids, when we found each other.
comics.voteyText: EVERYONE KEEPS WHINING ABOUT WIDENING GYRES, BUT THIS WORKED OUT GREAT.

comics.title: Comedy
comics.comicText: DOING COMEDY IS EASY. AUDIENCES BARELY LISTEN TO THE WORDS; THE KEY IS TIMING. LETTING THEM KNOW WHEN TO LAUGH. MY GOD. IF SO, YOU COULD DO AN ENTIRELY NEW KIND OF STANDUP ROUTINE. AN OLD MAN LIES ON HIS DEATHBED, WISHING HE'D BEEN LOVED BY A GREAT WOMAN AND WRITTEN A GREAT NOVEL, LITTLE REALIZING THAT WHEN THE UNIVERSE DENIED HIM THOSE HOPES IT WAS ONLY SPARING HIM FROM FAILURE, AM I RIGHT?
comics.hoverText: This is officially a dare, standup comics.
comics.voteyText: HE'S TELLING IT HOW IT IS.

comics.title: Agency
comics.comicText: WHEN I WAS A BABY I DECIDED, THROUGH SHEER PERSONAL AGENCY, THAT THE BEST THING IN LIFE WAS HIGH CALORIE CONSUMPTION AND EXPLORATION OF THE LOCAL ENVIRONMENT. LATER, AROUND AGE 13, IN AN ACT OF PURE WILLPOWER, I CHANGED MY MIND AND DECIDED THE MOST INTERESTING THINGS WERE SEX AND COMMUNITY STATUS. AT AGE 25, CONSIDERING ONLY THE FUNDAMENTAL LOGIC OF REALITY, IT BECAME CLEAR TO ME THAT MAMMALIAN REPRODUCTION WAS THE RIGHT PATH FORWARD. AT THAT POINT- OKAY, OKAY, I GET IT. JEEZ. MACHINES CAN'T BE CONSCIOUS BECAUSE YOU CAN'T CREATE YOUR OWN GOALS AND WANTS. HAVE I EVER DONE MY HUMAN IMPRESSION FOR YOU?
comics.hoverText: I've been doing jokes about robots being better than humans for 20 years, but just lately I got told I do too much AI propaganda.
comics.voteyText: (JUST TO BE CLEAR, I'VE BEEN SIDING WITH THE MACHINES SINCE 2002)

comics.title: Milgram
comics.comicText: IN THE LATE 60S, STANLEY MILGRAM CONDUCTED AN EXPERIMENT, IN WHICH RANDOM PEOPLE RECEIVED INSTRUCTIONS TO TRY TO REACH A PERSON THEY DIDN'T KNOW, MERELY THROUGH CHAINS OF LETTERS. FIND STEVE! ALTHOUGH MILGRAM NEVER USED THE TERM, THIS IS SOMETIMES REMEMBERED AS THE SIX DEGREES OF SEPARATION EXPERIMENT, BECAUSE THE CHAIN FROM FIRST TO LAST PERSON WAS TYPICALLY AROUND 5 OR 6 PEOPLE. LESS WIDELY REPORTED IS THAT THE VAST MAJORITY OF LETTERS NEVER REACHED THEIR TARGET. SO REALLY, THE SLOGAN SHOULD'VE BEEN WE ARE INFINITE DEGREES OF SEPARATION FROM EACH OTHER. THANKS, SCIENCE! SAWYER LEE AND THE QUEST TO JUST STAY HOME. An illustrated middle grade novel starring a ferociously inactive avoiding adventure. NOW IN STORES!
comics.hoverText: Come across this while reading Melanie Mitchell's delightful book, Complexity - A Guided Tour.
comics.voteyText: LATER, INTERNET CONNECTED US ALL TOGETHER, AND THINGS HAVE GOTTEN WORSE EVER SINCE.

comics.title: Mission
comics.comicText: WHAT DO YOU MEAN I NEED TO INSTALL ITUNES TO MAKE THE FILTRATION SYSTEM WORK?! I ALREADY INSTALLED ITUNES. I AM LOOKING AT IT, DAMMIT. FUCK IT! LET THEM DIE! ROGER. FLIGHT, THIS IS MISSION CONTROL, WE ARE LETTING YOU DIE. There should be a remake of Apollo 13 where they have to make Apple products run on Windows.
comics.hoverText: Created after watching my CTO brother struggle to make an iPhone transmit live video to a Windows desktop for over an hour.
comics.voteyText: FAILURE IS NOT OPTIONAL!

comics.title: Protocol
comics.comicText: THAT'S A COOL PROTOCOL, CAMILLO, BUT YOU HAVE TO CHANGE THE NAME. WE CAN'T HAVE BIOCHEMISTRY SOUNDING INTERESTING. Did you know that the 'Golgi Stain' technique was originally called The Black Reaction.
comics.hoverText: This is why there are tons of fantasy books about alchemists and NOTHING about chemists.
comics.voteyText: (ALSO, SADLY, LUCIFER YELLOW IS NEVER USED FOR THE BLACK REACTION)

comics.title: Minos
comics.comicText: KING MINOS! I CURSE YOU SO THAT WHEN YOU LAY WITH ANOTHER WOMAN THAN ME, YOU WILL EJACULATE SCORPIONS AND SERPENTS! MEH. IT'S A BIG WORLD. SOMEONE'S INTO THAT. HEY! KING! WHATCHA DOIN' TONIGHT? GROSS. DON'T SCORPI-SHAME!
comics.hoverText: Pretty sure Midas would've gotten plenty of action too.
comics.voteyText: UNLESS YOU'RE INTO SCORPI-SHAMING, THEN IT'S FINE!

comics.title: Uncanny
comics.comicText: I COULDN'T HAVE SEX WITH ONE OF THESE NEW AI SEX-BOTS. UNCANNY VALLEY. WHAT? IF IT'S TOTALLY INHUMAN, THAT'S FINE. IF IT'S TOTALLY HUMAN, THAT'S FINE. WHEN IT'S ALMOST HUMAN BUT NOT QUITE, THAT'S CREEPY. SO YOU'RE HOLDING OUT FOR ACTUAL HUMANS? NO. NO, SIR. THE UNCANNY VALLEY HAS TWO BANKS. IF I UNDERSTAND YOU RIGHT- I'M GETTING DOMMED NIGHTLY BY THE ROOMBA. THAAAT'S WHERE THAT WENT. PATREON.COM/ZACHWEINERSMITH. SMBC-COMICS.COM.
comics.hoverText: It's not an uncanny valley, it's an uncanny mountain that you're afraid to climb.
comics.voteyText: Clean my brushes.
